Heading: DDCA may throw open gates to pull in crowd - Indian Express
Content:
Mohita Sahdev hasn't lost a match in Delhi circuit in two years, and jumped 14 places in national rankings

Mohita Sahdev is a bundle of contradictions. She is undoubtedly one of the fittest badminton players in Delhi, but lacks strength in her attack.

She plays a defensive game, but had not dropped a game in the last two years – a tremendous record by any standard – till her 14-21, 21-15 and 21-10 victory over Nidhi Tiwari in the final of the Pramod Mahajan badminton tournament here on Monday. She also climbed fourteen places on the national ladder in the last one year to be ranked India number 22.

Mohita's No. 1 status on the capital's badminton circuit is undisputed. And though cynics may say that there is hardly any competition here, experts say it doesn't take anything away from Mohita's performances. "Delhi's badminton is in a pathetic state, especially women's. But Mohita's consistency shows she is far ahead of others by a fair margin," says Delhi chief coach Malvinder Dhillon.

However, fact remains that, outside Delhi, her performances have not been as encouraging – whether it is the seemingly routine pre-quarter-final exits, or her missed ticket to the Commonwealth Games 2010 trials which coincided with her final year exams.

"I know I haven't done too well outside Delhi, especially at the nationals. But this year I'm better prepared. The problem right now is my lack of power in the attacking shots. My coach Surjit Singh is working with me for that.

Despite suffering a shock loss in the first game against Nidhi, Mohita was least bothered going into the second game. "Even after losing the first game I knew I would win," she added.

The 20-year-old is as evasive talking about her weaknesses as her opponents' strengths. "I don't want to help my opponents out by revealing them, but my fast retrieving speed is one of my strongest points," smiles Mohita.

But Dhillon is more forthcoming. "Mohita is as fit as any national level player. Her only problem is the jerk that is required off the forehand smashes at their culmination. This is why most of her smashes lose speed and strength."

On the other hand, Dhillon gives just one example of what sets Mohita apart from the rest of the Delhi shuttlers. "Most of Delhi's girls are least bothered after their matches are over. It's visible from their attitude on the court and off it. In our time, we used to follow matches everywhere. If we lost to lesser-ranked players, we couldn't sleep for nights. But here, players are simply not interested," he says pointing to a top-five ranked player who lost in straight games to an injury-torn opponent.

Except Mohita, who was the only girl present at the venue watching the men's and boys category matches almost two-three hours after her win. Perhaps, that's what makes her the undisputed queen of Delhi badminton.

Heading: Act Two - Indian Express
Content:
After near empty stadiums for the first two Test matches between India and Australia, the onus is on Delhi & District Cricket Association (DDCA) to provide a 'fulfilling experience' to Test match cricket. With Diwali festivities falling on the same week, ticket sales have been painstakingly slow. And if the fans stay away from the grounds, like they did in Mohali and Bangalore, DDCA may mull throwing open the Kotla gates to get a full house for the third Test between India and Australia.

Sources in the top brass of the DDCA indicated that the DDCA executive board can also throw open the gates to get a sizeable crowd to the ground. "We'll have to wait at least for the first day's play to decide whether or not to throw open the gates," he told Sportline on Monday.

However, DDCA Vice-President Chetan Chauhan is confident of seeing 25,000 fans for the match. "Despite Diwali festivities and all the delays in ticket sales, we are expecting close to 25,000 fans in this Test match," Chauhan said. Interestingly, the revenues from the ticket sales have touched the Rs 20 lakh mark, which under these circumstances, is way above the target.

Kotla has seen big crowds, even for the nondescript matches, like the Mohammad Nissar Trophy match between Delhi and Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited. Even a practice match between Delhi and the visiting Pakistan team last year, saw a 10,000-plus cheering fans at the stadium. But there is a rider to this optimism — the fans visit Kotla, only if the entry is made free.

This would be viable solution to bring in the crowds. Further it would not dent DDCA's revenues, as in-house advertising and the television rights are their main earning channels during matches.

Heading: Wok’s Cooking? - Indian Express
Content:
Designer Anshu Arora makes a comeback with the Delhi Fashion Week

Five years ago, Delhi designer Anshu Arora was creating a sensation with her quirky, lovable designs and a unique aesthetic. But then Arora moved down South to Bangalore to marry fellow designer Jason Cheriyan, and disappeared from the fashion circuit. After missing for half a decade, an eternity in the fashion world, Arora is back with her label, Small Shop, and she held her first show at the Delhi Fashion Week . "It's been so long," smiles Arora sheepishly. "I must admit I was nervous."

It turns out she need not have worried. Their spring-summer collection, a non-fussy range of casual ensembles in cheery neon shades like orange and lime green, were low on embellishments and high on interesting drapes. The clothes, born out of a series of sketches done by Cheriyan, emphasised on living the eco-friendly way. "Jason had done these sketches which spoke of alternative forms of energy. Much of it was fantastical — things like chlorophyll energy and pumpkin dwellings done for our daughter, but later it developed into a lovely storyboard," says Arora.

The reaction, says Arora, has allayed her concerns. "We have quite a few offers. Even our kids line was appreciated by buyers from Saudi Arabia. Honestly, it made coming back to the city after so long, so special," says Arora, with a nod.

Of course, Arora and Cheriyan have made their presence felt in Bangalore. They have their own store in the city and retail out of Evoluzione in Chennai and Aza and Ogaan in Delhi. They have got into home furnishings, and after the birth of their daughter Tara, even branched into kids wear. "We want to look beyond India now, at markets overseas, so we thought showing at a fashion week would be a good option," she says, having sold out of Selfridges and Saks Fifth Avenue earlier in her career.

Jason and Anshu, as the two are now known, are wisely keeping the economic meltdown in mind. Arora says they ensure that the consumer gets his money's worth. "As a designer I need to go in for multiple products, rather than stick to ensembles alone," she explains. Accordingly, there are a gamut of other products — kitschy shoes, interesting ear-muffs, headphones and attractive jewellery that now form part of her stable. "In times such as these buying should be an experience. That's what our focus is on now," she says.

Heading: Second Innings - Indian Express
Content:
A unique Italian food culture comes to the city

Big boys don't cry, but at the tender age of 27 they are at times moved to tears by a steaming bowl of polpa della frutta minestre (a fruity dessert soup), like I was at the Italian food festival at the ITC Sonar. The heady flavour of olive oil and pesto combine in this piquant dessert, which is quite unlike anything I have tasted before. And for those who don't exactly have a sweet tooth, other Calitri delights like beckti al cartoccio (baked beckti with olive oil and sale) or risotto alla calitri (risotto cooked with pesto) may do the trick.

For Calitri, a quaint village in Italy has a gastronomic tradition quite different to the mainstream Italian one. It's located in the region of Campania, about an hours drive away from Naples and has witnessed many wars and invasions in centuries, which makes it a melting pot of cultures. Lentil stews, cereals, seafood and minimalist preparations of meat make for the staples, and the ingredients are almost always indigenously produced.

The Calitri menu at ITC, attempts to remain true to the simplicity of this indigenous food culture. Chef Sunayan Pramanik consciously tries to never overdo the dishes, like most overconfident chefs do. So the rock lettuce, which is used as a garnishing, retains its overwhelmingly herby taste (a thing most high-on-overcooked-palak-paneer Kolkatans will find to be offensive), and the humble lentil stew is not sexed up with a dash of oregano. Nor is the carciofi ripieni (stuffed artichoke hearts with walnut tapenade and anchovy) made crispier to play to the galleries.

The Calitri experience at the ITC Sonar will prove to be a bit heavy on your pocket (a meal for two will cost you about Rs 4000) but then it comes with the "authentic" tag.

Yet, one may argue that there is little sense in trying and replicating flavours deeply rooted in the specific ingredients of a small area of a different country. True, but then how else would big boys be moved to tears?

The Calitri menu is available at the West View Bar & Grill at ITC Ssonar, till November 9

Heading: The Man who would be King - Indian Express
Content:
Retired cricketer Jonty Rhodes talks about his new career in wine and his effort to fight against global warming

South African batsman Jonty Rhodes, known more for his aggressive play on the cricket field, has smoothly made a transition into business in his hometown, Durban. He is now the director of 10 Chapters, a wine label from Durban. Dressed casually in denims, Rhodes, 39, patiently signed autographs for fans at Sheraton Hotel in Saket. Playing cricket, he answered, was good while it lasted. "I don't miss the game. I'm involved with it, but there are several new, interesting spheres in my life," smiles Rhodes, who will be coaching the team Mumbai Indians for the Twenty 20 matches in April next year.

Rhodes is juggling a part-time job as banking executive in one of Durban's multinational banks, along with promoting wine from South Africa all over the world. "Whatever I know about wine is thanks to my winemaker Stefan Gerber, who educated me about the wine growing region around Durban. This is the first time when I am speaking to various importers and understanding the market in India. It is fun," he says, in between animated discussions of terroir and grape quality.

When he is not strolling through the vines with his winemaker, Rhodes prefers surfing, mountain biking and tackling the issue of global warming, which is close to his heart. "We are in talks with TATA-BP technologies to set up a plant in Durban as the CO2 emissions are its highest ever. We need to protect the future generation from the hazards of global warming. It was since the time of apartheid that such issues were brushed under the carpet and we are facing the consequences today," he says, easily slipping into the role of an amateur environmentalist. Eleventh chapter, perhaps?

Heading: Diwali Hues - Indian Express
Content:
Devdutt Pattanaik (in the picture) chuckled when I gaped at him in shock. "Yes, I wrote the book in four days," says Pattanaik, who was in town last week for the release of his latest work in Hindu mythology, The Book of Ram (Penguin, Rs 250). A mythologist for over 14 years now, earlier this year Penguin published Pattanaik's The Pregnant King, which has been selling very well. "I live, eat, breath mythology and I write every single day for different magazines, columns and books that I plan to put together. This book has been in my head for years now and in four days it all came together," says Pattanaik, who has also illustrated the book with his own drawings based on the Ramayan.

The Book of Ram deals with the story of the Hindu king Ram, the only monarch to be worshipped as a deity. "Ram is Eka-vachani, a king who always keeps his word, Eka-bani, an archer who strikes his target with the first arrow and Eka-patni, a husband who is eternally and absolutely devoted to a single wife. But within these roles, Ram is caught between desire and destiny. As Maryada Purushottam, the supreme upholder of social values, it is interesting to see how he balances the roles he was created to fulfill," says Pattanaik, who has put the story of the Ramayan and analysed every action as well as reaction in eleven essays in the book. He also explores the relevance of Ram in modern times by examining him in his various roles: as Dashrath's son, Lakshman's brother, Vishwamitra's student, Sita's husband and Ravan's enemy.

Heading: No complaint, but cops arrest seven for fraud - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), which today secured the permission of a court to conduct narco-analysis, polygraph and brain mapping tests on Sadhvi Pragyasingh Thakur in connection with the Malegaon and Modasa blasts case, is on the lookout for an ex-army Subedar Major from Farrukhabad district of Uttar Pradesh for alleged links with suspects.

The ATS also seemed to be narrowing in on the suspected role of retired Major Ramesh Upadhyay in helping the arrested Hindu activists.

A senior ATS official said the retired Subedar Major belongs to a village in Kampil area of Farrukhabad and his name came up during the interrogation of a Hindu Jagran Manch activist arrested from Indore. The HJM activist claimed that the ex-army man was an active member of the Bajrang Dal, had expertise in assembling timer devices and was called Master by the activists.

A Maharashtra ATS team is expected in Lucknow by Wednesday to trace the ex-army man and the UP police have been informed about it. The UP ATS team failed to trace the Subedar Major. His family members told the police that he had gone to Kolkata in June and had not returned ever since.

The Maharashtra ATS official said they had evidence that the ex-army man had visited the office of Hindu outfit Sanatan Sanstha in Thane last April. Two members of the outfit were chargesheeted, allegedly for planting bombs at a theatre in Thane on June 4, according to B G Kulkarni, senior police inspector of Navapada police station in Thane where the case was registered.

Meanwhile, the Maharashtra ATS has secured the permission of a court to conduct narco-analysis, polygraph and brain mapping tests on Sadhvi Pragyasingh Thakur. ATS counsel Ajay Misar said that investigators Hunt for Master, an ex-army man, takes ATS to UP wanted to conduct the tests on the 38-year-old sadhvi as she was "changing her statements and not co-operating with the investigation." The tests were needed to "channelise the investigation and to scrutinise facts with the help of scientific tests", he added.

The sadhvi, who police say is an extremely radical Hindu activist, will have to undergo 17 clinical tests before she is subjected to the forensic tests. Misar said that she would be taken to the Forensic Science Laboratory in Mumbai's Kalina suburb for the three tests but did not give a date.

The questioning is expected to mainly revolve around the origin of the RDX used in the explosives, the route taken to transport them and identities of others who may have helped her allegedly carry out the attacks.

According to the first forensic report from the Nashik laboratory, traces of RDX were found in 19 articles that were collected as evidence from the blast site in Malegaon and a final report on the same is awaited.

Meanwhile, sources said that the questioning of retired Major Upadhyay was progressing and they were closing in on his suspected role and links with the sadhvi and the two men arrested last week in connection with the blasts.

Another Hindu activist, Sameer Kulkarni, who was picked up on Saturday night by the ATS, was also being questioned. Suspected to have links with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) as well as the voluntary organisation 'Abhinav Bharat' — of which Major Upadhyay is the working president —Kulkarni was known to have organised an exhibition against terrorism at Gandhi Bhavan in Bhopal in April.

Sources today said that exhibits at the event were said to include pictures of Hindus being displaced from the Kashmir Valley, books on Islamic terrorism as well as literature about Veer Savarkar, Subhash Chandra Bose and Nathuram Godse. — (With inputs from Milind Ghatwai in Bhopal)

Heading: Sugar mills to challenge govt order - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow police arrested seven persons on Sunday night for fraud. But no police officer knew who had been their victims and when and where the alleged fraud took place.

Those arrested included two activists of the People's Union for Human Rights (PUHR) — Vinod Yadav and Sarafaraz — from Azamgarh. They had participated in a dharna at Azamgarh on October 6 against alleged harassment of innocent people in the name of fighting terror.

Others arrested with them, according to the police, were Badre Alam and Bal Govind from Azamgarh, Rizwan and Azam Ansari from Deoria, and Paras Nath from Barabanki.

PUHR activist Shahnawaj Alam said while Vinod and Sarfaraz belonged to his organisation, he did not know about others. He alleged that the two of them had been framed. "We had informed senior police and administrative officials about these persons having gone missing two days ago," he said. Vinod's brother Raju said he left Azamgarh on Thursday, telling his wife Sarita that he had some work in Lucknow in connection with his NGO, Karvan. Sarfaraz had gone with him.

On Friday morning, Vinod's cellphone went dead, Raju said. Later, his PUHR colleagues informed the police.

Sub-Inspector Deshraj Khanna of Alambagh police station said the police had arrested the men after a tip-off that some persons involved in fraud were coming to the Alambagh bus stand.

"We cordoned off the area and arrested them. A golden power, weighing about 250 gms, was seized from them. They used the powder to cheat people, telling them they could convert ordinary objects into gold," said Khanna.

But even senior police officers had no idea whom the arrested persons had defrauded and when.

Circle Officer Virendra Kumar said, "I have to check the details". ASP (East) Harish Kumar said, "I don't know much about the case." The IG of Lucknow zone, AK Jain, said he was "not aware of the details", while ADG Brij Lal refused to comment.

National general secretary of People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) Chitranjan Singh said: "Vinod was present for the dharna at Azamgarh. We will fight against injustice done by the police." The PUCL and PUHR had jointly organised the dharna. Defence lawyer BK Jaiswal said the accused have been remanded in jail custody for 14 days.

Heading: IIM-L students wait for summer placements with fingers crossed - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Sugar Mills Association (UPSMA), the apex body of the private sugar industry in the state, is likely to challenge the State Advisory Price (SAP) for sugarcane announced by the state government for 2008-09.

Cane crushing is likely to be delayed as UPSMA is not willing to commence operations of the sugar mills until the price issue is resolved.

On October 18, Chief Minister Mayawati had announced the SAP of Rs 145 per quintal for the early variety of sugarcane, Rs 140 per quintal for the common variety and Rs 137.50 per quintal for the unapproved varieties of the sugarcane.

"The SAP announced by the UP government is not acceptable to us. A meeting of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) is scheduled to be held in Delhi after Diwali, where a final decision to challenge the SAP in the High Court will be taken," said K N Shukla, UPSMA Secretary.

The government should either provide subsidy at a rate of Rs 20 to 25 per quintal to the private sugar mills or reduce the SAP, he added. The UPSMA will soon write to Mayawati apprising her of the situation.

"The UPSMA was not given adequate opportunity to put up its viewpoint before the advisory committee headed by the state chief secretary. We came to know on October 9 that the meeting will be held the next day," Shukla said.

Cane Commissioner Har Charan Prakash, however, claimed the government was committed to protect the interests of the farmers. The recent hike of Rs 15 per quintal in SAP will fetch an additional income of Rs 975 crore to sugarcane growers, he added.

Heading: SP claims to burn 50,000 effigies of Mayawati - Indian Express
Content:
As the Indian Institute of Management-Lucknow (IIM-L) is all set to begin its summer placements from November 7, the possible impact of the global financial crisis looms large on the campus.

The 320 students who await summer placements are ready for fewer offers. Some think the institute will be lucky if half the usual crop of multinational companies come back. For others, it is a wait and watch situation. The IIM-L administration, however, is not sitting idle. According to sources, the institute will wait for a few more days to see if too many companies drop out of the placement game. In which case, the institute will open doors companies disallowed earlier.

"There are some companies, which only register their presence in the campus but do not make offers. We usually keep such companies out of the placement list. This time, we may allow them to take part in the placement procedure," said a faculty member.

Last year, around 285 students had received 424 summer placement offers. There was also a sudden spurt in international offers — 28 in 2007 from a dismal six of 2006.

Apart from Lehman Brothers, companies like BNP Paribas Hong Kong, Citibank Hong Kong, Barclays Capital (London), Unilever (London), Proctor & Gamble, etc had made international offers.

Prof Shushil Kumar, Chairman of the Placement cell at IIM-L, said: "The number of offers may be lower as compared to previous years. But nothing can be said as of now. The domestic companies may be the frontrunners this time. Things will be clear when the placement week begins from November 7."

The assurance by Merrill Lynch, a leading financial management company of the US to participate in the summer placements as promised earlier, has brought some hope to the students.

"In the last few years, companies have started giving importance to summer placements. They also give preference to the same students during final placements. Thus, taking the right decision during this period will be crucial," said a student, who has decided to take up a job in the finance sector, despite the downfall.

Heading: UP plans panels to maintain quality of technical education - Indian Express
Content:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) claimed its cadres have burnt over 50,000 effigies of Chief Minister Mayawati across the state on Monday.

The workers burnt the effigies as part of the party's Dera Dalo Ghera Dalo programme to protest against thefts from the state exchequer by government officials.

"The programme has been extended to protests against police lathicharge and repressive measures adopted by the administration to crush SP's peaceful agitation," said a party leader.

State working president of SP, Shivpal Singh Yadav, said: "Effigies of Chief Minister Mayawati have been burnt in almost every village of the state. Courting arrest and burning her effigies will continue even during Diwali. It will be called off only after the chief minister bows out of her office."

He added that soon after Diwali, a state executive meeting of the party will be convened to chalk out a strategy to intensify the programme.

Targeting the bureaucracy, Yadav claimed that a section of the police and IAS officials were responsible for the brutalities meted out to the SP workers, who have so far staged peaceful demonstrations. "They will be taken to task after the Samawjadi party comes to power," he said. "Forty-one workers, along with the local MLA Anoop Sanda were arrested in Sultanpur today. We have received similar reports from Deoria, Kushinagar, Mirzapur, Sonebhadra and Bareilly. In these districts, the police have brutally lathicharged party workers," Yadav claimed.

Heading: When defence is linked to terror - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to improve the quality of education in the state, the government is setting up five committees to ensure that national standards are met at the state's institutions. It is also launching an initiative — "Learning while earning" to aid post graduates secure jobs in the education sector.

The mushrooming of technical colleges in the state this year — the exact figure being 141 — has created ripples of worry in its wake.

SS Ram, director, technical education, Public-Private Partnership Cell, UP government, said: "Most private sector colleges set up do not have good infrastructure and the lack of quality checks has led to a drop in the quality of education. The monitoring, too, is not up to the mark."

The five committees planned by the government will be responsible for conducting surprise checks on the 427 institutes in the state.

The colleges will be judged on basis of two indicative parameters — infrastructure and achievement.

Any college with a below average infrastructure and less than half of its students getting pass marks will be shut down. They will also have to forfeit their security deposits.

"Qualified post graduates, like MTech graduates, will be given priority for the post of guest lecturers in technical institutes," said Ram. With this scheme, around 50 new posts of guest lecturers will be created.

With a 60 per cent hike in salary approved by the Sixth Pay Commission, the teaching profession is expected to become more attractive. Around 5.5 lakh teachers will receive the benefit of University Grants Commission's recommendation of the commission from December.

Heading: Ex-major’s ‘detention’ stuns neigbours - Indian Express
Content:
Reflects loss of army's faith in government, says retired colonel

Retired army officers being questioned by investigative agencies for their alleged links with the Malegaon blasts has not come as a surprise to Col Jayant Chitale (retd), the man who once started a commando academy to form suicide squads for carrying out attacks in Pakistan.

Chitale said army officers were angry for the failure of the government in tackling terrorism. "They are also losing faith in the judiciary for its failure to give prompt and proper punishment to terrorists," he said.

"Incidents like India handing over a terrorist to the enemy in the plane hijack case and politicisation of the Afzal Guru issue are having a demoralising effect on the army, forcing the officers to plan their own ways for countering terrorism," he said.

Chitale had formed the Maharashtra Military Foundation (MMF) in Pune in October 1993 and a few years after that started a Commando Academy at Badlapur.

"I wanted to form suicide squads for carrying out attacks in Pakistan. I had also informed the Central Government and the Army Headquarters about my plan. My first suicide squad was ready in 2002. I had to close the academy for some reasons, but I am still training the youths in self defence techniques and motivating them to join the army," he said.

Asked about the association of retired army officers with Hindu outfits, he said, "Officers are generally not against Muslims. There are excellent patriotic Muslim officers in the Army. Politicians are showing no will to counter Islamic terrorism. So some retired officers may think of countering Islamic terrorism for which they may develop contacts with Hindu organisations".

VOICES
Even the top brass in defence forces are unhappy with the way politicians are tackling terrorism. But the possibility of retired officers joining extremist groups for countering terrorism is rare. Officers below the rank of major might be thinking on those lines...
hikant Mehendale, Military historian

Some officers feel there is no religion but a lot of politics and economics behind terror activities. But the majority of the officers, especially those who have worked more in border areas, feel that terrorism in India is religion based. These officers say they were not able to speak about it openly while in service,


Anand Saraf, founder Sainik Mitra Parivar

I don't feel that officers who have served the army would ever take to the extremism to counter Islamic terrorism.
Col (retd) Pradeep Brahmankar, Apex Careers

Heading: Abhinav Bharat’s site shut - Indian Express
Content:
The Rail Residency Cooperative Housing Society in Akurdi, where Major (Retd) Ramesh Upadhyay was reportedly picked up by the Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) on October 23 is abuzz with activity on Monday, with the media landing in droves.

But most of the neighbours of the Upadhyays preferred to stay indoors, away from prying eyes.

That was not the scene on Sunday when this reporter called on the Upadhyays where police officers in mufti were keeping surveillance despite the fact the ATS was yet to formally announce it had arrested Upadhyay in connection with any terror strikes.

A police inspector there tried to play down any connection with the Malegaon blasts. "We have come on a regular inquiry after we got to know that Upadhyay was picked up by the Mumbai ATS. Just because ATS picked him up does not mean he is linked to the Malegaon blasts," he said.

Neighbours tried to conceal their shock and spoke in hushed tones even as sleuths moved around the area. "The Upadhyays have been staying here on rent for nine years and we are family friends. Uncle has a sound knowledge of astrology. He has three daughters, Madhu, Poonam and Nidhi and a son Vishal, all in their 20s," said a woman of the neighbourhood. She said she was aware that the police had taken him away a few days back.

"Earlier they used to stay in row house number A/18 but a couple of years back they shifted to this house — row house number 17. We feel uncle has been framed by somebody. We don't believe he could be involved in any blasts," she said. October 23 onwards, the police have been camping outside the house, she added.

Another neighbour, also seeking anonymity, said: "Ramesh is good in astrology and I have seen people visiting him for guidance. He is a supporter of the Bharatiya Janata Party. When I asked police why they are camping outside the society for three days, they said it was none of my business."

"I read in the papers that ATS had nabbed two retired army majors in connection with the Malegaon blasts. That is how I figured out that ATS had picked up Upadhayay. I don't believe he could have indulged in any terror activity as he is a decent man," he added.

"We don't wish to speak to the media right now, but if needed, we will definitely contact you," Madhu, Upadhyay's daughter, had said on Sunday. But a day later it didn't appear as if any of them wanted to talk to anybody.

Heading: Khadki factory employee caught selling bullets - Indian Express
Content:
The official website of Abhinav Bharat has been shut, with members of the Pune-based organisation being detained for suspected links with the Malegaon blasts and also with one of the accused, Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur.

Working president of the organisation, Maj Ramesh Updhayay (retd) and a member, Sameer Kulkarni of Chinchwad, have been detained for questioning. Records show the website with domain name abhinavbharat.com was hosted on May 19, 2007 and was last accessed on Sunday. It has ben closed since.

The website stated Sant Kripa, 16/4, Erandwane, off Karve Road as the registered office of the organisation. The same address, along with a landline number, was mentioned as the technical contact.

When contacted on the number, the person who received the call said he was not aware of any Abhinav Bharat. The Indian Express visited the address to find a bungalow and a fabrication workshop at the place. The family residing at the bungalow said it was their property and they had been staying there since 1965. "We don't know about any Major Upadhyay," a family member said. The website was administered by Chitra Infotech in Nashik. When contacted on the number of Chitra Infotech mentioned on the website, the person who answered refused to speak.

Heading: Diwali: Play it safe, caution doctors - Indian Express
Content:
A major security breach was reported from the ammunition factory at Khadki, a premier defence establishment, on Monday, when the city police nabbed an employee of the factory selling 20 rounds outside.

He is believed to have smuggled out the bullets from the factory premises over a period of time.

Police inspector Rajendra Bahirat received information that a person named Bholenath Dhondiba Bhegde (31) was going to sell live bullets at Nashik Phata Chowk on Mumbai-Pune highway. Unit 3 of the city Crime Branch nabbed Bhegde who works in the case plant of the factory. Bhegde was caught selling bullets to Santosh Pawar (30) whose antecedents were not known. The police recovered 20 bullets worth Rs 4,000 of 9 mm and .38 mm calibre from him. Bhegde is a resident of Type 2, 77/23, Range Hills. Pawar is a resident of Chougule Wada in the city.

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajender Singh (crime) said Bhegde used to sell bullets to Pawar for Rs 50 each and he, in turn, sold it to other people for Rs 100.

Investigations revealed that Bhegde, who had been employed at the ammunition factory for the past 12 years, regularly smuggled out bullets from the premises.

Singh said a case had been registered against Bhegde at Bhosari police station. He was produced in court on Monday and remanded in police custody till November 1. Pawar has told police that he used the bullets for hunting animals. But police suspect he is lying. Bhegde's father, as also his brother, used to work at the factory. Bhegde got the job after his brother's death.

Senior general manager of the ammunition factory, A K Agarwal, said the matter was under investigation. "I will review the security situation tomorrow."

Factory security chief Santosh Sabnis said, "There are 4,000 employees in the factory. We frisk each and every employee.This employee might of smuggled out bullets, we don't deny that possibility."

Heading: Killed while realising dream of becoming a police officer - Indian Express
Content:
Firecrackers are fun but can be dangerous too if not used the proper way. It's children who often play the fool and tamper with firecrackers leading to injuries during Diwali, according to the head of the burns unit at Sassoon General Hospital.

"Negligence is often the cause if minor burn injuries," said the doctor.

But firecrackers burst in a tin box or a rocket lighted up after placing it in a glass bottle can be quite dangerous. Burn specialists and plastic surgeons are on 24-hour emergency call during Diwali.

The Sassoon General Hospital and Surya hospital have their special burns wards ready for any casualty.

Avoiding mishaps during the festival only needs the supervision and vigilance on the part of those celebrating the festival, said Devendra Potphode, chief of the Fire Brigade division of Pune Municipal Corporation.

Pothode said that this year, stringent conditions were laid down for licence to stall owners for selling firecrackers. "Against the usual 50-60 distress calls every day, we have been getting only three-four calls so far," said Potphode. About half the injuries during Diwali are burns, especially in the face, hand, wrist or arm, says Dr Jaisingh Shinde, Chief surgeon at Surya Hospital.

Loss of eyesight and damage to eardrums were also likely. Doctors have urged that firecrackers be lit in an open area and a bucket of water kept ready nearby for any eventuality.

Heading: Cooperate with mayor, Kalmadi tells Bagul - Indian Express
Content:
Right from his childhood Suhas Paraker wanted to be a police officer. On Sunday, his dream became the cause of his death and now a pall of gloom has descended on Mahesh Nagar, the area in Pimpri-Chinchwad where the family lives.

Police sub-inspector Suhas Paraker died in a Naxal ambush in Gadchiroli on Sunday, barely days after he took charge of his new posting. His neighbours said Parekar had been transferred to Gadchiroli on October 13.

The Parekar family hails from Dharur village in Beed district but his funeral will be held at Aurangabad where his sister lives. Parekar's neighbour Prashant Chandan Shiv said, "Parekar's family left for Auangabad on Sunday afternoon. Though he is a native of Dharur, none of his family members live there. So his funeral will be held in Aurangabad."

Parekar's neighbour Chetan Arun Nanavre (27) said, "Suhas was a very studious and sincere man. Their family has been staying at Mahesh Nagar for the past eight years and we had good relations with them. Suhas married two years ago."

Paraker is survived by his wife Samiksha Parekar (28) and a 10-month-old son, Rachit. "He had come here on October 11 and told me he had got his transfer to Gadcharoli and would have to join duty on October 13. He left on October 12 for Gadcharoli," said Nanaware. Suhas had completed his education in Aurangabad where he had stayed with his married sister.

Parekar's wife and his mother live at Mahesh Nagar with his elder brother Suresh Parekar, his wife and two daughters. Suresh Parekar is principal with a private college in Wakad.

One of Parekar's relatives said, "He was very tenacious and determined. Right from childhood, it was his dream to become a police officer."

Heading: Cylinder blasts: 3 in 2 month, 11 dead - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping an eye on the ensuing Lok Sabha elections, Congress MP Suresh Kalmadi seems to be softening his stand on Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). He has asked the newly appointed opposition party leader in Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) Ulhas Bagul to co-operate with mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale of NCP, for the sake of city's progress.

He also said that for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections, Congress is going to join hands with the NCP. "Alliance with the NCP is present at the national as well as the state level, therefore, we are going to do so in Pune as well," he said.

Kalmadi paid a visit to the PMC headquarters on Monday evening after a year and half with much pomp and retinue of party workers, to congratulate Bagul for getting the post of opposition party leader, after winning a legal battle against Vikas Mathkari, BJP leader in PMC.

While thanking the mayor for appointing Bagul on the post, Kalmadi said, "This post has increased the responsibility of the Congress. Our party will be working for the development of the city. Therefore, we need to work in accordance with other parties. We want to move ahead working in tandem with the mayor."

He added, "The Commonwealth Youth Games has proved a success. We want to continue doing such good works for the city and hold Olympics games here in future. The Olympics will naturally bring in much more investment and growth for the city. Our aim is to make Pune an international city. However, for Olympics, we need to have the necessary infrastructure in place, including the Metro Rail and new international airport. For this, we will have to work hard at least for the next 4-5 years."

When asked whether Congress wants to strike an alliance with the NCP at the municipal level, he said, "We are ready to join hands with them for the sake of the development of the city. However, it is up to them to make a decision, but they will always have our cooperation."

Bagul also vowed to work cooperating with other parties in PMC. City congress chief Abhay Chhajed and other corporators were present on the occasion.

Heading: Cops again talk tough, to arrest traffic violators without warrant - Indian Express
Content:
Citizens openly flout safety norms, say fire brigade officials. 'This is a very dangerous issue'

With the cylinder blast on Sunday night at the busy Appa Balwant Chowk area, the third one in less than two months, how far people abide by safety norms has become a serious concern now.

All the three blasts were caused due to explosion of LPG cylinders used for domestic purposes. Though fire officials attribute the Sunday incident to a stray firecracker that landed on the roof of the building, where three cylinders were kept, it was clear that the owner of the building had openly flouted safety norms.

This could have led to a huge disaster in the crowded Appa Balwant Chowk had the fire not been brought under control in time. A couple of weeks ago, another gas cylinder explosion in Dehugaon cost six people their lives with 12 others getting seriously injured due to the gas burns while another blast in the city in Lohia Vasti at Hadapsar had left five dead.

Devendra Potphode, chief of the Fire Department Pune Division, said, "it is indeed appalling to see such incidents of fire due to cylinders bursting on the rise. But there is little that we can really do about it. In all these three cases fires were caused due to the negligence of the owners of the house."

He added, "Most people, to avoid the cost of replacing faulty valves and tubes in the gas cylinders, take the easy way out by patching up the joint or using insulated tape to patch up the leaking tubes. The average age of a rubber tube is up to three years. People should get the gas valves and rubber tubing inspected once in every six months to ensure no such untoward incidents occur."

Speaking about the fire at Appa Balwant Chowk, Additional divisional fire officer, Prashant Ranpise said, "The owner of the building had dumped a lot of scrap materials on the terrace. Repair work of gas cylinders and cooking range was also done on the terrace. Materials were left lying carelessly in the open. Had the fire not been reported immediately, it could have spread and caused much more damage than what it did."

Potphode explained that cylinder fires could also lead to a backlash effect. Elaborating more on it he said, "The gas used in cylinders is heavier than air. When it permeates through any leaks it starts spreading in all directions and once it meets with even a spark fire it ignites and spreads rapidly. Sometimes it spreads in the reverse direction from where it started and reaches the source (cylinder) and then explodes. This is a very dangerous issue; the fire in Dehugaon had spread the same way. People should ensure that no flammable materials are stored on terraces. Keep cylinders stored in places where there in no visible fire source. In case there is a cylinder leak they should not operate any electrical switches or matches but should immediately turn off the cylinder and open the doors and windows to let in fresh air."

The fire department is also doing all that is possible to ensure that citizens have a safe Diwali. "We are going out at all major stalls selling crackers and are spreading out this message to the citizens: "We want the citizens of the city to celebrate a Diwali free of any accidents," Potphode said.

Heading: City girl in the finals of Halla Bol - Indian Express
Content:
Alarmed by the increasing attacks on police personnel on duty, the city police is once again talking tough. They have decided to arrest traffic violators without warrant under Section 202 of the Motor Vehicles Act. The city police is however keeping mum on Section 395, which entails dacoity charge. This section was applied over a month back against citizens after a scuffle with a traffic police on Laxmi Road.

Joint Police Commissioner Rajendra Sonawane attributed the tough police posturing to the increased frequency of attacks on policemen by traffic violators and other offenders. "There have been around 60 cases of assault on policemen registered against citizens. Out of the total of 60 cases, 25 cases are pertaining to the city traffic police. The police have arrested a total of 128 people in this regard," Sonawane said. In past three months, the situation has become alarming "Thirtyfive incidents of attacks against the police have taken place in the months of August, September and up to October 27. In these three months 18 pertain to the traffic police." He said adding that though a majority of the citizens are law abiding, it is just one per cent who create such nuisance.

He said that the citizens should themselves come forward to help the police if they are attacked. Many "goonda" elements are also threatening the police and assaulting them. "This is done to create a fear in their minds." He, however, refused to comment on the Section 395 of the IPC applied in the Laxmi Road case. "The matter is subjudice...I will not comment," he said.

Heading: Infantry Day observed at Southern Command - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-one-year-old Manasi Rajan Naik, a resident of Model Colony, has made it to the finals of the popular Airtel Halla Bol, a celebrity dance competition, on ETV telecast every Monday and Tuesday. A budding Marathi film actress, Manasi will now vie for honours along with other actresses Shalmali Tole and Deepti Samel. The finals will be held at Ravindra Natya Mandir in Mumbai on October 30.

"I have done all the hard work and expect to put up a good show. But, it won't bother me even if I don't win. Reaching this stage by outplaying 17 other tough participants has been a big achievement for me," says Manasi, a science student of Fergusson College.

There have been three different rounds including the Madhuri Dixit round and the Dada Kondke round. The competition has been going on from July and has been one of the popular shows of recent times. Manasi had played the central character in the Marathi film Jabardast. She says she has decided to be choosy while selecting roles.

Heading: China win junior badminton team championship - Indian Express
Content:
With a solemn but inspiring tribute to mark the triumph of the Indian Army in its first operation post-independence, the Southern Command headquarters on Monday commemorated the Annual Infantry Day.

It was on October 27 in 1947 that the First Battalion of the Sikh Regiment landed in Srinagar to protect the valley from Pakistani invaders, who had already advanced in a bid to take control of the region. A wreath-laying ceremony, jointly organised by the Southern Command, and the Shivneri infantry brigade, was held at the National War Memorial here. Several serving and retired army officers paid tribute to the heroes of the infantry — their valour and sacrifice in 1947 prevented Kashmir from falling into enemy hands. A ceremonial guard was presented and a two-minute silence observed in the memory of those who were killed in the line of duty. Lt Gen R K Chabbra, chief of staff, Southern Command, was the chief guest on the occasion. "October 27, 1947 was a significant day in the history of our nation. Thanks to the courage our soldiers displayed and the sacrifice they made, Kashmir remains an integral part of India to this very day," Chabbra said while interacting with media persons after the function. Procrastinating in the dilemma of choosing between remaining an independent state or joining the dominion of India or Pakistan, Hari Singh, the then Maharaja of Kashmir, found himself in a precarious situation in the wake of independence. Pakistan staked claim on Kashmir and exploited the vulnerable situation by launching an attack — Code-named 'Operation Gulmarg' — with the help of raiders and tribals on October 18, 1947. By October 26, the situation turned grave as the raiders advanced by road to Uri-Baramulla-Srinagar.

Much devastation had been caused; Baramulla was overcome and the enemy was within 30 miles of Srinagar when the Maharaja signed the Instrument of Accession to India on the same day. At around 5 am on October 27, a company of the First Battalion of the Sikh Regiment, commanded by Lt Col D R Rai was flown in to Srinagar by Dakotas of the Indian Air Force. The battles were mostly fought at an altitude of 8,000-10,000 feet. Almost fourteen months later, at midnight on December 31, 1948, the ceasefire came into effect.

Often referred to as the 'Queen of the battle,' the infantry is the primary combat unit of the Indian Army and has many gallantry awards to its credit.

Heading: Five from JN Petit to represent state football team - Indian Express
Content:
China beat Korea 3-1 to win the team event of the Yonex Sunrise World Junior Badminton Championships, held at the Shiv Chhatrapati Sports City, Balewadi, on Monday.

Korea began well, winning the first mixed doubles tie 2-1. The Korean pair of Kim Gi Jung and and Eom Hye Won beat Chinese opponents Zhang Nan and Lu lu 15-21, 21-15 and 21-14. However, China came back strongly in the men's singles event, winning the tie in straight sets. Huan Gao of China defeated Lee Dong Keun 21-14 and 21-15.

The men's doubles event was a thrilling encounter that went right down to the wire. Korea's Kim Gi Jung and Choi Young Woo took the first game 21-17. Then China's pair of Biao Chai and Qiu Zihan came back strongly to win the next game 21-19. The final game was the closest one of the match. After being down by five points early in the game, China staged a comeback and leveled the score at 20-20. They took the next two points with ease and won the game.

In the women's singles event, China's Li Xuerucruised past Sung Ji Hyun of Korea 21-13 and 21-14 and wrapped up the match.

Heading: Fantastic 4 - Indian Express
Content:
After emerging champions of the inter-district divisional championships, five players from JN Petit have been included in the Maharashtra football team that will participate in the nationals from November 1.

Riyan Yadgiri, Rohan Kadam, Abhijeet Mohite, Vaibhav More and Mayur Shelar put up some good performances and found a place in the state team. Riyan Yadgiri has been chosen the vice captain. "I am proud of these players. They have worked hard and they deserve to be in the state team," said Nandu Angirwal, coach of the JN Petit football team.

Heading: Away from home - Indian Express
Content:
For these talented teens, reaching out for the stars is just the first step, as they make a clean sweep at the International Astronomy Olympiad

While average teenagers, apart from going to school and inevitable tuitions hang out with friends, watch movies and party, these kids dispute mathematical theorems and surf the net for information on astronomy in their spare time. It is little wonder then that Abhishek Oswal of St Mary's School, Sarthak Chandra of Bishop's School, Aniruddha Bapat from Army Public School and Jayant Thatte of SP College returned as part of the best team at the International Astronomy Olympiad held in Trieste, Italy between October 13 and 20.

Aniruddha Bapat won a bronze while the other three won a silver medal each. Of the two students from other cities, Shantanu Agarwal of Patna bagged the lone gold while Nitish Kumar Singh of Mumbai took another silver.

The four from Pune reveal the hard work it took to get there. "We were able to make it to the second round without much study," says Thatte, who read Vedic History as part of his preparation, "However, in the third round the competition got serious," they add.

Around 6000 students in the age group of 14 to 17 years, across India, participated in the National Astronomy Olympiad of which only 10 per cent were selected for the National Camp held in Mumbai in May. "For 20 days, 13 to 16 hours a day we were trained rigorously on Math, Physics and Astronomy. We solved puzzles and discussed theory," enthuses 14-year-old Oswal.

Their proud parents have an equally major part to play in the honing of their skill — from taking them for star gazing to providing endless cups of coffee through the night. "We give them a lot of space to pursue their interests and don't impose our ideas," says Vandana Chandra, mother of Sarthak Chandra. "The main part is to channelise their energy. A lot of planning is required as these subjects are not taught in school or extra classes and time management is important," says Bina Oswal, mother of Abishek Oswal.

"The trip to Italy was fun," says Bapat, adding, "we saw beautiful castles, played basket ball and chess tournaments and went on an excursion to Venice." Yet honestly the best part for these little scientists was infact the tests. "We analysed real data from the Trieste observatory; the questions twisted and teased your mind for four hours at a time," adds Chandra. The team interacted with students from 18 different countries and even sang a song from the film Lakshya for them.

Each of them has a formidable list of achievements to their credit. Apart from amassing a hoard of scholarships Oswal, Bapat and Thatte have won medals at the Homi Bhabha Young Scientist competition. Bapat was also selected to attend the Physics Young Ambassadors Symposium at Taiwan in 2005, the World Year for Physics, while Chandra's model, Verifying Euler's Theorem drew the attention of none other than Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on his visit to Pune in 2006. That is not all; they are as passionate about their hobbies as they are about Astronomy. While Oswal plays the piano proficiently, Chandra enjoys football. Bapat is trained in Indian classical music and Thatte loves to draw and paint. Team India, it seems, is truly an all-rounder team!

Heading: Sweet takes - Indian Express
Content:
To share the ecstasy of the jolly spirits, vivacity and essence of the multifarious festival of Diwali and cheer to indulge into the jubilations of the festive carnival, all one wants is to be with his family. But there are a few, who though unwillingly, would miss the joy of uniting with the loved ones this Diwali.

Chandrakant Jha, student at International School of Business and Media, hails from Jamshedpur and is unable to go back home. He says,"I miss my family, the annual shopping spree and participating in the Laxmi Puja. We have therefore organised a college party and I am sure we'll have a blast."

While insufficient holidays is the main reason behind students cancelling their trips, assignments and class work make another. Nitin Soni from Gondia is too caught up with college work to take a break, but he plans to celebrate Diwali just as he does back home, although without the lively presence of his family members. "I have cleaned up my house here and also arranged for a puja, as we do back home. I will miss the blessings of my elders and their company though," smiles he.

A student of MIT, Pune, Saarthak Dutt is unable to make it to his hometown Lucknow as he has to complete college formalities due to term end. He however has planned a personal way of celebration as he explains, "I plan an eco-friendly and quiet Diwali with my friends. I will miss the festivities that we have at home specially the homemade food and sweets and most of all the large gathering"

Anamika Pandey who also hails from Lucknow says, " It is not just about missing home but all the trimmings that go along with, mainly shopping. Crackers and diyas do not really make my Diwali, it is the shopping spree that I will miss the most."

Heading: Lights delight - Indian Express
Content:
Mithai shops offer a colourful combination of mouth-watering Diwali delicacies

An age old trademark of celebration and cheer, lip smacking variety of sweets have flooded the market this Diwali to pamper the taste buds clamouring for their festive special. And there is something for all, even the calorie conscious.

Besides traditional offerings like motichur laddoos, karanjis, shankar palis and anarsas priced between Rs 160 and Rs 240 per kg, a varied range of typically nomenclatured ones have also found a good number of takers. "American butter rolls made of milkmaid and butter with lots of cashews, pistas and almonds, dry fruit kalakand, Gulkand sandwiches, Rajasthani dry fruit rolls and our badam katlis are some of the new arrivals that are high on demand," informs Shreyans Parekh of Bhavnagari sweets, Rasta Peth. While a kg of badam katli and dry fruit kalakand will cost Rs 500 and Rs 240 respectively, the butter rolls, dry fruit rolls and gulkand sandwiches range between Rs 360 and Rs 400. The sweet shops in the city are witnessing a heavy rush of customers. "Sale of sweets is very good. Specially there is a heavy rush for laddoos and pedhas" says Yuvraj Gadve of Kaka Halwai.

This year the sweet shops have also guaranteed a smile on the faces of diet freaks and diabetic patients who are forced to ignore their yearning for mouthwatering sweets. Sugar free sweets made in anjeer and khajur (dates) or with artificial sweeteners have created a special place for themselves in the sweet trays. Apart from selling its exclusive Cranberry sweets priced at 560 per kg and the regular kaju katlis and kaju rolls among others, Karachi sweet mart, one of the prominent sweet shops in the city, is also offering sugar free kaaju pista barfi at Rs 600 a kg and sugar free milkcake at Rs 360 a kg. Similarly Bhavnagari sweets is also offering malai barfis at 300 a kg which can be even stored for a month. " As usual the pure ghee motichur laddoos are selling like hot cakes, but at the same time there is also a good demand for sugar free sweets priced at Rs 500 a kg and khajur masti, with less sugar content , commanding a price of 420 a kg," says Virendre Singh of Purohit sweets.

Pooja Sharma, a housewife opines, " during festivals when as it is calorie intake is high, diet sweets prove to be a boon."

An intrinsic part of Diwali giftings, multifarious varieties of sweets are adorning the sweet boxes as part of Diwali extravaganza. "When it comes to gifting purposes, kaaju mithais and mewa mithais are a hot pick with the customers," informs Shrikrishna Chitale of Chitale Bandhu.

"We are selling a box of mixed sweets which is apt for gifting purposes. Each pack contains around nine to 12 varieties of sweets." Says Tarun Athwani of Karachi sweet mart, as he juggles between his customers yet not forgetting to wish a happy Diwali to all of them.

Heading: Let there be light... and a pollution-free Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Ecologic concerns or the price rise may have reduced the sparks during this season, but the spirit of Diwali remains unchanged

The market is flooded with golden king, Jiljil, mother baby and much more. If these headers seem difficult to decode, you have definitely not hit the firecracker market this Diwali. The festival of lights like every year has the virtual stars and rockets twinkling in the sky and the chakras and anars flickering on the ground but the market numbers have a different story to tell!

Kedar Kharadkar has put up his stall on Mhatre Bridge, the hub of cracker stalls in the city. He says, "The newest are the fancy items that sparkle in the sky and have around 120 to 240 shots. However the rockets, flowerpots and the crackers are the most sold items. The business is low this year. But I think it is because of the nearly 40 per cent increase in the prices. Correspondingly there is a 40 per cent down turn in the customers. Last year's wholesale prices have become this year's retail prices."

Rajendra Wagaskar has his six-day makeshift stall in Koregaon Park and has been donating the turnover from the sales to schools and children in the slum areas in the city. He too echoes the drop in demand as he adds, "It could be an eco-friendly measure by people but affordability has surely gone down because of the cost. The grand fireworks can go up to Rs 7000 but very few people buy them. The attractive ones in a reasonable range are colour changing butterfly, musical crackers and so on. According to me the buying has gone down by a flat 50 per cent."

While this is about the transitions in the market, there is a significant change in the mindset of the customers as well. For instance, Jyostna Roy, a BPO professional says, "I celebrate Diwali with mild crackers, that do not produce high sound. Although the festival brings in a lot of liberties, one must voluntarily avoid loud crackers, they are an interruption for employees like me who do not enjoy holidays and have odd sleeping hours. There might be several norms on the decibel limit but I doubt if they can be actually measured."

For Vibhav Kulkarni, a student, crackers are the most exciting thing to do, incessantly since they are limited to the festival. "Lighting them is more like a competition amongst my friends and family, I make sure we have at least one variety of different crackers available. The sounds, lights and displays make a frenzy and fantastic atmosphere, so I think people must enjoy the fire at the moment and forget the smoke," he smiles.

Heading: You are in safe hands, thanks to them - Indian Express
Content:
Change comes from within and this is something that this cash-rich city needs the most. With nothing changing on the front of making crackers more eco-friendly and less noisy, it would require a little effort on the part of residents to celebrate the Festival of Lights with candles and diyas.

According to the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB), Ludhiana recorded the highest pollution on Diwali last year. This city probably can take a leaf of advice from Patiala which was the least and the lowest-polluted city post Diwali.

"Being a flamboyant city, people prefer to flaunt money like anything. They buy crackers worth thousands of rupees to make a social statement," says Dr Charanjeet Singh, Senior Scientific Officer, Punjab Pollution Control Board.

Though the data shows a reduction in the noise level over the past couple of years, yet a lot more needs to be done. The PPCB has put hospitals, educational institutes, religious places and residential areas under the silent zone.

The average noise pollution over the last three years especially during the night hours hovers between 80 decibles to 93 decibles with last year recording a slight fall in the noise pollution.

Quite similar is the state of residential areas where the noise level hovers between 80 decibles to 100 decibles. The noise level is much higher in commercial areas where 125 decibles is the permitted level.

Dr Singh adds, "Crackers add to the suspended particulate matter in the air. They emit sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen apart from being a source of both air and noise pollution."

Dr Singh added, "While the city's air is highly polluted but the damage that these crackers do can be gauged from the fact that pollution level in the city rises by four to five percent during Diwali."

Pardeep Gupta, a well-known cracker trader, adds, "Every year, the city bursts crackers worth Rs 20 crore."

Heading: Dengue claims life of 12-yr-old - Indian Express
Content:
As we celebrate Diwali on Tuesday, only a few of us will spare a thought for the police personnel, doctors and firemen who will miss out on the captivating moments with their families just to stay on guard to save us from any untoward incident.

They term it as a call of duty rather than sacrifice. "We will also celebrate Diwali with the people and therefore pray that they have a safe Diwali. I do not think it is a sacrifice, it is just a call of duty," said SP (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor. He adds that the police personnel will be happy if the people have a safe Diwali and there are no problems like traffic snarls, brawls or accidents.

The city sees around 100 small and big fire incidents every year on Diwali. Therefore, all the firemen have been asked to be vigilant.

Assistant Divisional Fire Officer Kartar Singh said the holiday of many policemen have also been cancelled keeping in view the high number of fire accidents in the city on the occasion.

As many as 70 firemen will be on duty tomorrow evening along with 28 fire tenders. Apart from that, seven small vehicles will also be placed at key locations of the old and congested areas of the city where the fire tenders cannot enter.

Besides, the hospitals have also constituted emergency teams to deal with any eventualities on the day. "There will be five senior doctors on duty headed by a burn specialist round the clock," said Dr Raju Singh Chhina, medical superintendent at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital.

He added, "We get three types of patients on Diwali - burns, eye problems and accidents due to drunken driving. But we will all be prepared to deal with such cases."

Heading: Suspecting him to be a thief, residents lynch man - Indian Express
Content:
Another dengue death was reported from the district as a 12-year-old boy died at the Christian Medical College and Hospital last night.

Six persons have so far lost their lives to dengue, according to the figures released by the Health department.

Surinder (12), a student of Class VII and son of an employee of CMCH, had been suffering from dengue for the past few days and had been undergoing treatment at CMCH. Though the doctors at the hospital have confirmed that the death was due to dengue, district epidemiologist Dr JP Mangla said the Health department had received information about the death but has not yet verified it.

A 24-year-old patient, Deepmala of Barnala, is also believed to have died of dengue at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital yesterday.

Meanwhile, 37 fresh cases of dengue were confirmed today by the Health department, taking the total number of confirmed patients to 1,633 in the district.

The total number of cases has gone up to 2,780, with 390 suspected cases and 757 from outside the district but diagnosed in the city hospitals. The number of dengue cases in the district is the highest in the state and constitute 70 per cent of the total cases.

The number of patients reported from Dayanand Medical College has reached 1,700. Dr Raju Singh Chhina, medical superintendent, said that about 90 patients have tested positive for dengue in the past 48 hours. The hospital today registered 53 more cases .

"However, since the night temperature is falling now, it is expected that the cases will subside naturally," said Dr Chhina.

Heading: Don’t meddle in Maharashtra's affairs, Sena asks Lalu - Indian Express
Content:
A few residents of the Karamsar colony, under Basti Jodhewal police station, lynched an alleged thief by mercilessly beating him up on the early hours of Monday. An accomplice of the deceased was also beaten up by the mob but he did not sustain serious injuries.

The deceased Om Parkash alias Kala was a resident of the Grewal colony in the city. His accomplice Kiran Premi, a resident of Noorwala road, was also beaten up by the mob.

Following the incident, the Basti Jodhewal police have registered a case under Section 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) against unidentified persons.

On Monday morning, some residents of the colony spotted two persons roaming in the area. The residents, who were on self-vigilance patrolling, suspected them to be thieves and started beating them up.

Sources said while Om Parkash died on the spot, his accomplice Kiran Premi sustained injuries.

DSP Pannu told Newsline, "We have registered a culpable homicide case not amounting to murder against unidentified persons as these two men were beaten up by a mob. After investigating the matter, we would include the names of the people who are found guilty."

Heading: Withdrawing my security was a foolish act: Raj - Indian Express
Content:
Asking leaders from Bihar not to add 'fuel to the fire' over the raging controversy on the anti-North Indian campaign, Shiv Sena leader Uddhav Thackeray said Railway Minister Lalu Prasad should not meddle in Maharashtra's affairs.

The Bihar leaders should 'not add fuel to the fire' by making statements over the condition of north Indians in Mumbai.

Reacting to Lalu Prasad's demand that Sena should be banned, Uddhav said the 'real' culprits of Bihar people are their own leaders.

"Bihar leaders should ask themselves why people from their state have to migrate to Mumbai to make a living," Uddhav said.

"I would advice Lalu not meddle in Maharashtra's affairs," he said.

Referring to Monday's shoot-out in which a Bihar youth was killed, Uddhav said, "he had pistol in his hand, he could have killed somebody. Police were under pressure what were they expected to do?"

About arrest of Sadhvi Pragya Singh in connection with blasts at Malegaon and Modasa, Uddhav said, "it has to be proved that these people were behind the blasts but I don't defend them."

Heading: Rahul Raj's encounter: Nitish seeks CBI inquiry - Indian Express
Content:
Defying court orders, MNS chief Raj Thackeray has openly accused the Maharastra government of indulging in 'revenge politics' and said that its decision to withdraw his Z-plus security was 'foolish'.

In an interview to Marathi daily Loksatta, referring to the decision of the Congress-led Democratic Front (DF) government to withdraw the security following his arrest in a case relating to attack on north Indian job aspirants, Raj said, "The government's action was a foolish decision."

Claiming that his life is under threat, the MNS chief said, "It has been proved after the bus-shootout incident involving a boy from Patna. Even a criminal called Bunty Pandey has issued threats," he told the newspaper.

"In fact, I had never asked for police security. It was given to me in 1992 on grounds that I faced threats to my life. Now it has been withdrawn without giving any reasons," he said.

While granting him bail, a Mumbai court had ordered him not to give any interviews to the media and address rallies.

Police has also issued a gag order to the MNS chief preventing him from speaking to the media and making provocative speeches.

Raj also questioned whether the security arrangements were made based on threat perception or the cases registered against him.

"The decision on security is made by a high-level committee of the state government. Was the issue of withdrawal of my security on the agenda," Raj asked.

The MNS chief also alleged that in places like Malegaon his followers were mercilessly beaten up by the non-Marathi police officers.

"Cases are being filed against them in large numbers. If the government feels that MNS will buckle under such pressure, it is living in a fool's paradise," he said.

Raj also described the Congress leaders like Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil as 'spineless' whose political survival is at the mercy of 'Delhi'.

Raj said the government is working to hurt Marathi 'asmita' (pride) and Marathi speaking people. Instead of addressing issues concerning the Marathi people, the government is filing cases against me.

"However, I will not rest until I have achieved my goal of ensuring justice to the Marathi people. Governments keep changing but when our government comes to power, we will not behave in a revengeful manner like the way this government is doing. However, the Marathi people will never forgive the present government," he said.

Raj said all north Indian leaders have come together against Marathi people.

"But all the 48 MPs from Maharashtra are keeping quiet. In Tamil Nadu, Karunanidhi threatens to withdraw support to the UPA on the issue of Sri Lankan Tamils. But, nobody dare speak anything against DMK. When Karunanidhi rises to protect Tamil pride, the entire Tamil population are firmly behind him," he said.

"If Raj Thackeray speaks for Marathi people, some Marathis turn against him. UP and Delhi leaders take advantage of this disunity and hence the injustice meted out to them in jobs and all spheres," Raj added.

He also described Marathi people and the MNS workers as his 'kavach and kundal' and said that he would fight for the Marathi people till the last drop of his blood.

Heading: Diwali celebrated across India - Indian Express
Content:
Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar on Tuesday demanded a CBI inquiry into the killing of a youth from the state in a police encounter in Mumbai.

Kumar, who along with Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Kumar Modi and state NDA convenor and Health Minister Nandkishore Yadav, visited Rahul's residence in Kadamkuan, consoled the bereaved family.

"The Bihar government and the people of the state share the view that a CBI inquiry is necessary to bring out the truth. After all, why a young man carrying a country made pistol, who could have been easily overpowered, was shot dead by the police? The people of the state have every right to know," he said at the slain youth's residence.

He also asked the people of Bihar, particularly the youth to exercise restraint and not allow divisive elements like Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Raj Thackeray to succeed in their evil designs.

Referring to an article published in Shiv Sena mouthpiece Samna in which Rahul was reportedly described as a 'Bihari mafia', Kumar said, 'no words are adequate to denounce it. A young man, who had recently completed a diploma in radiology and wanted to pursue a decent career cannot be described as mafia'.

Heading: India tops Asia-Pacific political risk table in '09 - Indian Express
Content:
Fireworks illuminated the evening sky and earthen lamps dotted the houses as Diwali, the festival of lights, was celebrated across the country with traditional fervour and gaiety on Tuesday.

People clad in new attire thronged temples and distributed sweets among friends and relatives while children and youngsters burst firecrackers and exchanged 'Happy Diwali' SMSes.

President Pratibha Patil, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Union Ministers also celebrated Diwali.

Amid a global financial crisis and fears of its impact on India, pre-Diwali sales saw a downturn this year. Government agencies and NGOs campaigned for a safer and quieter Diwali.

Keeping in view the recent bomb blasts in various parts of the country, tight security measures were put in place around vital installations, markets and places of worship.

In the national capital, more than 3,400 personnel were deployed to maintain a strict vigil. Security was also tightened in Jammu where people in large numbers visited the historic Ragunath temple and Lakshmi Narayan temple.

In Amritsar, hundreds of devotees queued up since morning to pay obeisance at the sanctum sanctorum of Golden Temple.

According to Hindu belief, Diwali marks the return of Lord Ram to his kingdom after 14 years in exile. It also holds significance for Sikhs as on this day in 1620, sixth Sikh Guru Hargobind Sahib was freed by Mughal emperor Jahangir.

The celebrations were marred by tragedy in Bihar's Gopalganj district when three children of a family were killed and another was seriously injured in an accidental explosion in a heap of firecrackers. One man was burnt to death in a blaze at a cracker shop in Udham Singh Nagar in Uttarakhand.

Heading: Pakistan violates ceasefire, fires at Indian positions - Indian Express
Content:
India, Malaysia and Thailand face the highest political and social risk among Asia-Pacific countries in 2009, mainly because of internal instability, a political risk consultancy said.

India's highest risk score of 6.87 on a scale of 10 also reflected fears over Pakistan, the Hong Kong-based Political & Economic Risk Consultancy (PERC) said in a report, warning of social unrest and insecurity if things worsened in the neighbouring nation.

The consultancy assessed 16 countries on factors such as the risk of disruptive political change, the threat posed by social activism and vulnerability to policy changes by other governments.

A score of zero represented the best socio-political situation and 10 the highest risk.

Contributing to India's high score was uncertainty over the outcome of general elections next year, rising communal violence and increased militant attacks, PERC said in the report released on Monday.

"India, Thailand and Malaysia are not so much vulnerable to negative fallout from the global financial crisis as they are to factors that are mainly internal," Robert Broadfoot, Managing Director of PERC, said.

"For these countries, the coming global economic storm is only going to make a bad situation worse," he said.

"India's underlying attractions to foreign investors should remain no matter who wins the next election," the report said.

Thailand is the the second riskiest country in Asia for 2009 with a score of 6.28, as the current political turmoil threatens to drag into 2009 and is eroding the country's key institutions.

The consultancy projected Thailand's worst case scenario to be if the King of Thailand dies before the turmoil is resolved.

As for Malaysia, the third riskiest in the region, the report said the struggle for political power was aggravating racial and religious tensions.

"The status quo is changing in ways that will see a stronger political opposition than in the past," said the report.

Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore and Australia were ranked most stable and low in political risk for 2009 even though their economies are likely to be hurt by the global financial crisis, PERC said.

For the United States, being at the epicentre of the financial crisis has weakened the country economically and psychologically, PERC said.

The US political and military profile will be lower than before and it will become less aggressive in pushing its views on other countries. In Asia, the US may rely more on its regional allies such as Japan, Singapore and Australia to push its agenda. China scored 5.33 on PERC's scale and the consultancy expects the world's most populous nation to have a difficult year in 2009 as the government tries to sustain economic momentum and boost domestic demand in the face of weaker export markets.

"Despite a desire to get average Chinese to spend more, layoffs in factories, weak stock prices and lower real estate prices in key markets like Shanghai are likely to make average Chinese turn more cautious in their consumption," said PERC.

Heading: Anand still in driver's seat, just a draw away from title - Indian Express
Content:
Less than a fortnight after Pakistan promised to stop cross-border firing, its troops on Tuesday shelled Indian posts, again violating the ceasefire along the Line of Control in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir.

Pakistani troops fired mortar shells and rocket projectile grenades and opened small arms firing on Indian posts along LoC in Sabzian area of Poonch district at around 11.45 pm on Monday night, a senior army official said.

Around ten shells were intermittently fired for nearly half an hour, he said adding that these shells exploded away from the forward posts and there was no casualty on the Indian side.

BSF troops of 192 battalion guarding the border line observed calm despite provocation and did not retaliate.

The ceasefire violation by Pakistan came less than a fortnight after India and Pakistan decided to refrain from cross-border firing and shelling and to preserve the sanctity of the four-year-old ceasefire along Indo-Pak border.

This was agreed at a two-day long bi-annual meeting between Pakistan rangers and BSF at Lahore on October 16 during which Pakistan rangers Director General Lt Gen Mohammad Yaqoob Khan promised to Additional Director General BSF UK Bansal that there would be no ceasefire violations henceforth while acknowledging that there had been some violations earlier.

This is 35th ceasefire violation since January, 2008 and seventh in Sabzian sub-sector where two jawans were killed in September in Pakistan firing.

The ceasefire violation and firing by Pakistan is aimed at infiltrating militants into Jammu and Kashmir to target forthcoming assembly elections in the state, officials said adding that troops at the border are foiling infiltration attempts by militants.

Army has further beefed up the security along LoC after intelligence reports that several big groups of militants are waiting to enter Jammu and Kashmir, they said.
