Meanwhile, Aires Rodrigues alleged that his client was being harassed by the police at the behest of politicians. Distributing the copies of a letter written by Calangute police, he said, "The mother has been asked to give details of her daily activities, her business activities, source of income and vehicles purchased in Goa. These things are not relevant to the rape case."

He added that Calangute police had written a letter on Sunday asking the mother to provide the information in two days. "This is the first time it has ever happened in the history of Goa Police that they have given such a short notice to reply," Rodrigues said.

Heading: Khanduri vs rebels: BJP backs CM again - Indian Express
Content:
At his last rally, minutes before campaigning for elections to the country's most powerful municipal corporation ended on the evening of January 30, 2007, Raj Thackeray, chief of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, was addressing several hundred people crammed in a narrow lane in Lalbaug, central Mumbai. "I am seeking a chance, with a clean slate, to show you that change is possible," he said. Later, speaking to The Indian Express, he said stoking the 'Marathi Manoos' fire at every election will no longer be successful.

Nearly two years later, the change he guaranteed is visible less in civic wards governed by a handful of MNS corporators in the financial capital and more in his political strategy. A different election demands a different language, and Raj Thackeray's evolution as a politician is well underway.

In the past week, which was a blur of violence and name-calling, Thackeray persisted in what has been his only trajectory for all of 2008  jobs for the sons of the soil and ousting the "outsiders". Even the agitation against candidates from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar taking the Railway Recruitment Board exams in the state is reminiscent of his days with the Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena (BVS), the Shiv Sena's students' wing. His additions to the brew have been repeatedly targeting the 'Chora Ganga kinare waala' and those conducting the Chhath puja, apart from the opportunism displayed in jumping into the fray when Jet Airways announced a major retrenchment drive.

For all practical purposes, from their model of fund-raising to their street-fighting style, his is just another group of Shiv Sainiks. The MNS fund-raising patterns are modelled after the Sena as well  small-time shop-owners and entrepreneurs cough up small sums regularly, even as the MNS, like the Sena before it, makes inroads into major trade union fields like aviation, surface transport and hospitality. Raj's own speeches are peppered, alongside the Sena-style rabble rousing, with lowbrow jokes called 'Thackeri' by the Marathi press after a style patented by the senior Thackeray.

And yet, for all his mass appeal and the violence he appears to instigate, Raj Thackeray is a suave, urbane artiste with an eclectic taste in music, a love for fast cars  he enjoys a zip in friend Sachin Tendulkar's Ferrari in the dead of night  and with an expensive taste in everything from designer clothes and accessories, to art and alcohol. He is secular-minded, conscious about his appearance in public, has little understanding of caste (the Thackerays themselves belong to the politically insignificant CKP caste) and loves a good conversation over a smoke.

"Acchha chhokra," or good boy, is how he is described by Jairaj Salgaokar, owner of Kalnirnay, the Maharashtrian calendar-printing major. "I have seen him since he was a child, as I used to frequent the Thackerays' home. He used to be hot-tempered at one time, but no longer."

According to Salgaokar, who is considered quite close to Raj, apart from Bal Thackeray himself, the other big influence on his thinking has been Babasaheb Purandare, the writer-historian who has written extensively on the life and times of Shivaji. Like his father Shrikant Thackeray, an accomplished music director who composed for several Marathi films, he is moody. "Kaaka, kaaka, (uncle, uncle) was what we would hear from him when Raj was about three or four years old," says Pandharinath Sawant, now in his seventies and a close friend of Shrikant. Now editor of Marmik, launched by Bal Thackeray as a mouthpiece and then as a cartoon weekly, Sawant also remembers Raj's skill as a caricaturist. "In my heart, I would compare him to Balasaheb," says Sawant.

Having studied art at the JJ School of Art, Raj worked as a cartoonist with the publication for about four years since 1985, before getting more involved with the BVS and then launching the Shiv Udyog Sena. "He could react with a cartoon as quickly as a mirror shows you an image. His uncle stopped drawing cartoons when his hands began to shake, Raj has unfortunately stopped too early."

Extremely well-connected in Bollywood even in the early 1990s, Raj also organised the controversial Michael Jackson concert to raise funds for the Shiv Udyog Sena. When it did not yield the funds he wanted, he organised Shraddhanjali, a rare concert by Lata Mangeshkar, with appearances by the Bollywood who's who from Dilip Kumar to Amitabh Bachchan. While many in the Thackeray family have tested the Bollywood waters  Binda made a film, as did Jaidev and Smita Thackeray  Raj was once rumoured to be harbouring a big dream: a movie with Amitabh Bachchan.

The past three years have been busy, with him travelling across the state by road to help build a mass base. But senior political observers say he has no time or patience for serious reading, a deeper understanding of ideologies and economics. He also lacks humility, never losing his bearings as a man wielding some power.

And, like the Shiv Sena's other bete noir Narayan Rane  who last week surprised the Congress by echoing the MNS's supposed jobs-for-locals cause  Raj Thackeray believes he was denied what was rightfully his.

Uddhav and Raj had both been projected as the next generation of leaders of a newly dynastic party around 1992, but there was never any doubt on which cousin was more popular among the Sainiks.

Still, it could have been more than 'putraprem' that led Bal Thackeray to anoint his son as successor, over the more resourceful and well-connected nephew.

Many believe the turning point in Raj's career as a Shiv Sainik was the Ramesh Kini murder of 1996, in which Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena leader and key Raj aide Ashutosh Rane was a co-accused. Raj was exonerated by the CBI and never charged and Rane was discharged in 2002 for want of evidence. But the whispers of a scandal had done damage. The man found dead in a Pune cinema hall, after all, was a middle-class Maharashtrian. "He hasn't been able to cash in on the first 10 or 12 years of life as a Sainik," says a senior city politician associated with Raj in his student politics days. "Maybe he took too much for granted."

Raj was then cutting his teeth as a moonlighting businessman, dabbling in real estate. He now has considerable stakes in construction companies in Maharashtra and Dubai. As a leader, he is inspiring, says Haji Arafat Sheikh, an MNS vice-president, the Muslim face of the party and leader of the MNS transport wing. "During our training, he asked us to be his hands across the state," says Sheikh who, like most of the MNS top brass, has been with Raj since his BVS days.

A common grouse among senior Sainiks who severed decade-long relationships with the Sena to join the MNS was that Raj's men in the Sena had never got their due. While other student politicians went on to become corporators and were later in the reckoning for Legislative Assembly poll tickets, BVS men remained BVS men. "We stayed with him because he is our leader," says Sheikh.

But it is not just chance that many of his closest aides are also staunch opponents of Uddhav Thackeray and his now-abandoned attempts to give the Shiv Sena a moderate face through the Mee Mumbaikar campaign, an attempt to create a pan-community identity for supporters in a break from the party's strong regional chauvinism. In fact, February's tirade against North Indians by the MNS was triggered by Uddhav attending traditional North Indian 'lai chana' meetings and the Uttar Bharatiya Divas celebrations.

"He is not communal. I am a Marathi Manoos even if I am a Muslim, because I am a native of Pune. His words are misunderstood," Sheikh laments, adding that MNS men would now demand the arrest of Sonia Gandhi or Mulayam Singh Yadav every time a Congressman or Samajwadi Party member participates in a riot.

Such an attitude among his men, coupled with their willingness to smash windscreens and break bones, is what could alienate the Marathi intelligentsia among whom his line actually finds several sympathisers. "He is out to prove only one thing, that he is a better leader than Uddhav... But he is overplaying his cards and that could boomerang," says senior political commentator and former Loksatta editor Aroon Tikekar. Loksatta editor Kumar Ketkar, who has known Raj for several years, says: "He is sensitive. He saw the film Gandhi perhaps nearly 50 times and each time he was overwhelmed and even wept. Paradoxically, he has a fascination for Hitler, bordering on great admiration, not knowing the context and historical issues, nor bothered about them."

When his veneration of a dangerous icon proves counterproductive, Maharashtra will know in time.

His close aides

Rajan Shirodkar

MD of Matoshree Realty and a senior advisor to Raj, known to remain in the background. Was president of the Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena before going on to hold various positions in the Shiv Sena. He is also Raj's business associate. Together, Matoshree Realty and Kohinoor Group  owned by Manohar Joshi's son Unmesh  purchased Dadar's Kohinoor Mill property for a whopping Rs 421 crore in 2005, a record for textile mill deals then. His son Aditya now heads the MNS students' wing.

Shirish Parkar

Seen as a vocal representative of Raj's ideas and ideology, Parkar has been with the leader since the early 1990s and is a close friend. An MBA, he gave up a job with a multinational firm to turn full-time politician with the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena. Along with Ashutosh Rane, Nitin Sardesai and a few others, he was part ofthe famed "Azad Katta" group, named so for an Irani café named Azad in Shivaji Park where Raj and his friends would hang out till late in the evenings during their student days.

Bala Nandgaonkar

An MLA from Mazgaon, he won his seat this term on a Shiv Sena ticket following a keenly contested battle with the NCP's Pankaj Bhujbal, son of former Shiv Sainik Chhagan Bhujbal, who has a huge following in the Mazgaon-Tadwadi area. A true-to-his roots Shiv Sainik, was accused in a few cases of rioting during the 1992-1993 communal clashes. He travels with Raj extensively.

Atul Sarpotdar

Son of senior Sena leader Madhukar Sarpotdar, has been with Raj since his Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena days. Sarpotdar is now the general secretary of the MNS and handles the western suburbs of Mumbai for the party. He also is the contact person for Marathwada.

Shishir Shinde

A former Sena member of the Legislative Council, was in the headlines chiefly for his participation in destroying the Wankhede cricket pitch on the eve of an Indo-Pak match in 1991. Shinde is general secretary, spokesperson and handles the eastern suburbs of Mumbai.

Heading: Arrest warrant against Ashok Todi, kin in Rizwanur case - Indian Express
Content:
Uttarakhand Chief Minister B C Khanduri returned triumphant to the state capital on Sunday after being assured of the party high command's support for his continuance in office. This is the second time in the last three months that the central leadership has quelled a dissidence movement against him by ruling out a change of leadership.

"I don't think there was ever a threat to my government," a beaming Khanduri told media persons at a Diwali Milan programme at his residence on Monday. When asked whether the matter regarding dissatisfaction with his leadership had been resolved completely, he said," I think things have been sorted out."

He did not comment on why there were persistent voices of protest against him. "It would not be appropriate to reply to this question. In politics such minor irritants keep on happening,"Khanduri told The Indian Express.

Heading: SC breather to doctors: error of judgement not always negligence - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI court on Monday issued an arrest warrant against Ashok Todi, Pradip Todi, Anil Sarogi in the Rizwanur Rehman case. Delivering the order, Bibhash Chatterjee, magistrate of the court, directed the CBI to produce all three of them before the court on November 3 and remanded Mainuddin alias Pappu, a close friend of Rizwanur's family, to judicial custody till November 10.

The CBI had filed a chargesheet in the case on September 22 and had accused Ashok Todi, Pradip Todi, Anil Sarogi, Pappu and three police officers of abetment to suicide. Subsequently, the CBI court had issued summons asking them to personally appear before the court on Monday. But instead of personal appearance, the Todis and Sarogi filed a petition of the criminal proceedings of this case to be 'kept in abeyance'. The lawyers of Todis argued that the CBI court should not initiate the trials now, in compliance with a Supreme Court order passed on October 13.

Ashok Todi, father-in-law of Rizwanur, had moved a petition in the Supreme Court on October 13 seeking an order to stay the CBI probe, which was rejected by the apex court. Moving the petition, the counsel for the Todis said that the Supreme Court had stayed the commencement of trial in the case till the disposal of the appeal filed by Todis, which was pending before a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court.

The Supreme Court had asked the High Court to complete the hearing within six months. But the CBI court rejected the argument and issued an arrest warrant against the three who had not appeared before the court.

The CBI court had asked three police officers of Kolkata Police, Ajay Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das, to appear before the magistrate on November 3.

Heading: Andhra Govt cracks down on corrupt staff - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors, living under the constant threat of being dragged to courts for "erroneous" treatment, can now breathe easy.

The Supreme Court has underlined that "a simple deviation from normal professional practices in the high-risk medical profession is not always to be construed as an act of negligence on the part of doctors".

"An error of judgement on the part of the professional is also not negligence per se," clarified a Bench headed by Justice C K Thakker and D K Jain while quashing the prosecution initiated against a doctor, Mahadev Prasad Kaushik, from Mathura.

Dr Kaushik had challenged a court order dated February 9, 2007, later confirmed by the Allahabad High Court, whereby summons were issued against him under Sections 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 504 (intentional insult) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the IPC, in the Supreme Court.

The complainant had alleged that his father Buddha Ram died a few minutes after being administered three injections by Dr Kaushik on May 4, 2001. The two courts found prime facie negligence on Dr Kaushik's part.

However, the Supreme Court said, "Medical profession is often called upon to adopt a procedure which involves higher element of risk, but which a doctor honestly believes as providing greater chances of success for the patient rather than a procedure involving lesser risk but higher chances of failure. Which course is more appropriate to follow would depend on facts and circumstances of a given case."

The SC granted a breather to doctors, who, these days are hounded by ambulance chasers, a category of lawyers who convince patients to file cases against any treatment "gone wrong".

The Bench explained, "The standard to be applied for judging whether a person charged has been negligent or not would be that of an ordinary competent person exercising ordinary skill in that profession."

Taking a pragmatic approach, Justice Thakker, who wrote the judgment, said: "Higher the acuteness in emergency and higher the complication, more are the chances of error of judgement."

"At times, the professional is confronted with making a choice between the devil and the deep sea and he has to choose the lesser evil," the judge added.

Relying on the police report, which found that Buddha Ram had a renal failure and died before he was brought to the clinic, the court quashed proceedings under Sections 504 and 506 of the IPC. It also dropped the charge of culpable homicide and noted, at best, it could be a negligent act to be covered under Section 304A IPC.

Heading: Soren govt promises free rice, wheat for ‘primitive’ tribals - Indian Express
Content:
The Andhra Pradesh Government's anti-corruption drive has sent those government servants scurrying for cover for whom reaching under the table for that bundle of notes is a second habit.

What has given them the fright is Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) overdrive which has not only trapped 152 gazetted officers and 293 non-gazetted officers in the past 10 months either for accepting bribes or for having disproportionate assets, but also achieved convictions in 90 of the 100 cases that went to court in the past 10 months. It also achieved convictions in all 12 cases of disproportionate assets filed between January 1 and October 25, 2008.

There is also terror in the shady corners of government offices because the ACB is making watertight cases against the officials resulting in immediate punishments from disciplinary authorities besides facing the corruption charges. At least 81 officers have been suspended this year while four have been dismissed from service.

"We have simply raised the risks. We want them to think twice if the risk is worth taking. Especially when we are making efforts to make sure the risks are much higher now than before," says Director General (ACB) R R Girish Kumar.

"The traps are well publicised by the Bureau both when the official is trapped and if he is convicted in court. A lot of social stigma is being attached to such officials because of the publicity. With meticulous investigation, as properties are seized and all bank accounts are being freezed, corrupt officials if caught find themselves without a penny.

The ACB also ensures that disciplinary action is taken against the arrested officers by their respective departments which means either a suspension or dismissal. By making strong cases we are making them pay such a heavy price that the years of corruption would appear a small crime," Kumar explains.

Kumar says a three-pronged approach of traps, punishment by way of attached properties and bank accounts, and swift prosecution resulting in convictions is yielding results.

No one has been spared. Special deputy collectors, deputy collectors, assistant directors, general and zonal managers, police inspectors, superintending engineers, survey officers, executive engineers and revenue inspectors, officers of various government departments have had that heart-stopping moment of being caught red-handed by the ACB in the past few months. And, these are not small catches of Rs 10-15,000.

P Ram Gopal Rao, special deputy collector, land acquisition for Ranga Reddy Medak districts, was trapped while accepting a bribe of Rs 11 lakh through an accomplice. Rao actually demanded a bribe of Rs 80 lakh to denotify lands. The Rs 11 lakh was supposed to be the first installment.

An assistant engineer in the Panchayati Raj department was found to have Rs 1.27 crore worth of cash and jewellery at his home in Mahboobnagar. Properties worth Rs 2 crore were found to be owned by P Kasinath, a superintending engineer of irrigation department. A tehsildar of revenue department in Vizag district had assets worth over Rs 1 crore.

Heading: UPA may not clear manned mission plan: MoS Chavan - Indian Express
Content:
While Chief Minister Shibu Soren is yet to keep his August 27 promise of providing ration cards to BPL families, this doesn't stop him from making more such promises. On Diwali eve, he assured rice and wheat to some tribes living in the state.

In fact, 45,000 families have been identified as "primitive" tribes in Jharkhand. Apart from them, 29 lakh people living below the poverty line, who were supposed to get rice and wheat at Rs 6 and Rs 4.62 per kg respectively, have been now assured these at Rs 3 and Rs 2 respectively. Once these promises become a reality, the state would need Rs 110 crore per annum and as a result, the non-plan expenditure is estimated to shoot up from Rs 9198.11 crore to Rs 9933.11 crore. The state Government has proposed to borrow Rs 2,150 crore to fund its annual plan outlay of Rs 9652.96 crore during 2008-09.

If the full-page advertisements in local dailies to mark 60 days of the Soren Government are to be believed, the state Government has 26 achievements to its credit. These include inauguration of a dance centre, distribution of musical instruments to Adivasi artistes and launch of Mukhya Mantri Food Security project. The work related to the distribution of land records to the beneficiaries of the Centre's Forest Rights Act, MCA and BCA courses at the BIT Mesra's Dumka branch, six medical colleges, 14 hospitals with 50 beds each, a pilot training centre at Dumka and 898 bridges that are listed as achievements were started during the Madhu Koda regime.

When contacted, Soren said: "It may be so, but it is being executed now."

Heading: Rivals Nitish, Lalu unite in outrage, demand inquiry - Indian Express
Content:
While ISRO has publicly declared its intention of sending a man into space by 2015, the government is still to make up its mind on this hugely important mission. A top government functionary told The Indian Express that government clearance to the manned mission was unlikely to be cleared any time soon.

"I don't think this will be cleared in the life of the current Parliament. It is a major expenditure decision and it would not be proper for this government to make such a major financial commitment at the fag end of its tenure," Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office Prithviraj Chavan said.

ISRO, which launched Chandrayaan-I, India's first mission to moon earlier this week, has publicly announced that it was preparing for a manned mission to space by 2015, the likely cost of which would be Rs 12,000 crore.

The idea for such a mission was mooted quite some time back and it has received the endorsement of not just the scientific community but also the Space Commission.

ISRO had prepared a voluminous study report detailing the technical feasibility of this most ambitious project and also highlighted the tremendous benefits that are likely to accrue from it. This feasibility report, which received the backing of the Space Commission, was submitted to the government about two months back.

"As of now, we are waiting for the government's approval for the project," said S Satish, ISRO's Director of Press and Public Relations.

Chavan said the government was still doing a cost-benefit analysis of the project. It was carefully studying the various implications for such a huge mission.

He said the current economic environment was also restraining the government from committing itself to such a major financial decision. "Considering the current economic situation, I don't think many people would be very enthusiastic to undertake such a big financial commitment," he said.

ISRO's other space missions so far have generally been quite low-cost with Chandrayaan-I, which entailed a cost of just Rs 386 crores, widely believed to be the cheapest ever lunar mission. The budget for Chandrayaan-2, a lander and rover which is scheduled for 2011-12, is just a fraction more at Rs 425 crore.

But a manned mission would be an extremely complex project, very different from everything that ISRO has done so far.

Chavan said there was no danger of the project not getting cleared and pointed out that work in this direction was already continuing.

"Such a complex mission cannot be executed in a single day. The preparations have to go on. I am sure government clearance will also come at a suitable time after examining all the issues involved."

ISRO had completed one major milestone in this direction by successfully completing the Space Recovery Experiment in January last year. A space capsule was launched by the PSLV-C7 and successfully brought back to earth and descended over the Bay of Bengal. This was the first such technology demonstration of ISRO's capability to send a manned mission.

Tracking Chandrayaan DAY 5

Chandrayaan-I was on Monday moving around the earth in the elliptical orbit that it was put into on Sunday morning after the third orbit-raising manoeuvre.

In this orbit, the spacecraft is supposed to take 73-and-a-half hours to complete one revolution around the earth. One full revolution will happen in the early hours of Thursday. Till then, Chandrayaan-I would not be disturbed from its current orbit.

The next orbit-raising manoeuvre, to put the spacecraft in even a higher orbit, is slated to be performed on Thursday, after the completion of one revolution. All on-board equipment functioning normally.

Heading: Deshmukh Govt beefs up MNS chief’s security - Indian Express
Content:
In a rare show of unity, Lalu Prasad, Nitish Kumar, Ram Vilas Paswan and Union ministers from Bihar cutting across partylines on Monday met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and demanded a judicial probe into the killing of the gun-wielding Patna boy by the Mumbai Police. They also urged him to intervene for stern action against "elements" targeting people from Bihar in Maharashtra.

Shedding their political rivalry for the first time, the leaders spoke in one voice and alleged that the Mumbai Police had "murdered" the young boy from Patna. "The police could have easily overpowered him. They did not try to do so and instead killed him. What he did was wrong but this is not the way to deal. We have demanded a judicial probe into the incident from the Prime Minister," Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar said after the meeting even as RJD chief and Railway Minister Lalu Prasad and LJP chief and Union Steel, Chemicals and Fertilisers Minister Ram Vilas Paswan standing by his side nodded in support.

The all-party delegation from Bihar had gone to lodge its protest over the recent attacks on students from Bihar appearing for the Railway Recruitment Board exam but it was the killing of the Patna boy on Monday that dominated the meeting.

Sources said angry Bihar leaders told the Prime Minister that the kind of "valour" the Mumbai Police had exhibited in shooting down the boy should also have been shown against Raj Thackeray and his MNS "goons".

Prasad, Kumar and Paswan also expressed "shock" over the statement of Maharahstra Home Minister R R Patil justifying the police action. "Action should be taken against the Home Minister," they demanded.

The PM later spoke to Maharashtra CM and enquired about the shooting incident. "The PM spoke to the CM of Maharashtra this evening and enquired about the situation. He asked the CM to take all necessary steps to ensure safety of all sections of society," a statement from the PMO said.

Though a memorandum submitted to the PM by the delegation refrained from taking the name of either Raj Thackeray or MNS, the leaders from across the political spectrum came down heavily on the Maharashtra Government for its failure to rein in the leader. Some even demanded dismissal of the state Government.

Paswan was scathing in his attack against the Congress-led state Government. "The attacks show failure of the state Government. Such attacks are taking place repeatedly and the state seems to be doing nothing. Such a Government does not have the moral right to stay in power," he is learnt to have told the PM.

Even Bihar state president of the NCP Upendra Kushwaha demanded stern action against R R Patil (also from the NCP) and the state Government.

Heading: NCP first to pay after Maharashtra ordinance - Indian Express
Content:
Days after the Maharashtra Government downgraded Raj Thackeray's security cover, the state Government on Monday beefed it up after the shooting incident involving a youth from Bihar.

On Monday morning, a youth from Bihar fired at a passenger and assaulted the conductor on a BEST bus in Kurla demanding he wanted to meet Raj Thackeray. The youth was killed in police firing.

Following the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief's arrest last week in three cases, the state Government had decided to downgrade his security cover. He was being provided Z category security cover, which was reduced to Y category after he was released on bail. Raj had refused the Y category cover offered to him.

"It was a police decision to reduce the security. We have not opposed it nor asked for more security. We will not refuse the security cover and give the Government an opportunity to say that we did not accept it. MNS workers are capable of providing security to Rajsaheb. The Government felt a threat perception and increased the security. People need to see through this political manoeuvering. One person gets killed after taking law into his hands and leaders from across the country make all sorts of demands. We are fighting for the needs of the locals here and are being targeted," said Atul Sarpotdar, MNS general secretary.

Heading: Electoral pact: SP growing impatient with Congress - Indian Express
Content:
A week after Deputy CM R R Patil hurriedly brought in an ordinance to make political parties liable for damage caused to public property during protests, his own party has been slapped with the first case under the legislation.

In the wake of wide-spread violence witnessed in the state after Maharashtra Navnirman Sena activists went on a rampage after Raj Thackeray's arrest, the Congress-Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) government last week approved the ordinance making political parties and social organisations accountable for the damage caused during protests.

On October 25, NCP student wing activists attacked the office of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) in Nashik protesting the alleged involvement of Hindu right-wing organisations in the Malegaon and Modasa blasts. According to Nashik police, NCP students ransacked the office, damaged furniture and desecrated photographs of national leaders. The protestors also allegedly blackened the faces of some VHP activists who were present in the office. Nashik officials said the NCP has been asked to cough up Rs 20,000 for the damage.

"All the procedures are complete and the parties which need to pay under the new ordinance have been identified. Everything is ready. The legal formalities have to be completed and then the fine will be recovered. It should be done this week," said Nashik collector and District Magistrate S Chockalingam.

Chockalingam added: "The ordinance modifying the Bombay Police Act was notified on October 23 and this is the first case under the ordinance. Now all the rights have been concentrated with District Magistrate. We are being careful as it is the first case and we want to make sure that there are no legal problems later."

NCP spokesperson Hemraj Shah said: "They have made a demand of Rs 20,000 for damages. One of the leaders was an ex-office bearer, he will have to pay. But I think R R Patil has said that the party will pay for the damages as per the ordinance."

Heading: Probe Pragya’s links with BJP leaders: Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi Party's patience with the ruling Congress over a seat-sharing pact in Uttar Pradesh seems to be wearing thin. The party on Monday hit out against a section within the Congress for not being keen on an alliance with it.

"Congress has a history of sailing on two boats. There is a growing feeling within our party that while a section of the ruling party is trying to forge an understanding with us to counter Mayawati-led BSP, another section appears keen to open the doors for the BSP if our pact does not work out," SP general secretary Amar Singh, while talking to mediapersons, in the Capital said.

The two sides are yet to sew a poll pact despite two rounds of talks and exchange of letters.

After the Left had withdrawn its support from the UPA Government in July, the SP had offered its support to the government in lieu of a seat-sharing pact to counter the rising tide of Mayawati in UP.

Mayawati has already announced candidates for most of the constituencies in UP for the Lok Sabha elections.

What has further irked the SP is the Congress' demand of nearly a dozen seats that are being held by the SP without conceding its seats to the latter.

Singh once again demanded a ban on the Bajrang Dal. "Congress claims itself to be a secular party. It should impose a ban on the Bajrang Dal in the same way it has banned SIMI. The party otherwise will be blamed for being soft on terror," said Singh.

Singh reiterated his party's demand for a judicial probe into the police encounter in Jamia Nagar.

Heading: Modasa blast: ABVP members to be quizzed - Indian Express
Content:
Seeking to turn the table on the BJP over the issue of terrorism, following the arrest of former ABVP activist Pragya Singh and others in connection with the Malegaon and Modasa terror incidents, the Congress on Monday alleged that the Opposition party's members and associates were "directly linked" with terrorism.

AICC spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi referred to a photograph showing senior BJP leaders sitting with the accused. "The photograph showing Pragya Singh is recent and cannot be dismissed as just a public photograph of the BJP leaders. It is a very special photograph of a close and tightly knit group inside a small room with high-ranking BJP members like MP CM Shivraj Chouhan and party president Rajnath Singh with Pragya Singh. This is the photograph of a special circle of trust — an intimate and exclusive circle of trust," Singh said at a press briefing on Monday.

Asked if the Congress wanted police investigation into these BJP leaders' links with the accused, the AICC spokesperson said, "The police cannot be bound by limits. Once you get a lead, anyone remotely, here I am talking of direct connection with Pragya Singh, has be interrogated."

The Congress said that the investigation results in the Malegaon and Modasa blasts are terrifying "not only because they involve terrorism, but also because they involve and implicate almost every limb of a mainstream political party — the BJP". "Pragya Singh has admittedly been an active member of the ABVP. Major Upadhyaya is admittedly associated with the BJP ex-servicemen cell," Singhvi added.

"We call upon the Government to investigate the timing of the blasts. Who are the political beneficiaries of the blasts? Who are involved in financing them?" asked the AICC spokesperson.

He said the principal actors in this drama — from Pragya to Upadhyaya to Bhate to Phanse — and the principal locations at Pune and Nagpur are "reminiscent of the Gandhi assassination conspiracy". He reminded that the RSS "only narrowly, by a whisker" escaped conviction and permanent ignominy 60 years ago by pleading that the principal conspirators had supposedly resigned and left the RSS some months before the killing of Gandhi.

"The BJP's plea about Pragya and Upadhyaya in 2008 is thus a clear echo of 1948. That was Gandhi, the father of the nation; this is terrorism and the nation itself," said Singhvi. Asked if the Congress demanded a ban on the RSS, he said, "If investigations reveal culpable, incriminating evidence, banning is the least that can be done. The police should launch criminal prosecution of a vigorous kind."

Heading: Terror investigation throws up more Kerala links - Indian Express
Content:
After saffron outfits like the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Bajrang Dal and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), it is the BJP's student wing — Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) — that has come under the scanner in the Modasa blast probe case.

Deputy Superintendent of Police K K Mysorewala, who is heading the probe, on Monday said, "We have summoned some active ABVP members to record their statements to take our probe forward." Mysorewala, however, refused to name those who have been summoned and the reason behind doing so.

A 15-year-old boy died and several others were injured when a low-intensity bomb kept on a motorcycle went off near a mosque at the Muslim-dominated Sukka Bazaar in Modasa on September 29. The incident took place around 9.26 pm when people were offering special Ramzan prayers (tarawih) inside the mosque.

The Sabarkantha police, in its month-long investigations into the case, have until now recorded statements of about 500-odd people.

"More than 200 of these people are Hindus and include people associated with the VHP, Bajrang Dal and the RSS in Modasa. They were questioned due to their past records and not because of their association with any organisation. We have also questioned around 300 Muslims, including those associated with Islamic outfits," Mysorewala said.

Sources in the police said that the recent arrest of Sadhavi Pragya Singh Thakur from Surat and the Mumbai police claiming Indore-based Hindu Jagran Manch's hand in the Malegaon-Modasa blasts could have prompted the Gujarat Police to summon the ABVP members.

The 15-member police team probing the blast case was banking on two things — an eyewitness who could have possibly seen the person parking the bomb-laden motorcycle and forensic experts finding the original chassis number of the motorcycle. "Unfortunately, we failed on both counts," a police inspector, associated with the probe, said.

About the Mumbai police claiming to have solved Malegaon as well as Modasa blast cases, Mysorewala said, "We will get in touch with the Mumbai police in this regard soon."

Accusing the police of inaction in solving a "politically motivated" blast in Modasa, Sabarkantha Congress MP Madhusudhan Mistry said, "I had forwarded names of three suspects to Sabarkantha police officers but they did nothing. If the accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts could be arrested so soon, then why is there a delay in nabbing those behind the Modasa blast?"

Heading: Detained retd Major rose from the ranks - Indian Express
Content:
The terror trail in Kerala widened with the arrest of three more people, based on inputs gathered from one of the arrested recruiters. The abovementioned arrests were carried out on the basis of information gathered from Faizal, a native of Kannur who was arrested on Saturday on charges of recruiting youth for terror outfits in Kashmir. One of the arrested persons had allegedly maintained direct links with the terror groups in Kashmir. The confessions of the recruiters have revealed how scores of youth from Kerala have been indoctrinated and pumped into the stream of terrorism over a period of time.

Apart from the slain Varghese Thomas alias Muhammed Yasin, many Hindu and Christian youths from suburban Kochi have been converted to Islam before being sent to spread terror. Thammanam Shaji, a criminal-turned- reformist, was taken into custody for his alleged role in converting his one-time colleagues and other persons with criminal background. Shaji had played a key role in converting Varghese and handing him over to extremists.

"At least 40 persons have fallen into his trap. It has to be verified how many have been missing," police sources said. "Shaji used to feed a Kozhikode-based conversion centre with many youths with criminal background. Some external agencies might have given him a task for converting youths and then supplying them to the prescribed sources. It has to be juxtaposed with his recent aborted attempt to fly to Sri Lanka using a fake passport," sources said.

Quoting the confession of Faizal, police said the new recruits were taken to Hyderabad for an all-round training envisaged at moulding them into hardcore extremists. Investigation would be extended to other states after completing urgent arrests here, sources said.

Heading: Ex-Kenyan lawmaker held in Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Major Ramesh Upadhyay, the former defence services officer who has been detained in connection with the Malegaon blasts by the ATS from Pune, was a hard-working soldier who rose from the ranks to join the officers cadre.

While not much is known about his earlier service record, the officer joined the Army as a soldier and cleared Army Cadet College (ACC) tests to join the officers cadre. Army officers say Ramesh would have been an exceptional soldier as the ACC special entry scheme is aimed at inducting above average troops as officers.

While Ramesh was an infantry soldier — where he would have picked up knowledge about arms, explosives and bomb making — his posting as an officer was in the Army's Air Defence Artillery (ADA), a specialised regiment assigned air protection roles of vital Army units and formations.

While the officer retired as a Major in 1998 and his last posting was with the Southern Command, he was placed in Pune — the place from where he was picked up for questioning — for at least two years.

Sources said the Maharashtra Police had been keeping a watch on him in recent years after the 2005 accidental blasts in Nanded pointed to certain explosives training being imparted in Pune area. However, no direct link could then be established and now too, the investigations are in the form of agressive questioning and no charges have been pressed yet.

A month before he was arrested, CPI(M) leader Hanan Mollah wrote to the Prime Minister pointing to charges that the Nagpur-based Bhonsale Military School was being used to impart training in arms and bomb making to Hindu youth.

In a letter dated September 2, Mollah wrote about the "serious situation" arising due to the strengthening of fascist organisations and pointed to allegations that the CBI was covering up the role of Hindu terror organisations in carrying out serial blasts across the country.

The letter specifically named the school and pointed to charges that "neo-fascist organisations" were imparting training in arms, bomb-making and bomb explosions at the educational institute. It also said retired army officers were imparting the training. The first came under the scrutiny of investigating agencies while probing the 2006 blasts in Nanded.

Heading: J-K Police await identification of bodies - Indian Express
Content:
A former Kenyan Member of Parliament and his woman accomplice were arrested this month by the customs department at the Indira Gandhi International Airport on charges of carrying large amounts of undeclared foreign currency (smuggling) into the country. Raphael Wanjala, 44, the former MP for Budalangi and Kenya's former assistant minister for water and irrigation, had travelled from Uganda via Dubai on board the Emirates EK- 514 flight on October 8. He was accompanied by 24-year-old Joyce Akinyi. Custom officials said that the purpose of his visit with so much currency and his links were being investigated.

According to customs officials, any amount more than USD 5,000 has to be declared at the airport and owners obtain a currency declaration certificate for the same. When a passenger has nothing to declare, they pass through the green channel. "Raphael Wanjala and his partner were arrested after being caught with an undeclared amount of USD 150,000 while walking through the green channel," customs official said.

The duo have refused to give the names and addresses of people they were to meet and stay with in Delhi. "The two were arrested on October 8 and are in Tihar Jail at the moment. Even as all the concerned departments are investigating — including the revenue intelligence and the narcotics bureau — nothing subsequent has come out of the arrests yet, as the two have not revealed anything about the purpose of their visit. They have claimed to be husband and wife," an official said.

Officials at the Tihar Jail confirmed that the two are lodged in jail number 4 of the Tihar prison. "As per their passports, the man is Raphael Wanjala, while the woman's passport has her name as Ochieng Teresa, 24. The two have given the same address-Westlands, Nairobi," a jail official said. According to sources, investigators have found several Pakistani telephone numbers in a personal diary.

Heading: 5 Hizbul men killed in Valley - Indian Express
Content:
Although the identity of the four militants belonging to Kerala killed in north Kashmir earlier this month has been established, J-K Police are yet to decide about the burial of the slain militants. The bodies have been lying in the police mortuary in Srinagar for the past three weeks.

J-K Police say they are expecting the bereaved family members of the militants to arrive in the next few days. "We can't dispose of the bodies without the permission of their families or the Kerala Police," Senior Superintendent of Police, Police Control Room, Shokwat Malik told The Indian Express. "The Kerala Police have informed the families of the four slain militants but there has been no response from them."

Heading: In Patna, they say he had a Mumbai dream - Indian Express
Content:
Joint team of state police and Army on Monday killed five Hizbul Mujahideen militants in Nawapachi forest areas in mountainous Kishtwar district, more than 240 km north-east of Jammu.

Deputy Inspector General of Police, Doda-Ramban range, Hemant Kumar Lohia said a joint team of state police and 11 Rashtriya Rifles launched a search operation in Methwal area of Nawapachi forests falling under the jurisdiction of Marwah police station.

"During searches, the troops came under fire from militants and retaliated, killing five militants," he added.

The militants were identified as Dodu of Kellar in Marwah, Mohammad Rajab Code Imtiyaz of Afti in Warwan, Mohammad Shafi of Bungam in Kaderan, Yasir and Junaid.

Lohia said four AK rifles, arms, ammunition and explosives were recovered from the site.

The search operation was still going on to flush out the other accomplices of the militants in the area, if any.

Heading: Assam relief camps take toll, 6 dead so far - Indian Express
Content:
Kundan Prasad was decorating his two-storey home with Diwali lights when suddenly his world was plunged into everlasting darkness. Several hours later, after the news had been repeatedly confirmed by police calls and TV pictures, his emotion remained frozen under the paralyzing weight of his disbelief.

Not one person in the throng of friends, relatives and family that visited Kundan Prasad's home would hazard a guess on why his son Rahul Raj would take a busload of people hostage in an unknown city where he had arrived only the day before, looking for a job.

All of them were aware of the politics around Biharis and jobs in Mumbai — trains have been burning in Bihar in protest against the attacks on north Indians there. But the idea that Rahul would actually want to murder Raj Thackeray was too fantastic for anyone to even consider.

Of course, no one believed that Rahul was, as suggested in sections the media, "mentally unstable". The whole thing just didn't add up.

"How could he have done this? There was no provocation. He was only slightly unhappy with the paltry salary here in Patna," said Kundan Prasad. Rahul, 25, was the eldest of his three children. His daughter Puja, is a probationary officer with the State Bank of India in Kolkata, and his other son, Rohit, is an automobile engineer in Ambala.

It was the desire to do at least as well as his younger siblings that pushed Rahul to leave Patna in search of a new job.

After passing out of Raja Ram Mohun Roy Seminary, one of Patna's oldest schools, Rahul got a diploma in radiology from the Indian Institute of Health Education. But he was unhappy with the Rs-5,000 job that the diploma got him. His friends advised him to try walk-in interviews at Mumbai hospitals. Rahul arrived in Mumbai on Sunday, and checked into a hotel.

His family had not heard from him since he left home. Rahul had forgotten to take the charger of his mobile phone along, Kundan Prasad said.

"How could my son who wouldn't hurt a fly and never fought with anyone, pick up a gun," Prasad asked. "And even if he did have a gun, how can he hijack a double-decker bus all on his own? Please do not go by what TV is showing. Let the CBI inquire and tell us the truth," he pleaded with folded hands.

Rahul lost his mother long ago, said neighbours. His father, who runs a fairly flourishing auto garage across the road from the family's home, remarried, and Rahul's stepmother Renu Devi looked after him well.

"Rahul was good in studies, and a great Sachin fan," said his friend Amit. "He was picky about who he associated with, and preferred to watch TV in his spare time."

Heading: Cyclone hits Meghalaya, 4 killed - Indian Express
Content:
Udalguri and Darrang, the two northern Assam districts which hit the headlines earlier this month for riots between immigrant Muslims and ethnic communities leading to the death of over 55 people, may be limping back to normalcy. But the deaths that have occurred, particularly of women and children, have caused worry for the authorities.

On Sunday, Sunela Daimari, 25, died in a relief camp at Ikrabari in Udalguri district, taking the death toll to six since relief camps were set up in the two strife-torn districts after violence broke out on October 3. Over one lakh people are currently lodged in about 80 relief camps in Udalguri and Darrang.

"Sunela had some health problems and was admitted to a hospital from October 10 to 16. She was also referred to a better hospital, but she refused to go," D N Das, Joint Director (health) in Udalguri, told The Indian Express on the phone. Das also confirmed the death of a pregnant woman, Rita Biswas, in the relief camp at Lal Bahadur Shastri School. "The woman who was eight-months pregnant was provided treatment for pregnancy-related complications on October 20, but she died two days later," he added.

Earlier, while an eight-year-old girl called Anita Marak had died in the Bhakatpara relief camp on October 13, a three-month-old girl had died due to respiratory ailment in the Ranipukhuri Middle School relief camp. Another eight-year-old girl called Mohida Khatun too had died in the Ranipukhuri relief camp on October 24 while an elderly woman called Johana Marak, another tribal, had died in Bhakatpara last week.

Udalguri, a newly-created tribal-dominated district, faces an acute shortage of doctors. "Several posts of medical officers have been lying vacant for a long time and we have been drawing doctors from the adjoining district of Sonitpur," Das said. Udalguri Deputy Commissioner Kamal Chandra Mahanta, however, said, "Medical teams are visiting camps everyday, and we also have at our disposal a well-equipped mobile medical unit," he added.

Meanwhile, NGOs have urged the Government to look into the health needs of the camp inmates, especially women and children.

Heading: Efforts on to revive NEPF - Indian Express
Content:
Four people, including a three-month -old baby, died in Meghalaya as the powerful cyclone Rashmi hit the state on Monday morning. Two women and the baby died when the wall of their house collapsed at Lumsohra while a 12-year boy was drowned as the surging waters of Wah Umkhrah River swept him away, East Khasi Hills Deputy Commissioner B Dhar told reporters.

Cyclone Rashmi caused incessant rainfall together with gusty wind and several trees, electric and telephone poles were uprooted leading to traffic snarls throughout the day. In Upper Shillong area, near the Eastern Air Command headquarters, traffic was brought to a standstill by uprooted trees during the day. Electricity and telephone lines were snapped and could be restored only in the evening in Shillong.

The Meteorological Department said that cyclone Rashmi, which was centered (0830 hours) 250 kms south west from here at Bangladesh, was weakening. It however predicted isolated rainfall in Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura over the next 24 hours. The tropical storm also led to the temperature plummeting below seven degree Celsius in the day.

Heading: In final week, candidates focus on Bush’s states - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a cue from the return of Prafulla Kumar Mahanta to the Asom Gana Parishad, a concerted effort is now being made to revive the defunct North East People's Forum (NEPF).

Former Lok Sabha speaker and NCP leader Purno A Sangma said the non-Congress political parties of the northeastern states will be meeting in Shillong in November-end to talk about modalities to forge an alliance in view of the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.

Days before Mahanta's re-entry to AGP was formally announced, the former Assam chief minister had met Sangma and discussed the necessity of reviving the NEPF. Six years ago, Sangma had floated the NEPF but it soon became inactive.

Sangma said: "If the non-Congress parties can come together under a common umbrella, the Congress will have a tough time in the region."

Former Manipur chief minister Radhabinod Koijam, who was in Shillong to attend an NCP meeting recently, also felt that there was a need for reviving NEPF.

Heading: NY-based group swamps swing states with movie on radical Islam - Indian Express
Content:
John McCain and Barack Obama are heading into the final week of the presidential campaign planning to spend nearly all their time in states that President Bush won last time, testimony to the increasingly dire position of McCain and his party as election day approaches.

With optimism brimming in Democratic circles, Obama presents on Monday what aides described as a summing-up speech for his campaign in Canton, Ohio, reprising the themes he first presented in February 2007, when he began his campaign for the presidency.

From here on out, Obama's aides said, attacks on McCain will be joined by an emphasis on broader and less partisan themes, like the need to unify the country after a difficult election. McCain has settled on Pennsylvania as the one state that Democrats won in 2004 where he has a decent chance of winning, a view not shared by Obama's advisers.

But McCain and his running mate Sarah Palin are planning to spend most of their time in Florida, Ohio, Virginia, North Carolina, Missouri, and Indiana, all states that Republicans had entered the campaign thinking they could bank on.

As Obama uses his money and political organisation to expand the political map, McCain is being forced to shore up support in Indiana and North Carolina that have not been contested for decades. His decision to campaign on Sunday in Iowa, a day after Palin campaigned there, was questioned even by Republicans who noted polls that showed Obama pulling away there.

Republicans and Democrats said there were signs that two states that had once appeared overwhelmingly Republican, Georgia and South Carolina, were tightening, in part, because of surge of early-voting by African-Americans. An Obama win in the states seemed unlikely but it is a sign of how volatile a year this is that more states would seem to be coming into play, rather than being settled, as the election approaches.

The contours of these final days suggest a culmination of a strategy that Obama's advisers put in place at the beginning: to use his huge fund-raising edge to try to put as many states in play as possible and overwhelm McCain in the final days of the race.

"It's now a big map, so you have to be in a lot of states over the last eight days," said David Plouffe, Obama's campaign manager.

As of right now, Pennsylvania is the only Democratic-leaning state Obama is planning to visit. Obama also is making a vigorous push in Florida, after a campaign stop there last week convinced his advisers that he has a real shot of winning there.

Heading: McCain’s brother apologises for swearing at 911 - Indian Express
Content:
A New York-based organisation has sent copies of a movie about Islamist extremism to more than 28 million houses and religious institutions in presidential election battleground states over the past several weeks.

The 60-minute documentary-style production, Obsession: Radical Islam's War Against the West, includes images of terrorist attacks from around the world, historic footage of Nazi rallies and modern-day scenes of Muslim children reciting poetry that celebrates suicide bombings. The costs of producing and distributing the film — an effort that one Muslim advocacy group estimates at $50 million — were paid by the Clarion Fund, a non-profit group that says it is seeking "to educate Americans about issues of national security to influence voters".

Members of several Muslim groups have condemned the film.

"It's a mind-boggling massive campaign. When you send material like this almost exclusively to presidential swing states that sends a message that you are trying to influence the election," said Ibrahim Hooper, a spokesman for the Washington-based Council on American-Islamic Relations.

The council filed complaints with the Federal Election Commission and the Internal Revenue Service last month, accusing the group of promoting the candidacy of John McCain over Barack Obama's.

One of the Clarion Fund's websites, www.radicalislam.com, posted an article two weeks ago that stated, "McCain's policies seek to confront radical Islamic extremism and terrorism and roll it back while Obama's could in fact make the situation facing the West even worse".

The Clarion Fund has since removed the article, but its website still links readers to a vast network of sites that promote McCain. The election has also dominated panel discussions at dozens of Clarion-organised private screenings of the film and its recently released sequel, The Third Jihad.

Clarion Fund spokesman Gregory Ross said the group's intent had been to distribute The Third Jihad in the mass mailings but that the production was not completed in time. In an e-mail, a Clarion staff member and fund-raiser said the sequel's planned rollout in September was meant to coincide with the elections.

"The film is in post-production now and we will be able to take it to the masses in time to make the issue a central topic in the Presidential elections," fund-raiser Matt Weisbaum said in a July 15 e-mail obtained by The Washington Post.

Distribution of the film has been focused primarily on battleground states such as Virginia, Colorado, Florida and Ohio. Virginia residents began receiving DVDs of Obsession last week.

Ross called the film "educational" and said its release was scheduled to coincide with the anniversary of 9/11, not the elections. "It was done in order to commemorate and remind people of the tragedy of 9/11 and that the threat still remains in America for terrorist activity," Ross said.

The Obama campaign declined to comment on the Clarion Fund and the distribution of the films. Brian Rogers, a McCain campaign spokesman, said there is no coordinated effort between the campaign and the Clarion Fund.

Heading: Blast in high security area of Quetta kills two in Pak - Indian Express
Content:
The younger brother of John McCain has withdrawn from campaign activities and apologised for swearing at an emergency dispatcher after he called 911 to inquire about a traffic jam on the Woodrow Wilson Bridge.

Joe McCain, 66, said he was stepping aside to avoid becoming a liability for the Arizona senator before the November 4 election. In an interview on Saturday, he described the 911 call as "the biggest mistake I will ever make in my life, at least in politics", and said he thought he had hung up the phone before uttering an expletive.

The apology marked the second this month for him. He also apologised after referring to suburban Alexandria and Arlington County as "communist country" at a rally in suburban Loudoun County.

Asked about the expletive recorded in the 911 incident, he said: "I swear to you, I never, ever meant to say those words to a live voice... The truth is, I had no idea there was anybody on the other end of the phone."

It was early Tuesday when Joe McCain, en route to his home in Alexandria from campaign events in Scranton, Pennsylvania, approached the span in his Toyota Camry. He encountered a red light as he pulled up to the bridge, but traffic was flowing freely in the other direction.

Joe McCain said he flipped his radio to WTOP (103.5 FM), where he learned that a test on the bridge was to blame for the stopped traffic. After about 40 minutes, he called 911.

"911. State your emergency," the dispatcher said, according to an audio clip first played by ABC television affiliate WJLA. "It's not an emergency. But do you know why on one side at the damn drawbridge of 95 traffic is stopped for 15 minutes and yet traffic's coming the other way?" McCain said.

"Sir, are you calling 911 to complain about traffic?" the operator asked.

"(Expletive) you," McCain said, hanging up the phone.

The dispatcher then called back and was sent to his voice mail, which enabled authorities to identify the caller.

Campaign spokesman Tucker Bounds said in an e-mail: "Joe recognises his mistake and has apologised. We are moving on."

McCain said the decision to step aside from the campaign was his alone.

Heading: Pak, Afghan officials to work together on terrorism - Indian Express
Content:
At least two persons were killed and 12 injured in a powerful car bomb attack in a high-security zone in the south-western Pakistani city of Quetta on Monday.

The blast occurred when explosives hidden in a car in the parking lot at the busy Liaquat Park area were detonated by terrorists, Balochistan's Inspector General of Police Qazi Abdul Waheed said. Police said 10 kg of explosives were used in the blast, which sparked panic. Officials said one of the two persons killed in the attack was an auto-rickshaw driver. Two of the dozen injured are in a critical condition, they said.

No group claimed responsibility for the attack but similar bombings in the past have been blamed on Baloch nationalist groups waging a violent campaign for a greater say in the exploitation of the province's abundant natural resources.

However, the three main national groups - Baloch Liberation Army, Baloch Republican Army and Baloch Liberation Front - had announced a unilateral ceasefire last month.

The explosion, which occurred in a high-security zone where the district courts, Chief Minister's secretariat and Governor's House are located, destroyed five cars and five auto-rickshaws that caught fire. Waheed said experts from the bomb disposal squad examined the site and collected evidence. Some police officials said locally-made explosives were used in the blast. Traders closed their shops in several commercial areas in Quetta in panic after the blast, which was heard from several kilometres away. The head of one victim was severed from his body and the other's body was completely burned, doctors said.

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani, Balochistan Chief Minister Nawab Aslam Raisani and Governor Zulfiqar Ali Magsi condemned the blast. They said such attacks were against humanity, Islam and Pakistan. Zardari said Pakistan is committed to fighting terrorism in all its forms and such acts cannot deter the Government from its resolve. Gilani said the perpetrators of such heinous attacks will be awarded exemplary punishment.

Heading: Ahmadinejad’s health stirs debate on election - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan and Afghanistan on Monday pledged to step up cooperation to counter-terrorism and extremism as leaders from both countries gathered here to discuss modalities for engaging the Taliban and other militant groups in a dialogue.

Addressing the inaugural session of the two-day Pakistan-Afghanistan jirga gai or mini-jirga here, Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi emphasised the need for close cooperation between the two countries.Both countries have "suffered immensely and continue to suffer" due to extremism, militancy and terrorism and the situation demanded a joint and comprehensive strategy to bring peace and stability to the whole region, he said.

Heading: Israel poll bounce shows Livni leading Netanyahu - Indian Express
Content:
Reports about the health of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad have stirred speculation about whether the controversial populist will run again for the country's highest elected office in June.

In an interview published late on Saturday by Iran's official Islamic Republic News Agency, a close associate of Ahmadinejad said the president had fallen ill because of overwork and exhaustion.

"Every human being can face exhaustion under such a workload," lawmaker Mohammad Ismail Kowsari, an ally of Ahmadinejad, said in the interview. "The President will eventually get well and continue his job."

The exuberant and media-hungry Ahmadinejad, who turned 53 on Monday, missed several public appearances last week, although he appeared at several low-key events over the weekend.

The absences have prompted whispers that Ahmadinejad is on his way out. But Kowsari and others close to Ahmadinejad have accused his critics of trying to use what they describe as a routine illness for political advantage.

Observers in Tehran, the Iranian capital, cautioned not to read to much into news of the illness. Although Ahmadinejad is said to suffer from low blood pressure, there is no evidence that he has serious health problems or that he is being nudged out of his post by the country's religious leadership.

But the incident shows how openly the knives are out for Ahmadinejad within Iran's ruling circle. On Saturday, Parliament moved to impeach pro-Ahmadinejad Interior Minister Ali Kordan, who, according to Iran's Fars News Agency, admitted submitting a fake honorary Oxford law degree as evidence of his qualifications for the job.

Some Iranians and Western diplomats have voiced hope that moderate former President Mohammad Khatami would run against Ahmadinejad next year. Khatami's supporters say he will consider running for office if Ahmadinejad does not stack the deck by doling out cash to would-be voters.

Heading: Novelist Tony Hillerman dies - Indian Express
Content:
TZIPI Livni has seen a sharp turnaround in fortunes for Israel's ruling Kadima party since she became leader last month and could now beat the Right-wing Opposition in a coming election, polls on Monday indicated.

Two newspaper surveys published a day after Livni abandoned her efforts to forge a new coalition Government and recommended to the President that he call a parliamentary election showed Kadima just beating Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud — a reversal of the results forecast in previous polls, published in August.

The Centrist Kadima party has been battered by the 2006 Lebanon war and then the corruption scandal that forced Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to resign last month.

But a poll in Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper predicted it would take 29 of 120 seats while Likud would take 26, up from 12 seats. The Labour party of Defence Minister Ehud Barak, Olmert's main ally in the outgoing Government, was seen taking 11 seats, down from 19 at present.

The results broke with past surveys that saw Netanyahu, his popularity boosted by Israeli jitters over regional security, easily beating Kadima and Labour.

Heading: US troops say Afghan security guards attacked them - Indian Express
Content:
Tony Hillerman, author of the acclaimed Navajo Tribal Police mystery novels and creator of two of the unlikeliest of literary heroes — Navajo police officers Joe Leaphorn and Jim Chee — died on Sunday of pulmonary failure. He was 83.

His daughter, Anne Hillerman, said her father's health had been declining and he was at Presbyterian Hospital in Albuquerque when he died at about 3 pm. Hillerman lived through two heart attacks and surgeries for prostate and bladder cancer. He kept tapping at his keyboard even as his eyes began to dim, as his hearing faded, as rheumatoid arthritis turned his hands into claws. "I'm getting old," he declared in 2002, "but I still like to write". Anne Hillerman said that her father was a born storyteller. "He had such a wonderful, wonderful curiosity about the world," she said. "He could take little details and bring them to life, not just in his books, but in conversation, too."

Lt Joe Leaphorn, introduced in The Blessing Way in 1970, was an experienced police officer who understood, but did not share, his people's traditional belief in a rich spirit world. Officer Jim Chee, introduced in People of Darkness in 1978, was an officer studying to become a "hathaali" — Navajo for "shaman". Together, they struggled to bridge the cultural divide between the dominant Anglo society and the impoverished people who call themselves the Dineh.

Hillerman's commercial breakthrough was Skinwalkers, published in 1987. It paved the way for A Thief of Time, which made several best seller lists. In all, he wrote 18 books in the Navajo series.

Heading: Raj his ‘target’, Patna youth takes over Mumbai bus, shot by police - Indian Express
Content:
US forces in Afghanistan said on Monday they had launched an air strike that killed a number of private Afghan security guards only after coming under fire from that position.

Afghan provincial authorities said on Sunday they were investigating reports that 20 private security guards had been killed in a US-led coalition air strike southwest of Kabul.

A provincial Government source said US-led forces called in the strike to fend off an attack by Taliban insurgents on several posts of the local security company that guards a road construction project in the Giro district of Ghazni.

But a spokesman for US forces said coalition troops called in air support after they were ambushed from multiple positions, including that occupied by the private security guards.

"Early yesterday, a coalition unit was on their way to their objective when they came under fire from multiple locations," said US forces spokesman Colonel Gregory Julian.

"They tried to withdraw but could not and they had no alternative but to call in close air support," he said.

Heading: Why falling crude oil is hope rising - Indian Express
Content:
A gun-wielding youth from Bihar, who was apparently upset with Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray and his campaign against north Indians, opened fire in a Mumbai city bus and injured a passenger before being shot dead by police, sparking outrage and fresh tensions between the two states.

Late night, after the entire political leadership from Bihar put pressure, the Prime Minister spoke to Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh who in turn asked the chief secretary to carry out a probe.

The incident occurred at around 9 am in Kurla's Bail Bazar area in a double-decker BEST bus headed to Kurla from Andheri. According to passenger Abdul Rashid Sheikh, the bus had just pulling out of Bail Bazaar stop, when the gunman, identified as Rahul Raj, left his seat on the upper deck of the bus.

"There were about 12-15 of us on the top deck. There was nothing unusual about the man except that he kept shifting seats. He suddenly went to the back of the bus where the conductor was sitting, and threw a thick chain of the sort used to tie luggage around his neck. he simultaneously whipped out a gun from his pocket, and ordered us to stay in our seats," Sheikh said.

According to passengers, Rahul kept saying, "I have not come to harm any of you. I want to send Raj Thackeray a message. I have come here to kill only him." He also shouted that he wanted to speak to the media and to the Mumbai police commissioner. He suddenly shot passenger Manoj Bhagat in his thigh, apparently because Bhagat was trying to divert Rahul's attention from his gun.

As the passengers cowered in their seats, the second conductor, Shivaji Borade, came up from the lower deck. Rahul ordered him to go back. "I immediately rushed down and told the driver to slowly bring the bus to a stop. I then jumped off and rushed to the police chowki nearby," Borade said.

Police teams surrounded the bus almost immediately, and called out to passengers to keep their heads down. "When he knew he was surrounded, Rahul scribbled something on two currency notes and threw them from one of the windows. On a Rs 50 note he had written 'Call the police commissioner' and on a Rs 10 he had written, 'I have not come here to harm anyone. I only want to kill Raj Thackeray'. Both messages were in Hindi," said DCP Milind Bharambe.

ACP Mohammad Javed said, "When we rushed to the spot wearing our bullet proof vests, we realized we had to do something quickly to neutralise the situation. We also got to know from witnesses that a few rounds had been fired and that a passenger was lying injured in the bus. We yelled at the youth to put his weapon down, but he did not obey and started waving his gun, which further heightened our apprehension that he might shoot again."

Finally, a team of policemen, including Javed, entered the bus. After calling out another warning, they fired 13 rounds at the youth, who was sitting at the head of the staircase leading to the upper deck. Four bullets hit him, and he collapsed. Police said they found a lapsed ID card from the Indian Institute of Health Education and Research, Beur, Patna on Rahul.

Dr V V Shukla, medical superintendent of Rajawadi Hospital, said the injured passenger, Bhagat, had been operated upon and was out of danger.

Heading: In his hotel room, he had vented rage, broken window pane, lamp, say police - Indian Express
Content:
It may be gloom, doom and bust on Dalal Street this Diwali as the economy braces itself for a "cloudy" growth outlook and the Finance Ministry admits that fiscal deficit targets for this year won't be met. But if there is one silver lining — and for India, Asia's third largest economy, a bold one at that — it is the dramatic fall in global crude oil prices from nearly $150 a barrel this June to $56 now.

This slide in crude oil presents Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and his lieutenants a significant fiscal headroom to pump-prime the economy and risk some adventure in big-ticket infrastructure spending, both social and physical. Besides, it also helps the rupee hold on to its own because of lesser demand for dollars by oil refiners. Last, but not the least, it douses inflationary expectations, giving the government and the Reserve Bank of India more leeway in lowering lending rates and infusing more liquidity into the system to spur growth.

India imports almost 70 per cent of its fuel needs, and oil is the biggest item. In 2007-08, it imported 121.672 million tones of crude oil and the bill was a staggering $68 billion. The softening of crude oil prices in the past four months has reduced the monthly oil import bill of Indian refiners by nearly 40%. It is true that part of the gains may be neutralised by the sharp 21% depreciation of the rupee, but still, Indian refiners will have to buy much less dollars for their crude needs.

Not just does the fall give fiscal headroom, it also smoothens the volatility in the foreign exchange market, which is already reeling under huge capital outflows. This calendar, foreign institutional investors have pulled out over $13 billion from stock markets that exerted considerable pressure on the rupee. Lower demand for dollars by oil companies will ease the pressure on the rupee and will help the domestic currency hold on to its own.

Even if domestic prices are not cut, cheaper oil means it will pare the fertiliser subsidy bill that has already crossed the Defence budget for this fiscal year. Inflation is expected to ease further if commodity prices keep falling in line with crude prices, giving monetary authorities some room for lowering prime lending rates to ensure credit is freely available to Indian industry.

"As far as fiscal deficit is concerned, the Centre's fuel subsidy will be less. Also the fertiliser subsidy in the second half of the year will be less. Fertiliser prices are linked to energy prices internationally as well as in India, where naphtha is used for making fertiliser. But the overall fiscal deficit situation may not improve tremendously as the government's expenditure has also risen," said Saumitra Chaudhuri, member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council.

According to government estimates, the subsidy will be at least Rs 40,000 crore lower from the originally estimated Rs 1,20,000 crore.

When crude was at $145 a barrel, oil companies' under-recoveries were estimated at Rs 2.4 lakh crore, at $75, under-recoveries will also come down substantially to Rs 52,800 crore. If oil prices stabilise at current levels resulting in an average price of $75 per barrel for 2008-09, a dip in fuel oil/naphtha prices alone would translate into a reduction of the subsidy bill by around Rs 14,000 crore.

Lowering subsidy bills would mean the exchequer can focus its resources more aggressively on social sector programmes like the NREGS. With the fall in prices of fuel oil and naphtha, the cost of industrial production will come down as also the diversion of subsidised diesel to industry, thereby bringing down the Centre's oil subsidy bill further.

"The fall in crude prices will have some impact on inflation. Prices of many commodities such as edible oil, rubber and plastics and man made textiles may also come down as they are linked to crude oil prices. But it must be kept in mind that prices of other commodities are also decreasing in international markets," Chaudhuri added.

"The fall in crude oil prices brings good news on all fronts for the economy," said D K Joshi, chief economist at CRISIL. "It will help fight the growth deceleration. Fiscal deficit will come down as the government will have to issue lesser bonds. Even if domestic prices are not cut, the fall in international prices will help control inflation as prices of aviation turbine fuel and other industrial fuels will come down."

Decreased pressure on the inflation front would give the country's monetary managers some leeway for an interest rate cut, essential to ease up the credit squeeze that's threatening to cloud the real economy's growth prospects.

"The cost of production for some industries will also come down, which will help lower inflation. With inflationary expectations lowering, interest rates may also be gradually brought down," said Joshi. "But it must be kept in mind that the rupee has weakened significantly and so imports are not as cheap. About 40% of the fall in international

crude oil prices will be offset by rupee depreciation," he added.

The UPA had hiked domestic prices for petrol, diesel and cooking gas (LPG) by Rs 5 a litre, Rs 3 a litre and Rs 50 a cylinder, respectively, in June. Reversing part of the hike soon would make immense political as well as economic sense, experts say.

A back of the envelope calculation suggests that cutting petrol and diesel prices by Rs 2 per litre each, would bring inflation down by over 1%. If prices for metals and other commodities remain stable, overall inflation could fall to single digits from the current 11.04% sooner than the government expected.

BETTER MILEAGE

Oil prices have fallen from $150/barrel in June to $56 now. Why this plunge is the silver lining for India in a gloomy global economic scenario

MORE FISCAL HEADROOM: In past 4 months, Indian refiners' monthly import bill has come down 40%.
