Aides said he will attempt to draw connections between national security, energy and the economy, arguing that Barack Obama is not ready to lead on those issues.

But the rest of his day will be rallies listed on his schedule as "Joe the Plumber Events", part of a final appeal charging that his rival would raise taxes on hardworking Americans and give the proceeds to others, driving down the economy. As they stump across Pennsylvania, Florida and other battlegrounds, McCain and his running mate, Sarah Palin, now refer to Obama as the "Redistributionist in Chief" or "Barack the Redistributionist" or "Barack the Wealth Spreader".

At a campaign rally in Chester, Pennsylvania, held in a cold rain, Obama hit back on the economic assault, saying: "There's only one candidate with a plan that could eventually raise taxes on millions of middle-class families, and it isn't me." The Democrat told the thousands of people who braved temperatures in the 30s and blustery winds that McCain lacks credibility on the economy and taxes.

"John McCain has ridden shotgun as George Bush has driven our economy toward a cliff, and now he wants to take the wheel and step on the gas," he said. "When it comes to the issue of taxes, saying that John McCain is running for a third Bush term isn't being fair to George W Bush."

The focus on the economy is a far cry from the October argument McCain once thought he would make to voters. In the days before Florida's Republican primary in January, he said that national security would be the central focus of his campaign.

"Even if the economy is the, quote, number one issue, the real issue will remain America's security," McCain told reporters in the back of his Straight Talk Express bus. "And if they choose to say, 'Look, I do not want this guy, because he was not as good on home loan mortgages,' or whatever it is, I will accept their verdict. I am running because of the transcendental challenge of the 21st century, which is radical Islamic extremism, as you know."

Now, though, McCain focuses almost all of his time on the economic crisis that began in mid-September. Inspired by Obama's offhand comment to Ohio plumber Joe Wurzelbacher about "spreading the wealth around", McCain is betting his White House hopes on taxes, whipping up his crowds with predictions of further economic decline in an Obama administration.

"Senator Obama believes in redistributing wealth, not in policies that grow our economy and create jobs," McCain thundered to almost 10,000 supporters who gathered Tuesday morning at a stadium in Hershey. "There's nothing fair about driving our economy into the ground."

Heading: More US kids getting kidney stones now - Indian Express
Content:
John McCain and his allies say that they are wrong. The country, they say, could be headed to a 2008 version of the famous 1948 upset election, with McCain in the role of Harry S Truman and Barack Obama as Thomas E Dewey, lulled into overconfidence by inaccurate polls.

"We believe it is a very close race, and something that is frankly very winnable," Sarah Simmons, director of strategy for the McCain campaign, said.

Few analysts outside the McCain campaign appear to share this view. And pollsters this time around will not make the mistake that the Gallup organisation made 60 years ago — ending their polling more than a week before the election and missing a last-minute surge in support for Truman. Every day brings dozens of new state and national presidential polls, a trend that is expected to continue up to Election Day.

Still, there appears to be an undercurrent of worry among some polling professionals and academics. One reason is the wide variation in Obama leads: On Tuesday, an array of polls showed the Democrat leading by as little as two points and as much as 15 points. The latest Washington Post-ABC News tracking poll showed the race holding steady, with Obama enjoying a lead of 52 per cent to 45 per cent among likely voters.

Some in the McCain camp also argue that the polls showing the largest leads for Obama mistakenly assume that turnout among young voters and African Americans will be disproportionately high. The campaign is banking on a good turnout among GOP partisans, whom McCain officials say they are working hard to attract to the polls.

"I have been wondering for weeks" whether the polls are accurately gauging the state of the race, said Steven Schier, a political scientist at Carleton College in Minnesota. Borrowing from lingo popularised by former defence secretary Donald H Rumsfeld, Schier asked what are the "unknown unknowns" about polling this year: For instance, is the sizable cohort of people who don't respond to pollsters more Republican-leaning this year, perhaps because they don't want to admit to a pollster that they are not supporting the "voguish" Obama?

If so, that could mean the polls are routinely understating McCain's support. "I have no evidence that this is happening," Schier said, but he added: "I'm still thinking there's a 25 per cent chance that this is a squeaker race and McCain pulls it out."

Other experts are less uncertain. Ruy Teixeira, a political demographer at the Center for American Progress and the Century Foundation, said averaging the daily polls points to "pretty much the same thing — that the race is pretty stable and that Obama has a stable lead. Typically, when you are this far ahead at this point, it's hard to lose."

"It is very unlikely that we are going to get surprised by a last-minute movement," said John R Petrocik, chairman of the political science department at the University of Missouri. "Obama has been running six to eight points ahead for the better part of two weeks, and it's hard to imagine that turning around."

The McCain campaign's case that the race is closer than many polls suggest appears to rest largely on the proposition that the composition of the electorate this year will closely resemble that in 2004.

McCain pollsters do anticipate that turnout could be even higher this year than the robust turnout four years ago, but they also expect that Democratic gains among African American voters and younger voters will be offset by higher turnout among more Republican-leaning voters. They also assert the race is tightening in battleground states, with independent voters increasingly receptive to McCain.

Heading: LTTE aircraft attacks Colombo, Mannar - Indian Express
Content:
To the great surprise of parents, kidney stones, once considered a disorder of middle age, are now showing up in children as young as 5 or 6.

While there are no reliable data on the number of cases, paediatric urologists and nephrologists across the country say they are seeing a steep rise in young patients. Some hospitals have opened paediatric kidney stone clinics.

"The older doctors would say in the '70s and '80s, they'd see a kid with a stone once every few months," said Dr Caleb P Nelson, a urology instructor at Harvard Medical School. "Now we see kids once a week or less."

In China recently, many children who drank milk tainted with melamine — a toxic chemical illegally added to watered-down milk to inflate the protein count —developed kidney stones.

The increase in the United States is attributed to a host of factors, including a food additive that is both legal and ubiquitous: salt.

Though most of the research on kidney stones comes from adult studies, experts believe it can be applied to children. Those studies have found that dietary factors are the leading cause of kidney stones, which are crystallisations of several substances in the urine. Stones form when these substances become too concentrated.

Excess salt has to be excreted through the kidneys, but salt binds to calcium on its way out, creating a greater concentration of calcium in the urine and the kidneys.

Heading: Gayoom’s 30-year reign ends in the Maldives - Indian Express
Content:
In daring strikes, Tamil Tiger aircraft bombed a power plant in the Sri Lankan capital and an army camp in northwestern Mannar, even as rebel combatants continued to be under siege in their nerve centre of Kilinochchi.

The raids, the first air attacks by the LTTE in six weeks which left one person dead and three soldiers wounded, came late on Tuesday night as government troops closed in on the rebels' administrative headquarters in the island's north.

The aircraft first bombed the Thallaadi military base in Mannar at around 11 pm and carried out the attack on the power plant on the outskirts of Colombo 15 minutes later.

"LTTE aircraft attacked a military camp in Thallaadi and then dropped two bombs over the capital," a defence official said adding, the blasts have caused minor damage to the power plant in Grand Pass area.

The authorities in Colombo apparently detected a suspicious aircraft flying over the capital shortly before the strikes and switched off power in and around the city. The electricity was restored after one hour.

Sri Lankan Navy fired anti-aircraft guns into the sky to prevent any attack on the harbour, an official said.

The LTTE had carried out an air and ground attack on a military establishment in the northern town of Vavuniya in September, killing 11 soldiers. Ten Tiger suicide commandos also died in the attack.

The Tamil Tigers are believed to operate five Czech-built Zlin-143 aircraft, smuggled onto the island in parts and reassembled.

According to military sources, the rebels operate more than one airstrip in areas under their control.

The military had earlier claimed to have shot down one of the aircraft after the Vavuniya attack but the rebels denied the report.

Heading: 175 dead in Baluchistan quake - Indian Express
Content:
A former political prisoner won the Maldives' first democratic presidential election, defeating longtime ruler President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom and sending euphoric opposition supporters pouring into the streets Wednesday in celebration.

With all the votes counted from Tuesday's election, opposition leader Mohamed Nasheed won 54 per cent of the vote to Gayoom's 46 per cent, according to Election Commission results.

The outcome spells the end of the 30-year reign of Asia's longest-serving ruler, who won six previous elections but never before faced an opponent.

"I accept the results of the run-off election and I respectfully congratulate Mr Mohamed Nasheed and his party," Gayoom told the nation in a live concession speech. "I am declaring my full support to him. In this change we are approaching, I assure you we will make this a peaceful process," he said, priding himself on "the introduction of a new age of democracy."

"My prayer is that God gives prosperity to the Maldives and shows us peaceful and affluent days," he said.

Acting opposition party head Ibrahim Hussein Zaki said the country had "embraced democracy for the sake of the next generation and the people of the Maldives". Gayoom "ruled for 30 years. It should be a very short and harmonious transfer of power," he said.

Nasheed is expected to be sworn in on November 11, 30 years to the day that Gayoom took office in 1978.

"It was a very close race and the (opposition) alliance won," said outgoing Environment Minister Abdullah Mausoom. The country's first "multiparty elections have been held freely and fairly," he said.

Heading: City needs to be beautified, stresses Bakersfield mayor - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: To paint the city green, 40,000 saplings planted - Indian Express
Content:
Harvey L Hall, mayor of Bakersfield, 11th largest city in California, USA, said on Thursday Ludhiana city needed to work on the beautification front and improve the road and infrastructure to look better.

"There is a greater need for beautification in this city and it's important that quality of air gets better. The infrastructure and transportation are therefore in dire need for improvement here," said Hall, who was speaking at a function held in his honour at Guru Nanak Girls College, Model Town, in an answer to a question on what he thought needed to be changed in the city to make it better.

"From my travelling here, I find it difficult to know very few road accidents occur here," he remarked about the traffic. He was speaking at a function held in his honour at Guru Nanak Girls College, Model Town.

Hall, who has himself been actively involved in beautification programme in his native city apart from a monthly programme of picking up trash from freeways there, is visiting the city as part of a programme to strengthen relations between the two cities.

Commenting on the role of public officials in improving the quality of life in a city, he said, "Public officials should understand the value of volunteerism. It is important that they recognise the value of people of the city and therefore give back further to the community by volunteering to undertake beautification projects."

Harvey L Hall himself follows this model in his city of Bakersfield, where he is currently serving the third term. Hall is also known for donating his entire mayor's salary for the scholarships of the students aspiring to study further in the local colleges or the university. He has so far donated over 125 thousand US dollars as scholarship and supported education of 92 students.

Showering appreciation for Punjabi community for being so hospitable, he said he liked the sense of belongingness and positive energy spread through smiles all around in Punjab which he so strongly felt about.

Speaking about the euphoria that gripped the people on Diwali, he remarked, "It was a spectacular opportunity to watch such a large number of people taking part in fireworks and celebrating together." This is Hall's second visit to India and first to the city. He was also accompanied by John Hefner, director, International City Relations, Bakersfield, along with Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda, and city mayor Hakam Singh Giaspira. Also present were principal of the college, Dr Charanjit Kaur Mahal and president of college trust, Gurbir Singh.

Heading: Small Scale Trade Board chief holds meeting with excise officials - Indian Express
Content:
Save humanity, fight starvation and plant trees — is the slogan of Nishkam Sewa Ashram, a non-government organisation.

Living up to its motto, the NGO has just completed the first phase of planting trees. Under this, members of the ashram sowed 40,000 saplings through different schools, colleges, organisations and village panchayats.

Shruti Bansal, project manager of the NGO said: "The first phase which started from May and ended in September. The second phase of plantation will start from February."

Sharwan Kumar, founder chairman of the ashram, Daad village, said: "We don't want anyone to go to sleep on an empty stomach. After a decade or so, when more concrete structures come up, land to grow plants will automatically reduce. This may result in widespread starvation. And, a fruit plant starts bearing fruits after five years of plantation. So our aim is to have enough such plants all over the world, enough for the poor and the needy to fill their stomach."

Shruti said: "The saplings planted include banana, malta, kinnow, lemon, gauva, aamla, mango, jamun, mausami and pomegranate among others. We have distributed free-of-cost saplings to all schools and colleges in the city. Earlier, the ashram would buy these plants from Malerkotla. Howver, owing to the shortage of stock, we started buying these from Maliyabad in Lucknow. Being good in quality, we hope that these will start bearing fruits soon."

She said that in the second phase, seeds of plants like pear, peach and cheeku will be distributed free of cost to different organisations.

Interestingly, whenever the saplings are distributed, volunteers of the ashram also instruct the beneficiaries on how to make a disinfectant pit. "This will help produce healthy plants along with early fruits," Sharwan Kumar said.

Heading: ... gets a low-down on PAU - Indian Express
Content:
Madan Lal Kapoor, chairman of Small Scale Industries Board, held a meeting with excise officials and industrialists at the Circuit House here today.

This was his first visit after he took over as chairman of the board. Kapoor asked the excise officials to solve the problems of industrialists on priority even as he urged them to work towards increasing the tax revenue. Vice-chairman of the trade board, Madan Lal Bagga was also present at the meeting, which lasted for about an hour. Industrialists raised issues like delay in VAT refund and C-form shortage at the meeting.

Heading: DEO denies bias in giving teachers places of choice - Indian Express
Content:
Harvey L Hall, Mayor of Bakersfield, California visited Punjab Agricultural University on Thursday. During an interaction with Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU and officers of the University, he sought to know about Punjab agriculture and Punjab Agricultural University. The team is on a Punjab visit regarding establishing a city of Amritsar at Bakersfield.

Dr Kang gave a synoptic view of the organisational set up of PAU. He said that PAU was established in 1962 on the Land Grant Pattern with technical support from Ohio State University, USA and informed that the two institutions held strong ties till date. Informing about the student-strength, Dr Kang said the university had some 1,800 students of which almost 50% were girls. The regular alumni meets helped PAU to keep record of students' success in different fields of their profession. Dr Kang said that Bakersfield and Punjab had a lot of common ground in agriculture.

Introducing his city, Hall informed that Bakersfield was the 11th largest city in California that had only single digit unemployment rate indicating its business prosperity. He interacted with the participating officers of PAU on various issues concerning agriculture such as the role of women in agriculture, strength of international students at PAU, evaluation of student success, supporting agricultural ventures, etc.

Dr S.K. Mann highlighted the PAU's initiative towards vocationalisation of education. She elaborated on the integrated curricular programmes operative at PAU. Responding to the query of Hall about practical aspects of agricultural education, Dr M.S. Aulakh, Dean College of Agriculture, said that under "Earn while you learn" scheme for students, a piece of land is allotted to them where they could grow a crop during the final year of their study and thereby earn profit.

Similarly, he highlighted about a new programme, which is being started with an accent on experiential learning in areas such as mushroom growing, tissue culture, bee-keeping etc., for which PAU would pay for internship during the eighth semester. Dr Kang presented Hall with a memento, a set of publications and a docket of PAU brochures.

Heading: Three get 10-year jail term for possessing poppy - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has recently appointed teachers in primary as well as senior secondary schools. Many of these teachers were earlier working in good private schools and were drawing handsome salaries. But what fascinates them towards government schools is lesser work-load.

A lady teacher requesting anonymity said, "My school is far away. Although I will get Rs 2,000 less here as compared to the private institute but I am happy that there would be less burden."

Expressing similar views, another teacher said, "After a long wait, I have landed a relaxed job. My station is 35 km away from the city, but I will manage that. I hope I will get 28 to 30 periods to teach and that too will not be very exhaustive."

Meanwhile, some teachers who otherwise welcomed their recent appointment, accused Sudesh Bajaj, district education officer (secondary), Ludhiana, of favouritism while allotting the stations. A group of teachers said,"The people who are well connected were issued near-by stations while others were issued far way stations."

Denying all these allegations, Sudesh Bajaj, DEO (Secondary), said, "I did not favour anyone while allotting stations. The orders have been issued as per the instructions of Harcharan Kaur Brar, Director, Public Instructions (Secondary). Yesterday, some teachers faced problem in joining as school headmasters/principals were not aware about the posts created in their schools. Today, we told the school heads and helped these teachers in joining new stations."

Heading: Man held with smack, kin protest - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Judge-cum-Additional Session Judge (ASJ), Ludhiana, M.S. Virdi has sentenced three persons to undergo 10 years imprisonment for possessing poppy husk.

These persons are Baljit Singh alias Pappu of Mandar Kalan village in Moga district, Surjit Singh alias Sita of Jalandhar and Kuljit Singh of Parjian Kalan village in Jalandhar. The judge also ordered the accused to pay Rs 1 lakh each as fine. In default of payment, they will have to further undergo imprisonment for six months.

Delivering the verdict, the judge held that prosecution had successfully proved with convincing evidence that poppy husk had indeed been recovered from the accused even as he turned down the plea of leniency raised by the accused.

An FIR was lodged against the accused on January 2, 2003 under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985. On January 2, 2003, when sub-inspector of police Bikramjit Singh and ASI Balwinder Singh along with other police officials were on petrol duty and checking of suspected persons present at Jalandhar Bye Pass Chowk and about 7.30 pm Sucha Singh met them there, then the informant informed to the police party that the accused Baljit Singh alias Pappu of Mandar Kalan in Moga, Surjit Singh Alias Sita of Jalandhar and Kuljit Singh of Parjian Kalan village in Jalandhar, who are dealing in selling the poppy husk in the area of the city, Jagroan and Nakodar etc and they bring the poppy husk from Himachal Pradesh.

After receiving the information, the police party reached the Bahadur ke Road, and after conducting the raid, the truck of the accused was rounded up and police party searched the truck of the accused and poppy husk were recovered. In defence, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication but he failed to prove it.

Heading: Dengue claims life - Indian Express
Content:
Relatives of a man arrested by the police for allegedly possesing smack, blocked traffic on Ludhiana-Chandigarh highway in front of the DSP office at Samrala on Thursday. More than 50 persons, including women, blocked the road for more than half-an-hour alleging that Samrala police had slapped a false case.

The police had arrested the accused, Sudesh Kumar, a tea shop owner, at Samrala and recovered 100 gm of smack from him on Wednesday. The wife of Sudesh Kumar, Geeta Rani alleged that police had made a false case against Sudesh Kumar, and she along with her relatives had met Khanna SSP Arunpal Singh, who marked an inquiry to Samrala DSP Ravinder Loomba. Meanwhile, the court remanded Sudesh Kumar in police custody for two days.

Geeta Rani alleged that the smack belonged to a youth, Bablu but the police ha arrested her husband. When contacted, Samrala DSP Ravinder Loomba said, "As per NDPS Act, the person, who is in possession of the drug is accused and in this case smack was recovered from Sudesh Kumar."

Loomba said, "Sudesh Kumar told police that the smack was placed in his shop three days ago by Bablu. But Sudesh Kumar failed to inform police despite that fact he had knowledge of smack." "An inquiry will be conducted and allegations maded by the relatives of Sudesh Kumar will be verified," said Loomba, adding, "I was away at Machhiwara when the protesters blocked traffic and I mmediately rushed to the spot and cleared the blockade."

Heading: Dhussi dam repair: delay in payments irks contractors - Indian Express
Content:
The dengue count in the district today climbed up to 1,775 confirmed cases, health department report said today. Besides, as many as 400 patients have been put in the suspected dengue patients category.

Meanwhile a patient of dengue breathed his last at Mohan Dai Oswal Cancer Hospital, confirmed the hospital authorities. Manjit Singh, 58, died of dengue on Sunday, said the hospital authorities.

More than 20 patients of dengue were also reported at different hospitals across the city today. While CMC&H reported 11 fresh cases, MD Oswal Cancer Hospital reported 10 patients while SPS Apollo Hospitals recorded two.

Heading: In post-Diwali smog, city gasps for breath - Indian Express
Content:
Though the threat of flood which loomed large over the state is long over, the district administration has failed to release the payments — amounting to Rs 96 lakh — to the contractors who had worked at various sites to strengthen the banks of Dhussi dam.

Sources revealed that now the patwaris had been told to assess the actual work done at various sites because the deputy commissioner wanted to satisfy himself about authenticity of the payment bills submitted by the contractors for clearance.

The work was done more than two months ago at various vulnerable points of the banks of Dhussi dam using sand bags, wires etc. The contractors who had done work at various sites are reportedly making endless rounds of the Irrigation Department for payments, while official machinery is taking too long for verifying the claims.

Meanwhile, it needs to be mentioned that work was done at sites Kherabet, Kasabad, Mattewara, Maneawal besides a few other sites. Sources said most of the contractors had started work on verbal instructions keeping in view the flood threat, but now the administration was dragging its feat on the issue of making payments.

The authorities, it may be mentioned, had admitted that works at these sites had not been done for more than 10 years and following floods in Moga and Jalandhar, repair work had been started at some vulnerable spots in Ludhiana area as well.

Drainage executive engineer S.S Brar said, "We have already sent the bills to the DC and are hopeful that the same will be cleared soon because the contractors are asking for payments from us repeatedly."

Heading: Flouting Kang order on rally, PAU non-teaching union to hold another - Indian Express
Content:
As a thick blanket of smog engulfed the city for the second consecutive day after Diwali, experts claimed it was the result of smoke from firecrackers, vehicular pollution, dust particles and water vapours suspended low in the air.

Doctors across the city advised patients suffering from chest infections to stay indoors even as people queued up outside hospitals and clinics complaining of irritation in the eyes and throat due to the smoky conditions.

On Thursday as well, a thick cloak of smog hanged over the city since morning, leading to low visibility conditions in turn. Weather experts said the Diwali celebrations were largely to be blamed for the situation.

"Dust particles and vehicular pollution, which have combined with water vapours present in the air, have resulted in this smog. Though weather has been recorded normal, the minimum temperature is a bit high, adding to the problem," said Dr KK Gill, assistant agro-meteorologist at Punjab Agriculture University.

Dr Gill added that apart from Diwali crackers, late harvesting of paddy and in turn late burning of stubble have also added to the present problem. Notably, about 27 cases of fire incidents were reported during the Diwali celebrations in the city.

Doctors have meanwhile advised patients suffering from chest infection or asthma to stay indoors to avoid complications.

"There is a sudden spurt in the number of patients suffering from various problems. Post Diwali, the smoke due to fire crackers hangs in the air along with vehicular pollutants and dust particles. For the last three days, a large number of patients have come complaining about irritation in the throat, eyes and breathing problems," said Dr J Whig, professor and vice-principal, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital.

"Patients who are already suffering from chest infections should keep taking their medication regularly. And in case of any complications in breathing, they should immediately consult the doctor," advised Dr Sanjay Saluja, MD Medicine and senior consultant at Guru Teg Bahadur Charitable Hospital.

Heading: Chandigarh-Ludhiana rail link soon, says official - Indian Express
Content:
Trouble seems to be brewing on the Punjab Agricultural University campus. Going by the claims of the PAU non-teaching employees union, it's tough times ahead for Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang.

The hitch is the result of an order that is not going down well with the 1,400-member strong PAU non-teaching employees union.

Displeased with the frequent protests that the campus had witnessed in the last few weeks, Dr Kang had asked a few head of departments to refrain employees working under them from such protests in future.

In a reply to PAU V-Cs direction against those non-teaching employees who participated in a rally on September 24, the employees have decided to hold another rally on November 5.

Lakhwinder Singh Sandhu, vice-president of the union, said: "Till now, we have been cooperating with the V-C but by issuing such an order, he has tried to take away our fundamental right to oppose. We will not let this happen. Either the V-C takes back the order or faces ire," he said.

Harbans Singh Mundi, president of the union, said: "We held a meeting of all groups of non-teaching employees today and the decision was unanimous. Moreover, the V-C had promised to convert the post of Secretary to V-C from teaching to non-teaching within fifteen days. It has been over a month now."

Mundi added: "We met the V-C once on the issue and he asked us to send a panel. We told him that the panel of names is with the registrar but no action has been taken on this issue till time."

"The V-C is trying to gag us," said D P Maur, another senior leader of the union.

In the letter, employees who had been instrumental in arranging a rally on September 24 had been warned against disturbing peace at the campus.

Heading: Migrant youth found murdered - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh-Ludhiana rail link will soon see the light of the day as the land acquisition process is over. This was stated by VK Roy, Chief Operations Manager of Northern Railways, on a visit to the Ludhiana railway station. The rail link has been completed till Morinda so far.

Roy said 12 extra trains have been running from the northern side to meet the heavy rush of passengers in wake of the festive season.

"We ran nine extra trains on Wednesday and today we are running 12 extra trains to meet the passenger rush ahead of chhath puja," said Roy.

Speaking about the proposed high speed rail network, he said the Delhi-Chandigarh high speed rail link is in its conceptual stage and is being worked out for expenses that it will entail.

He added that the road network at the Dhandari railway station is being developed for the convenience of the passengers. Roy said a high-level platform would also be developed at Dhandari station in addition to providing better facilities to the passengers.

Added security
In the wake of blasts in Assam, the Railway Protection Force stepped up the security at the station today. The RPF held a meeting with the officials of the district to discuss the security measures at the station.

Heading: Shining Armour - Indian Express
Content:
An unidentified youth was found stabbed to death at Tibba Road under Basti Jodhewal police station on Thursday morning.

Sources said passersby spotted a body near BK Estate and immediately informed the police. The deceased appears to be a migrant and was in his early 20s, a police officer said. Sources added that the deceased had been stabbed with some sharp-edged weapon and was murdered somewhere else before the killers disposed of his body here.

The Basti Jodhewal police started investigating the matter after registering a case against unidentified persons. The body was sent to the Civil Hospital for postmortem. Sources, however, said that the postmortem would be conducted after 72 hours, within which the police would try to establish the identity of the victim.

No breakthrough had been made in the case till the filing of this report.

Heading: Two in One - Indian Express
Content:
An animation firm that challenges the meltdown

Frameboxx Animation confidently claims thatthe animation industry will be one of the few sectorsthat will remain untouched by the economic recession.

And there may be truth in that. South Asia has seen asteady growth in animation professionals over the last fewyears. And India is at the heart of it. The overwhelmingnumber of films and television series that flood our TVchannels signals a trend that promises new opportunities.

Roadside Romeo has been hailed as a triumph in fusingthe best of western animation technology with the rightamount of Bollywood punch. Hindu-mythology-exploringshows on Cartoon Network and Pogo compare withthe highest standards of animation in the global mainstream.A recent NASSCOM report states that the animationindustry is expected to grow at a rate of 24 per cent toaround US $869 million by the year 2010.

Though there is a great demand for animation professionalsin the market, studying the technique is a luxuryfew can afford.

But Frameboxx Animation, a relatively new but alreadyrespected animation firm hopes to spearhead the growthof animation professionals in the country with a uniqueset of scholarship.

They're providing educational assistance programmes ranging from Rs 10,000 to Rs 2 lakh to those who qualifythrough a test they organise throughout Maharashtra. Backed by Former CMD Adlabs, Manmohan Shetty,the scholarship schemes are initiated by Naveen Guptaand Rajesh Turakhia who set up the Frameboxx brand.

"We're sure that Animation as an Industry will notface the brunt of the economic meltdown. We are thusencouraging students with an inclination in Animation,to choose this as a lucrative career option," Gupta, executivedirector and CEO, Frameboxx. Frameboxx will launch its programme on November 10 and would continueit till November 30. Students can appear at one oftheir 15 test centres. Students who clear the test will receivecertificates that state the percentage of scholarshipwon.

What is promised is a range of word-class facilities andlectures by experts in the field. The firm recently tied upwith Cambridge School of Art at the Anglia Ruskin University,UK for accrediting courses. Frameboxx has alsolaunched an online training website for computer graphics,animation and visual effects - Clickboxx.tv. Frameboxx's200 protégés have found their place in famousproduction houses like Big Animation, Paprikaas,Dreamworks, Rhythm & Hues, Crest Communications,Red Chillies, Dq Entertainment.

Heading: An American Route - Indian Express
Content:
Grammy-winning band Jethro Tull are set to tour India with Anoushka Shankar, fusing Celtic and Indian music

When Jethro Tull, which pioneered the use of flute in rock 'n' roll, beat Metallica to win the Grammy for the Best Metal Performance in 1989, it became one of the biggest Grammy upsets of all times. The band, which has evolved from being a progressive rock act to an experimental group with elements of jazz, classical and folk sounds, is on its way to India, collaborating with the sitarist Anoushka Shankar for the first time.

"We have never met and I have never worked with the band before," says Shankar, of the band and its founder member Ian Anderson. "But we know each other's music and have spent the last few months communicating and e-mailing ideas back and forth.

The 61-year-old Anderson, who called flute a heavy metal instrument, still leads Jethro Tull amid the changes in its line-up since the band's inception four decades ago. Shankar, who recently completed her American tour with father Pandit Ravi Shankar, says, "Jethro Tull have been to India several times and each time they came someone got in touch with me to ask if I could be involved in a series of duet concerts. But the timing was always off, and I'd be booked for other shows right when they were touring India. Now I am thrilled to be able to work with such a legendary band."

Anderson and Shankar will be performing five shows from November 27 onwards — in Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi, Bangalore and Hyderabad, followed by a trip to Dubai.

Although their focus is on the new material that is special to this tour, the set list includes a couple of pieces from Shankar's solo albums as well as pieces that blend sitar in more acoustic-oriented Jethro Tull songs. "From our first communication, Anderson was so aware and caring about the logistics of playing these different music styles together. And, I found the lack of the modern casual attitude of just jamming at the last minute and winging it so refreshing," smiles Shankar.

The Delhi show is on November 30 at Hamsadhwani Amphitheatre

Heading: Painting is on the Wall - Indian Express
Content:
Get a taste of the US of A — with steaks, hotdogs and pancakes served in humungous portions

Here's a question. Route 04 is a highway running from New York to New Hampshire. What on earth has that got to do with a diner in the narrow middle lane at Khan Market?

A) It is a fancy name and anything American goes at Khan Market these days. B) The owners got lost on Route 04 while trying to get to Vermont. C) The eatery, which is set up by the owners of Turquoise Cottage and Days of The Raj at Adhchini, wants to replicate the culinary map of America's Golden Highway which is actually Route 40, but the restaurateurs blissfully decided to play with history since their address is 4 Khan Market. Correct answer: C. Never trust restaurateurs for historical accuracy, but, thankfully, you can't argue with the food here.

The diner, spread across two storeys, moves away from the casual ambience of the All American Diner. Done up in a travel theme, it has mini versions of vintage and classic cars parked on the shelf that runs across the wall, and helicopters hung from the ceiling. While the first floor has a bar counter that will be operational in a month, the second floor opens into a terrace space and a live kitchen — best for breakfasts. The menu is a melting pot of the classic and the contemporary, and its Power Breakfast comes with a complimentary copy of a pink newspaper. News of the meltdown sure goes well with the steak.

Must-Try
Route 04 sticks to the notoriously humungous portions that characterise American food. The thumb rule here is to never order more than one dish, and pair it with a juice or a coffee. For instance, an order of Pancake Stax with Maple Syrup (Rs 225) will fetch you six large pancakes stacked together and served with a scoop of whipped cream and maple syrup. The dish accompanies a bowl of melted butter that is generously poured over the mount. We tried the blueberry pancakes that were loaded with berries and are a meal in itself. The Classic All American Hotdog (Rs175) is well-done. The sausage is deep fried, and is accompanied by mandatory portions of finger fries and coleslaw in a lettuce cup. The menu combines different cooking styles and even offers cottage-cheese quesadillas (Rs 195). Buffalo Chicken Wings (Rs 225), tossed with Tabasco sauce, probably ranks the highest in the heat metre here. Lip-numbing, they can be toned down only if you douse the stick in a blue-cheese dip that comes along. Pan-fried Ham Steak (Rs 350) resembles a nouvelle platter after all the binging. A narrow elongated plate brings in two portions of steak, with buttered toast and scrambled eggs on the side. The restaurant also offers some of its grills in skillets that truly bring alive the western café ambience. Tenderloin Chicken Fired Steak (Rs 325), a typical Bronx recipe, is served in the pan with portions of rice and fries.

The menu cleverly lists healthier options and some dishes are rolled out in small portions. For instance, you can swap a creamy shake for a fresh carrot and ginger juice blend (Rs 145) or a soy milk fruit smoothie (Rs 175), and the humungous burgers can be exchanged for Sliders (Rs 155) which offer smaller buns with less fillings, or a soup-and-salad combo. The diner also has an in-house bakery that begins work at 5 am. So, for breakfast you can munch on some fresh crusty bagels and flavoured croissants for Rs 45 a piece.

Give a Miss
Poutine (Rs 195) is a big no for calorie watchers. The very sight of the dish has the potential to pack you off on a guilt trip. Our order with chicken served a pyramid of fries, jalapenos and chunks of chicken, all topped with curd cheese and barbeque sauce. Mac n' cheese (Rs 250), a popular order with expats, is equally laden with cheese.

Meal for Two: Rs 1,000
Contact: 4352180
Location:First Floor, 4 Khan Market

Heading: Days to go for Chhath, parties all out to woo Bihari vote, cash in on MNS controversy - Indian Express
Content:
French graffiti artist C215 aka Christian Guémy has left his mark on the walls of Karol Bagh

Delhi walls have seldom been canvas for art. We do have cell-phone advertisements, pretty heroines on hoardings and political slogans, but hardly art on roadside walls. But if you drive down the bylanes of Karol Bagh these days, you'll see striking stencil work that will force you to take a second look.

A few metres from the Clarks's International Hotel, in an open space littered with refuse, a black-and-white goat shares wall space with a turbaned man. On the wall of a run-down building nearby, vivid red scooters look down on an overflowing drain. Each picture is detailed and the stenciling is so intricate that it stands out in its dismal surroundings.

These are the works of French graffiti artist C215 aka Christian Guémy, who is travelling the streets of the world, leaving a mark of his journey in unlikely places — on buildings, broken boundary walls and a rusty autorickshaw. He passed by Delhi on October 7-16, and the walls of Karol Bagh bear witness to that.

"Street art is like surfing. You have to travel to experience new situations, new contexts and new people. Karol Bagh is the very heart of Delhi. It was the right place for me to feel the real, urban atmosphere of India," says Guémy, before rattling off his previous trips to the US, Brazil, Israel, Morocco, Poland, France, England, Spain, Italy and the Netherlands. "I love to place my characters in abandoned buildings. They inhabit those places like ghosts, they underline the life that once was there," he says. His images are solitary faces and figures, captivating in their loneliness. Chand Prakash, who faces a Guémy work from his shop Prakash Electricals, says, "Everyday I look at the face of the woman on the opposite wall and wonder why it moves me so much. I wonder about that firang artist. Cars slow down and people take pictures with their camcorders and cell phones."

Graffiti artists often carry their instinct for subversion, rebellion and anonymity to their names and strange signatures are scrawled beneath their art. TAKI 183 was one of the earliest graffiti artists that took New York by storm, in the early 1970s, spawning others like Barbara 62 and Cay 161. Beneath the Karol Bagh artwork is the signature C215. "I chose this name because it sounds like a code or a jail number. Life, sometimes, is like a prison. Also, it implies that we are nothing more than anonymous numbers in a city," says the 35-year-old Guémy, who has also spent time behind the bars "in another century when I was 20".

Guémy, who has been drawing since childhood, has a master's degree in art history from the Sorbonne. "It was only three years ago that I turned to stencil art in order to place nice pictures on the streets quickly and without authorisation," he says. Armed with stencils and aerosol cans, he was often the centre of public attention at Karol Bagh. "The crowd was sometimes a problem, especially with so many excited kids," he says. Nevertheless, they were his focus in Delhi, painting portraits, animals and scooters that he knew they would enjoy. "The onlookers loved it and gave me a good feedback which made my day," he says. He will be back in India soon, this time probably in Puducherry "since I am French". Walls, be ready.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Aakriti Alreja - Indian Express
Content:
The Capital's nearly 30 lakh migrants from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar feel they have been given short shrift by successive governments

With the Assembly elections round the corner and the Chhath Puja to be celebrated on November 4, political parties have kicked off campaigns to woo the 25-30 lakh strong votebank of migrants in the Capital.

The Bharatiya Janata Party, Samajwadi Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party have bared fangs against the Congress government in Delhi, echoing issues similar to Maharashtra. They have started accusing the Congress of neglecting voters from Poorvanchal (eastern UP) and Bihar living in Delhi.

Bharatiya Janata Party
While the BJP is caught between its allies in Maharashtra, the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena and the Shiv Sena, the Delhi BJP has decided to rake up the issue of "neglect of the migrant voters" in Delhi and attacked Sheila Diskhit. "Chhath puja is going to be observed on November 4 and the Delhi Government has made no preparations for the festival till now," he said.

BJP leader Harshvardhan also recalled comments made by Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on migrants from Poorvanchal and Bihar in Delhi.

"Dikshit had said some time ago that the people of UP and Bihar are a burden on Delhi.

She had spoken about basic amenities in Delhi becoming scarce and hinted at stopping people from Poorvanchal coming to Delhi," Harshvardhan said.

Voters from UP and Bihar are expected to prove decisive in the final results in at least 10 constituencies in Delhi including Matiala, Uttam Nagar, Dwarka, Sangam Vihar, Vikas Puri, Kirari, Badarpur, Rajender Nagar, Wazirpur.

Samajwadi Party
The party's state unit held a rally in the Karawal Nagar Assembly seat and burnt effigies of Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Dershmukh and his deputy R R Patil. Terming the attacks on Poorvanchalis and Biharis in Mumbai an example of "state-run terrorism", Gauri Shankar Sharma, spokesperson of the party, said, "It is the Congress government in Maharashtra and the Congress government in Delhi that have inflicted pain on migrants from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

Bahujan Samaj Party
With party chief Mayawati expected to arrive in the Capital to address rallies in November, leaders of the state unit of the party say the neglect of migrant voters will feature prominently in her speeches. "We have already made it an important issue for the elections and Behenji will also underline on problem in her rallies," Brahm Singh Bidhuri, head of the state unit of the party, said.

Newsline talks to the man in the street:
"The MNS is trying to cull out a nation within a nation. It is like creating another Pakistan. All for petty politics. The Congress has been sleeping over the issue and has taken no decisive action. My family and I have been in Delhi for 25 years and feel if the country is left in the hands of the Congress, we will have no future."
— Gopesh Mishra from Darbhanga, Bihar; South Ganesh Nagar, East Delhi.

"Both the BJP and the Congress try to get votes by bribing the labour population and giving them ration cards at the time of elections. The Congress is to blame for whatever is happening to innocent Biharis in Mumbai and the BJP has always supported the Thackeray family.
— Ram Shakal Gupta from Sitamarhi, Bihar; daily wage labourer and a resident of Bihari Colony, Shahdara.

"My family and I have always voted for the Congress. What is happening in Mumbai is wrong but the Congress cannot be blamed for all of it. Moreover, it has good people in its ranks."
— Bhrigunath, Azamgarh, UP; daily wage labourer and resident of Bihari Colony, Shahdara

"The Congress seems to have failed in every quarter. The economic condition of our country has worsened. What is happening in Maharashtra is being taken lightly. The government needs to deal with it strongly."
— Shailesh Singh, Kishanganj, Bihar; Resident of Gandhi Vihar

Heading: BJP likely to pit Jolly against CM - Indian Express
Content:
It is going to be the first chance to vote in the Assembly elections for Aakriti Alreja, 20. She is excited about the elections and she wants to caste vote. "I am only worried about my voter I-card. I hope to get it on time," said Aakriti a voter from the Lajpat Nagar constituency.

Aakriti a final year student says she reads newspapers regularly these days. "With elections round the corner, I think I should be clear about various political parties and their plans before I cast my vote," she says. "I've even started taking interest in political discussions that take place at home."

On roads
"Bad roads in Lajpat Nagar put me off. The roads in our area are repaired only during elections, otherwise nobody bothers. For the first time in five years, I have seen roads being made in our colony," she says.

On the safety of girls
"We live in a city that is not at all safe for women. Every day we hear reports of crime against women. I have friends in Pune and Bangalore and when they talk about their city, I feel ashamed. We are way behind when compared to them," she says.

On the security of Metro commuters
"The government has een taking credit for Delhi Metro. But the security check inside the metro trains is poor. They don't even check bags properly. Just removing dustbins from the stations is not going to help. It is very easy to carry a bomb inside Metro. I think the government needs to pull up its socks and ensure safety of commuters to avoid any mishap."
— As told to Rohinee Singh

Heading: Frame laws that heal scars of rape, judge tells govt - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party's candidate list will be out on Friday and it looks as if MLA from Saket Vijay Jolly is emerging as the frontrunner to take on Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on November 29.

Vijay Jolly till recently had kept himself aloof from the head-hunting process, but has now taken up the "challenge" to fight Dikshit, sources said. He had instead been lobbying hard for a ticket from Malviya Nagar.

The party has struggled in recent weeks to find suitable candidates against Congress heavyweights, and not many are eager to face Dikshit at all. However, state president Dr Harsh Vardhan insisted that 11 partymen had thrown in their hats for the chief minister's New Delhi constituency. "Several other names are being looked at," Dr Harsh Vardhan said.

The BJP had initially considered Vani Tripathi, a member of the BJP's national women's wing and also a familiar face in television serials. She developed cold feet, sources said, and has set her heart on the Vikaspuri constituency. The only other candidate considered for the seat was Meera Shastri, who heads the state women's wing. The BJP has finalised the name of sitting MLA Moti Lal Sodhi against Transport Minister Haroon Yusuf, who has triumphed thrice from Ballimaran. Sodhi had fought from Ram Nagar last elections, which no longer exists after delimitation. He had won narrowly.

The BJP has said there are nearly 20 candidates for Finance Minister Dr A K Walia, but none weighty enough to topple the balance in his constituency Laxmi Nagar. Murari Singh Pawar, former MLA and head of Delhi BJP's Uttaranchal division, is trying for a ticket. There are only new faces being considered for Urban Development Minister Rajkumar Chauhan, sources said. The party says nearly 20 names are doing the rounds for this Mangolpuri seat. It is learnt party office-bearer Yogesh Attre has almost got the nod here.

In Gandhi Nagar, 27 partymen wanted a face-off with Education Minister Arvinder Singh Lovely, including Yuva Morcha leader Jeetu and Mahila Morcha leader Kalpana Jain. BJP sources said their candidates were not strong enough to take on Lovely who won last with a huge margin. The party might hand over the seat to the Akali Dal.

The party has drawn a blank against Industries Minister Mangat Ram Singhal too but two probable contenders are Roshan Bansal and Jai Prakash Yadav.

The Congress has not made up its mind in Malviya Nagar. But the BJP has frittered away this edge because local leaders don't see eye to eye in this constituency. While state Health Minister Yoganand Shastri wants a ticket from the Congress, a section of the BJP want heavyweight Ram Bhaj to fight him, while another faction wants chartered accountant Sunil Vashist.

Other names that might figure on the list include former judge Rajesh Kashyap, who is trying to get a ticket from Seemapuri, and former additional district magistrate S H Jafri, who is eyeing Mustafabad.

Delhi decides Cong not ready yet
The Congress is yet to come out with the list, but it is likely that heavyweight ministers will stay put in their old constituencies. After 53 names were leaked recently, the party is playing safe and keeping even speculation under wraps. Sources said the final list was with party president Sonia Gandhi. "It should be out in a day or two when the All India Congress Committee gives the final nod," Delhi Congress president J P Agarwal said.

Heading: IGNOU to reach rural areas through mobile phones - Indian Express
Content:
Hearing the case of a four-year-old's rape recently, a city court echoed the simmering grouse of the judiciary that penal provisions to punish the perpetrators of this deeply violating crime are inadequate, particularly when it is committed on a child.

The girl had been raped last November by her 37-year-old neighbour Pradeep Kumar, against whom a case was registered at the Aman Vihar police station. The girl's mother has said her daughter had been in a state of shock and pain ever since the incident.

Additional Sessions Judge S K Aggarwal urged the legislature to "wake up" and frame stronger laws to deal with the rape of minors. He said: "The legislature should make the law more stringent than Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code in case a girl of such an age is made to gratify the devil's lust of a person aged around 37 years."

The accused's counsel at that time was arguing that the charge be changed from rape to an "attempt to outrage modesty". However, the victim's lawyers would hear none of that and said the man should be tried under the strictest of penal provisions. They also bared before the judge the trauma this girl had gone through, and how she had writhed in pain during the medical examination.

Judge Aggarwal — visibly upset — went through the case records and observed that justice could not close its eyes on the ordeal a minor goes through in cases of sexual assault. He said the court was "stunned" that a man could stoop so low merely for sexual gratification. He also threw out the defence's plea and framed charges of rape against Kumar.

In recent times, several trial court judges have advocated stricter punishment for rapists, and also the rehabilitation of victims. At present, the section concerned, 376, can get the rapist a maximum of life imprisonment and monetary penalty.

Judges say it is imperative for the law to also heal victims, particularly minors.

Want legislation
"Judges are absolutely right when they urge law-making bodies to rehabilitate rape victims. Any such step by the legislature is always welcome. It will correct the wrong committed against society at large."
R K Naseem, criminal lawyer

Need psychiatrists
"Rehabilitation is an issue that needs to be addressed very urgently. There is no state machinery to help victims. No psychiatrists are available to talk to the girls. The legislature should show its will and draft relevant laws. The courts are doing their best by referring the matter to the state."
Viraj Dattar, senior advocate

Give more power to judges
"Not only should the government frame comprehensive laws on rehabilitation, more power should also be given to trial court judges so that they can direct relevant agencies to help victims. At present, judges have no teeth and can only refer the matter to the state. But they are the ones who witness the victim's trauma during court hearings."
Ajay Digpaul, advocate

376 not enough
"The legislature should make the law more stringent than Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code in case a girl of such an age is made to gratify the devil's lust of a person aged around 37 years"
S K Aggarwal, judge

Recent verdicts that upheld care to minor victims
This February, Additional Sessions Judge A K Mendiratta acquitted a man accused of raping his minor daughter since there wasn't much evidence supporting the case. The girl's mother and sister had turned hostile under pressure. The judge showed his frustration and also said the court could not imagine how the victim would stay with her father under the same roof.

The judge had said: "Some steps need to be explored to ensure that the dignity and honour of the victim — a minor child — is protected, at least till the age she reaches a rational understanding, and that she is not exploited under the same roof."

He then directed the police to work with a non-governmental organisation in monitoring the girl's safety.

* In another verdict, Additional Sessions Judge D K Sharma put a handicapped man away for life, holding him guilty of raping his minor stepdaughter. The judge had said the convict's physical condition did not lessen the heinousness of the crime.

He had sent a copy of the order to the state home secretary asking him to ensure the victim was emotionally rehabilitated.

Heading: Air Deccan to pay up for cancelling flight without notice - Indian Express
Content:
In an initiative to take education to rural areas, the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU), in association with the Communication and Manufacturing Association of India (CMAI), has decided to deliver educational content to remote areas of the country through mobile phones.

Talking to mediapersons at the India International Centre, IGNOU Vice-Chancellor Professor V N Rajasekharan Pillai said: "We want to tap the technology of the ever-improving mobile phones as a medium to provide educational content."

This will be done through the transmission of texts and audio-video content to mobile phones of students who register themselves for the courses. When asked if people in rural areas will be able to afford a multi-media mobile phone for their educational needs, Pillai said: "We should not underestimate their capabilities."

N K Goyal, president of CMAI, said one way of making phones cheaper was by customising them with advertisements so that the advertiser paid a large chunk of the cost. "At present, the features in the mobile sets are not user-friendly but after introduction of improved technology-based sets, it would be more effective, both in terms of quality and cost to deliver and receive study materials," he added.

Keeping this in view, IGNOU and CMAI will jointly convene a round-table conference on November 4. The conference aims to address the issue of rural connectivity for the capacity building of students and learners and the identification of other cost-effective communication technologies for delivery of technology best suited for distance education.

Heading: Karim’s vs Rahim’s: dispute mars the taste in Vasant Kunj outlet - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has pulled up Air Deccan and slapped on it a penalty of Rs 1 lakh for abruptly cancelling a flight and refusing to make any alternate arrangement for passengers.

In a recent order, the commission rejected the airline's claim that its liability to provide alternate arrangements, refreshments and compensation, was restricted by its contract with the consumers. "Any such term of a contract between the service providers and the consumer, which runs against the interest of the consumer and to his detriment, appears to be unconscionable, is void and not enforceable," the commission observed.

"Can a term empowering the service providers like the airlines to cancel or re-schedule the flights without prior notice to the passenger be called a valid term? By no stretch of imagination, a passenger can be left stranded high and dry at the airport after reaching there without being informed of the cancellation/delay/re-scheduling of the flight," said Rumnita Mittal, presiding member of the commission, holding the airline guilty of "deficiency in service".

In January 2007, Anil Bhandoola, a resident of Lodhi Colony, had booked four tickets from Pune to Delhi with Air Deccan, for himself, his wife and two children. The flight was to take off from Pune at 2.30 pm. When the family reached the airport two hours before the scheduled departure time, they were informed that the flight had been cancelled.

Bhandoola said his efforts to contact the airline manager failed, while the staff members expressed their inability to provide alternate arrangements or refreshments, leaving the family stranded at the airport.

Bhandoola later approached a district consumer forum, which ordered Air Deccan to pay a compensation of Rs 60,000. The airline challenged the order in the State Commission.

The airline argued that the flight had been cancelled owing to bad weather conditions and that the passengers had been informed about the cancellation through SMS. It said it was not liable to provide alternate transport accommodation as it ran on a very low profit margin, and hence it mentioned clearly in its contract that no alternate arrangements would be made or rescheduling of flights done in case of cancellation.

The commission, however, dismissed the defence. "The harassment and inconvenience suffered by the complainant in such a situation can be well imagined when neither an alternative flight is provided nor are the queries for other arrangements for meals, transport or overnight accommodation answered or provided. Even though the flight was cancelled on account of bad weather at Delhi, the absence of any alternate arrangements amounts to gross deficiency in service, for which the service provider is bound to pay due compensation," the commission observed in the order, directing the airline to pay Rs 1 lakh.

Heading: Caste engineering formula again on Behenji’s mind - Indian Express
Content:
For almost six months, the residents of Vasant Kunj did not have to travel all the way to Old Delhi to tease their taste buds with the mouthwatering seekh kebabs, mutton burra, tandoori raan and other delicacies offered at the iconic Karim Hotel. The popular restaurant had a branch in Vasant Kunj after all.

While the joint still exists, it no longer carries the brand name of Karim's. Reason: a dispute between the partners. The name has been tweaked a little and it's called Rahim's now. Though the food remains the same, the menu card and the takeaway pamphlet retain the design of the brand Karim logo — the crowning border of a dome structure and intricate floral carving. (See pamphlet)

The fight dates back this July. Karimuddin Sani, one of the cousins from the legendary Karim family, set up the outlet in February in partnership with Tahir Ismail. The honeymoon lasted just four months and a dispute ended the partnership in July.

"Our agreement was cancelled on July 23, but the current owners are still cashing in on our brand name. We issued them a legal notice in July to stop using our family name," says Sani, who now works at the Old Delhi outlet.

"They have cleverly tweaked the name and are calling it Rahim's," says Sani. "From a distance, anybody will read it Karim's and get misled," he adds.

His former partner, however, has a different take on the issue. "We retained the name Karim's till last month since the accounts were not settled and a lot of arrears were due. I have got new menu cards and pamphlets printed and will soon roll them out after my last due sum comes in," says Ismail, who claims to be a distant relative of Sani.

"Like in case of Karim's other partnership ventures, where the third party bears all the costs, I set up the place at Vasant Kunj and bore the rent and expense for interiors. I was given 12 per cent of the sales," says Ismail. He fears a 5 per cent dip now in his clientele that comes looking for Karim's food. In early August, Sani says, he had issued public notices in newspapers, stating that the Vasant Kunj restaurant was not associated with the legendary Karim's.

This is not the first time that a clone of the iconic brand name has surfaced. "We keep hearing that there are Karim outlets in Mumbai and Bangalore. Those eateries are not associated with us at all," says Sani.

The legendary Karim Hotel is run by four brothers, while their sons run Dastarkhwan-e Karim in Nizamuddin. The other branches in Noida, Gurgaon, Preet Vihar and Malviya Nagar are run by their cousins, says Zaeemuddin Ahmed, director of Karim Hotel Pvt Limited. "When you collaborate as partners, disputes are bound to surface. At the end of the day, our patrons can tell the original from a copy. Thanks to the Metro, our outlet opposite Jama Masjid is easy to access," says Ahmed.

The history
In 1911, Haji Karimuddin set up a dhaba, selling aloo gosht and daal with rumali roti. In 1913, he established the Karim Hotel in Gali Kababian opposite Jama Masjid. Now run by the fourth generation, the hotel stands firmly at the same spot, while four more outlets try to mirror their legendary food and ambience. "The Old Delhi eatery has nothing to do with the other Karim outlets. We have lent our name to cousins, who have set up outlets with different partners," says Zaeemuddin Ahmed, director, Karim Hotel Pvt Ltd.

Heading: Bid to utilise LADS funds violation of model code: chief electoral officer - Indian Express
Content:
Serving society, eye on votes
While bijli, sadak, pani and other basic amenities are the "main issues" for the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), aiming to clinch "at least 15" seats in the upcoming Delhi assembly elections, one of the candidates has decided to provide the basic amenities at his own expense. Kanwar Singh Tanwar, general secretary of the party's Delhi unit and contestant from Chhattarpur Assembly seat, has started drinking water supply in water-starved areas, generator facility for the areas where there are incessant power cuts, and has been investing in other infrastructure needs too. The latest addition to his fleet of vehicles involved in "samaj sewa" is a mobile mini-hospital. Tanwar claims people have benefited from the van, which has been imported from England, and has been treating patients in the rural areas of his constituency. On the question of election commission's guidelines, however, he says he hardly knows what they are!

The Vijay Goel problem
It seems senior BJP leader and former union minister for state Vijay Goel is miffed these days. The three-time MP who has fought from Chandni Chowk and Sadar Bazar it seems is not getting his way in candidate selection in both the constituencies. In protest it seems Goel is not attending most of the meetings to discuss the candidate's list and even campaigning. Insiders claim Goel who had been vying for the chief ministerial candidature himself can even be detrimental for BJP's vote bank among traders.

Heading: CHATTER BOX - Indian Express
Content:
A few youngsters bring together some bold short films

How does the world look from a different angle? The answer is yours for the viewing at Breaking Stereotypes, a two-day film festival by the YP Foundation, an organisation by and for the youth. The festival, in its second year, brings together 15 bold and thought-provoking films.

There is the curiously titled No Bed-Space for Long Lines. And it gets curiouser, given that first-time filmmaker Sreedeep didn't even use a video camera. "It is a collection of several hundred still images, both black-and-white and colour, that were juxtaposed to narrate a story," says the 25-year-old research student from JNU, who made the film during an academic break. If Sreedeep experimented with the form of filmmaking, another Delhiite turned his camera lovingly at the villains of modern India — religious terrorists. Shiladitya Moulik, who honed his talent at the London Film Academy last year, uses his film 30 Seconds to bring a Hindu and a Muslim terrorist together as friends "who want to have all the fun of their lives before resuming their duties as soldiers of god". In 15 minutes, Moulik packs in a touching narrative of young men who are no longer in control of their actions.

Irengbam Debashish Singh, on the other hand, takes a satirical look at the labels that wind themselves around the people of the Northeast in My "Funky" Date, while Fable by Nitin Das zeroes in on a boy living near the mountains of Tibet who has found the solution to global warming.

The festival is part of the Butterfly Project, an arm of the YP Foundation, which gives a forum for creative expression. "There is minimal editing and nobody has to conform to any ideology or agenda," says Diksha Singh, project manager of the foundation.

Breaking Stereotypes will be held at India Habitat Centre on November 1 and 2. Time: 7 pm. Contact: 41551222

Heading: Denied food after 11 pm, man roughs up waiter - Indian Express
Content:
With the Assembly elections less than a month away and the Model Code of Conduct on legislators in place since the announcement of the Assembly elections two weeks back, the Chief Electoral Office of Delhi has taken strong exception to the government's move of constituting a special team to completely utilise funds of the outgoing MLAs in the Capital and has asked for an explanation from the department.

As reported by Newsline on Thurday, the Urban Development department of the Delhi government has recently formed a special team to utilise the remaining 'Local Area Development Scheme' or LADS funds just before the Assembly elections. As reported earlier, barely 50 per cent of the LADS fund had been used until September this year. The commitee has been reportedly formed at the behest of Congress MLA and minister for Urban Development department, Raj Kumar Chauhan.

Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Satbir Silas Bedi said the move is a violation of the Model Code of Conduct which has been in place since the announcement of the elections on October 14.

Once an election is formally announced, ministers and other authorities cannot sanction grants or funds out of dicretionary funds like LADs or make any promises of construction of roads, provision of drinking water facilities or even make ad-hoc appointments in the government or public undertakings, as in this case.

"We have asked the Delhi government to submit a report on the matter and if the matter is found objectionable, we will then take necessary action," Bedi said.

The Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines meant to govern the conduct of political parties and candidates in the run-up to the elections.

While the intention is to provide a level playing field to all candidates and political parties, the main aim is to ensure the ruling party at the Centre or the state does not misuse its powers. Election candidates are allowed to campaign by praising their leaders in mass meetings and releasing their manifestos only.

Heading: Questions on encounter and ‘witch-hunt’ at Jamia convocation - Indian Express
Content:
Police arrested a Pitampura resident on Wednesday night after he allegedly hit a waiter at a restaurant in Chanakyapuri.

According to the police, the man was asking the waiter to serve him dinner though the restaurant had closed for the day. He allegedly punched the waiter on his face and damaged the restaurant property.

The incident took place around 11.15 pm at Moti Mahal restaurant on Malcha Marg when Navneet Kumar, 28, came to the restaurant with his girlfriend and asked the waiters to serve them food.

When he was told that no food was served after 11 pm, he told the waiters that he was a regular customer and should be served food, said a police officer. As the waiters refused to oblige, he hit one of them.

The restaurant manager then called the police and Navneet was taken to the police station. On the complaint of the restaurant owner, he was booked but got a bail later.

"Navneet is a divorcee and unemployed too," said an officer, adding that his medical examination did not prove he was drunk.

Heading: NGO worker gets two years in jail for child trafficking - Indian Express
Content:
The annual convocation of Jamia Millia Islamia held on Thursday at the lawns of the Ansari auditorium in the university saw honorary degrees being awarded to actor Naseeruddin Shah, art scholar Dr Kapila Vatsyayana, social reformer and theologian Dr Asghar Ali Engineer, and actor and social activist Shabana Azmi.

Addressing students, the Vice-Chancellor of the university, Mushirul Hasan pointed out that his address at this year's convocation was more as a concerned citizen dealing with problematic issues that had been raised in the context of the recent Batla House encounter in proximity of the university.

Speaking on the effects of the stereotyping of the university following the recent incidents, he asked, "Already students are being denied jobs because Jamia is supposedly the breeding ground of terrorism. Cab drivers warn passengers not to enter the premises. Delivery vans and service providers baulk at entering our neighbourhood. Where will this madness end?" He also questioned the categorising the activities of a few with those of the entire university.

The issue of questioning stereotypes was also raised by U R Ananthamurthy, eminent Kannada writer and Padma Bhushan award winner, who presided over the convocation.

"How it is still difficult for a Muslim to get a house in a middle class locality in Bangalore? There is a need to bridge the gap between the 'secularists' and the 'traditional believers' while extricating Islam and Muslims from misrepresentation by the Western media."

Critiquing the nature of the recent encounters in the locality and the city, he said, "The illusion of safety that is created by capturing those suspected in the acts of terrorism seems only momentary, as it is soon broken by another terrorist act somewhere. Even if those under suspicion are found to be not guilty later, the damage is already done by revealing their identities before the verdict is out".

As many as 3213 degrees and 105 PhDs were awarded to students for the year 2006-07, which also included 130 toppers who were given gold medals.

Heading: Defanged cobra bites man, snake charmer arrested - Indian Express
Content:
While the legal fraternity continues to delve upon the admissibility of sting operation tapes as evidence in court, a city court has sentenced a person to two years in jail in a child trafficking case, based on a sting aired on a television news channel.

Chander Shekhar was arrested by the Delhi Police in September 2006, when a television journalist made a written complaint after conducting a sting operation, exposing the trafficking racket.

Shekhar, an employee at Prayas Kendra in the Nabi Karim area, had allegedly been selling off the children residing in the NGO.
