On September 23, 2006, Harish Sharma, a journalist, conducted a sting operation. He allegedly got in touch with Shekhar through two middlemen, Raja and Ravi, saying he required children to help him smuggle gold.

According to the complaint, Shekhar agreed to give him three children from the NGO for Rs 30,000. He brought them (names withheld) to Sharma at Connaught Place after the latter paid an advance of Rs 7,000.

Sharma later handed over the children to the Connaught Place police along with a copy of the CD and the script containing details of the entire episode that was aired on Star News the same day.

Shekhar's counsel argued that he should be let off as there was no evidence to suggest that the children were to be employed in "harmful" or "abusive" activities and since Shekhar had no previous criminal record.

Additional Sessions Judge S K Sarvaria, however, dismissed the arguments and convicted Shekhar under penal provisions pertaining to trafficking and criminal conspiracy.

The court held that the sting tapes, the credibility of which could not be impeached during the trial, could very well be relied upon to secure the conviction of the accused.

The judge also ordered that a separate chargesheet be filed against the two middlemen, Raja and Ravi, who were yet to be traced.

Heading: 52-yr-old commits suicide in Shahdara - Indian Express
Content:
A 25-year-old man was admitted to a hospital after being bitten by a cobra. Fortunately for the man, the snake, whose one fang had been knocked out, did not inject any poisonous venom, circumventing a fatal accident.

The snake was being illegally carried by a brightly garbed snake charmer, who was displaying it and asking for money in Shahdara.

Acting on the complaint, police have booked the charmer, Dhanpal Nath for violating three sections of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. At present, Nath is in judicial custody.

The partly defanged snake bit Naresh when he tried to handle it. "Though no venom seems to have been injected, there is a possibility of septic infection," said Sanjay Acharya of Wildlife SOS, who rescued the snake. Naresh is recovering at GTB Hospital.

"The snake charmer has violated sections 9, 42 and 49 regarding illegal trapping of the animal, and keeping it in possession without license or certificate. He did not have any licence for keeping the snake, and trapped it illegally. His conviction can be between three and seven years," said Wildlife Inspector S S Negi.

"Such activities are totally banned. Snake charmers like him usually come from different states to make money," he said.

"Displaying a cobra for money can amount to extortion, as people give money after a level of intimidation. Snake charming is banned by law. People who indulge in such exercises usually knock off the fangs of snakes like cobras, which die in a few days. In this case, the snake had been partly defanged," said Kartick Satyanarayan co-founder of Wildlife SOS, which runs Delhi's official wild animal rescue helpline.

The cobra is under observation and will be released in the natural habitat if it is fit for survival in the wild. Many snakes, including cobras, live in the city, which falls in their geographical belt. And cobras have turned up in the unlikeliest of places: including the Delhi Airport.

Heading: Delhi sees three murders in 24 hrs - Indian Express
Content:
A 52-year-old cloth merchant from Shahdara, Nandnagri allegedly committed suicide by consuming poison in a Ghaziabad lodge on Wednesday night.

Pramod Kumar Goyal was found dead in room 103 of Aditi Lodge today morning. The lodge is located in Bajeria behind the office of the superintendent of police.

The body was first seen by the waiter who had gone to give him the food bill. "When Goyal did not respond to calls, the waiter peeped through the window and saw him lying in the bathroom," said Vijay Bhushan, SP (city).

"We have informed his family members.... We have questioned them of the possible reasons of the suicide," the SP said. "According to Goyal's family members he was short-tempered and used to rebuke his sons for not being able to handle the cloth business. Whenever arguments over the issue took place, he would leave home and stay at his friend's house in Meerut. But this time, he decided to stay at a lodge in Ghaziabad," said Rajesh Chowdhary, chowki-in-charge, Kotwali.

Meanwhile, police have found a rat poison cake from Goyal's room.

Heading: Five held for Green Park robbery - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons, including a seven-year-old boy, were murdered in different parts of the capital in the last 24 hours.

The first incident took place at Nangloi in West Delhi late last night. Anju Rani, 22, was found murdered with her throat slit at her Bakkarwala village residence. The police have sent her body for autopsy. Anju was alone when the incident occurred. The house was not ransacked and there was no physical assault on her.

The police have registered a case of murder, but the reason is not known yet. Preliminary investigations reveal that there were differences between her and her in-laws. Anju married Sanjeev in 2004. Her father works as a driver in the External Affairs Ministry. No arrest have been made yet.

In the second incident, the body of a seven-year-old unidentified boy was found inside a burnt bedsheet in the bushes at Shahpur Dairy area in outer Delhi on Thursday morning. The boy had not received burn injuries, but may have died of suffocation as the body was found tied, officials said. DCP Atul Katiyar, Outer District said, "We are questioning several persons. The killers will be arrested soon".

In another incident in Outer Delhi, a 23-year-old man, who worked as a labourer-cum-chowkidar at the Delhi State Industrial Development Corporation area in Narela was killed by three persons when he saw them attempting theft in a factory.

The incident happened around 8.45 pm on Wednesday when Pradeep saw Ravi, Deepak and Praveen, trying to commit a theft. When he intervened, Ravi reportedly stabbed Pradeep with a sharp glass-cutter and fled. Pradeep was declared brought dead at Raja Harish Chander hospital. Narela police lodged a murder case. Pravin has been arrested. DCP Katiyar said the other two will be arrested soon. All three are residents of Tikri Khurd village in Narela.

Heading: ‘I will be like Zohra Sehgal’ - Indian Express
Content:
Three members of a family were killed on Wednesday after they came under a BMC tanker.Officers of the Bangur Nagar police station have arrested a BMC driver in connection with the case.

On Wednesday, the accused was allegedly driving his truck in a rash and negligent manner. He mowed down a family of four, claiming the lives of a 40-year-old man and his two children. The wife of the deceased suffered some injuries. The driver, one Francis Fernandes (48) has been charged with causing death due to negligence.

 According to the Bangur Nagar police, the incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon when Samta Nagar resident Raghuveer Malviya (40), who owns a furniture business, was on his way from Charkop towards Andheri through the Link road on his bike with his wife, Savita (35), a housewife and two children, Bhavna (9) and Bhavesh (6), who study in a local school.

Senior police inspector, M Telang, from the Bangur Nagar police station said, "At the time when they were on the bike going towards Andheri, the BMC truck driven by Fernandes in a rash and speedy way rammed into them from the rear, causing Raghuveer to lose his balance. He fell from his bike along with his family. When they fell in the path of the oncoming truck, Fernandes, who was driving at a high speed, could not stop in time and ran over them, killing Raghuveer and his two children. Savita suffered severe injuries on her right hand and some superficial injuries on the forehead."The family was immediately rushed to the Evershine Nursing home however Raghuveer and his children were declared dead on arrival. Savita is still in the hospital.

The driver was immediately apprehended by the public and handed over to officers of the nearby Malvani police station.

Fernandes was later handed over to the Bangur Nagar police station as the area comes under its jurisdiction.

Heading: Sex no bar - Indian Express
Content:
Kareena Kapoor says she has no plans to shed the reasepaint anytime soon

Dressed in a red gown, Kareena Kapoor tilts her head just enough to give the photographer that rapturously perfect shot. There are three costume changes, which usually mean a tedious wait but this one is wrapped up in record time. And between a sitting with her dietician, staccato exchanges with her publicist and checking out messages on the phone, the actor, looking every inch the incredible, envy-inducing size-zero, tackles this interview.

Kapoor's Golmaal Returns has her playing a suspicious housewife with a penchant for watching saas-bahu serials. It's difficult to imagine the glamorous gal playing a bored housewife but that, as she never fails to reiterate with her actions and words, is a testimony to her skill. "Acting is in my genes," she laughs. There's

also Kambakkht Ishq opposite Akshay Kumar, set in Los Angeles, in which she plays "a character who is arrogant, doesn't like men and does a bit of modelling to earn a few bucks". So what's a girl like her doing in a film reported to boast some incredible stunts, with Akshay playing a Hollywood stuntman? "The second half of the movie has an emotional angle which ends in a Taming of the Shrew-like plot," returns the 27-year-old star.

But the big-ticket release in 2009 that is likely to wash down well with both masses and critics is Rajkumar Hirani's Three Idiots, wherein she comes together with Aamir Khan for the first time. Incidentally, it was Raja Hindustani opposite Aamir that turned around elder sis Karisma's career.

The hugeness of it all is not lost on her. "I'm blessed to be coming together in a movie that involves Aamir, Vidhu Vinod Chopra and Rajkumar Hirani." The film is about the pursuit of excellence as opposed to success. Kareena maintains that it's something that she has always followed in her life. "I have never chased box-office success. I have always been very confident that I will be able to pull off any kind of role. Apart from losing weight, nothing about me has changed. I work equally hard for every film."

While she has always been considered a natural, Kapoor of late has come into her own as a fashionista. Among actresses, she is probably endorsing more products than any other and her slim look for Tashan and romance with actor Saif Ali Khan have added to her chutzpah. Perceived as free spirited with a mind of her own, besides being enormously talented, she does not seem to be buying into her own myth of a style diva.

"Dressing up is part of the job; every woman likes to dress up. It's not my personal style. In Hollywood, outside of the red-carpet events, the stars really believe in dressing down as they don't want to draw attention to themselves. It's only here that stars have security guards around them. I must be the only Bollywood star to not have security surrounding me," she laughs sarcastically.

But she insists, she will continue acting into her old age. "I will be like Zohra Sehgal."

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Samir Soni - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood is warming up to homosexuality, and so is the audience

The film industry has had a long tradition of comic sequences or songs featuring effeminate and cross-dressing male stars. One of Sanjeev Kumar's avatars in the 1970s blockbuster Naya Din Nayee Raat was that of an effeminate character. Amitabh Bachchan donned a sari in Laawaris. But these portrayals have been largely perceived as elements of comic relief and don't interfere with the main plot.

This was replaced by films like Deepa Mehta's Fire and Onir's My Brother Nikhil that made conscious efforts to break the stereotypical representation, but were categorised as 'parallel' cinema. However, the current wave of films, like Fashion and Dostana, may be able to bring the topic of homosexuality to the forefront and into mainstream cinema.

In Karan Johar's Dostana that releases next month, the Bollywood hunks and lead actors, Abhishek Bachchan and John Abraham, pretend to be a couple in a bid to rent an apartment in Miami. Madhur Bhandarkar's recent release, Fashion, in one of its sub-plots, has Harsh Chayya and Samir Soni play a homosexual fashion designer-couple.

This may just be an indication of the acceptance of queers by the audience.

Says Bhandarkar: "My characters are real people, and not caricatures. And the audience will not accept them as normal if we stereotype them." Bhandarkar's film Page 3 also included a gay sub-plot wherein the protagonist Konkana SenSharma's lover is involved with her best friend. These representations of hunky men with queer tendencies are indeed symbolic of the change.

Nandita Das, who acted in Fire, acknowledges the change but feels that "misrepresentation or derogatory connotations by Bollywood can stigmatise the community and force them to remain closeted". Her co-star in Fire, Shabana Azmi, also feels the need for strong scripts to kick up the debate. Azmi was also part of Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd, where one of the couples split after the husband confesses to being a closet homosexual.

Onir feels the acceptance of homosexuality in films will happen only when characters are portrayed without creating much fuss. "For example, why not let one of the band members in Rock On!! be gay and leave it at that without elaborating on it?" he explains and adds that hopefully things will change once homosexuality is legal.

As a movie-goer from the gay community, interior designer Krsna Mehta appreciates the industry's efforts but understands that one can't expect much so soon, given that on-screen kissing between a heterosexual couple is a recent phenomenon. "Of course, it can be better since so many people in the film industry are homosexuals themselves," smiles the designer, promising to watch Fashion and Dostana, "Hopefully Karan's will be a good job." Johar's first attempt at the concept was through Kal Ho Naa Ho, which had a funny 'gay' subplot between Shah Rukh Khan and Saif Ali Khan. And though the two also camped up to bring homosexuality on to film award shows, there's a long way to go before a Bollywood film, solely focusing on homosexuality, wins an award a la Brokeback Mountain.

Heading: Very filmy - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
The soundtrack of my movie Fashion. A personal favourite from the album is the track Marjavaan.

What's your DVD pick?
It would have to be Raging Bull. I just finished watching it for the 20th or maybe 30th time.

Your favourite romantic scene in a movie.
The scene from Out of Sight when George Clooney introduces himself to Jennifer Lopez, and then flashbacks are inter-cut through the conversation. It's one of the most sensuous scenes I've ever seen.

Which actress would you love to go on a date with and why?
Natalie Portman because she's so beautiful and extremely cerebral. We would have a good conversation.

Which dialogue have you mouthed the most in front of the mirror?
It would have to be Al Pacino's final speech from Scent of a Woman where he says, "I too old, and I'm too blind…" The movie is actually full of unforgettable lines.

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Truthfully, I wanted to be an actor ever since I was eight years old, before I even saw a film. It started with a musical theatre workshop in school where I couldn't sing. An inspiration, I would say, is watching Amitabh Bachchan die in Sholay. It's a heartbreaking performance.

The worst film you ever watched.
There are so many. But one film that really disappointed me was The Giant starring James Dean. It was Dean's last film and I had heard so much about it. But it was just too long and I couldn't sit through it.

Which film do you wish you could be a part of?Definitely The
odfather. Al Pacino's role if I'm young, and Marlon Brando's if I'm old.

What makes you an actor?
My need to express myself and my ability to express myself well.

Quiz: From which film is this line: "Follow me, secretary."
No idea. (Answer: Biwi Ho To Aisi.)

Heading: England ODI in Guwahati is on, assures BCCI - Indian Express
Content:
Sun Microsystems Inc. posted a $1.7 billion loss for its latest quarter on Thursday as the maker of servers and business software wrote down the value of the company because of the slow economy and the huge decline in its stock price.

"The economic downturn continued to weigh on our customers, especially those that contribute to our traditional high-end businesses," said Jonathan Schwartz, the chief executive. The financial services industry has been one of Sun's big customers.

Even excluding the goodwill write-down, Sun's results came in at the low end of its own forecast, which was lowered last week, and below analyst expectations.

The Santa Clara, California-based company lost $1.68 billion, or $2.24 per share, in its fiscal first quarter, which ended Sept. 28.

In the same period last year, it earned $89 million, or 10 cents per share.

Excluding the $1.45 billion goodwill impairment and a $63 million restructuring charge, Sun lost 9 cents per share. Analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters expected a loss of 8 cents per share.

Sales fell 7.1 percent to $2.99 billion, coming in below the analyst forecast of $3.05 billion.

Last week, Sun warned that it lost between 25 cents and 35 cents per share in the quarter, or 2 cents to 12 cents per share excluding charges. Analysts adjusted their estimates accordingly.

Sun shares rose 46 cents, or 9.5 percent, on Thursday to close at $5.29. In extended trading after the release of the results, the shares were at $5.14.

Heading: Security tightened after Assam blasts - Indian Express
Content:
The serial blasts that rocked the state of Assam may have cast a shadow on the India-England ODI match that is slated to be played in Guwahati on November 29. But the BCCI is confident that the high-profile match will be played there as scheduled.

Speaking to 'The Indian Express', BCCI president Shashank Manohar asserted that the one-dayer will be played at Guwahati's Nehru Stadium as scheduled. "The India-England match in Guwahati is very much on as scheduled, that's clear enough," the Board president categorically said later this evening from Nagpur.

However, even as the BCCI is trying to allay fears that today's turn of events could have an impact on the ODI match in the troubled Assamese capital city of Guwahati, the final call is eventually expected to come from the England & Wales Cricket Board (ECB).

In the past, the English Board had often expressed concerns over venues which they didn't find satisfactory on the security front. And despite the BCCI's full assurances that the arrangements would be foolproof for the November 29 one-dayer at the Nehru Stadium, there's every likelihood that the ECB could ask some niggling questions in the coming days over the safety of Guwahati hosting the match.

Assam Cricket Association (ACA) secretary Bikash Baruah, too, reckons that the ODI match is quite far away and there would be no problems in hosting the match on November 29.

The Englishmen will come to India on November 1 for a marathon tour comprising seven ODIs and two Test matches. The Nehru Stadium in Guwahati is expected to host the sixth one-dayer.

Heading: Mamata to revive agitation in Singur from November 2 - Indian Express
Content:
The security blanket that the Kolkata police had put in place during the Pujas will not be lifted as of now. A decision in this regard was taken after the serial bomb blasts in Assam on Thursday.

Over 8,000 policemen were deployed for security purposes during the festive season. "The policemen will not be withdrawn as it is usually done after the festive season is over," said Vineet Goyal, Deputy Commissioner (Headqarters).

Though the police have not issued any alert following the Assam blasts, a state of constant vigil will be maintained, he added.

Heading: Buddha seeks Centre’s help to solve PTTI crisis - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee is all set to revive her agitation in Singur, where she will again demand land to be returned to the unwilling farmers.

After a break of about a month, Banerjee is slated to visit Singur on November 2 to take part in a rally scheduled to start from gate no. 1 of the project site to Shanti ceramic.

"Our demand has been the same for the last two-and-a-half years. We are not against industrialisation, but 400 acres within the project area has to be returned. The rest can be used for industrial purposes," said Leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee.

He added since the agreement between the state government and Tata Motors was not made public, Trinamool has no idea about the exit policy of the company.

On Novermber 3, Trinamool workers will demonstrate in Behala to protest against the alleged atrocities committed by the police on the public.

"The police are working for the CPM and against the public. We will protest against the nexus between the police and the ruling party," said Chatterjee. On the same day, the youth wing of the party will hold a protest in the city against the "breakdown" in the law and order machinery in Maharashtra.

On November 10, the Trinamool chief will visit Nandigram. Party workers will agitate in front of the office of the Burdwan superintendent of police (SP) on November 12.

The next day, the agitation will be taken to the SP office in Suri.

Heading: Tatas to return Singur land, Bengal CM tells Front - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee has written to External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee regarding the fate of the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTIs) in the state, said state Left Front chairman Biman Bose.

"The Left Front has asked the Centre to intervene in the issue and see that the crisis is resolved," said Bose after a Left Front meeting on Thursday.

School Education Minister Partha De had also sought Mukherjee's intervention in the issue. On a visit to Delhi, De will approach the Union Human Resources and Development Ministry and the office of the National Council of Teachers Education (NCTE) there for a solution.

Earlier, a three-member team of the school education department had gone to the Bhubaneswar NCTE office.

While the school education department is keen on having more teachers appointed in the state through open advertising, thousands of students in the state are opposing the move. Even the Left teachers and students' organisations are opposing the recruitment process. According to government sources, the state may not go in for the recruitment of primary teachers.

The students wing of the CPM, Students Federation of India, have also joined hands with the protesting PTTI students.

On October 1, the Calcutta High Court had declared that the certificates of the students who have passed from the PTTIs were invalid as the institutes were not functioning as per the norms of the NCTE. With the order, fate of 75,000 students from 142 PTTIs in the state was left in the lurch.

According to sources in the school education department, in an understanding with the NCTE, the state government has decided to change the existing one-year PTTI diploma into a two-year course.

The degree will be henceforth called Diploma in Education (D Ed) and the minimum qualification for the course has been raised from Madhyamik to Higher Secondary.

Heading: Bitten and beaten, he still managed to save this python - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee told Left Front leaders on Thursday that Tata Motors has informed the government that they will return the Singur land to the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC).

In a meeting of the Left Front at the CPM headquarters at Alimuddin Street, Bhattacharjee said the vendors will first shift their equipment and materials. Only then, they will return the land, the CM reportedly said.

Of 997 acres acquired, the WBIDC had leased out 657 acres to Tata Motors in May 2007. The remaining 340 acres were kept for the vendor park and other socio-economic and environmental projects.

The Singur land issue was discussed on Thursday after the Forward Bloc and RSP mounted pressure on the CPM to ask the chief minister to write to Ratan Tata for return of the land.

Front chairman Biman Bose told the media: "We have asked the state government to go ahead and set up alternative industries at Singur."

Since the Tatas had decided not to utilise the acquired land for the Nano project, they must return the land to the state government for alternative industries. Otherwise, the land has to be auctioned. Under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, it cannot be returned to the farmers, Bose said.

According to sources in the CPM, the chief minister had said the possibility of setting up alternative industry at the site was being explored. Although there is no concrete proposal yet, the government is looking for a large manufacturing industry to set up base there. Talks are on in this regard, Bhattacharjee had said, the government is looking into all possibilities.

Heading: City in sick bed, but authorities sleep - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of a small locality in Howrah's Domjur, 20 kms from Kolkata, can still recall the events of October 12: a victory procession carrying a gigantic python is not a sight to be forgotten soon.

And they speak proudly of the courageous act of a local youth  — Dheeraj Batabyal  — who shielded the reptile with his body from a gang of locals intent on killing it. Over a fortnight after the incident, the python has finally found a safe home in Alipore Zoo.

According to Domjur residents, the python, whose slithering presence in the neighbourhood had given them sleepless nights, was proving elusive for months. Finally one evening, the locals managed to corner it.Luckily, Dheeraj was around and he realised that the poor creature was in considerable danger. "I had seen pythons only infilms. I knew that they are non-poisonous and figure in the list of endangered animals. I decided to hand it over to the Forest Department before the people killed it," Dheeraj recalled. "Already they were poking it with bamboo sticks. I tried to stop them, but failed," the youth recalled.

Finally he dived and guarded the python with his own body from the blows that followed. "But he got bitten for his pains and we panicked when we saw blood dripping from his chest and arms," said his brother Manoj.

When the mob realised that Dheeraj would not budge, they agreed to hand the python over to the Forest Department.

The 22-kg snake was kept in a cage at Dheeraj's house. The police were informed but it was 14 hours before forest officials took it away.

The python, the locals say, had been left behind by a group of snake-charmers who had been camping in the area around nine months ago. "The police had picked up the snake charmers, suspecting them to be burglars. The snakes were released," a resident said.

Quiet and submissive, 29-year-old Dheeraj is not a self-proclaimed "wildlife lover". But snakes always intrigued him. And to catch a glimpse of this python, he once waited on the roadside for four hours. "I heard people saying that the python crosses the road after sundown. I tried to track it, but that proved impossible. So I knew that I had to save it this time," Dheeraj said.

Heading: From centres of healing, hospitals turn garbage dumps - Indian Express
Content:
Health centres of KMC close as officials celebrate in disease season

The official death toll in vector-borne diseases is 15 and rising. But health units and dispensaries of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation are either closed for the festive season or are simply not functioning.

The health unit in Ward 39 near Marques Square is a breeding ground for mosquitoes. The manhole remains open for days. Locals allege that the unit opens at 10 am and closes after two hours and often runs short of health officials.

"It is supposed to open at 8 am and often we see people queuing up since morning," said Sheikh Alauddin, who runs a shop in front of the unit.

A spot check found several potholes filled with stagnant water and heaps of stinking garbage that house the adult mosquitoes.

"Our repeated appeals to the local councillor were fruitless. We are cleaning up the surroundings as several people in the locality are suffering from malaria. I have been affected by malaria twice," said Jamil Ahmed, a resident.

Similar condition prevails in Wards 37 and 38.

The health units either stay closed or open for a short duration as the health officials were busy celebrating Bhai phonta —never mind the ailing locals who queued up at its doors and went home without treatment.

"We have no idea when the unit opens and when it closes. It was closed today and I saw people returning home after waiting for hours. Moreover, it does not have a doctor and runs with only two health workers," said a local, who happens to be on the KMC staff.

Ward 29, the ward of Subodh Dey, MMiC, Health, is a mess. There is no medicine, no provision for blood tests and no attention from civic doctors.

The councillor has not yet found time to visit his own ward, which is badly affected by the vector-borne disease.

Although Jhuruni Sahani, a resident of 245, Manicktala Main Road died of malaria, her daughter-in-law Aparna Sahani, who has identical symptoms, is yet to be taken for a blood test by the civic health officials. Several other residents of a slum in the ward are suffering from malaria and high fever. Kanailal Das, a resident of 245 B, Manicktala Main Road is suffering from high fever but has been left unattended. Moreover, a backyard dairy owned by Bawan Roy thrives in the slum flouting all civic rules and provides shelter to several vectors on its dirty premises.

"We have not seen the councillor for years. Even after the death of Jhuruni Sahani, he did not come to see the conditions for himself. We are destined to suffer and die in this way," said Rajib Das, a resident of the area.

Heading: Fresh dengue cases in Murshidabad, Midnapore - Indian Express
Content:
Kolkata's top medical colleges are the perfect breeding grounds for mosquitoes. The Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, the NRS Medical College and Hospital and the Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research (SSKM) are places where hygiene is often given a miss. Authorities care little about cleanliness despite the recent outbreak of vector-borne diseases.

When a team from The Indian Express visited the three institutions, they found garbage vats overflowing with hospital rubbish, unclean drains and open hydrants.

At Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, visitors seldom use the first gate as it is right next to a garbage vat. Members of the staff claimed the vat was cleaned once a week by municipal authorities who were callous and cleared rubbish only from the front of the gate.

Santosh, a cobbler, on hospital premises for 18 years, said: "Sweepers clean the roads and leave rubbish in scattered heaps around the place. In the last three months, it has become impossible to sit here because of the mosquitoes."

A Group-D staff said many employees of the hospital had suffered from malaria in the past two months though none of the cases were fatal.

Nani Gopal Basak, a resident of Konnagar whose relative is admitted to the hospital, said mosquitoes are a menace even during the day. Narayan Chandra Ghosh of Memari in Burdwan has been living on SSKM premises for a fortnight.

He said, "There are many like me who come and live here as we cannot afford to travel back and forth. Since it is quite cold at night we cannot even switch on fans. Mosquitoes have made life difficult."

Paritosh Mondol (name changed), a canteen staff, said the rubbish heaps, and pools of stagnant water were breeding grounds of mosuitoes. "Although there is a big waterbody on the premises, it is cleaned regularly," said Mondol. At the first glance NRS looks spic and span. The backyards, however, are full of garbage.

Krishna Haldar (name changed), a member of the hospital staff, claimed the big waterbody is seldom cleaned. "Even the staff quarters are dirty as they are never cleaned. Though the authorities appear concerned and are cleaning up the roads, they are not bothered about keeping each and every corner of the hospital premises clean," she said.

Vector-borne diseases
In all 561 cases of dengue, 212 cases of chikungunya, and 12 cases of Japanese Encephalitis have been reported from different districts, including Hooghly, Howrah, Midnapore, Bankura, South and North 24-Paraganas. Besides, there is the scourge of the "unknown fever" which is also stalking the state.

Heading: Students take over where civic body quits - Indian Express
Content:
Two fresh cases of dengue were reported from Murshidabad and Midnapore districts on Thursday.

Director of the state health services, Sanchita Bakshi, said: "Medical teams are visiting the districts and collecting blood samples on a day to day basis. We are trying our best to check the outbreak. But due to climatic change, sporadic rainfall and global warming, it will spread and more people will be affected."

She accused the Kolkata Municipal Corporatrion (KMC) of not coordinating with the state Health department to contain the situation.

"Often we discuss measures to control the outbreak with the civic bodies. But the work done by KMC is not at all satisfactory. The civic officials should have been more careful before the outbreak of vector-borne diseases," said Bakshi. On Thursday, Left Front Chairman Biman Bose called Subodh Dey, Health (MMiC) and asked him about the prevalent situation. He also asked Dey to begin awareness campaigns in the city at the earliest.

Heading: Bank employee accused of fraud slips into coma - Indian Express
Content:
While the political parties of the city battle it out with the Election Commission to bring graffiti and slogans back on the walls, students of six schools on Thursday took to the streets of Dalhousie to give a facelift to the heritage buildings of the area.

Armed with soap, buckets, water and brushes 30-odd students from various schools were busy removing graffiti and political posters from the walls of the old buildings like the General Post Office, RBI building and a host of others. The schools involved in the drive included St James, Pratt Memorial, La Martiniere for Girls and Boys, Loreto House and Modern High School.

"We chose this area as this is a heritage area with numerous old buildings that have been covered by posters now," said Akshay Chandak of St James School.

All students are members of the respective nature clubs in their schools.

They had been cleaning the same area on Tuesday and will be continuing the initiative on Saturday. Students of Classes IX, X, XI and XII were involved in the initiative. They have themselves chipped in with buckets, soap and brushes.

"We have done it after school hours so that we do not miss any classes," said Gurchahat Aluwalia of La Martiniere for Girls.

Most of the political posters that the students removed belonged to the several Left trade unions of the state.

Many students felt that it would be a good idea to whitewash part of the walls that were filled with political messages.

"Political parties should refrain from scribbling on the walls and sticking posters as it makes our city look dirty," said a student.

Environmentalist Bonani Kakkar supported the students in their endeavour and accompanied them in their cleaning spree.

Heading: Village on Wheels: an IRCTC initiative for small-budget tourists - Indian Express
Content:
An employee of Canara Bank went into a coma two days after he was arrested on charges of bank fraud. Although no external injury marks were found on his body, his colleagues blamed the police for his critical condition.

Tarun Chattopadhyay (59), who is working at the Prinsep Street branch of Canara Bank, was arrested from his home in Belghoria in connection with an alleged bank fraud of Rs 42 lakh by the Kolkata police on October 27. Chattopadhyay was produced in the Bankshal court on October 28 and was remanded in police custody for 10 days.

The next day, however, the police informed his colleagues that Chattopadhyay was seriously ill and was admitted to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital.

"When we spoke to his doctor, he told us that Chattopadhyay was in coma and was very critical. We were also informed that he was clinically dead," said Ranjan Pal, a colleague.

He added that Chattopadhyay was a patient of chronic hyper-tension. "The police were informed about his condition, but they did not take proper care," Pal added.

"Chattopadhyay was brought to hospital in the afternoon after he fell sick. The doctors, however, declared him fit and he was again taken back to the Lalbazar central lockup," said Sribas Dutta, secretary of the Canara Bank Employees Union.

A cheque of Rs 42 lakh was allegedly encashed in the name of Thacker's Diary, who lodged a complaint with the police on October 22. Chattopadhyay was arrested for the fraud, as he is the special assistant cash supervisor of the Prinsep Street branch of the bank.

"Chattopadhyay was wrongly arrested by the police because he was entitled to pass cheques worth up to Rs 50,000 only. The cheque was approved by the branch manager who put a stamp on it before the cheque was encashed," alleged a colleague.

Questions are being raised as to how Chattopadhyay could fall so ill that he slipped into a coma while in police custody. The police, however, remain tight-lipped over the issue.

"We are looking into the matter," said Deputy Commissioner of Police (Detective Department) Jawed Shamim.

Heading: Fire destroys wooden building in Topsia - Indian Express
Content:
To attract small-budget tourists, the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Development Corporation (IRCTC) will soon launch a new train, "Village on Wheels", in its eastern zone.

The train will leave from Kharagpur or Balasore stations on a nine-day "Bharat Darshan" tour on November 15. "It will cover popular tourist destinations like Howrah, Gaya, Agra, Mathura, Delhi, Hardwar and Varanasi," IRCTC's Eastern Zone General Manager Vivek Srivastav said.

"Ticket bookings were started on Wednesday. Depending on the number of passengers, we will decide whether the train will be flagged off from Kharagpur or Balasore," said Sayed Anwarul Kareem, Assistant Manager (Tourism), IRCTC.

According to Kareem, the train will not have any AC coaches as it is conceptualised as a budget train. "We will extend its route to cover some areas in Assam, Bihar and parts of Orissa," he added.

As per the IRCTC plan, 350 passengers will be accommodated in seven sleeper coaches. Beginning its journey either from Balasore in Orissa or from Kharagpur, the train will stop at Burdwan, Durgapur and Asansol en route. "Passengers will be charged Rs 4,900 for the tour. This includes train fare, meals, bus fares and night accommodation where applicable and group guide charges," Srivastav said.

On IRCTC's pilot run of the "Village on Wheels" earlier this month, Srivatav said that the response was highly encouraging.

"The presence of a large number of travel buffs in Bengal prompted us to launch this train from the east India," he added. One can book the tickets from the IRCTC office or on the website of the corporation. The duration of the tour can be extended depending on the itinerary.

Heading: Constable killed in road mishap - Indian Express
Content:
A fire destroyed a two-storey wooden house on 1C Nabasta Park in Topsia on Thursday. Though no one was injured, the building, which housed a vehicle repair workshop, was completely destroyed in the fire.

According to the residents of the locality, the owner of the workshop lived on the first floor of the building, but the workshop was closed on the occasion of bhai phonta.

"There was no one in the house. Around 2 pm, we saw the first floor in flames and we informed the police and the fire brigade," said Sadhan Sarkar, a local resident.

The building which was gutted is located in a area where there are a number of log mills around. "Initially, we feared that the fire might spread to the mills," said Sushil Sharma, local councillor. Seven fire tenders were pressed into service and the fire was brought under control in a couple of hours.

"The cause of the fire is not clear. It could have been a spark or a gas leak that triggered it," said Uday Adhikari, Divisional Fire Officer. Two buses parked in the garage were also damaged in the fire.

Heading: Bengal’s Ranji opener in limbo - Indian Express
Content:
A constable was mowed down by a truck at the Strand Road-Mahatma Gandhi Road crossing on Thursday morning.

Debasish Roy, the 42-year-old Kolkata Traffic police constable, was crossing the road when the truck (AP 16 T W 5397) hit him.

Roy was rushed to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

According to locals, Roy tried to stop the truck and demanded a bribe from the driver.

The police have, however, refuted the claims saying that the constable was trying to stop the truck from entering Posta because it was already overcrowded with lorries.

According to eyewitnesses, the driver fled from the spot after the incident. Later, the truck was seized by the Burrabazar police.

Heading: Young guns shine in youth Chess - Indian Express
Content:
ACA wants match deferred, CAB says Eden Gardens is ready; Murali's chances ruled out

The serial blasts in Assam have cast a shadow on Bengal's opening match in the Ranji Trophy Plate Division that was slated to be played on November 3-6 in Guwahati.

Laxmi Ratan Shukla & Co were scheduled to take on Assam at the Maligaon ground, near Guwahati in the Ranji Trophy opener. However, in the wake of today's explosions, the Assam Cricket Association (ACA) has sought permission from the Indian cricket Board to postpone the four-day match to later in the season.

The development after the state-wide blasts in Assam also jeopardised chances of ace off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan turning up for Bengal in the Ranji opener. The Sri Lankan team is scheduled to leave for Zimbabwe on November 8, and the November 3-6 match would have been the only chance for Muralitharan to play for Bengal this season. Murali will have to set off for Zimbabwe on November 8.

After after the blasts rocked the entire state of Assam, the state cricket body went into an overdrive to ensure that the match stays with the ACA. The state body's secretary Bikash Baruah approached the BCCI and the CAB with the proposal of deferring the November 3-6 match to some convenient period later in the season.

CAB joint-secretary Arun Mitra said that the Eden Gardens office has no issues with the ACA's proposal of deferring the match. After the BCCI advised the Assam state body to seek the CAB's go-ahead for the postponement, CAB assured to that the ACA officials that it had no problems.

Heading: Web Wonders - Indian Express
Content:
Vishwanathan Anand is right now the toast of the nation after winning the World Chess Championship crown for the third time in his sparkling career. At the same time, young guns from India who have grown up idolising Anand are also doing a great job in their own circuit at the highest level, enhancing India's image as a fast-growing chess powerhouse.

At the World Youth Chess Championship, which concluded today at Vung Tau, in Vietnam, Indian youngsters bagged as many as four gold, two silver and two bronze medals to finish with flying colours.

In the Under-12 Boy's section, Sayantan Das struck gold by scoring 9.5 points out of 11 points. 11-year-old Sayantan is a student of Goodricke National Chess Academy, which is run by the Alekhine Chess Club.

The Goodricke Academy has also produced players such as Grandmasters Surya Sekhar Ganguly, Sandipan Chanda, Neelotpal Das and Woman Grandmaster Nisha Mohota. International Masters Shankar Roy and Saptarshi Roy coach Sayantan at the Goodricke Academy. He is also the first player from Bengal to win a gold medal at any World Chess Championship. Sayantan is a student of Scottish Church School.

Another student of Goodricke Academy, Diptayan Ghosh, also performed creditably, finishing fourth in the Under-10 Boy's section. 

The other players to win gold medals at the World Youth Chess Championships were Vidit Santosh Gujrathi in the Under-14 Boy's section, Padmini Rout in the Under-14 Girl's section and B Adhiban in the Under-16 Boy's section. The silver medallists were SP Sethuraman in the Under-16 Boy's and R Preethi in Under-18 Girl's event. Pratyusha Bodda and Debashish Das won bronze in the Under-12 Girl's and Under-16 Boy's sections respectively.

Heading: Shared Imagination - Indian Express
Content:
Blog 'awards' are the new virtual tickets to fun, bonding and recognition

There's a Rockin' Girl Blogger and there's a Thoughtful Blogger. You might be tempted to think that 'rockin' girls' are essentially not thoughtful and be damned to misogyny, but Ushati Das could probably help. The web world and its stereotypes are a little more adventurous than the uncles-next-door, so it acknowledges Das both as a rocking girl and a thoughtful one at that. Welcome to the world of blog awards. "You've not found the next Kiran Desai here. I know at least ten who have the same awards," laughs Das, a postgraduate student at IISC, Bangalore. Web awards for the blog addicts of this generation is a way to travel beyond the drab comments page and express their admiration with help from some cool logos and some cooler nomenclature. Sample this: the Yummy Blog Award, the Blogging Community Involvement Award, the Yum Yum award or the Blogging With A Purpose Award.

Who commissioned the awards, very few know, but bloggers are hardly bothered. For them it's an out-of-the-box way to acknowledge fellow bloggers, who over time turn into virtual friends. "I don't blog to connect, but at times while reading a blog you feel like somebody has been reading your mind," says Ishani Dasgupta, an avid blogger working with a publication house. Bonding follows, and here's when these 'awards' come handy which can be passed on.

It's not always that a particular award comes as a stamp of quality, but it does ensure your blog a couple of more readers than usual. "If I bump into a blog with an award logo, I would want to go through it at least once," says Arunlekha Sengupta, an employee of Google, Hyderabad. Bloggers like Sengupta agree that most blogs with award logos are worth a read, and therefore, the latter helps you find interesting new blogs. "If not for anything else, the awards liven up your template," laughs Das.

However, the same doesn't follow for awards like Indibloggies. When Pune-based software professional Debashish Chakraborty started the web event in 2003, quality bloggers didn't come by hundreds. "The concept of blogging was still catching on when I started Indibloggies Awards. Then, an acknowledgement like this encouraged more people in India to start blogging," says Chakarborty. Over time the number of bloggers swelled and the award turned into a sophisticated acknowledgement for writers. "I set up a jury of recognized bloggers through virtual networking who screened the entries. It was a completely community driven project," says Chakraborty. And Indibloggies can be credited with nominating some fine writers in its awards-roll.

"The nomination list of awards like these boast of some really good writers we wouldn't know of otherwise," says Ankur Sharma, founder of Culturazzi.org. While one of the Indibloggies winner went on to bag the Young Journalist's award given away by a TV channel, a jury member gave up a plush job to turn into a professional blogger. "Getting nominated in a award list like this ensures that your blog is read by writers of some quality," adds Sharma.

Indibloggies, which could not be organized this year till now due to time constraints faced by Chakraborty, plans to go the whole hog with sponsors and advertisements soon. "It's a web even all right, but needs a lot of involvement. My fingers are crossed," says Chakraborty. So are ours.

Heading: Beyond Pasta - Indian Express
Content:
While short films in Kolkata are exactly not giving the blockbuster at a theatre near you a run for its money, but things are sure to take a turn for the better. The Kalpanirjhar International Short Fiction Film Festival, into its sixth year, has 19 short films from Indian filmmakers this year. "Last time we had just four entries from Indian filmmakers. It's definitely an encouraging trend," says S V Raman of Max Mueller Bhavan, Kolkata.

The film festival organised by the Kalpanirjhar Foundation in association with the Max Mueller Bhavan, Alliance Francaise and American Centre, has seven sections featuring films of varied flavours.

While Short & Sweet presents selected animation films from Germany, GenNext features works by students from film schools across India and Germany. Apart from these, there are films from France, Belgium and Netherlands.

"Short films are gaining significance in the city with the growing number of film schools and film courses. Aspiring filmmakers have to take the short film route if they want to prove their mettle," adds Raman. So, the Kalpanirjhar Festival is banking on the growing league of young filmmakers and film students to popularize short films in the city.

The festival will be on at the Max Mueller Bhavan from November 1-5

Heading: Scary Story - Indian Express
Content:
Retired cricketer Jonty Rhodes talks about his new career in wine and his effort to fight against global warming

South African batsman Jonty Rhodes, known more for his aggressive play on the cricket field, has smoothly made a transition into business in his hometown, Durban. He is now the director of 10 Chapters, a wine label from Durban. Dressed casually in denims, Rhodes, 39, patiently signed autographs for fans at Sheraton Hotel in Delhi. Playing cricket, he answered, was good while it lasted. "I don't miss the game. I'm involved with it, but there are several new, interesting spheres in my life," smiles Rhodes, who will be coaching the team Mumbai Indians for the Twenty 20 matches in April next year.

Rhodes is juggling a part-time job as banking executive in one of Durban's multinational banks, along with promoting wine from South Africa all over the world. "Whatever I know about wine is thanks to my winemaker Stefan Gerber, who educated me about the wine growing region around Durban. This is the first time when I am speaking to various importers and understanding the market in India. It is fun," he says, in between animated discussions of terroir and grape quality.

When he is not strolling through the vines with his winemaker, Rhodes prefers surfing, mountain biking and tackling the issue of global warming, which is close to his heart. "We are in talks with TATA-BP technologies to set up a plant in Durban as the CO2 emissions are its highest ever. We need to protect the future generation from the hazards of global warming. It was since the time of apartheid that such issues were brushed under the carpet and we are facing the consequences today," he says, easily slipping into the role of an amateur environmentalist. Eleventh chapter, perhaps?

Heading: Water Wonder - Indian Express
Content:
Till about a while back they invited curious glances. But now sitting pretty on the T-shirts, handbags, in the rooms and at times our ears and fingers are skeleton and demon faces. Today, on Halloween's Day we check out exactly how popular are dark and mysterious symbols. Supporting skeleton danglers about two inches in size, we spot Mahima Sharma, an IELTS teacher, walk down Sector 17. "I bought them about two months back," she tells us that since then she has not taken them off. Raman of Jewels, Sector 11, says that goblins among others have outdone cartoon characters this year. The plastic skull bracelet (Rs 25) and the metallic rings (starting at Rs 50) are very popular, mentions Raman. "Popular among college students throughout the year, they have emerged as a great gifting item too," he adds.

Elsewhere, Palak Sharma, a B.Com final-year student of GCG-11, is happy with her latest buy from Levis — a white tee with ghost figures. If you are looking for something similar you can grab them at Ebony, Sector 9, and Emerge, Sector 10. As for Khushdeep Kaur, a third-year student of Government College of Arts, she is in love with her shrieking zombie. "Zombie has been my companion for a while now and is my shield. It scares off anybody I do not want to meet," Kaur agrees that her mom was initially apprehensive about the toy, but over the months has gotten used to it. "We arrange slumber parties around it," chips in friend Kiran Tomar stating that they usually get out their collection of horror reads and flicks on the night. With some opposing the highlighting of the dark side of life, there are others who enjoy it as the mysterious new beginning. But then, there is one thing for sure, "Witches, mummies and cryptic dummies have many takers," states Diwakar Sahoonja of Dewsons, who because of the increasing demand, is all set to open a store dedicated to the scary. "While a shop in a mall has been booked and a company has been finalized in Australia to source the products, what is left is to name the store," he says, showing off the hot selling caps and wallets emphasizing the Halloween feel.

Heading: Bone Up - Indian Express
Content:
There's a lake in Ladakh that will leave you mesmerised. Here's how to get there

The beauty of Pangong Lake in Leh has mesmerised all and sundry who have witnessed it. So, this week, I write about the enticing place called Pangong Tso of Ladakh. To travel to this place and to experience the beauty is an adventure in itself. Situated at 4,250 m (13,900 ft) approx, the lake is 134 km long and extends from India to China. Two-thirds of the length of this lake lies in China. The lake is 5 km (3 miles) wide at its broadest point. In the winters, the surface freezes completely despite being salt water. Surprisingly, the lake shows no traces of aquatic life. All the same, visitors see numerous ducks and gulls on the lake surface. The lake acts as an important breeding ground for a variety of birds including a number of migratory birds. And now, we head towards this awesome place. Come, join me on this journey.

GETTING THERE: Many travelers do the Leh-Pangong Tso excursion as a day trip and come back to Leh by nightfall. However, this is not recommended, since the 340 km long round trip leaves little time for Pangong Tso, which is a magnificent lake and doing this excursion in the span of two to three days is highly recommended. Instead, start from Leh - Karu (45 kms). Start off from Leh early in the morning after breakfast and start driving/riding on the Leh-Manali highway till you reach the town of Karu. This will take you less than an hour. Once you are at Karu, head for Chang La (35 kms). From Karu you need to take a left that would take you to the village Shakti, roads are mostly straight till you cross Shakti and a few kilometres thereafter the real ascent for Chang La starts. For most part ascent is steep and initially roads are in good condition. As you approach the final few kms of the ascent to Chang La, road conditions start to deteriorate and steepness increases, making the affair of reaching the summit of Chang La more challenging and memorable. Once you reach the summit, you will be greeted by the Indian Army troops. There is a temple on top of Chang La pass, called Chang La Baba ka Mandir, as well as a cabin built by the army where you can warm up yourself while chatting with the soldiers.

Chang La - Tanksey (58 kms): After a few minutes rest, its time to begin the descent from Chang La, road is in bad condition for few kilometers, beyond which superbly laid tarmac coupled with beautiful scenery awaits you. Your next big break will be at Tangste; a big town with few shops, hotels and an internet café. It is a good idea to have your lunch here or in case you have arrived late in the evening, then spend the night here instead of continuing to Lukung or Spangmik where finding accommodation in peak season can be an issue.

Tanksey - Spangmik (Pangong Tso) (32 kms): Journey beyond Tanksey for most part is through fantastically laid tarmac and views, however don't indulge in over speeding, since there are quite a few water passages built in the middle of the road, which essentially mean 8-10 feet long depression in the middle of the road without any warnings.

As you approach the lake, the sheer size of it starts becoming more apparent as you finally reach its shores. On the banks of the lake is a military camp and also Lukung which is a collection of tents and newly built Eco Huts. From here you can carry on to the road that turns in to sand and rock filled dirt track. The small settlement visible from here is the village of Spangmik, the last village up to which you are allowed to go on normal inner line permits.

Spangmik - Marsimek La (42 kms): 10 kms before Spangmik on the Spangmik -Tanksey road is a diversion that goes towards the village of Phobrang and finally to the highest Motorable pass in the world, Marsimek.

Restricted Area: Pangong Tso, Marsimek La and Chang La are restricted areas and to visit them, you need permits, which are easily obtainable from the DC's office in Leh and can be procured by either submitting the application yourself or through a travel agent. The permits are issued for a maximum period of three weeks. If you want to attempt Marsimek La then you need to specifically mention that while applying for permits. Make at least four photocopies of the permit per region, since you would need to submit them at various check posts.

ACCOMODATIONS: Tanksey: Even though Tanksey is 32 kms before Pangong Tso, it is a good place to spend the night, due to sheer number of accommodation options.

Lukung: Eco Huts at Lukung are just right of the shore of Pangong Tso. Be warned there is no electricity or proper toilet, just camping grade toilet and warm water courtesy solar water heater. Besides, one can also pitch ones own tents here.

Spangmik: The place has one hotel, which offers rooms as well as luxury tents; however get ready to shell out any where between Rs 700 - 1200 for these. One can also find accommodation in guest houses that some inhabitants of Spangmik run from their home.

AMENITIES: Petrol pumps: It is essential to fill up your vehicles petrol tank at Leh and carry enough petrol for the return journey, since there are no petrol pumps beyond the outskirts of Leh.

Phone services: Beyond Thiksey there are no phone booths and mobile phone coverage, however there is an internet café at Tanksey.

Well, as someone said that more than the destination it is the journey, which is important and Pangong Lake offers not only a marvelous journey but also a treat for senses. I am sure you wouldn't miss out on this one.

Caution: Before you plan your trip to Pangong Tso, make sure about clear weather and road blockage, if any.

(The writer is a city based gemmologist and owns an adventure club, www.clubfootloose.com. Mail him at solisethi@gmail.com)

Heading: Wedding Wows - Indian Express
Content:
Actor Priyanka Chopra has been doing a lot of modelling lately. Besides living the life of a clotheshorse in Madhur Bhandarkar's film Fashion, she recently walked the ramp for designer Vikram Phadnis at the Lakme Fashion Week in Mumbai. "I almost felt that Madhur would jump out from the audience and yell action. It was so chaotic being under the lights with people staring at you," smiles Chopra, who was promoting the film at Ambience Mall, Gurgaon. Dressed in a purple off-shoulder dress, she fielded questions about Fashion. "It is not a documentary-drama based on any particular model's life," insists Chopra.

She plays Mugda Mathur, a girl from Chandigarh who goes to Mumbai to fulfil her dream of becoming a supermodel. "I can relate to the character because I was also from a small town and had dreams of becoming an engineer. Fate had other plans and I joined the fashion industry when I was 17," she says.

Though Chopra had a short stint in modelling, lasting six months, she says she misses the chaos of fashion shows. But shooting for Fashion was hard work. "Madhur would allow us five or six retakes for every scene," she says. Chopra has a slew of films lined up for release, which includes Tarun Mansukhani's Dostana where she turns up the heat on a Miami beach. "Dostana is a movie of fun, frolic and masti," says she. The debacle of Love Story 2050 is finally behind her.

Heading: Hooda’s statement not enough to take action against Haryana deputy CM, say police - Indian Express
Content:
There were times when all it did to put together a trousseau were a few shopping sprees coupled with the stuff your magnanimous mother had collected over the years. Well, those times are over and done with. For now, the bride and her family sit with the trousseau specialists working out the look not just for the D-day but for the better part of the bride's first year! You know there's a serious market for wedding wear when the fashion industry rolls out a one-of-a-kind Couture Week. Closer home, designers in the city are working in overdrive specially with the wedding season ready to roll out. So we got down to work too by compiling a what, where and how of all your trousseau needs. Read on:

COLOUR ME WILD: It's one of those years when it's unfair to say one colour rules the roost. "It's a wild palette with colours such as topaz yellow, tiffany blue, emerald green, fuchsia, pearl white, charcoal black and even amethyst making individual statements," lists of Bridal Asia's CEO Divya Gurwara. Agrees city-based designer Poonam who specialises in trousseau wear through her label Amara, available in Sector 8. "This year contrasts are much in vogue. Expect colours like green and red, magenta and brown to do the rounds," adds Poonam who plays with rich colours for winters. Speaking of colour tones, designer Babi Grewal puts "hot pink" as the new black. "It's really the colour to flaunt. Specially in silks," she asserts.

THE YARD LENGTH: Ok, now that the colours are in order, how to go about draping them? "I would put brocade right on top," mentioned international designer Varun Bahl who was in the city recently. Bahl finds that the Indian bridal fashion has come a full circle. "Yes, fabrics like net and silk are back in demand," agrees city based designer Sonika Khanna whose collection for Autumn-Winter 2008 brings in her trademark lace sarees with embroidered petticoats as well as pre-stitched sarees with exhaustive work on the pleats. Working with fabrics like crepe, silk, georgettes, lace, velvet, Sonika incorporates a lot of the jewelled look. "Embellishments are in but in a subtle way," feels Poonam while Babi finds gota and gold antique work a must-sport this season. "If you want to keep away from one thing, then it's the colour silver," she smiles to say.

THE ENSEMBLE: Having an insider's view, thanks to her annual show, Divya Gurwara finds tapered lehengas, which look more like skirts, are now structured. "They are figure enhancing and put a bride at ease. At the same time blouses like corsets and backless cholis, puff sleeves, experimental necklines are in," adds Gurwara. If you have been dying to sport an Anarkali, the good news is that it's still in fashion. "In varying styles though," points out Grewal who finds the shirts longer with a straighter fit. When it comes to the D-day ensemble, the lehenga is still your best best. "But we now have double dupattas," mentions Poonam who sticks to lighter fabrics such as net to cover the bride's head while going with the heavier one as a shoulder drape. The choli, they tell us, is shorter and snug with exposed backs. "For the more conservative, I would recommend longer jackets with lehengas. Traditional with a contemporary twist," Bahl sums it up for us.

Heading: Lawyers unite against ‘nepotism’ in judicial system - Indian Express
Content:
The police have said that no action can be initiated against Haryana deputy chief minister Chander Mohan on the basis a statement made by Ajit Hooda, president, Haryana Lok Dal, recorded with the police. "No offence can be made out of the statement. According to the statement of Hooda, he was neither threatened not assaulted in any way," said the police officers.

Ajit Hooda, while speaking to the mediapersons, had claimed that Chander Mohan had threatened him with dire consequences on last Monday outside the Haryana MLA Hostel.

Station House Officer (SHO) of the Sector-3 police station, Har Sahai said Hooda did not mention any such threat in his statement with the police. "He said somebody had called him up and said he was standing outside his room. When he opened the room there was nobody there. He then called up the police control room and told the police about the phone call," he added.

Hooda said he had gone to Hotel Grand Park in Sector 43 on Monday for a cup of coffee, where he found Chander Mohan along with a few others.

"We had verbal duel with each and Chander Mohan then left. Around 12.15 am, he called me up on the landline and threatened with dire consequences. I then informed the police about the matter," he added.

He, however, refused to comment regarding the difference in his statements to the media and the police.

Heading: Mohali councillors to ‘expose’ faults in civic admn - Indian Express
Content:
The lawyers practicing in Mohali and Kharar have united against the alleged "nepotism" in certain wings of the judicial system. Making the move, the Bar Associations of Mohali and Kharar unanimously resolved to seek the immediate shifting of judges from those places where any of their relatives were practicing as lawyers.

At a joint meeting held today, the advocates decided to launch a movement for a "clean" judicial system, said senior lawyer Tara Chand Gupta.

The meeting was jointly presided over by Avtar Singh Sidhu and Vijesh Chaudhary, presidents of the Mohali and Kharar Bar Association. Around 40 lawyers expressed their views on the matter.

The lawyers said the root of the alleged favouritism lies in the delivery of justice.

"It is imperative that all such judges should be transferred out from the state to ensure a clean system," stressed the lawyers.

Gupta said in order to spread the message and press for its fulfillment, all the Bar Associations across the state will be requested to join the movement and adopt similar resolutions at their respective levels.

Heading: Kids suffering from congenital heart ailments to get free treatment - Indian Express
Content:
A majority of the municipal councillors in Mohali have joined hands against the employees of the Mohali Municipal Council (MC) for their alleged acts of "omission and commission halting the city's development", besides non-responsive and non-accountable municipal administration.

Retaliating to the recent protest by the civic employees against the elected municipal councillors at the MC Bhawan, 16 of the 31 councillors have decided to expose the alleged corruption, negligence and dereliction of duty among the MC officials and employees.

Cutting across political lines, Amrik Singh, Rajinder Prasad Sharma, Bharat Bhushan Maini, Manjeet Kaur, Gurmukh Singh Sohal, Gian Chand Aggarwal, Harwinder Kaur Lang, Phoolraj Singh, Prakashwati, Mohanbeer Singh Shergill, Sukhminder Singh Barnala, Gurmeet Singh Walia, Paramjeet Singh Kahlon, Harpal Singh Channa, Kuldeep Kaur Kang and Usha Rani have formed a united front to take on the municipal employees.

The councillors rued that the local residents were at the receiving end due to encroachments, bad condition of roads, unhealthy sanitary conditions, stray cattle and dog menace but the civic administration was least bothered to tackle these issues despite raising them repeatedly at the MC meets.

Holding the civic officials and employees responsible for lack of basic civic amenities in Mohali, the councilors recollected that at the MC meeting on August 29, MC Executive Officer (EO) had promised to free the city from illegal rehris within a month but still the problem remains as before.

The councillors alleged that an MC clerk deputed in the enforcement wing was caught red-handed while accepting bribe from a rehriwala but was not shunted out. "At an MC meeting on October 17, when we resisted against the clerk and demanded his immediate transfer, the MC employees held a demonstration against us," the councillors said.

Heading: Delegation from Bakersfield meets civic officials - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Laxmi Kanta Chawla, today announced free treatment of students suffering from congenital heart ailments in the state. She said Rs 5 crore has already been earmarked to cover the students of government and aided schools under this initiative.

She said that Mohali and Ropar have been chosen for the pilot project, where a survey has also been conducted to identify students suffering from heart diseases.

The minister was in Mohali to handover appointment letters to 97 new doctors, including 61 for posting at mini-primary health centres, 12 paediatricians, 11 obstetricians and 13 female medical officers for posting at the round-the-clock emergency medical obstetric care centres.

She said the Punjab Health department has also tied up with the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) whose experts will provide their services.

Chawla also announced the launch of the Emergency Medical Response Services in the state in December. She said 76 emergency response vehicles will hit the roads and their number will be increased to 224 by 2010. These vehicles will deal with all sorts of medical emergencies and will be available on a single telephone number.

Addressing the newly appointed doctors, Chawla exhorted them to serve humanity. "Medicine is a noble profession," she said while urging the young recruits under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

Those present on the occasion included Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Punjab, Vijay Kain, NRHM Mission Director Satish Chandra among others.

Heading: Administrator cancels inauguration of Halfway Home - Indian Express
Content:
Harvey L Hall, the Mayor of Bakersfield in California, accompanied by John Hefner, vice-president of Sister City Corporation, and four other members met Mayor Pardeep Chhabra and Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria in the Punjab Bhawan today. The delegation is on a tour to the heritage cities of India.

The delegation was given a brief overview of the various projects of the MC, including the sanitation system, water works and electricity among others.

Talking about Chandigarh's sanitation system, Dr Sunkaria said the city is spread over an area of 114 square kilometers and the total municipal area is nearly 84 square kilometers.

He gave details about projects, including the automatic management of water supply through SCADA, a modern automatic slaughterhouse in the public sector, remediation of landfill, plan for 100 per cent sewage treatment, latest fire fighting equipment and machinery among others.

While talking about the working of Bakersfield, Harvey L Hall said the annual budget of the town is $ 375 million for development work. He said that there are seven council members in the town and 17 departments.

Heading: Six PGI professors to be felicitated by NAMS - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administrator General SF Rodrigues today refused to inaugurate Halfway Home, the project being constructed for the physically and mentally challenged persons who have been abandoned by their families. He also took the entire team of officials to the site in Sector 47 and explained the entire concept.

The UT Administrator had called a meeting of senior officials of the Health department including Secretary (Health) Ram Niwas. While discussing the project, he realised that the officials were confused about the concept and thus took the entire team to the site.

He also inspected the under-construction sites for the mentally challenged and the vocational training centre for the disabled.

While senior officials remained tight-lipped on the issue, all of them gave the same reason for the cancellation the Administrator was not happy with the concept plan.

A senior official said: "The name, Halfway Home, does not gel with our concept. In a layman's language, 'Halfway Home' means a transitory home for a mentally challenged person, who is stays there till his medical condition improves and is ready to go back to his family. The Administrator, however, wanted a home for those who have been abandoned by their family and have no place to go. Besides, the place is not fully furnished yet and the the inauguration was thus called off."

UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas said the project is now likely to be inaugurated by November end.

Dr Chavan, Head of Psychiatry department, GMCH-32, meanwhile, refused to comment. The officials who were taken to the site included UT Secretary Ram Niwas, Secretary to Governor, MP Singh, Director (Health Services)

Dr MS Bains, Director (Social Welfare) Amandeep

Kaur, Director Prof Raj Bahadur, Head of Psychiatry Department Dr Chavan among others.

Other sites inspected
Home for Mentally Challenged, Sector 31 Rodrigues also visited the construction site of the Home for the Mentally Challenged in Sector 31 and directed the officials to expedite the construction work and complete the same by January.

Vocational Training Centre for Disabled, Sector 46
The construction of the centre is on the verge of completion.

Working Women's Hostel, Sector 24
The Administrator inspected the expansion work of the hostel. He was told that over 90 per cent of the construction is complete and the remaining will be over in the next few weeks.

Heading: Haryana govt gets 3 months to fill vacant consumer forum posts - Indian Express
Content:
The National Academy of Medical Sciences (NAMS) has decided to confer the Dr V R Khanolkar Oration award for the present year upon Prof Amod Gupta, head of department, Ophthalmology, PGI. Five PGI professors will also be awarded with a fellowship by the academy.

The recipients of the scholarships include Prof Kusum Joshi, head of department, Histopathology, Prof A J Kanwar, head of department, Dermatology, Prof Madhur Gupta, former head of department, Anatomy, Prof Jagat Ram, department of Ophthalmology and Prof G D Puri, department of Anaesthesia.

The awards will be formally conferred upon the doctors during the 48th annual conference of NAMS to be held in Jammu soon.

Prof Amod Gupta will be bestowed the award for his contribution to the field of Intraoccular Tuberculosis and its management. Prof Gupta has 194 publications to his credit and is also the recipient of the Dr R N Mathur award and A W Sherrit memorial award. He has also been the president of the Vitreoretinal Society of India and the founder of the Uveitis Society of India.

Prof Kusum Joshi, on the other hand, has 186 publications in indexed journals, 34 other publications and 8 chapters in books/monographs to her credit. Her major research contributions have been in the field of breast pathology, oncopathology and renal transplantation pathology.

Pigmentary disorders, vesiculobullous disorders and paediatric dermatology are Prof A J Kanwar's main areas of interest. He has published more than 425 articles in various national and international journals. "His being elected as a fellow of the academy is a rare honour as only a few dermatologists have been conferred this distinction," stated a spokesperson of the PGI.

Prof Madhur Gupta has published more than 60 national and international scientific research papers and 8 chapters in various textbooks. Her research on muscular attachments of the scapula published in the journal of Radiological and Surgical Anatomy is cited in the various books including the Gray's Anatomy.

Prof Jagat Ram is the only ophthalmologist in India who has been awarded the fellowship for his work on cataract surgery. Prof GD Puri, a cardiac anaesthetist at PGI, has more than 70 international publications to his credit.

Heading: A dishonoured cheque: Boon or bane? - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Haryana government to fill the three vacant posts of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission within three months.

The directions were passed by a division bench headed by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur on a petition filed by Kulbir Singh, a resident of Yamuna Nagar. The petitioner had sought directions to the Haryana government to create additional bench in the Commission so that decision can be taken on more than 14,000 appeals pending before it.

At present, 14,807 appeals are pending before the Commission. On January 23, 2002, the petitioner had filed a complaint before the Haryana Consumer Forum after his motorcycle was failed to give proper mileage as per the company's claim. The case was decided by the forum but the appeal of the petitioner is pending before the commission. Thus, the petitioner submitted that like his case, several other appeals were pending.

In its reply, the Haryana government told the court that the process to fill the posts was already on and advertisements in newspapers.

Heading: Oriental Insurance asked to pay for deficiency in services - Indian Express
Content:
Complainant unable to purchase shares after State Bank of India wrongly credited a cheque, bank argues that lapse saved complainant from loss due to fall in share prices

The District Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum has directed the State Bank of India to pay Rs 2,000 as compensation for deficiency in services for wrongly crediting a cheque. As a result, the complainant was unable to purchase shares and moved the forum alleging loss and mental agony.

Interestingly, the bank's counsel argued that the mistake had instead saved the complainant as the fall in share prices would have resulted in huge losses had the cheque been honoured.

The complainant, Parvesh Chander Avasthy, had two savings accounts in the State Bank of India.

In 2007, he applied for shares of Power Grid Corporation of India at the rate of Rs 52 per share.

For this, Avasthy moved two applications, one in his name and the other in the name of his son, Gaurav. Along with the applications, he submitted two cheques of Rs 97,500, a debit voucher and a credit voucher for transferring Rs 65,000 from his savings account to his current account on September 13, 2007.

But one of the cheques was returned unpaid by the bank citing insufficient funds.

As a result, Avasthy's application for allotment of shares was rejected. Upon inquiry, the complainant discovered that the bank had wrongly transferred an amount of Rs 6,500 instead of Rs 65,000 from his savings account to the current account.

In its reply, the bank stated that the amount had wrongly been credited due to an oversight.

"The mistake was neither willful nor intentional," stated the bank.
