Ruling in favour of the complainant, the forum directed the bank to cross-check all account entries so that such like instances are not repeated. However, keeping in view the present scenario of the market, the forum decided to keep the compensation low.

Heading: Civic body approves rehabilitation budget - Indian Express
Content:
Dismissing an order of the Ferozpur District Consumer Forum, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission today directed Oriental Insurance company to pay Rs 96,364 as insurance claim for a car broke down while driving.

The case had earlier been rejected by the Ferozpur District Forum on the ground that a mechanical breakdown does not fall under the purview of the insurance policy.

The complainant, Mathura Kumari, had bought a Maruti Zen in March 2003 and had insured it with Oriental Insurance in April 2003.

The warranty period of the vehicle was for 24 months, but it broke down in August 2003.

The car was then taken to the workshop but was not repaired nor the claim paid to the complainant despite all formalities having been completed.

The insurance company, in its reply, said the vehicle had not suffered any loss due to an accident but owing to a mechanical breakdown and was thus not covered under the policy.

The Ferozpur District Forum held the claim to be self-contradictory and rejected the complaint. The complainant then appealed to the Punjab State Commission, which then transferred it to the UT State Commission.

The Commission found that the district forum had erroneously dismissed the complaint without appreciating the documents. Justice K C Gupta held: "The complaint was dismissed because the complainant had taken a contradictory stand. While on the one hand, she had said her car was damaged in an accident, in another plea, she said it was due to some mechanical breakdown. 

The District Forum had dismissed the complaint on a very technical ground ignoring the evidence on file." He added that the insurance company is deficient in services by getting the claim assessed but not paying the same on technical pleas.

Heading: Encroachment issue: ‘Hawkers, vendors MC’s sole target’ - Indian Express
Content:
Estimates for development works to be carried out colonies of the city were passed in the House Meeting of the Municipal Corporation (MC) held today. The agenda for this month was dominated by issues of the rehabilitation colonies.

A number of new projects would be taken up. These include construction of the periphery road of rehabilitation colony, Kajheri in Sector 52. While an estimate was passed earlier, it was revised after the road got damaged due to the rains.

The main road between Hallomajra and rehabilitation colony of Ram Darbar will be strengthened and recarpeted at a cost of Rs 53.25 lakh. Another road will be built in the rehabilitation colony, Maloya. The main road in Dadumajra Colony will be widened. An amount of Rs 66 lakh would be spent.

The House also approved purchase of two sewer cleaning jetting machines for cleaning sewer lines in the city. It has also been decided that the water supply in Hallomajra village, including recently notified Deep Complex will be augmented.

The councillors decided that the forms of the tenders will be available online, since many times those who want to apply cannot do so because the officials refuse to give them forms. An estimate of Rs 1.12 crore was approved for construction of community centre in Maloya village.

Projects in focus
* Construction of the periphery road of rehabilitation colony, Kajheri
* Road between Hallomajra and rehabilitation colony of Ram Darbar will be strengthened
* Main road in Dadumajra Colony will be widened
* Water supply in Hallomajra village will be augmented

Heading: ‘Neglected’ councillors rock House - Indian Express
Content:
The issue of encroachments led to heated arguments in the House Meeting of the Municipal Corporation (MC) on Thursday. The councillors said that the MC enforcement staff were targetting only the rehriwalas and hawkers, while other defaulters were being given a free hand.

Raising the issue, Councillor M S Chohan said that the issue of reducing fines for the encroachers was pending for a long time without any result. BJP councillor Gurcharan Dass Kalaa added that the vendors were not allowed in Manimajra for three days. This resulted in their fruits and vegetables getting spoilt. The enforcement staff is scared of the rich. So encroachments may thrive all over Manimajra, but the vendors were not allowed to sell their goods.

Most elected councillors were in favour of reduction of fines, which are charged from the vendors.

Councillor Davinder Singh Babla highlighted that when the officials are informed about the encroachments they refuse to take any action. "I have raised the issue of encroachments being present in Sector 27 a number of times. But the officials have taken no action. The auto mechanics have extended their shops due to lack of checks."

Dr A P Sanwaria stressed that the heritage of the city should be maintained. Meanwhile, councillors Arshad Khan and Dr Amrit Bolaria said that the councillors are right in saying that the hawkers and vendors should be allowed to function. However, there has to be a policy for the same. "They cannot be allowed to thrive everywhere in the city. This comes under social sector reforms. The vendors could be provided alternate employment or some sites should be allocated where they can set their shop."

The councillors also stressed that a check should be there on the vendors coming in from Panchkula and Mohali.

Meanwhile, Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria congratulated the enforcement staff on the way they kept a check on encroachments in markets in the past few days.

"The enforcement staff has braved mobs and angry protestors without help from the police. If we allow a free for all, encroachments would thrive. The city will become chaotic. We are not against the poor. But work has to be undertaken as per rules. The enforcement staff is working in the interest of the city," he said.

Heading: We need to change our mindsets: Kapil Sibal - Indian Express
Content:
The councillors of the Municipal Corporation once again expressed resentment for being 'neglected' by the officials. They said they were given no importance and had no say in the development projects in their wards.

An inquiry has been conducted into the issue of submission of wrong information in reply to the questions by Councillor Chander Mukhi Sharma. The report was submitted in the House.

Sharma said that the sanctity of the House was at stake. "How can wrong information be supplied to the House? The officials do as they will. The councillors are not consulted on many issues. The official concerned who supplied wrong information should apologise to the House," he said.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner stated that on basis of the inquiry report, the official cannot be held guilty. The report states that while the XEN (Horticulture) did not inform Sharma about the completion of work the same was done by his subordinates.

However, Sharma stuck to his stand and was supported by other councillors. Dr Pam Rajput moved a resolution that the official should apologise. The situation was diffused only after the XEN apologised.

Former Mayor Harjinder Kaur also reiterated that the officials were not keeping her informed about the development in her area. She produced pictures clicked by her of a pipeline for supplying tertiary treated water, which was being extended.

Kaur said: "Tertiary treated water is for watering of lawns and green belts. However, the pipeline is being extended towards marla houses where there are no gardens. While I contacted the officials a number of times, they have not given me any information about the project which is going on in my ward. The information that I had demanded about pipes being laid for supply of tertiary-treated water has still not been given to me."

Councillor Davinder Singh Babla added that the officials do not listen to them when issues about the wards were brought to their notice.

He added that the councillors should be asked before payment is made to the contractor. In case of problems the councillor should be held liable.

Mumicipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria, meanwhile, said that the councillors and officials should work in tandem. In case of problems he was there to offer solutions.

Sidelights
* A two-minute silence was observed in the House in the memory of fireman Amarjit Mavi who died after receiving serious injuries in a firefighting operation in Sector 22.
* Additional Commissioner P K Sharma said that the disciplinary action has been initiated against a fireman who had to distribute the agenda for the meeting but he did not do so on time. This resulted in the agenda reaching late to nine councillors.

Heading: Mohali lads ‘charge’ ahead in IPL selection - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister for Science and Technology, Kapil Sibal, laid the foundation stone of the Centre for Emerging Areas in Science and Technology, near the Botany department in Panjab University on Thursday.

Addressing the gathering, the minister congratulated PU Vice-Chancellor Prof RC Sobti and the university for initiating new courses and setting up a centre which will equip the students to keep pace with new developments.

"The new courses and the centre will enable everyone to open their eyes to the world at large," Sibal stated.

He also offered support to the university to encourage science and research in the country.

The three-storey Centre will be built at an estimated cost of Rs 8 crore and will have seven postgraduate departments, a laboratory and multi-display library. Sibal also emphasised on the need for collaboration with other institutions to bring about the desired results.

Speaking on the occasion, he said, "We need to change our mindset, thinking and work culture. This change will enable our country to make rapid progress in science and technology. The times are changing fast and the present scenario offers immense opportunities for creating knowledge unlike the past."

He also suggested evolving public-private collaborations for realising the objective.

He further added that Panjab University was among the three universities which have been identified as Centres of Excellence in Bio-Technology.

Vice-Chancellor Prof RC Sobti, meanwhile, in his welcome address, briefed the minister about the achievements and challenges being faced by the university.

Heading: Mohali, Ropar govt hospitals mere ‘referral’ centres? - Indian Express
Content:
Pacers Jaskaran Singh & Harmeet Bansal selected for Deccan Chargers

Bowling to Adam Gilchrist at the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) Stadium nets during the Indian Premier League has changed 19-year-old Mohali pacer Jaskaran Singh's life. For Gilchrist, now skipper of the Hyderabad-based Deccan Chargers, carried 'home' a good impression of the tall pacer, which resulted in a call to the selection trials for this year's IPL. A good word from former national selector Bhupinder Singh followed and Jaskaran was drafted into the side for the next edition.

Fortune favoured another Mohali pacer, Harmeet Bansal, as well. Now, both the lads will be sharing the dressing room with the likes of Gilchrist, Andrew Symonds, V V S Laxman and Shahid Afridi among others. Bhupinder Singh had asked five Punjab cricketers — Ravneet Ricky, Ravi Inder Singh Rajji, Harmeet, Jaskaran and Rahul Sharma — to appear for the selection trials held in Hyderabad on October 1. The trials were conducted by former Australian cricketer and now the coach of Deccan Chargers, Darren Lehmann.

Jaskaran, a big fan of Brett Lee, had only dreamt of sharing space with the Aussies. "I idolise Brett Lee's bowling style and it will be a memorable moment for me when I play against him. Everything has happened so fast, the feeling is still sinking in. I am really excited and looking forward to IPL and my Ranji Trophy debut."

Harmeet, at present in Patiala for the C K Nayudu Trophy in the North Zone league championship, expressed excitement over his inclusion. "It is a dream come true. I never thought I would play in the IPL and it is a great feeling being part of such an illustrious team. I hope I deliver when the opportunity arises," said the lanky pacer who has signed a three-year contract with the Deccan Chargers.

"Both Jaskaran and Harmeet are energetic and talented cricketers with immense potential," Bhupinder told Newsline. "There is great demand for players from Punjab for different teams in the IPL. Robin Singh called me up and asked to send a few medium pacers and batsmen from the state for his team."

In last year's IPL, Mohali medium-pacer Manpreet Singh Gony was roped in by the Chennai Super Kings. Later, Gony represented the Indian side in ODIs. Incidentally, all the three have trained under coach Sukhwinder Tinkoo, who played for India in the Youth (U-19) World Cup in '88-89. Tinkoo said: "Jaskaran has pace in his bowling while Harmeet is a big swinger of the ball. Both are tall which lends more effect to their bowling. Last year, Jaskaran had also managed to impress Sachin Tendulkar while bowling at the nets. In fact, Sachin had called up the MRF Academy to inform them about Jaskaran."

Heading: Two injured as Innova hits bike - Indian Express
Content:
In 2008 (till July), 41 per cent of emergency patients in Mohali, 60 per cent in Ropar were referred to hospitals in the city

Despite the state government spending over Rs 850 crore to improve healthcare services in the last four years, government hospitals in the Chandigarh periphery are still ailing.

If we go by the figures of patients referred from eight hospitals — four each in Mohali and Ropar districts — it seems government hospitals around Chandigarh have turned into mere referral centres.

Passing the buck?
According to information procured under the Right to Information Act, a total of 2,911 emergency cases were reported till July in 2008. Of these, 1,722 were admitted while 1,189 (41 per cent) were referred from Mohali district government hospitals.

In 2007, of the 4,144 emergency patients reported in Mohali district government hospitals, 1,801 (43 per cent) were referred while 2,343 were admitted.

In Ropar, 569 (60 per cent) of the 955 emergency cases were referred while 386 were admitted in government hospitals till July 2008. In 2007, of the 1,821 emergency cases, 1,081 (59 per cent) were referred and 740 were admitted.

All the cases were referred to PGIMER, GMCH-32 and GMSH-16 in Chandigarh.

Interestingly, the government hospitals were also reprimanded several times by the city hospital authorities for the large numbers of referrals.

In Mohali district, Kurali tops the chart by referring 242 (82 per cent) emergency patients of the 296 reported in 2008 followed by Kharar Civil Hospital, which referred 239 (72 per cent) patients of the 330 emergency cases.

While Anandpur Sahib referred 201 (71 per cent) of the total 285 emergency patients in 2008, Ropar Civil Hospital referred 275 (63 per cent) emergency cases of the total 435.

Infrastructure
Seven of the total eight government hospitals in both the districts have 540 beds with sanctioned posts of eight Senior Medical Officers (SMOs), 94 Medical Officers (MOs) and eight dental surgeons.

While the Mohali Civil Hospital has 200 sanctioned beds, Ropar and Anandpur Sahib hospitals have 100 sanctioned beds each. Kharar has 50 sanctioned beds, Kurali, Chamkaur Sahib and Nurpur Bedi have 30 sanctioned beds each.

Mohali has the maximum sanctioned strength of 31 doctors while Ropar and Anandpur Sahib have 22 doctors each. Kurali, Chamkaur Sahib and Nurpur Bedi have seven doctors each while Kharar has 14 sanctioned posts.

According to the norms, every 200-bed hospital should have two specialists each in Medicine, Surgery, Gynaecology, Pediatric, Orthopedics, Anaesthesia, Dental departments and one specialist each of Pathology, Ophthalmology, Radiotherapy, Psychology, Skin, Vaginal diseases, ENT, Micro and eight general MBBS doctors. 100-bed hospitals require one specialist in each department with seven general doctors.

Heading: Scribe alleges attack by MNS in Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
Strongly condemning the continuing violence against North Indians in Maharashtra, Chief Minister Mayawati has shot off a letter to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, asking him to intervene in the issue with immediate effect.

She has demanded that the Maharashtra government be dissolved for its failure to control the situation and stringent action be taken against all those involved in these violent attacks.

Mayawati pulled up Union ministers Lalu Prasad and Ram Vilas Paswan as well for their "rhetorics" in the matter.

And she criticised the Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) for staying silent on the issue. The attitude of these leaders, she said, indicates their silent permission.

"The demand of action in the Maharashtra incident by Lalu and Paswan is a mere gimmick, as they both are part of that very government before which they are putting forth their demand," Mayawati said. Their appeal is only meant to misguide the innocent public. "Had they been serious about their demand, they would have tried to pressurise the government to take some action," Mayawati said.

She suggested that these leaders should leave the UPA and open a front against the Central government on this issue.

Mayawati said the Maharashtra government has completely failed to control the situation.

Referring to the recent statement by the Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Desmukh, Mayawati said: "The government has become a silent spectator to this violence and on top of that the state Chief Minister has expressed his inability to protect his people, in such situation he does not have any right to hold the charge of office any longer''.

The BSP, she said, strongly condemns the role the Maharashtra government and demands that the Prime Minister take measures to safeguard the rights of people from other states who have gone to Maharashtra in search of livelihood. Any delay in action would be costly for the Congress and it will be held solely responsible for whatever is happening in Maharashtra.

Mayawati, meanwhile, has condemned the death of Dharmdeo Narain Rai of Sant Kabirnagar district in Mumbai on Wednesday, following violence against north Indians in Maharastra. The chief minister has sanctioned Rs 2 lakh to the family of the deceased.

Heading: ‘Too early to trace Assam blast terrorists’ - Indian Express
Content:
Says he was beaten up outside police station

Deena Nath Tiwari (45), originally from Allahabad and his friend Kamlesh Dubey from Varanasi's Sherpur, sustained injuries when they were attacked — allegedly by men of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena. The attack took place outside the Kurar police station in Mumbai late on Wednesday. Tiwari, who works in a vernacular newspaper, have been admitted at the Bhagwati Hospital at Boriwali alongwith Dubey.

The two had lodged separate FIRs at the Kurar police station. In his FIR, Tiwari had named three persons — who, the police say, belong to the MNS. The rest are unidentified.

According to Tiwari, on Wednesday evening, a few MNS workers had beaten up milk-trader Sabarjeet Pandey outside his shop. Pandey was also from Uttar Pradesh.

"In the evening, when I went to the Kurar police station to collect information about the incident, the MNS activists were waiting outside the station. They beat me up with sticks and rods," said Tiwari.

Dubey, who had gone to drop him at the police station, was beaten up as well.

Tiwari's brother Bhola Nath Tiwari said: "Yesterday, I received a call from unidentified persons who told me about the incident. We have been staying in Mumbai for the last 25 years and it is shameful that we are still considered North Indians."

Shiv Ram, Tiwari's brother who lives in Allahabad, said:

"It is very unfortunate. I had asked my brothers to return to Allahabad."

Shiv Ram is a resident of Gaura Chauta village.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Kurar police station in-charge Ram Chandra Ahir said: "In regard to Pandey's case, we have detained 10 people. Tiwari's case is still under investigation. The three persons he had named in his FIR are MNS activists."

Heading: Magh Mela authorities blacklist 20 religious organisations - Indian Express
Content:
Strongly criticising the serial blasts in Assam, Union Minister of State for Home Shriprakash Jaiswal said it was too early to trace the terror organisation responsible for the blasts.

Addressing mediapersons at the Tilak Hall on Thursday, he said: "The seven northeastern states have been declared 'disturbed areas'. For nearly three decades now, such terror activities are being frequently witnessed in this belt." Paramilitary forces have been deployed in Assam and relief operations are in progress, he added.

Jaiswal did not rule out the possibility that fight for supremacy between two terror organisations was behind the blasts. "The blasts will have no impact on the forthcoming Assembly elections in Mizoram. The Home Ministry has asked for a report on the serial blasts from the Assam government," he said. The minister claimed that due to sincere efforts of the UPA government, terror activities in northeastern states have gone down by 50 per cent in the last four years.

The minister refused to link any religious organisation or political party with the recent blasts witnessed in different parts of the country.

Chief Minister Mayawati, meanwhile, has strongly condemned the serial blasts in Assam. She has also demanded that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh take effective measures to ensure that such incidents are not repeated.

Though the Mayawati government has given a clean chit to the security arrangements made during the recent visit of Amethi MP Rahul Gandhi to Kanpur, Jaiswal termed it a major security lapse. "The UPA government has taken up the issue seriously," he added. Terming it a planned move on part of the state government, he said: "There was no point in withdrawing the security when the programme was decided two days in advance."

Heading: First flight fails to take off, Hajis waiting for visas - Indian Express

The Magh Mela administration has begun its exercise for the month-long annual religious festivity by debarring 20 odd religious organisations and muths.

Heading: Patel a ‘terrorist’: BJP to launch protest - Indian Express
Content:
The first flight that was scheduled to take off with the Haj pilgrims at 1 am from the Lucknow Embarkation Point, was cancelled on Thursday as the Central Haj Committee failed to deliver visas and passports to the 290 Haj pilgrims.

The Uttar Pradesh government has accused the Centre of deliberately ignoring the problems of the Haj pilgrims of the state.

Chief Minister Mayawati said this is a glaring example of yet another step-motherly treatment meted out to the state by the Centre.

She asked the chairman of the Haj committee to extend all facilities to those who could not get visas and passports on time and arrange for their smooth departure at the earliest.

The minister for Public Works Department Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who is also the chairman of the state Haj committee, said the Centre is deliberately harassing the Hajis. "The flight scheduled to take off at 1 am from Lucknow airport on Thursday was cancelled without consulting the state Haj committee. The Central Haj committee did not inform us about its cancellation," Siddiqui said.

The state committee received the information about the cancellation from the Saudi Airlines.

"The state committee has been trying to contact the foreign ministry to apprise them of the problems faced by the Hajis. I also tried to talk to the foreign minister. But I failed to get any response," the minister told reporters.

"We requested them to give us the responsibility of communicating to the Hajis. The state Haj Committee has not even the right to information," he said.

He suggested that the Central Haj Committee share its responsibility with the state committee.

As per the letter to the Haj Committee of India, though the pilgrims' passes were submitted to the Royal Saudi Consulate, Mumbai, for endorsement of Haj visas in advance, they have not returned the same till date.

The letter added: "In view of the non-receipt of the pilgrim passes from the Saudi Consulate, Haj Committee of India is compelled to postpone — on the advice of Saudi Arabian Airlines — the first flight SV-5263 dated 30.10.2008 departure 13.00 hours from Lucknow Embarkation Point".

The pilgrims, meanwhile, continue to face problems.

Yahia Khan, a scientist working with Lucknow's B B Ambedkar University, was to take the Thursday's flight.

"I have not received my visa and passport. Now I am waiting for a decision," Khan said.

Israil Khan, who has brought his parents to the Haj House from Lalitpur, said: "We have visa and passport for my mother, but are waiting the same for my father Munir Khan."

Heading: Defence Ministry nod to railway overbridge - Indian Express

Engineering and management students of Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) will now have to work on their final year projects from the beginning of the session. The university has decided to monitor the progress of the projects on a monthly basis so that students take their assignments seriously.

The UPTU has started to set up project evaluation committees, which will be functional from the current academic session. The committees are being set up at three levels. The state level committee, which has already been constituted, comprises the vice-chancellor, additional examination controller and six professors — from university and engineering and management institutes.

The other two types of committees will be set up by each of the institutions. While one will comprise selected faculty members headed by the concerned college director, the other will comprise senior teachers of different engineering and managements streams of the same college.

"Engineering and management institutions have been issued circulars to set up the committees and inform the university at the earliest," said UPTU Vice-Chancellor Professor Prem Vrat.

Project assignment is a part of the final-year syllabus of BTech and MBA courses. Marks scored in project are valuable, as it considered during placement interviews, he added. "There are some students who do not take projects seriously and start working on them a few days before the final examinations. The university also gets less time to go through the projects and students mostly score average marks," Vrat said.

The UPTU Additional Controller of Examination, J P Pandey, said: "From the next academic session, committees will have to provide us details like the list of final-year students, the projects chosen, etc.

After a long wait, the construction of the railway overbridge at Allahabad Crossing, Shanti Nagar, finally received the green signal from the Defence ministry.

Railways will spend Rs 9 crore for the construction of the overbridge, the Defence Ministry has approved Rs 7 crore for the project.

Despite several requests, the state government refused to provide 50 per cent of the funds for the construction of the overbridge. "As it will act as a link route between Cantonment and city area, the proposal was raised before the Defence ministry and was later approved," he said. Jaiswal said efforts were being made to lay the foundation of the project before November 15.

Heading: B -School Band - Indian Express
Content:
With P1 and P3 polio cases escalating, experts have decided that the vaccination rounds will take place every three weeks instead of the four to six weeks.

The experts are finding it difficult to formulate a strategy that can combat the outbreak of this virus in western Uttar Pradesh, which has re-entered the state through Bihar.

The next vaccination drive has been scheduled for November 16 for the entire state, three weeks after the recently concluded mop-up round on October 24 in the 18 P1-affected districts of the state.

According to sources, the experts are also planning to conduct a vaccination drive across the state again in mid-December and if required,another mop-up round will take place anytime in between this period.

In comparison with other states, Uttar Pradesh has an uphill task, as it has to keep a check on both the Types — P1 and P3 poliovirus.

"Both Types of virus are rapidly spreading in the state. We are trying our level best to ensure that the children of this state are safe," said Ajay Saxena, coordinator of the Pulse Polio Committee of the Rotary International.

"The dates of the November round have been finalised, though the experts are still undecided which vaccine should be used for this round — Monovalent P1, which will have a better impact on the Type 1 virus or the Trivalent vaccine that will create immunity for all the three viruses Type 1, 2 and 3," said Saxena.

Speaking to The Indian Express, a WHO expert said: "Our plan is to hit the virus with successive rounds. It has already been established that more doses of the vaccine is required to create immunity among the children in UP than in any other part of the world."

According to the recent report of the Polio Surveillance Project, an initiative of WHO, UNICEF, Rotary as well as the Centre, Uttar Pradesh has reported 11 fresh polio cases in the last one week.

Seven of these cases are of Type 3 poliovirus and the remaining of type 1. All the Type 1 cases were reported from western UP — the traditional epicentre of the virus.

This year itself around 254 polio cases have been reported in the state, of which 51 are of wild P1 poliovirus and rest of Type 3.

IEAG meeting on polio may be rescheduled
According to sources, following the spread of the type 1 virus, the Centre is planning to reschedule the meeting of the India Expert Advisory Group on Polio Eradication from December to mid November. The meeting will aim at redefining the eradication strategies and finalising plans for 2009 towards eradication of polio virus in India.

Like otherIIM students have their own hobbies, it isour passion and hobby to pursue in sparetime." On the other hand, the organiserswere also happy with the response theband got. "They were good and even ourmembers gave a good response. We willbe using the amount that we have gotfrom the show for the upliftment of theslum children in the city. We will be givingit to an organisation working for thecause," said Wg Cdr AN Rai (Retd), vicepresident,operations at Genesis Club.

Heading: ANIMATED - Indian Express
Content:
Retired cricketer Jonty Rhodes talks about his new career in wine and his effort to fight global warming

South African batsman Jonty Rhodes, known more for his aggressive play on the cricket field, has smoothly made a transition into business in his hometown, Durban. He is now the director of 10 Chapters, a wine label from Durban. Dressed casually in denims, Rhodes, 39, patiently signed autographs for

fans while promoting his delicious beverage.

Playing cricket, he says, was good while it lasted. "I don't miss the game. I'm involved with it, but there areseveral new, interesting spheres in my life," smilesRhodes, who will be coaching the team Mumbai Indians for the Twenty 20 matches in April next year.

Rhodes is juggling a part-time job as banking executivein one of Durban's multinational banks, along with promotingwine from South Africa all over the world.

"Whatever I know about wine is thanks to my winemaker Stefan Gerber, who educated me about thewine-growing region around Durban. This is the firsttime when I am speaking to various importers and understandingthe market in India. It is fun," he says, inbetween animated discussions of terroir and grapequality.When he isn't strolling through the vines with hiswinemaker, Rhodes prefers surfing, mountain bikingand tackling the issue of global warming, which is closeto his heart."We are in talks with TATA-BP technologies to set upa plant in Durban as the carbon emissions are theirhighest ever. We need to protect the future generationfrom the hazards of global warming. It was since thetime of apartheid that such issues were brushed underthe carpet and we are facing the consequences today," he says, easily slipping into the role of an amateur environmentalist. Eleventh chapter, perhaps?

Heading: Confession? What confession, ask suspected Mujahideen - Indian Express
Content:
North Indian labourer was killed over seat argument, say cops

Two days after a North Indian labourer was murdered by a group of 10 to 12 people in a local train, the Mumbai railway police arrested six people from villages near Khopoli. The police said no political implications were involved and the murder had happened in a fit of rage.

Dharamdev Rai (25), a labourer working with a chemical company in Khopoli, had been murdered on Monday in a local train between Khopoli and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus.

Those arrested on Thursday were Vikas Duttu Wahgmare (26), Manoj Palande (30), Avinash Thombre (24), Ajay Harishchandra Hadap (18), Ketan Kashinath Hadap (23) and Ajay Dilip Hadap (18). Waghmare is from Dolavli village and works as a watchman at a farmhouse; Ajay is a student of the Janta Junior college in Khopoli; Palande and Thombre both live in Mankivli village; the Hadaps are from the Navde village. All villages are in Raigad near Khopoli.

The six were produced before the Kalyan railway court and have been remanded to police custody till November 3. "There will be few more arrests," said Krish Pal Raghuvanshi, Additional Director General (Railway).

Cops refused to comment how they identified the men to arrest. "We received information from local people that led to the arrest," said a senior officer.

"There was no motive behind the murder. The incident occurred in a fit of rage," Mumbai railway police commissioner Ashok Kumar Sharma said. He clarified that there was nothing to suggest that the arrested men had links to any political party. On Wednesday, activists of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) had been among the 17 people detained by railway cops.

Rai and three relatives were attacked by a group of 10-12 men in the local train. Cops said the fight initially started over seats as the four had occupied a window seat, but later turned out to be regionalist fight after the four identified themselves as North Indians. Rai was punched hard which led to a rupture in his liver. He was taken to the B K Dubey Hospital in Badlapur where he was declared dead on admission.

Sensing the gravity of the situation, the case was personally supervised by senior railway police officers. Sharma and DCPm (Central Railway) Vasant Koregaokar had camped at Karjat.

R R Patil, deputy chief minister, has announced ex-gratia to the family of Rai. Rai was married a year ago and is survived by his wife, a daughter and his father.

State explains to Centre
The state government has sent a preliminary report to the Centre about the killing of the North Indian youth not being the result of a hate crime, but because of a scuffle over a seat in the train. Chief Secretary Johny Joseph said that the report had been dispatched to the Union Home Ministry by the state home department and police on Wednesday. The Union Home Ministry had asked for a report. Joseph added that he had not yet received any formal order to inquire into the incident.

Heading: Sports in development: Youth to  play and discuss health, social issues - Indian Express
Content:
Three of 12 suspects retrace statements, say recorded under duress

Three of the 12 suspected Indian Mujahideen (IM) operatives who had given confessional statements moved an application before the special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court on Wednesday retracting their confessions, claiming that they were recorded under duress.

The three accused - Fazal-e-Rehman Durani, Ahmed Bawa Abubakar, and Mohammed Naushad Ali - informed the court that the police forcibly made them sign on some papers, the contents of which they were not aware of, before being produced in front of a magistrate where the confessions were confirmed.

Their defence lawyer Amin Solkar said, "The police remand application has not yet mentioned any specific role of the accused. It only mentions that they were part of the conspiracy to commit terrorist acts by causing bomb blast in Ahmedabad and Surat. The police theory is very unclear till now."

Under MCOCA, a confession given before the police who is of the rank of deputy superintendent is admissible in court unless proven involuntary, provided it is confirmed before a magistrate within 24 hours of its being recorded by the police officer.

The crime branch had arrested Fazal from Pune while Abubakar and Ali were nabbed from Mangalore in a nationwide operation to bust the alleged terrorist module believed to be behind serial blasts. The police have till now arrested 20 alleged IM operatives including software engineer Mansoor Peerbhoy, who is alleged to have sent emails claiming responsibility for the blasts to media houses minutes before the explosions.

Peerbhoy last week moved a plea before the court seeking to be turned an approver. A decision on his application is still pending.

Ali also complained to the court of physical torture by crime branch officials because of which, he claimed, his hearing has suffered. The court directed the police to take Ali to an ENT specialist and submit a report on November 3.

Reacting to these allegations, Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime) Deven Bharti said, "Their confessions were recorded before a Deputy Commissioner of Police and confirmed in court. These allegations are just a strategy after consultation with their lawyer. It will have no effect on our case."

Heading: Drunken man thrown off from flight for misbehaviour - Indian Express
Content:
State, civic body and UNICEF come together to create sports arenas where children can discuss issues like HIV, malnutrition, besides playing

After winning the bid for the 2012 Olympic games, the UK promised to share a part of the funds to promote sports in developing countries, and that money is now beginning to trickle into Maharashtra.

Starting a new project called 'Sports in Development', the state government and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) are collaborating with the UNICEF to use sports to introduce health and developmental concepts among children and youth. The project would be executed through schools and community which will eventually become a place for spreading various social messages. Moreover, it also aims at inculcating team building and leadership qualities among youth which will lead to their involvement in community programmes.

In Mumbai, seven wards would also be implementing the project. "We will be implementing the project along with UNICEF," said Chandrashekhar Rokade, joint municipal commissioner (education).

Currently, coaches are being trained for the purpose. The first such training for 30 participants — including teachers, volunteers and community members—¿ has recently concluded in Chandrapur district. "The idea is to create sports coaches who will not only train children and youth in various sports but spread development messages as well. Sports will be an integral part around which health, education and sanitation messages can be revolved," said Gopi Menon, UNICEF Maharashtra chief. "The plan is to use sports to inculcate team building and leadership qualities," Menon added.

According to the project, the trainers, which include teachers, volunteers and community workers, will be given a sports kit. The plan, eventually, envisages a playground for each village where youth and children can assemble. "It becomes an arena for youth to discuss issues and spread awareness on topics like HIV and malnutrition," said Angela Walker, chief communication officer, UNICEF India.

"We implemented a similar thing in Africa and it really benefited the children there. It was able to break through the social class structures. We found that poor children could use their sports achievement to get into college, or at least they stayed a year longer in school," said Walker. "Moreover, there were other tangible results like community participation, increased use of condoms, and reduction in HIV prevalence," Walker added.

Heading: BARC starts celebration of Homi Bhabha birth centenary year - Indian Express
Content:
A drunken man onboard the Air India flight to New Jersey from Mumbai was offloaded from the plane, after fellow passengers complained that he misbehaved with them. The flight— AI 191— which was supposed to depart from Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA) at 7:45 am for New Jersey's Newark Liberty International Airport was delayed by approximately three hours after the passenger created ruckus on board and was eventually handed over to the Sahar police by the flight's captain.

According to an airport official, the passenger was in a stupor when he boarded the flight. Immediately after boarding the flight he went to the aircraft's washroom where he left his cellphone. When he could not locate his phone he started misbehaving with the passengers as well as the cabin crew.

"The flight was ready to depart and the push-back command had already been given when this particular passenger kept on changing his seats. He also kept shouting at co-passengers, threatening to shoot them," said a spokesperson of the National Aviation Company of India Limited (NACIL) which runs Air India. "His actions were very suspicious and for the safety of passengers the cabin crew reported the matter to the Captain who handed him over to the local police," the airline spokesperson added.

The flight eventually took off at three past 11 in the morning. While there are no written rules or a set of procedures to be followed when it comes to drunken passengers misbehaving on board, a cabin crewmember, told Newsline that they are advised to restrain the passenger if he poses a threat to the people on board or crewmembers. "Usually we restrain them and only ask the ground staff to offload them when they pose a threat to the passengers," said a crewmember.

Senior Police Inspector Dilip Patil confirmed the incident and said the passenger has been sent for a medical check up after which required action would be initiated.

Heading: Journalist beaten up in Kurar village - Indian Express
Content:
To be celebrated till Oct '09; PM inaugurates 4 new projects in and around city through video conferencing, says our scientists, engineers have shown they can compete with world's best

The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) on Thursday celebrated Dr Homi Bhabha's 99th birth anniversary amidst its Founder's Day festivities and also marked the beginning of the Homi Bhabha Birth Centenary Year, which will be celebrated till October 30 next year.

The highlight of the function was a live telecast by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh from New Delhi, which was beamed to all Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) institutions. The PM also inaugurated six new BARC facilities through video conferencing. These include the multi-stage flash desalination plant and the barge-mounted desalination plant — both in Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu; a new training school at Anushakti Nagar in Mumbai; the Critical Facility for Water Reactors and New Hot Cells Facility— both in Trombay and an Electron Radiation Facility in Khargar, Navi Mumbai.

"It gives me great pleasure to begin these celebrations to enter the centenary year celebrations of Homi Bhabha's 99th birth anniversary," said the Prime Minister. "These two sons (Jawaharlal Nehru and Homi Bhabha) were the fathers of our nuclear energy programme," he added.

The PM also gave away four Lifetime Achievement awards in the national capital to Govind Swarup of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), S R Paranjpe of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), S L Kati of the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL) and H S Kamath of the Nuclear Fuel Group. "I congratulate the four distinguished scientists who have been honoured with the Lifetime Achievement awards and wish them more success in the coming years," said the PM, adding that the nation had come a long way since the inception of TIFR in 1945. "Our scientists and engineers have shown that they can compete with the best in the world," he said.

The centenary celebrations are expected to continue throughout the year with the different institutions of the DAE holding various events in the year up to the 100th birth anniversary and the year that follows. "We have an apex committee which has a different convener every year to see to the Founder's Day celebration itself," said R S Bhalerao, who is the convener this year. "We plan to have a drawing competition for the entire DAE family at some time in January, as Homi Bhabha himself was an artist," said J N Kayarkar, registrar, TIFR.

Heading: State to introduce stamp duty amnesty scheme for developers too - Indian Express
Content:
A reporter from the Nirbhay Pathik tabloid, Dinanath Tiwari, was allegedly beaten up by a few assailants while covering an alleged MNS attack on a dairy in Kurar Village on Wednesday.

Tiwari reached the site, Navdurga dairy in Vaishadpada at midnight. He was asking routine questions regarding the attack when a few men present there allegedly assaulted him, said the police. He is currently recovering at Bhagwati Hospital and has filed a complaint in Kurar Village police station.

According to Senior Police Inspector, R Aher of Kurar Village police station, the role of MNS activists in this attack has not been confirmed but the reporter's claim that the assailants were MNS activists has been registered in the complaint. "All we know is that he went to the location and was asking who the culprits were when a few men assaulted him. We have arrested few persons but are still conducting investigations into the matter."

The 8-year-old son of the dairy owner was also injured in the violence.

Heading: Keep politics out of Chhat Puja celebrations, say organisers SHWETA DESAI - Indian Express
Content:
State earned Rs 70 cr from an amnesty scheme for flat owners, announced in June

After an overwhelming response received for its stamp duty amnesty scheme for flat buyers, the state government is now planning to introduce a similar scheme for developers.

All developers, who have not paid stamp duty on Transfer of Development Right (TDR) certificates, development agreements and conveyance, will be allowed to pay the sum sans penalty during the duration of amnesty scheme.

"We have received proposals from various segments asking us to introduce an amnesty scheme for developers who have not paid stamp duty. We are considering the demands as well as looking at all the statutory provisions necessary," said Ramrao Shingare, Inspector General of Registration for Maharashtra, and added that a decision will be taken next week.

Usually, the penalty is 2 per cent of the total duty amount per month from the date of execution of the agreement to a maximum limit of 200 per cent. During the amnesty scheme, developers will be spared the penalty amount and will have to pay the normal 3 per cent of the TDR certificate's value and 5 per cent of the market value of the property in case of conveyance and development agreements.

From the time the amnesty scheme for flat owners was announced in June, it has attracted over 70,000 flat owners across the state and led to a revenue collection of over Rs 70 crore.

"All these cases are predominantly from Mumbai, Thane and Pune," said Shingare. The tremendous response, despite a lack of clarity in the scheme from time to time, has led the state government to extend the scheme for flat owners till the end of November.

Stamp duty experts have termed the state government's move as an attempt to garner in as much as revenue for the state exchequer as possible before the election. "Also, first for flat buyers and now for builders, this comes as a pre-election sop," said Vinod Sampat, advocate and president of the Cooperative Societies' Residents and Users Association.

Sampat added that many developers evade stamp duty under section 3 of the Bombay Stamp Act, even as the government can attach and auction the property in case the developer fails to pay stamp duty on TDR, conveyance or development agreement.

Heading: A peaceful Diwali in city, but western suburbs exceeded deadlines: report - Indian Express
Content:
Union Railway Minister and RJD leader Lalu Prasad Yadav may have commented earlier this year that if possible he would celebrate Chhat puja in Mumbai, but organisers of the puja in the city have appealed to keep politics out of the festival. With Mumbai currently on tenterhooks after the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) launched a fresh tirade against north Indians, organisers of the Chhat Puja are expecitng a low turnout this year.

An estimated 30 per cent of city's 1.3 crore population comprises migrants from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. They usually celebrate the festival on the beaches at Juhu, Madh and Marve. While preparations are on for the puja which will be held on November 4, there is uncertainty over whether many people will show up this year.

"If people want to perform Puja, they definitely should, but no one should try and make it a political 'hungama'. Chhat puja in Bihar and UP are never political. Lalu performs it with his wife in a swimming pool. Has he ever arranged it for his people on a large scale the way it is celebrated in Mumbai?" asked Prem Shukla, Executive Editor of Dopahar Ka Saamna, the Hindi mouthpiece of the Sena.

The religious fest has become the subject of controversy in January this year after MNS chief Raj Thackeray's outburst against the north Indians and mass mobilisation.

Tulsi Singh of the Young Rajput Charitable Trust who has been organising a Chhat puja at Madh Island in Malad for more than five years also echoed similar sentiments. "Why should Chhat Puja have political overtones? Raj is right when he opposes its politicisation though we do not support his violent means," he said. He also said that the Marathi Mitra Mandal and Uttar Bhartiya Sangharsh Samiti together would organise the Chhat Puja in Malad.

While the local north Indians keeping themselves away from the religious fest—preferring to celebrate it privately rather than celebrating on a public platform—following the current situation, the focus is on the migrants. "Performing the Chhat Puja has become more fashionable only recently. We always celebrated it privately at home. So there is no question of going to the beach," said Anilkumar Pandey who has been residing in the city for last 42 years.

The recent Supreme Court order allowing the use of loud speakers for the festival while keeping restrictions on political speeches and entertainment quotient is also bound to keep the festival's low key this year. "There will be no political speeches and entertaintment programmes. The puja will strictly be religious with bhajans and religious songs," said Congress leader Sanjay Nirupam who oragnises Chhat Puja with a group called Bihari Front. "Although I agree that the puja should not be made political, such restrictions should also be imposed on other celebrations like Ganpati and Dahi Handi also. Why discrimination against north Indians?" he asked.

Heading: Two customers dead, 6 injured  as restaurant ceiling caves in - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the global meltdown and the communal tension took its toll on this year's Diwali celebrations, city's suburbs seemed to be in full form, bursting crackers — well into the wee hours— on all three major Diwali nights, revealed a release by the Awaaz Foundation, an NGO working to curb noise pollution in Mumbai.

The report measured decibel levels in the city and suburbs on October 26 and 29. According to the report, while the usually noisy areas like Marine Drive and Worli Seaface abided by the rules, western suburban areas disregarded not just the 10 pm deadline but also the residential or silent zones limits in many areas. Use of banned crackers like sutli bombs and 'serial crackers' were also recorded in several suburban localities, including upmarket areas in Bandra, Khar and Juhu.

"In many of these areas, though public complainted to police control room and local police stations, they paid heed to them," the report said. Sumaira Abduallali, founder-president of the Awaaz said, "Especially, in Bandra and Khar, usually quieter suburbs, serial crackers that exceed the 125db limit and the banned 100-series crackers were found to be used in a silent zone and on public streets. These are areas where crackers are not allowed at all." In many other suburban areas, loud crackers continued to burst till 2.30 am, she said.

However, Hassan Gafoor, commissioner of police, claimed that despite a few sporadic complaints from the western suburbs, an overall implementation of the 10 pm deadline was maintained. "We had deployed more than 100 police personnel at every station to keep a check on noise offenders. Complaints from suburbs were slightly higher, but these suburbs were under control," he said.

Abdullali said that the suspect areas like Marine Drive were very vigilant this year. "There was comparatively less firecrackers from 9 pm to 10.30 pm on sea facing side of the Marine Drive and Worli sea face promenades," she said.

"This indicates that a shift towards community style celebration noticed last year has become more remarkable. Many bystanders did not burst crackers, but enjoyed the spectacle from a distance," she said and added that the government could, in fact, cash in on this trend and encourage a state-sponsored firecracker display during Diwali.

Heading: Man arrested for killing nephew - Indian Express
Content:
Two patrons were killed and six persons injured on Wednesday as the ceiling of Hotel Anand Restaurant and Bar at Lewis Mansion in Prabhadevi caved in due to excess weight of rubble piled up on the floor of a room. The flooring of a room at the second floor was weak and broke down at 8:45 pm on Wednesday.

The impact made the flooring of the first floor cave in as well. Two patrons Siddhesh Raut (24) and Indrajit Yadav died in the incident and six others were injured. All the victims were rushed to the KEM Hospital. The MHADA has sent a team to clear the remaining rubble on an emergency basis. None of the hotel staff was injured. The Dadar police have registered a case of accidental death.

According to sources, Lewis Mansion was due for redevelopment by the Chaitanya Developers in collaboration with one Nandu Naik and one Chopra who had received permission for the same from the BMC, MHADA and SRA. Though all the tenants, except one had vacated the building, the shopkeepers and restaurateurs on the ground floor refused to vacate the building, said sources. The builder could carry out the demolition work only in the upper floors as the businessmen and restauranteurs on the ground floor have filed a case citing that they wished to occupy more space in the building. However, after the incident the commercial establishments were shut fearing a repeat of the accident.

"We wanted to see the plan and we're angry that we will be getting less space than that we occupy at present after redevelopment of the building," said Ashok Bhatkar, the owner of Hotel Anand. "We had filed a case in the court of small causes against the builder," he said. "Finally, we reached an agreement that we would get more vertical space than horizontal space. But, as we have received no written surety , we kept our shops open," said Bhatkar.

"About 15 days ago, the builder said that the MHADA had given him permission to carry out demolition work in the upper floors," said Pravin Zanzeerkar, a shopkeeper at Lewis Mansion.

"A few days ago, we had told him to remove the rubble out of the building. However, he then said that it he would find it difficult to park a truck to do the same since we are on a VIP road," Zanzeerkar added. Chaitanya Developers were unavailable for comment.

Heading: Doctor arrested for selling infant - Indian Express
Content:
A man who murdered his two- and- a- half- year- old nephew in far away Tamil Nadu was arrested here in Mumbai. The officers of LT Marg police station made the arrest on Diwali. The accused Jugnu Jain (33) alias Chandrakant was held from Kalbadevi road near a clothes' shop called after the police received a tip off that a criminal from Chennai was loitering in the area. He confessed to the crime upon interrogation. He has been sent to police custody till Friday and was taken back to Chennai by a police team.

The Tamil Nadu police had been trying desperately to arrest Jugnu but this was difficult as he kept changing his location first going to Kolkata and then to Gaya and Nashik before finally landing in Mumbai. The Tamil Nadu police had even put a reward on. Twenty days back a team from the Chennai police had come in search of the man to Byculla.

Jugnu's motive seems to have been vindictive, as he wanted to settle some scores with his family. Jugnu lived in Chennai and his brother Anand Jain was the owner of a steel company. Jugnu on was unemployed, and used to take money from his sister-in-law Shaila.

On September 25 when his brother was out of town, Shaila refused to lend him any money. He behaved normally and was playing with his nephew Monik. After being denied money by Shaila he told her that he wanted to take Monik for a walk. Shaila not suspecting anything allowed him to do so.

After Jugnu didn't return for a while Shaila called him several times and Jugnu told her that they be returning in half an hour. Jugnu then called Monik's grandmother and told her that he would take Monik to Delhi and kill him.

The family immediately lodged a complaint in Chennai at the Elephant gate police station. A day later they found Monik's bludgeoned body lying on the railway tracks at Tirumale station near Chennai.

Heading: Fake cosmetics worth Rs 5 cr seized, court says destroy them - Indian Express
Content:
A doctor working in a private nursing home in Goregaon was arrested by the Social Service Branch for allegedly selling an infant for Rs 2 lakh. The accused, Dr Avinash Sankhe, was arrested from his residence in Borivali on October 25.

According to the Social Service Branch officials, the arrest came following a complaint filed by Qatar citizen Noora Ali Khalil. "According to the complaint by Noora, she came to Mumbai for the delivery of her daughter who became pregnant before her marriage in 2006. After arriving in the city, Noora got in touch with one Dr Avinash Sankhe," said DCP Sanjay Mohite.

After the delivery, she decided to leave the child behind in the custody of Dr Sankhe since the family wasn't carrying the relevant documents . After leaving the infant in the city, Noora and his daughter went back to Qatar from where they faxed the required documents to Dr Sankhe. However, according to Noora, Dr Sankhe did not get back to the family even after getting the documents and a sum of Rs 1.4 lakh. "In September 2007, Noora's husband came to Mumbai to take his granddaughter back, but at the time Sankhe avoided to meet him ," said an official from the Social Service Branch. 

Finally, in October, the complainant approached Dr. Sankhe again through the Qatar embassy. This time Dr Sankhe told them that the infant was in Surat under the custody of a family and demanded Rs 20,000 as fare to get the baby back to Mumbai. Even after payment, Sankhe did not hand over the child.

"After receiving the complaint, we arrested Sankhe. He told us that the infant was with a family at Eksar Road in Borivali. When we traced the family, we found the 2-year-old in their custody. The y told us that the baby was sold to them for a sum of Rs 2 lakh," said Mohite. The infant has been sent to the children's home in Dongri temporarily. and Sankhe has been remanded to police custody till October 30.

Heading: BMC tanker claims three lives - Indian Express
Content:
Supposed Nivea products worth over Rs 5 crore were seized from a godown in Byculla raising fears that the market might be flooded with such fake cosmetic products.

Based on an application moved by Beiersdorf A G a multinational corporation based in Germany, responsible for manufacturing of personal care products, through Nivea India Privte Limited, the Mazgaon Metropolitan Court recently ordered to destroy the seized goods after taking the samples for testing.

Interestingly the court ordered for the destruction of seized cosmetics before the filing of the charge-sheet by the Crime Branch of the Mumbai police.

According to advocate Avesh Kayser, who appeared for Nivea, fake Nivea products worth over Rs five and half crore were seized following a raid at Great Eastern Mill compound in Byculla in May this year.

The application states that Beiersdorf A G which is incorporated under the laws of Germany, is conducting business activities in India which include manufacturing and distribution of various types of cosmetics, beauty and personal hygiene products through its representative Nivea.

The application states that they are owners of copyrights which include the artistic and literary works of the labels of Nivea Lipcare, Nivea Visage, Nivea for Men, Nivea Crème, Nivea Soft and Nivea Deodorant. Based on a complaint to the Crime Branch filed by Director of Safe Guard Anti Piracy Private Limited, the premises was raided and the suspect Hanif Memon, in-charge of the godown, was arrested.

Subsequently, the police called for Nivea representative Harendrasingh Shahi, who inspected the goods and confirmed that they were in violation of the copyright of the company.

Later the police came to know about another consignment of 200 cartons of infringing goods stored at the same premises and the same drill was repeated.

Since the quantity of goods was too large (678 cartons, 168 boxes, 2304 pieces) to be stored by the police, the same was requested to be kept in the company's custody.

The application states that as per the Copyright Act, the goods seized need to be handed over to the company whose copyright is infringed and the goods need to be disposed of as soon as possible.

Metropolitan Magistrate B N Jadhav in his order has observed that the investigating agency and the Drug Inspector did not have any objection with destroying the spurious cosmetics after taking sample of each cosmetic for material evidence.

According to Kayser the authorities are now awaiting permission from environmental agency to destroy the goods.

Heading: Cheers Pune! Country’s 7th metropolis in the making - Indian Express
Content:
Cheer-leading
Preity Zinta is known to put her heart into whatever she does. And her IPL team, Kings XI, is quite a weakness. The dimpled dame is already preparing for the next season of the game — she has designed salwar-kurtas bearing the Kings XI logo for her women supporters. Preity wants her supporters to make their presence felt on the field and since the IPL matches are to be held in Punjab, she has opted for the traditional outfit, as a short jersey may not go down well with orthodox Punjabis.

Run Vidya, Run
If you're planning a vacation to Wai, expect to spot Vidya Balan there. The cherubic beauty who is shooting in Wai currently has been going for long walks and runs between her shoots, instead of staying holed up in the vanity van. Though the lady prefers her iPod to company, the film crew does not let her head out alone for fear that she will get mobbed. Now, who are they thinking she is? Shah Rukh Khan?

Snip
Unfortunately for Tusshar Kapoor, his most renowned role has been that of a mute. But the actor really does put in a lot of effort into a role. Tusshar, who plays a hair dresser in Golmaal Returns, has not only learnt the ways of a hairstylist by observing celebrity hairstylist Hakim Aalim, but has also acquired a flair for the art. Aalim, who has given Tusshar the various hairdos in the film, agreed to a role reversal when Tusshar insisted that he tried his hand with the scissors. Really cute of Aalim, right?

Heading: Terror suspect was a hardliner whom VHP disciplined - Indian Express
Content:
Pune is set to become the country's seventh metropolitan city, having beaten three other contenders - Chandigarh, Ahmedabad and Lucknow - on five of the eight parameters evaluated in a study by the New Delhi-based ASSOCHAM.

As of now the country's metros are Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkatta, Hyderabad and Bangalore.

The report, titled The 7th emerging metropolitan city in India, was released today. It placed Pune in the number one position in business environment, infrastructure availability, real estate cost and availability, educational institutes and employment opportunities.

Predictably, the city finished low in terms of transportation facilities, financial services and social infrastructure. Overall, though it came out tops making it the strongest contender for being designated the next metro, according to the report. Ahmedabad was next in line, Lucknow third and Chandigarh last among the four tier-2 cities considered.

The study, conducted between October 5 and 25, took into consideration the commercial importance that Pune has been gaining in the last few years as also the need for a seventh metro city given the pressure the existing six face due to rising migrant population, crumbling infrastructure and manpower and space crunch, said Koteshwar Prasad Dobhal, spokesman for ASSOCHAM.

With nine universities, 80-100 private and public institutes and six government-recognised R&D centres, Pune had no trouble bagging the number one position in the education sector.

The report graded Pune the city with the most optimistic business environment, taking into account its share of 32.71 per cent of the total jobs tracked for the period January to June 2008.

The number one position in infrastructure availability may surprise many Puneites. This may be explained by the fact that the study ranked cities on the basis of such aspects as the number of entertainment avenues, malls, multiplexes and star hotels. Here Pune, with 26 malls and multiplexes and 25 star hotels, bettered the other three cities. On the flip side, the absence of a railway junction left Pune at third position in transport facilities. It also lagged behind in literacy, which denied it the top position in social infrastructure. The study took into account the presence of quality institutes, quality workforce and cost of living.

In financial services, where the study considered number and density of offices of scheduled commercial banks, transparency in trading systems and presence of brokerage firms, Pune was third.

Pradeep Bhargava, chairman of the Maharashtra cell of Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), explained how Pune could compete with three major cities and come out tops. He said it can be attributed to the city's proximity to Mumbai, which gives it access to many of the facilities that the capital enjoys, such as the presence of RBI and an international airport. "Also this shows the contribution of private entrepreneurs towards the city's social, educational and cultural infrastructure as against the neglect by the state government towards the city's physical infrastructure," he said.

Unless the infrastructure and other facilities in the city are upgraded, the metropolitan tag will do little for the city other than giving it a place in the pecking order, Bharagava warned. Otherwise, he said, among the four cities only Ahmedabad was capable of offering serious competition to Pune in such an evaluation.

Heading: Police escort on local and northbound trains - Indian Express
Content:
VHP members in Chinchwad remember Sameer Kulkarni (35), the prime accused in the Malegaon bomb blasts, as a hardliner who was at the same time indisciplined.

Kulkarni was arrested on Tuesday for his alleged links with the blasts. He was a full-time worker with the VHP a few years ago but he was removed because he was not following discipline.

Kulkarni, a science graduate, lived at Runal Nets in Bijlinagar, Chinchwad. He ran a computer shop in the building but was not able to manage it properly as he devoted most of his time to the "Hindu cause". When this reporter went to his home on Thursday, it was locked.

Kulkarni also had a reputation for dishonesty. Neighbours said a resident of Chinchwad had ordered a computer from Kulkarni's shop a few months ago but Kulkarni was not able to provide it. The customer then sought his money back and Kulkarni gave him a cheque but it bounced. The customer then filed a complaint against Kulkarni at a local police chowky.

Sources said Kulkarni was in touch with various Hindu groups in Pune. "Kulkarni was very aggressive. He used to study Islam and the Bible too," a source said.

After being sidelined by the VHP, he joined Abhinav Bharat and was posted in Bhopal, where he came in contact with Pragya the sadhvi. Investigators say that Kulkarni was also in contact with retired Major Upadhyay, working president of Abhinav Bharat, who was also arrested on Tuesday in the Malegaon blast case.

Kulkarni's name also appeared during the attack on pastor Peter David Silway of Vineyard Workers' Church on August 25 last year. A few days after the attack, Abraham Mathai, vice-chairman of State Minorities Commission and general secretary of All Indian Christian Council, had named five persons linked to the VHP as being involved in the attack; one of these was Sameer Kulkarni. Pastor Silway's car was stoned by motorcycle-borne youths on the bridge linking Dapodi and Bopodi. The car suffered severe damage and a complaint was lodged with the Bhosari police. Mathai had demanded police action against Kulkarni and the four others.

Heading: Measurement of land for international airport soon - Indian Express
Content:
Following fresh instructions from the Railway Board, the Railway Protection Force has begun deploying teams to escort all northbound trains to enhance security. The Gorakhpur Express on Thursday was the first train to be escorted by an RPF team from Pune.

The Government Railway Police has also been deploying two to three men on all locals on the suburban Pune-Lonavala route and has enhanced security at major stations within the Pune division. Forty additional GRP men have been posted at Pune station alone.

A force of 35 RPF men has been earmarked. "We will escort nine northbound trains from Pune within of our jurisdiction. Each train will have four or five policemen," said R B Rupnawar, divisional security commissioner, RPF. The northbound trains include Pune-Howrah, Mysore Nizamuddin, Jhelum Express, Goa Express, Pune-Patna, Pune-Gorakhpur and Pune-Lucknow.

GRP superintendent (Pune) Vittal Jadhav said at least two GRP men have posted on all local trains after the fatal attack on a youth from UP in a Mumbai local. "Besides Pune-Lonavala locals, we are joining the RPF in patrolling north bound trains," Jadhav said. The forces deployed by the GRP at railway stations during Diwali will not be withdrawn for some more time. Additional GRP force has been drawn from all 'side branches' like control rooms, security branches or local crime branch and deployed for patrolling.

The RPF has also been forced to draw away men from their regular beats that include stations, platforms, seal checking of cargo on the trains, security on the railway yard - to provide escorts on northbound trains. "Duty hours have been extended from eight to 12. We have had no respite since Ganesh Chaturti, for that was followed by Diwali, then the Commonwealth Youth Games and now this," Rupnawar said.

Heading: Strip-search on staff at theft-hit ammo unit, if necessary - Indian Express
Content:
The international airport project has got a push with the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) set to start the process of evaluating the area of irrigated land that can be left out. Regional officer of MIDC (Pune) Purshottam Jadhav, along with district land acquisition officers, will carry out the measurement process in a week's time. "An overall measurement will be conducted and then it will be easy for us to mark out the irrigated land," he said.

Villagers had met the district collector twice and requested him to leave out irrigated land. They were assured that mainly non-irrigated land will be used for the project.

The Maharashtra Airport Development Company will develop the airport while the MIDC will carry out the land acquisition process at the site, about 30 km from Pune.

With nearly 3,330 hectares to be acquired from seven villages, talks are on with the villagers. Jadhav said that the meetings with the collector yielded only positive results and farmers are now at least willing to give up their land. "Negotiations will begin only after they are fully convinced," he said.

District collectorate officials said that along with the airport work, the administration also plans to develop the region that includes construction of roads. Authorities will chalk out airport plans and develop road links simultaneously. The seven villages that will see the development are Chandoos, Shiroli, Waki Budruk, Pimple Budruk, Kiwle, Koregaon Budruk and Wadgaon.

A farmer from one village, under condition of anonymity, said that he had given in writing that he does not want to part with irrigated land. "The collector has assured me that it will be considered," he said. Earlier MADC had submitted the preliminary feasibility report of the 3,332 hectares for which MADC has sought seed money of Rs 200 crore.

Heading: News of serial blasts shake Assamese in city - Indian Express
Content:
Shaken by recent thefts, officials of Ammunition Factory in Khadki, the nation's premier arms production unit, will launch security measures of a kind never seen before. An employee will be stripped to the bare minimum if required to ensure that he is not smuggling out any arms.

AFK security chief Col SN Sabnis said apart from checking a worker from top to bottom, they have also decided to keep a strict vigil at all factory gates and the gates leading to the premises. "Without valid identity cards issued by us, nobody will be allowed to enter the vicinity of the factory. Even if one has some bank card or some multinational company's card, he or she will not be allowed to enter," said Col Sabnis. The four-member defence security core (DSC), which keeps a hawk's eye from the security towers, have been asked to be extra vigilant. "Besides, internal checks at different units and movements of certain employees are being tracked," said Col Sabnis.

The rigorous steps are being taken in view of the increasing incidents of thefts of bullets from the factory premises. On Monday, the city police revealed that they had nabbed a 31-year-old Bholenath Bhegde, a worker with case plant of the AFK, who was trying to sell 20 bullets to a man identified as Nashik Phata. Bhegde, who is in police custody, had smuggled bullets from the factory premises, according to the police.

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajinder Singh said they are investigating the matter and will soon disclose further details. At least five incidents of thefts have been reported in the last six months. While it is generally observed that workers steal bullets in tiffin boxes, in one particular case a worker had stolen bullets in a cycle tube, sources said.

AFK senior general manager AK Agarwal said on Tuesday that they have decided to place assembly section workers under watch. "There seems to be a chain of employees at work. The arms are just passing hands," he said. Agarwal said while the matter is being investigated, tougher security measures will be implemented to put a curb on smuggling of arms.

Heading: ‘Hang culprits... but don’t harass innocent persons’ - Indian Express
Content:
The news of serial blasts that rocked Assam on Thursday, have sent shivers among the Assamese students in the city. A word from home was all they wanted to hear. The tension was palpable as students huddled to each other.

"Phone networks are jammed. No mobilephones are contactable. I am worried about my family as I haven't been able to contact them since morning. I first got the news from a friend and they said the situation is heated up. The only way I can keep myself updated is through news channels," said Krishna Rajkhowa of Lakhimpur near Guwahati, a student of ISBM. "I will stay with a friend from Assam today, so that if any news from home will be accessible to both of us," Rajkhowa said.

"Going by the news channels, the areas that have been affected by the blasts are just one or two kilometres away from my home. Till now, I just know that all in my family are safe. But I don't have any news of my other relatives and friends as all telephone lines are jammed. Maybe, I will go online and try to get in touch with them over instant chat or e-mail," said 29-year-old Kamal Kumar Tanti, a software professional.

As news channels flash visuals from blast scenes, they only add to the tension. Says another software professional Amanyabarta Chakraborty, "the visuals and reports on the channels and internet sites are disturbing. The blasts seem massive and caused enormous damage to life and property. My family has informed that the situation is tense there. At the moment, we are concerned about the life of our loved ones."

A mall manager in Camp, Sadiqur Rehman who is from Jorhat said, "The loss of innocent lives is irrecoverable. All we want to do now is to ensure whether our dear and near ones are safe."

"I have been trying to call home since morning, but could not reach my family. Finally, in the afternoon, my brother called up and assured that everyone in my family was safe," said Mahen Konwar a scientist at IITM.

Heading: Diwali buzz: Rlys earns Rs 3 crore - Indian Express
Content:
"Now, liberal Muslims are also being targeted and put behind bars... I am not only concerned about the educated and progressive Muslims, who are not in any way connected to terrorist or fundamentalist activities, but also about the message going to Hindus in this country, of whom I believe 90 per cent are secular. If these 90 per cent secular Hindus start believing that liberal Muslims are also involved in terrorism, the country won't be far away from a civil war…"

This reaction from a history professor in Poona College sums up the mood at the institution in the backdrop of the arrests of educated Muslim youths in connection with the bomb blasts. Some of the accused were allegedly said to have connected to Poona College.

However, Mohammed Qudratullah, principal of Poona College categorically denied that the arrested youth were in anyway connected to the Poona College. "The persons you refer to were not in Poona College at any point in their career," he said.

If you visit Poona College, everything seems to be normal. But when you start talking to some of the faculty members, you get a sense of disillusionment in their reactions.

The faculty is vociferous about the issue even as they request anonymity. "Culprits should be hanged in public, but at the same time innocent persons should not be tortured unnecessarily," said a professor.

"We agree that some fundamentalists exist in the society. But now as the innocent educated people are being caught, it seems progressive Muslims will also be targets," said the history professor.
