While the Worli-Haji Ali section is currently in the tendering stage, a joint venture of Arup-CES has been given the job of carrying out a feasibility study to explore alternative alignments for the Haji Ali-Nariman Point stretch. The alternatives included the proposed tunnel and a sea-side road built on reclaimed land. "The report is still to be submitted by the consultants. It would suggest whether a sea link or a road or a tunnel will be best for this section. The report is expected within a week," Anil Deshmukh, Minister of Public Works, told Newsline.

On the CM's announcement regarding the tunnel, the PWD minister added that although the report is awaited, the government believes it would be better to opt for a tunnel from Haji Ali junction to Nariman Point or a tunnel from Haji Ali to Bhulabhai Desai Road and a flyover from there to Nariman Point, since a sea link which would alter the view from the Marine Drive precinct significantly. It is also believed that if a sea link is opted for the section it would jeopardise the Chhatrapati Shivaji statue project.

Meanwhile, in a release on various achievements of the government as it completes four years, the Chief Minister's office stated that in a bid to make Mumbai a world class city, around Rs 35,000 crore has been spent on various transport and infrastructure projects in the city.

Heading: Lonavala rave party: Chargesheet  soon, no sparing officials, say cops - Indian Express
Content:
The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) on Friday issued notices to the state Director General of Police, additional chief secretary (home) and other senior police officials of Mumbai and Thane district, directing them to explain the recent untoward incidents and the reasons behind the attacks on north-Indians at different parts of the state.

The notices were issued by SHRC chairman Kshitij Vyas after the Samajwadi Party (SP) filed a petition regarding violence against North Indians, alleging total collapse in the law and order situation in the state. The petition was filed by SP Youth Wing regional president Farooq Ghosi, and the respondents have to file their reply on November 17 before the Commission.  

However, Ghosi in his petition has not named the Raj Thackeray-led Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) for being behind the attacks, and has just levelled allegations against the state.

The petition mentions various incidents of violence that took place in October, including the recent shootout on a BEST bus and the killing of two members of a north-Indian family at Pisavali village in neighbouring Thane district. The petition prayed that the SHRC direct the state government to provide adequate protection to those who are vulnerable and action be taken against the culprits.

Heading: Greenfield airport: state govt in race with time - Indian Express
Content:
Two months after the Lonavala police broke up a party at a private bungalow in a hill-resort and arrested 22 customs officials, along with 11 bar dancers, on charges relating to obscenity, police will filed a chargesheet in the case in a couple of days.

"We will frame charges against all the 22 officials, 11 bar dancers and seven others under section 292 of the Indian Penal Code relating to obscenity and also book them under sections 65 and 66 B of the Prohibition Act. We will file the chargesheet in Wadgaon Maval court, which is expected to open in the next couple of days after the vacation," said Sudam Darekar, Senior Police Inspector, Lonavala police station.

Acting on a tip-off, Darekar had led the raid along with officials from the Pune Rural police's Local Crime Branch in the wee hours of August 27. They had entered the bungalow at a resort in Lonavala to find bar dancers allegedly dancing and a pornographic movie playing on a laptop. The police had also nabbed two DJs playing the music, four 'organizers' of the party as well as a driver and a caretaker of the bungalow.

"While the caretaker is in our custody, we traced the owner of the bungalow to Mumbai. It was, however, established that he had bought the bungalow only a couple of days prior to the party and did not have any role to play," said Darekar, stressing that the chargesheet includes no new names besides the 40 accused arrested during the raid.

"There is no question of any of the officials being exempted from the charges. They have been booked for indulging in acts of 'obscenity', which is against the law. We had seized the CDs containing pornographic films as well as the laptop, all of which are crucial evidence. The fact that the accused are Government servants is an aspect of the case that can't be ignored," said Darekar.

"Besides, the caretaker did not possess any document allowing the place to be used as a dance bar and hence he was arrested. We also found several bottles of foreign liquor being served there without a permit and hence have booked the accused under the Prohibition Act as well," he added.

The police had also seized Rs 55,000 in cash from the spot. "At the time of the raid there were currency notes strewn all over the place and it was obvious that that those attending the party had thrown them at the dancers. During the investigation we found that over Rs 1.9 lakh was spent in organising the party, including cost of procuring dancers, the rent for the bungalow and the drinks," said Darekar.

Heading: ChildLine Foundation to reach 310 districts by 2011 - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure that the work on the ambitious Greenfield airport at Navi Mumbai is started as per the schedule- April 2009, the state government has made a strong pitch to the Centre for the Coastal Management Zone (CMZ) regulations to come into force or the prevailing coastal regulation zone (CRZ) rules to be modified to enable its construction.

Of the 2,100 hectare of land required for the airport, around 115 hectare falls in the eco- sensitive CRZ I (i) zone. In a meeting at the Prime Minister's Office in New Delhi on October 10, senior state government official pressed on the demand to ensure that the airport completion sticks to its earlier deadline.

Mumbai is expected to see around nine crore air travellers annually by 2030 and the existing international and domestic terminals at Sahar and Santacruz are expected to cater to around 4 crore travellers annually. The Navi Mumbai airport, with two parallel runways and an estimated cost of over Rs 9,970 crore is expected to augment the capacity. It is scheduled to have a construction period of 3.5 years. Though the state has received an approval from the union cabinet for the airport, no CRZ clearance has been received.

Heading: BMC to install electronic water meters in city - Indian Express
Content:
The ChildLine India Foundation, an organisation for the welfare of street children, will soon finalise plans to launch itself in 310 cities and districts across India by 2011-2012, supported by the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) in the Eleventh Five Year Plan.

The organisation, which provides the toll-free 1098 helpline for street children all over India is looking to reach at least half of the total number of districts in India by the end of the plan.

The move was made as per the stipulations set by the Ministry of Women and Child Welfare in its Child Protection initiatives included in the plan.

"The government's plan was to reach all 596 districts in India but we decided that with the budgetary provisions it would be better to start by hitting 310 or so," said Nishit Kumar, head, awareness and advocacy, Child Line India.

The organisation is India's response to UN's Convention on the Rights of the Child and is the nodal agency for all child help lines in India, providing a link between the Ministry and various NGOs.

While the organisation has already begun a 'need assessment' process across 20 cities and towns across the country in order to map out resources for children in these areas, the ICPS proposal for the entire expansion process is still awaiting the cabinet committee's approval. The process will help develop a resource directory and identify NGOs from various areas. 

 "We are trying to structure a model and have a ChildLine advisory board that has representatives from different fields. It is a three to six month process," said Kumar, adding that this phase is without any budgetary support from the government. He also said that once the ICPS is passed, it will be easier for the expansion process to continue.

ChildLine currently receives around 45,000 calls a month and 1500 calls a day, in Mumbai only. Nationally, the organisation receives 6000 calls a day and two million calls a year and the number is expected to jump to 20 million a year once the expansion process is completed.

The organisation is also looking to segregate its tele-counselling and outreach systems, which will result in a more streamlined approach as far as rescue operations are concerned. The model was piloted in Mumbai, where the voice aspect and intervention were segregated to upgrade the level of response.

Sources in the Ministry of Women and Child Development say that budgetary support for expansion of ChildLine services will be made available once the Integrated Child Protection Scheme is launched.

Heading: Central Railway plans 12 car trains on Harbour line - Indian Express
Content:
Weeks after corporators in Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) raised a storm over water crisis gripping the city and the problem of water wastage due to leakages, the BMC is all set to install electronic water meters known as Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) systems in the city.

The civic body claims that this is a first-of-its kind move by any municipal corporation in the city. As part of a pilot project, the civic body will install water meters in each zone falling under it. The BMC has invited three companies for the pilot project — Actaris and Sapple from France, and Arad.

At present, the BMC will install 3000 water meters in the city, western suburbs and eastern suburbs.

The civic body believes that these water meters will bring some respite to consumers, who at times end up shelling out a lot of money as water tax. "Consumers will know exactly how much are they charged for water. We hope to bring down complaints from consumers who claim that they shell out exorbitant amounts on water. Also with these meters, the administration will know exactly how much water the city gets," said Additional Municipal Commissioner, Anil Diggikar.

The work on the pilot project is expected to start within a year. The civic body has pegged the amount for the pilot project at Rs 20 crores. If the pilot project is successful, it will shell out an additional amount of Rs. 800 crores.

The civic body claims that these water meters will drastically reduce cases of leakages and water theft. "These meters are made of very strong material and cannot be tampered easily. They are strong, long-lasting, and tamper-proof," said Diggikar. Another plus for these water meters is that they will make for accurate meter reading. "These meters cannot be manually manipulated. Hence it will provide the customers with accurate bills," said Diggikar. What's more, the civic body will install these meters in all areas.

From high-pressure areas to low pressure areas, from elevated areas to slums, this will help BMC to check the feasibility of all the three kinds of meters in all the areas.

The decision, however, has not impressed all the corporators, who claim that the civic body should first arrange for continuous supply of water and then come up with these techniques. "What purpose will these water meters solve, if there is no proper supply of water? While our lakes and reservoirs are overflowing, we are still grappling with water shortage. This problem needs to be addressed first," said Congress corporator, Vinod Shekhar.

"The BMC should first make sure that we get proper water supply, then it should make sure that all water meters remain in working condition. Most of the times, the civic body does not maintain these meters after installation. We should seriously be working towards that," said BJP corporator, Yogesh Sagar.

Heading: Children worst hit by eye injuries this Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
CR carries out a feasibility study; to also conduct trials on the Thane-Nerul line, services to start soon

 

The Central Railway (CR) is planning to introduce 12 car train services on the Harbour Line for which it is conducting a feasibility study.

 "We are conducting a feasibility study for introducing 12 car services on the Harbour Line," confirmed Sriniwas Mudgerikar, chief spokesperson for the CR. "Introducing 12 car services on this line is the need of hour as the areas on this line are experiencing rapid urbanisation. Satellite cities like Navi Mumbai and Panvel are seeing a demographic change. Plus, introducing fast train on these services has still not been conceptualised and introducing 12 car train services is the only option," said a senior rail official.  

Currently 12 car services, which include the new swanky rakes, run on the main line of the CR- mostly on the stations beyond Kalyan.

The feasibility report is required to be done as the current platforms on the Harbour Line are meant for 9 car trains. If 12 car trains are introduced it would be a daunting task for the railway because almost all the platforms are meant for the 9 car trains and needs to be extended.

The Harbour Line, which runs parallel to the Thane creek starts from the CST to Panvel and from Turbhe to Nerul and has over 29 stations. There are many stations like the Sandhurst Road, Cotton Green and Reay Road which are built on an elevated deck. But only 9 car train can run on it as platform is one if the issues. 

"We are also conducting trials on the Thane-Nerul services which should also start soon," added Mudgerikar. The CR had completed the work on the Thane-Nerul last month. Currently, another section on the Harbour line commences from Thane terminates at the Vashi station, but it would now terminate at Nerul as well.

Plans to extend the service from Thane to Panvel is also in store.

Heading: Youth found dead in Virar resort - Indian Express
Content:
The festival of lights once again has resulted in high number of eye injuries in the city. On Wednesday and Thursday, children who have been the predominant victims flocked the out patient department of hospitals across Mumbai. "This year there were no serious cases of burns and eye injury. All patients were treated on OPD basis," said Dr Sanjay Oak, dean King Edward Memorial hospital, Parel.

However there were some cases of serious burn injuries to the eye. Fireworks revelry turned into a nightmare for eight-year-old Jagatbandhu Tripathi when soot went inside his right eye. "He was not bursting crackers. After Laxmi Pujan, he went to see the fireworks in the compound; a firecracker burst next to him and the soot went into his right eye. Things worsened as he rubbed his eye," said Krishnagupta, Jagatbandhu's father. He adds, "Like how tobacco selling is banned for minors, even selling crackers should be banned. Also one elder person should be there while bursting crackers."

Jagatbandhu was rushed to Sion Hospital and after primary treatment, he was admitted to Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital. "T he boy sustained thermal injury and the whole outer surface of the eye was damaged. Also the stem cell is damaged," said Dr Vandana Jain, head of department and consultant, Cornea, cataract and refractive surgeon, Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital. 

"Currently he is on medication to reduce the pressure as it is grade four thermal burns with total limbal stem cell deficiency. He can barely see objects. He will need repeated surgery but only after his pressures come under control," said Dr Jain. According to city ophthalmologists, some children suffered injuries while burning used crackers on the last day of Diwali. "Two cases of minor injuries were also brought in last week where splinters burnt the cornea of the patient," added Dr Jain.

Heading: No more darkness while waiting for rescue - Indian Express
Content:
The youth had checked in alone in the resort, say police

 

The body of a 20-year-old youth found inside a resort room has left the cops baffled. The deceased, identified as Shailendra Ramshankar Shukla, was a resident of Manvelpada area in Virar.

Shukla allegedly committed suicide by hanging himself in a room at a resort in Rajwadi near the Arnala beach.

The body was spotted on Thursday morning by the manager of the resort, who then informed the police. The youth had checked in alone at the resort, which is usually frequented by picnicking groups on weekends.

 According to Deputy Superintendent CA Chowghule (Vasai division), "The body was found by the manager of the resort who had gone to inquire about the youth who had checked in alone. When the door to his room was not opened even after repeated knocks, the management broke open the door to find Shukla hanging from the ceiling. He had used a bed-sheet to hang himself."

Alarmed by the sight, the hotel staff alerted a police chowky at Arnala. 

On reaching the spot, the police found certain phone numbers on a piece of paper inside the deceased's pocket. "After calling the numbers on the piece of paper, we managed to trace his family and his address," said Chowghule. The police also found that his parents had filed a missing person's complaint with the Virar police a day before his body was discovered.

"On questioning, his parents informed that Shukla had left home at 9:30 on Wednesday night after telling them that he was going out for an ice-cream. When he did not return after a long time, the parents tried to call him up, but he did not answer their calls. Worried, his parents approached the Virar police and filed a missing persons' report," added Chowghule.

As per Chowghule, though there was no suicide note found inside the resort room where the body was found, investigators suspect that a love affair might have been the reason behind the suicide.

"We have no evidence to suggest this so far. We are conducting further inquiries to find the motive behind the suicide and are also questioning his friends and other acquaintances to find out if he was suffering from depression," said Chowghule.

Heading: Patient records in civic hospitals to be computerised soon - Indian Express
Content:
LED-based emergency lights are on their way

It's a train commuters' nightmare. Power connections getting severed plunging coaches into darkness after a minor mishap or a derailment at night, compounding the panic of people waiting for the rescue van.

The Railway board has decided to end all that. A decision has been taken to install emergency lights in coaches of outstation trains. The devices, which make use of Light Emitting Diodes (LED), would be switched on automatically in case of any mishap.

Tenders for the emergency lights opened on Friday and will be decided within a month.

Chief Design officer (electrical), Railway board, on behalf of the Chief electrical engineer, in a recent order had asked all 16 zonal railways to issue tenders for LED-based emergency lights. In any accident or derailment of trains, these lights will switch on automatically. The approximate cost of installing the lights will be Rs 400 crore.

According to Western Railway sources, as per the board's direction, WR is inviting a bid for around 5,200 units of LED-based emergency lights, with a reserve cost of Rs 4 crore. A condition has been set that these lights should be manufactured either by Seoul Semiconductors, or Nichia Corporation of Japan.

"This (emergency LED lights) is a new concept for Indian Railways. During mishaps at night, passengers panic in the darkness. This arrangement (emergency lights) will be for the convenience of passengers," said an official of the Western Railway.

"Each of these LED-based emergency lights weigh around 10 kg," said a source at the WR. Shyam Sunder Gupta, Chief Public Relations Officer, WR, had earlier confirmed that tenders would open on Friday. "The emergency lights will be installed in the four corners of each coach," said Gupta.

Heading: Crowd sets three coaches of Ranchi-LTT express on fire - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is all set to computerise health care systems in civic hospitals in the city. The move has been taken to facilitate the tedious data gathering process of patients information.

As part of its e-governance process, the civic body aims to connect all its hospitals. Precious time is often lost in the process of information gathering and the civic body now hopes that the move will reduce the time lapse and help patients.

At present, the civic body is starting the project on a small scale. Kishore Gajbhiye additional municipal commissioner said, "As part of the pilot project, we first take up the plan in seven to eight medical units in the city. They would include Sion Hospital, Bhabha hospital in Bandra, maternity homes and some dispensaries." BMC claims that all the information gathered through the process will be kept confidential. "We will also make sure that no information especially sensitive information is leaked out," added Gajbhiye.

With this centralised system, information about a patient can be stored in a single file and the same file can be accessed from other units that uses the same technology. "A patient's personal information and his medical history will stay in a system for 6 to 8 weeks. The same will be archived for the next 5 years too," said vice-president of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) Suresh Mhatre. The company will be helping out the civic body in this initiative. 

Explaining the technology behind the system, Mhatre stated that data upto three tetra bytes, that is 3,000 giga bytes can be stored. Back up system will also be created. The hardware of the system will be at Worli. "There will be a system where the data of the result will be made available online too. Each doctor will have a personal code from which he will have access to the file of a patient," explained Mhatre.

The civic body is spending Rs 84 lakh on this pilot project, with Rs 5.5 crore spent only on the software.

Heading: Man held for looting women by posing as cop - Indian Express
Content:
Yet another incident of damaging railway property took place on Wednesday when some coaches of the weekly Ranchi-LTT express were put on fire. The incident occurred when the train was about to depart from Ranchi.

According to sources a crowd ignited three coaches of the train and also damaged two of its coaches. Officials at the Ranchi station managed to attach three spare coaches and the train reached Mumbai only with 21 coaches (two coaches less).

The 8609 Ranchi- LTT express departs from Ranchi at 9 pm on Wednesday and reaches LTT Mumbai at 12.05 pm on Friday.

A source at LTT said, "This was a protest against Raj Thakre and also what a result of , what is happening in Mumbai.But today, when this train reached Mumbai , two coaches were less.  It created lot of problem to the officials of Mumbai division as from Mumbai to Ranchi, there is a lot of rush."

JN Lal, Divisional Railway Manager, Central Railway, Mumbai division said, " For the convenience of the passengers, we have arranged two coaches for this train (8610), which will depart from LTT at 3.50 pm on Saturday."

Heading: Bright sun kept air pollution on Diwali in check - Indian Express
Content:
Cops say accused, a hardened criminal, used to impersonate with confidence; recently looted ornaments worth Rs 28,000 from a 73-year-old woman

The Kandivali police have arrested a man who looted an elderly woman of her gold bangles worth Rs 28,000 by pretending to be a policeman.

Faizal Shaikh (50), a resident of a slum near Ambivili station, and his two accomplices known so far only as Muhammad and Iqbal approached Chandrakanta Shah (73) on Friday near Kandivali station while she was going to a temple. They told her that there was some sort of a disturbance ahead and it would not be safe for her to keep wearing the gold bangles. They then said that they were policemen and advised her to put her ornaments in her purse and on the pretext of helping her spirited them away.

Shah only realised this when she reached home, and later filed a complaint at Kandivali police station. On Saturday, the police arrested Shaikh from near a restaurant close to Kandivali police station based on a tip off received by DCP M Ranade of Zone 11. The police have recovered Shah's bangles.  

Shaikh has been charged with cheating and impersonating a public servant. He is also named in two other cases in the jurisdiction of the Kandivali police. These cases include duping a woman of her jewellery worth Rs 60,250 and another in which he stole Rs 33,000 from a customer of HDFC bank's Mahavir Nagar branch through sleight of hands. Shaikh's police custody ends on Friday and the Kandivali police said they would be approaching the court to increase it. "Shaikh is a hardened criminal and used to impersonate a police officer with confidence. He used to frequently prey on elderly women as they are quite gullible," said Senior Police Inspector S Jaiswal.

"In the HDFC Bank case, he dressed up as a bank employee and approached customers who were about to make deposits. Since customers now need to write down the numbers printed on Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes, he would offer to help them count them. And in the process, he would quickly fold few notes in his hand and a keep them in his pocket," he added.

"Though he looks unclean now, he would be the very picture of a helpful bank employee and would completely fool his victims," Police Inspector (Crime) S Vede said.

"We believe he is wanted in similar cases in Kalyan, Malad and Nagpada and he may even be wanted in the attack on the Thane Crime Branch vehicle in the area a month ago," Vede added.

Heading: 100th year of existence, but Diwali ank gets lukewarm response in the state - Indian Express
Content:
Noise pollution may be the immediate villain in Diwali revelry but the visible smog hanging low over the city tells a different story. Experts say that more harm may be caused due to the air, solid-waste and soil pollution that the city was exposed to during Diwali.

According to Professor Shyam Asolekar, head of the Centre for Environmental Science and Engineering, IIT-Mumbai, "Noise pollution is a significant — but not the only — outcome of Diwali celebrations. The poisonous gases expelled during combustion of firecrackers affects respiration. The particles of metallic dust, known as particulate matter are suspended over the surface causing several health problems. The chemicals and paper waste are highly toxic and pose a solid waste problem. "

The Ambient Air Quality measured on the three Diwali days (from October 28 to 30) released by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) on Friday, however, is heartening. The data reveals that the Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) levels in the western suburb (Bandra) and eastern suburb (Mulund) only minimally exceeded the normal level of 200 microgram per cubic meter.

On October 28, Bandra recorded 262 microgram per cubic meter of particulate matter, 62 units above normal while Mulund recorded 208 microgram per cubic meter, just eight units above normal. On October 29, the figures rose to 285 and 236 respectively and further more on October 30, to 339 and 238 microgram per cubic meter in western and eastern suburbs respectively. In Navi Mumbai, Vashi reported a high particulate matter level at 359 microgram per cubic meter on October 28.

However, Dr Ajay Deshpande, regional officer (Air), MPCB, cautioned, "The report shows no significant increase in air pollution but that may not be an indicator pointing a decrease in use of fire crackers. This Diwali the low levels of air pollution may have more to do with the existing climatic condition."

Dr Deshpande explained that in sunny weather the thin air carris pollutants upwards, thereby clearing the ground level atmosphere.

"This year, October has been rather humid. Had winter set in properly, the fine particulate matters would have hung low. But due to ample sunshine in Mumbai, the vertical transportation of air is easy," explained Dr Deshpande. MPCB officials said that the vehicular pollution in the city has always kept the mono-nitrogen oxides (NOx) and the Sulphor dioxide (SO2) high.

Pointing at the need for a regulation to control the ambient air levels and the waste contamination caused during Diwali, Asolekar said, "Solid waste and air pollution often has a long term impact and these need to be considered as important consequences of use of firecrackers."

Heading: Let’s talk about stocks - Indian Express
Content:
More and more couples are opting for television-free lives

Kishore Majgaonkar has vivid memories of the day his wife, Lalita, unplugged the television and put it away on the loft 12 years ago. "There was too much time being spent watching television even though the only channels being telecast back then were DD1 and DD2, and that annoyed her no end," laughs Kishore. The Majgaonkar household has not since bothered to reinstate "idiot box" and nor do they miss it. The Majgaonkars may have been "unusual" a decade ago but today, they won't find themselves alone as many young couples are following suit and ditching the idiot box for" a better lifestyle". When Richa and Mohit Kathuria got married ayear ago, one of the three TVs owned by the joint family was promptly moved to their room.

Though busy with their careers, they would spend their free time flipping through the channels. But after a few months the TV went for repair and they never bothered to bring it back into their bedroom. "Today, it shocks me when over family get-togethers, which are anyway rare, people prefer to discuss TV shows than chat up—it's becomea tool of judgement," remarks Mohit.

Like the Kathurias, Jinita and Himanshu Kode also happened to chance upon this phenomenon. After moving into a new apartment, the couple postponed the purchase of a TV set due to financial constraints but realised that they don't really miss it. "Not only have we invested that money but also our time," says Jinita, as she readies to leave for a weekend trip to Alibaug. "I think we would have wasted this weekend watching TV if we had one."

A few couples, on the other hand, took calculative measures to throw the "evil" out of their lives.

Prapti Dangwal and Sandeep Suvarna are one. They have planned to get rid of their TV before they get married next year. Dangwal, an advertising professional, was a TV buff but decided that they had to do away with the "junk box" because, given their work schedules, they cannot afford to compromise their couple time. She does miss TV at times but makes up for it by watching films on her laptop. But it was no big deal for Dinesh Narayanan, a media professional, when he decided to junk his set in 2000 — it was eating into his reading time. However, he wasn't sure how his fiancé would react to a television-free lifestyle. But

Archana Choudhary played a sport and decided to test it out only to realise that it gives her enough time to cook and pursue singing — activities she thought she never had time for. Jinita too, claims that her culinary skills can be attributed to the missing TV set.

The couples accept that there are times.when they miss the tube, "especially when there's important news or an interesting match on" but Choudhary sums up the benefits when she remarks, "We are better off than others — at least our lives aren't ruled bycommercial breaks".

Heading: Talking point  with  Rajeshwari Sachdeva - Indian Express
Content:
The Gul & Tulsian Show

CNBC Awaaz
Saturday, 9:30 pm
Rating***

What's it about? As the global economy suffers one of the worst meltdowns in history, the faces of shocked investors at Dalal Street plaster every magazine and newspaper. We all know what these faces look like. They look a lot like us— discussing stocks with friends while taking cigarette breaks, passing by on pavements, or in between jumping in and out of crowded local trains. Everybody is worried about their money. Will the market recover from this blow? Will we ever see our money again? These are question on everybody's lips. And in such a time, CNBC Awaaz has identified the need of the hour and responded with The Gul & Tulsian Show— a talk-show that promises to give investors, traders and players the right advice to guide them towards risk-free investments.

Who's in it? The CNBC team brings together Gul Teckchandani, Chief Investment Officer of Sun F&C Asset Management Company, a big player in the mutual fund industry, and S P Tulsian, of sptulsian.com and editor of Premium Investments. The two financial experts debate it out at a coffee table along with the anchor and a guest.

What's hot? Virtually every sector has taken a beating this time around and investors are worried about whether or not the government or somebody else can bail them out. Teckchandani and Tulsian are clued into the latest bulls and bears and they also seem well in tune with the ethos of the common investor on the street. The two analysts discuss the problem at large giving investors the bigger picture as well as analyse sectoral trends. Listening to them one could know what a Merrill Lynch or a Morgan Stanley is really thinking. They also put things in context, at times citing moments of similar crisis in the past and the lessons learnt.

What's not? As theories are propagated and suggestions made, the cacophony sometimes descends into the din one imagines inside the stock-exchange or the your everyday commute. There is also an over-abundance of market-jargon and name-throwing assuming the common viewer to be well-versed in such matters. A show on the stock-market is no more a niche or special interest programme, and some lucidity in the discussions would be helpful.

Should you be watching it? In times like these, everybody's a self-proclaimed investment guru. But it's important to get the 'low-down' straight from the horse's mouth. And this duo is one of the best in the stable. The show is certainly worth it.

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
The actress spills the beans on reality shows

What is the format of your new reality show Jalwa 1 2 Ka 4?
The show involves singing, acting and dancing. A theme will be given to the contestants and they'll have to create an act around it.

Will the scripts for the acts be created by the contestants?
We'll obviously have some help from scriptwriters, but we'll have to do a lot of work ourselves.

Do you think that increasingly the reality shows are scripted?
My first reality show was Nach Baliye. Back then we were all so new to the idea. We had no idea what to do, so everything was fresh. We didn't cook up anything. But by the end, we'd figured out what works and what doesn't. It's the same now. People see what worked before and they go ahead and try out those same formulae. But I wouldn't blame the contestants entirely. It also depends on the questions that they're asked on the show by the hosts or the judges. If a certain kind of question is asked, everyone will react the same way, so it looks scripted.

Do you think that's why there's an audience for such shows?
If a person is revealing their innermost thoughts on the screen, then of course people want to see it. It's natural. As for whether these people can control themselves on screen, it's very difficult. They come on the show thinking that they can master their emotions, but trust me, it's very difficult. The first day of rehearsals and they're bawling their hearts out. And that baring of emotions |is something that everyone, unwittingly or otherwise, is very attracted to.

You're also starring in another show. Tell us about that.
I have a cameo on Meet Mila De O Rabba. It's a very spicy cameo. But I won't reveal more than that. You have to watch the show to find out more.

And how about a music album?
Making a music album is hard work and I haven't gotten down to creating a new one. But as soon as I get a good idea, I'll start working on it.

Any chances of seeing you with your husband Varun Badola on screen?
Not in the near future.

Content:
Upsets second seeded Rian in U-10 final; Karan, Jinisha win U-12 crowns

Third seed Aryan Goveas was the toast of the finals as he rallied to a thrilling 6-4, 4-6, 7-6 (7-1) victory over No. 2 seed Rian Pandole to clinch the boys under-10 title, in the Vazirani All India Talent Series Tennis Championship, which concluded at the Vazirani National Sports Academy, Nerul on Friday.

After Pandole kept his hopes alive by snatching the second set, Goveas recovered from a 2-5 deficit in the third and deciding set to seal a memorable victory via the tie-breaker in the closest contest of the day.

Pandole broke Goveas at 15 in the crucial sixth game for a 4-2 lead and held serve in the next game to set himself up for the first of two titles.

Pandole then reached match point in the eighth game on Goveas' serve but he squandered the golden opportunity as the latter held serve.

An inspired Goveas broke Pandole at 15 in the ninth game to close in at 4-5 and held serve to draw level at 5-5.

From a position of despair, Goveas broke Pandole in a dramatic 11th game after trailing 0-30 and 30-40 as Pandole hit wide after the first deuce.

But Pandole remained in the fray by breaking back for 6-6 as he fired two brilliant double backhand down-the-line winners to force the tie-breaker.

A confident Goveas though raced to a substantial 5-1 lead in the tie-breaker before taking the match away.

Error-prone Rian

"I just tried to keep the ball in play and allowed Rian to make the mistakes. I also was more consistent and that turned the match in my favour," said a relieved Goveas after the match.

Boys under-12 sixth seed Karan Mehta denied Pandole his second title of the day following a hard-fought 7-6 (7-3), 6-3 triumph in a keen final.

Overcoming scorching heat and fatigue after enduring challenging encounters over the last two days, a gallant Pandole stretched Mehta in the opening set before losing his way in the tie-breaker, while Mehta took an early lead in the second set to seal the set and match.

Top seeds Jinisha Patel and Ria Vardhan claimed the girls under-12 and under-10 titles, while No.1 seeds Poojan Desai and Sanjeevani Patil bagged the boys and girls under-8 titles, respectively.

Girls under-12: 1-Jinisha Patel (Mah) bt 4-Mahrukh Kokni (Mah) 6-3, 6-1.

Girls under-10: 1-Ria Vardhan bt Simran Kejriwal 6-0, 6-1.

Girls under-8: 1-Sanjeevani Patil bt Shireen Dotiwala 6-2.

Heading: Skinny guy - Indian Express
Content:
The iconic artist Rekha Rodwittiya celebrates life and turning 50

Rekha Rodwittiya at 50 is not very different from Rekha at 40, except for a few greys in her jet-black mane. She remains as iconic and charismatic as she was a decade ago.

Celebrating her birthday on Friday, the Baroda-based painter brings a solo titled Rekha@fifty to Sakshi Art Gallery, Tanna House, in Colaba.

The body of breathtaking, larger-than-life canvases, each rendered around a single woman protagonist, surrounds Rodwittiya, as she takes time out from e-mailing and lunching at the gallery, to chat with an old student from her alma mater.

"My work has usually been about celebration. In this instance, it's about my personal journey that I have lived mostly on my terms.

My work also deals with the collective— an interesting pendulum that I swing between. I feel privileged to have collided with situations that have nurtured me and created a context for my spiritual and intellectual growth," says the artist. She chose a path less trodden when she decided to be a single mother.

In small-town Baroda it wasn't easy and she took on the chauvinism of her contemporaries, while she taught at the Faculty of Fine Arts, MSU, after she returned to India after doing her Masters at the Royal Collage of Art, London.

Now, her son Mithun is settled in Mumbai where he is floating his own design firm. Partner Surendran Nair and Rodwittiya lead a quiet yet fulfilling life where their studios nurture their creativity.

"One has to be committed to asserting one's rights, since it often becomes tedious to fight. By this, I do not mean violence by assertion, for one's rights. It's easy to become complacent. I'm not apologetic or defensive about my feminist space. I am privileged to have been born into that skin of thinking," says the 50-year-old artist.

In a day and age when a lot of younger female artists are not keen to own the label of feminism— some find it outdated—

Rodwittiya is firm that issues related to gender inequality are far from resolved. "At a time when an eight-month-old baby is raped by a 22-year-old man, it is important to be feminist. One is not suggesting it is the only concern but it's one of the many politics of alertness," says the artist.

Rodwittiya is holding a seminar to discuss the politics of exhibition spaces and policing of art works. The event is hosted by Sakshi Art Gallery on November 12 and is an invite to like-minded people. "It is time to bind together once more since we are facing much opposition," says the artist, obliquely referring to the current condition at her former art school.

This body of works, resplendent in colour, depicts women in several avatars— as warrior, nurturer, mother, homemaker and vigilante. They encompass the artist's beliefs and celebrate her triumphs. "I do not tell stories; I paint life-scapes."

The show continues till November 18 at Sakshi Art Gallery.

Heading: Joint venture - Indian Express
Content:
The skinny guy seems sharp. He seems earnest. He makes jokes about himself before you do. And he talks sense. All this worries me.

Because if they make him President, in one fell swoop the American people will have taken away the whole world's opportunity to laugh. Mr Bush will disappear quietly into the sunset. To graze where rich retired Presidents go to graze. And in little time the world, in its return to grimness, will forget. The shoulder-shaking chortle. Those wonderful, literature-defying sentences that twist words and combine phrases in jolly abandon. That trademark look, delicately balanced between confusion and blankness, as he comes out of the tailend of another of his famous "Bush-isms".

Instead, we get the skinny guy. Whose eyes burn with passion and intensity. Yet sparkle with intelligent humour. But what can you do with this? You cannot eat cleverness nor laugh at it. It is completely, utterly useless.

And yet the American people, against all expectations, seem to be going for it. I mean, I always thought that a country of people who swung their cricket bats from the shoulder and played football with their hands couldn't be all that smart. But they seem to be in the historic process of proving me wrong. At least that's what their polls indicate. And what if their polls are right? The world gets the skinny guy. Against all odds.

Actually, I think the American people were just so embarrassed with their previous, rather monumental, goof up, that they decided to swing completely the other way. It's like they all conspired in their bars and football fields, over their T Bone steaks and hamburgers, and said: "Let's make him young. And funny. Awesome. And, oh yeah, why don't we colour him, not pink, not splotchy, just some other colour, okay dude? Like any other colour, at least lightly. And you know man, it doesn't matter if his name ain't Jack or John or George, and sounds like someone sticking his tongue out, Baraaaaack! Let's just make sure he's a teeny-weeny bit intelligent, okay?"

And so now, they are a nation poised on the brink of returned intelligence. Already their dollar is looking more powerful. And all our jokes are gone. Along with the state of the economy, that is entirely too much to bear.

The other thing is, that a nation takes on the image of its leaders. Take us for instance; completely non-violent like Gandhi, we only occasionally quibble among ourselves.

So what will become of America? Will Americans miraculously lose weight and get smart and light brown like Diet Coke? Or can we inject a glimmer of hope here? May we suggest for example, that in recognition of his yeoman service to mankind they give Mr Bush some kind of special, "kicked upstairs", job?

Not building houses in third world countries like they gave Mr Carter nor the cutting ribbons and smoking cigars one that they gave Mr Clinton. But something more substantial. Like Chairman and Managing Director for External Affairs and Geography. Or President of the Free Republics of Iraq or something. That should keep us smiling for a bit.

And speaking of which, what will they do about Iraq? Will the skinny guy just withdraw? Just say "Oops! Sorry!" and tippy-toe away? "Okay guys, pack all those tanks and missiles and thingies along with the rest of your lives and let's get the flock outta here!"

Nah! I think he'll do something thoughtful and dynamic and clever. And then he'll turn his breezy attention to the economy and that'll get fixed and they won't need any more Indians to do the jobs their unemployed youth won't do and, guess what, we'll get shafted again.

But what to do, it's as inevitable as those old Charles Atlas comic strip ads: The skinny guy always wins.

(Write to the columnist at adipochas@yahoo.com)

Heading: Colour Pink - Indian Express
Content:
Shankar Mahadevan and Ustad Rashid Khan prove they're in tune with each other

Classical and pop music sensation Shankar Mahadevan and Hindustani classical maestro Ustad Rashid Khan have shared the stage before. But that was many years ago on the shores of Benares, along with other renowned artistes. And ever since, many fans have hoped that the two artistes would take the stage together once again. Thanks to the efforts of Shashi Vyas of Pancham Nishad, Mumbai will witness their union on Sunday, November 2. Being touted as a "first time ever unique jugalbandi", Samanvay will be a programme to watch for several reasons.

Indian classical music's history has had a tradition of unforgettable jugalbandis, with the likes of Ravi Shankar with Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Bhimsen Joshi with Dr Balamuralikrishna. This concert will be especially interesting to music lovers as it is the coming together of a singer trained in the Hindustani classical tradition (Rashid Khan) and another in a Carnatic school (Mahadevan).So how did the two artists from such diverse musical styles decide to join hands?

Mahadevan, who has been actively involved with the Hindi cinema music scene —with recent chart toppers like the Rock On soundtrack — says: "It is our mutual appreciation and admiration for each other's work

that brings us together to begin with. The idea was to share a space and explore what will happen. It is also an attempt to expand our own horizons and styles."

Khan, whohas emerged as one of the most promising names in the younger generation of Hindustani singers, comes from the Sahaswan Gharana. He has had a long association with the Sangeet Research Academy in Kolkata, which he quit in 1999 to found his own academy. Today, he is something of legend in classical music circles, poised to rise to the stature of greats like Bhimsen Joshi and Kumar Gandharva.

The artists are quick to clarify the purist nature of the concert. "It will not be a fusion concert. It will be a classical bandish" says Mahadevan. The two musicians are confident about a good audience. The notion that there are no takers amongst the youth for classical music may also be changing as more and more independent musicians in the country display strong strains of classical influence. And Khan is happy to join hands with Mahadevan to promote the art. "The kala is the most important thing. Such concerts are an effort in the right direction because the new generation will get to listen to music they normally might not listen to."

Content:
To overcome matters of jurisdiction often coming in the way of executing schemes under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), the Women and Child Welfare Department has finally decided to give corporations the control of anganwaris in urban areas. After malnutrition and related deaths were reported in Mumbai, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) had wanted to take over anganwaris in Mumbai.

Principal secretary, Women and Child Welfare Department, Vijay Satbir Singh said, "We just received a letter from BMC showing willingness to take over the anganwadis.

We will send a reply and it will be applicable to all corporation areas."

Over the last one-and-a-half-year, the Health Department, the Women and Child Welfare Department and the BMC have been trying to resolve problems of urban malnutrition.

According to ICDS, over 500 children died of malnutrition in Mumbai this year alone. Cases cropped up last year in the tribal belt of Aarey colony, where ICDS and BMC neither had any services, nor had they conducted any estimate of children and their nutritional condition.

After being severely criticised, the state set up a committee to address the problem. In zilla parishads, ICDS monitors anganwadis, pays anganwadi workers and bears other related expenses. Local parishad workers are able to decide food and nutrition contents and requirements as per need.

The same concept will now be extended to anganwaris in urban areas by bringing them under BMC and other corporations.

"Anganwaris will be handled by BMC and other corporations. We will continue supporting them financially. All costs will be borne by the Women and Child Welfare Department," said Singh.

In Mumbai, the ICDS runs 6,000 anganwaris.

"The new move will make the work smoother as they can be supervised locally and decisions taken independently," added Singh.

BMC had sent the letter last week. "The Commissioner sent the letter saying BMC would like to run the anganwaris in Mumbai," said Dr Jairaj Thanekar, executive health officer, BMC. A BMC health official said the letter was a follow-up of the meetings held with the state government last year. "We made several proposals about anganwari management. The same letter was sent again to the government to take the matter forward," BMC official said.

Heading: OUT OFTHE BOX - Indian Express
Content:
The move is expected to boost connectivity with proposed airport and Raigad growth centres

In a bid to ensure better connectivity, with the proposed international airport at Navi Mumbai and the growth centers in Raigad district, the state government is planning a monorail route on the Mumbai Trans Harbor Link (MTHL).

Work on the 22-kilometer long MTHL, which will connect Sewri in mainland Mumbai to Nhava across the creek, is due to begin on January 26 next year, and senior state government officials said that a lot of thought is being given on whether the civil structure for a monorail route could be incorporated in the design of the bridge.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has already set in motion the process for the first monorail service between Jacob Circle in Central Mumbai to Wadala and from there to Chembur in the eastern suburbs. Officials said the same route could be extended across the creek from Wadala. They added that there were technical problems in incorporating the design for a metro railway in the Rs 8,000 crore, eight- lane MTHL, as the resonance and vibrations caused by the comparatively heavier metro were not suitable to the present design of the bridge. "Minor modifications in the foundation and pillar (of the MTHL) can accommodate the monorail on the divider," said the official, adding that the issue was discussed with engineers including officials of the company which was involved in the monorail work.

It would be easier to integrate the monorail in the MTHL design rather than set up a separate link across the creek for the purpose, said the official, pointing out that though airports in China and Malaysia were located far from the city centers, they were linked with them through rapid mass transit systems. The pillars of the MTHL could be strengthened for accommodating the civil structure of the monorail. Private parties could be invited to set up and operate the rolling stock on the monorail route through a build operate transfer (BOT) basis.

The issue may be explained in the pre- bid process of the MTHL and the concerned parties would be asked to give their commercial bids accordingly.

In June, the state cabinet sub- committee on infrastructure had decided that the work on the sea link would be undertaken by the government itself without public private partnership.

The cable stayed MTHL will also save 15 kilometer and two hours of commuting time. The 4,400 square kilometer MMR, which had a 16 million population in 2001, is expected to see the numbers rise to 24 million by 2021.

By 2015, the Vashi bridge which connects Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, is expected to see a traffic of 1.90 lakh passenger car units (PCU) daily without the MTHL. The MSRDC estimates that by 2015, the MTHL may see traffic of 55,000 PCU without the SEZ and international airport and 68,000 with the SEZ and airport. The Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (ILFS) estimates this traffic to be 62,000 PCU and the REL lead consortium estimates it to be 76,000. The MSRDC estimates that by 2011, the traffic on the MTHL will be 46,580 PCU per day. The state also plans to link the MTHL and the Eastern Freeway through an approach road.

Heading: TALKING POINT WITH RAJESHWARI SACHDEVA - Indian Express
Content:
The Gul & Tulsian Show
CNBC Awaaz
Saturday, 9:30 pm
Rating***
What's it about? As the global economy suffers one of the worst meltdowns in history, the faces of shocked investors at Dalal Street plaster every magazine and newspaper. We all know what these faces look like. They look a lot like us— discussing stocks with friends while taking cigarette breaks, passing by on pavements, or in between jumping in and out ofcrowded local trains. Everybody is worried about their money. Will the market recover from this blow? Will we ever see our money again? These are question on everybody's lips. And in such a time, CNBC Awaaz has identified the need of the hour and responded with The Gul & Tulsian Show— a talk-show that promises to give investors, traders and players the right advice to guide them towards risk-free investments.

Who's in it? The CNBC team brings together Gul Teckchandani, Chief Investment Officer of Sun F&C Asset Management Company, a big player in the mutual fund industry, and S P Tulsian, of sptulsian.com and editor of Premium Investments. The two financial experts debate it out at a coffee table along with the anchor and a guest. What's hot?Virtually every sector has taken a beating this time around and investors are worried about whether or not the government or somebody else can bail them out. Teckchandani and Tulsian are clued into the latest bulls and bears and they also seem well in tune with the ethos of the common investor on the street. The two analysts discuss the problem at large giving investors the bigger picture as well as analyse sectoral trends. Listening to them one could know what a Merrill Lynch or a Morgan Stanley is really thinking. They also put things in context, at times citing moments of similar crisis in the past and the lessons learnt. What's not?As theories are propagated and suggestions made, the cacophony sometimes descends into the din one imagines inside the stock-exchange or the your everyday commute.

There is also an over-abundance of market-jargon and name-throwing assuming the common viewer to be well-versed in such matters. A show on the stock-market is no more a niche or special interest programme, and some lucidity in the discussions would be helpful. Should you be watching it? In times like these, everybody's a selfproclaimed investment guru. But it's important to get the 'low-down' straight from the horse's mouth. And this duo is one of the best in the stable.

The show is certainly worth it.

Heading: Restive Koris a new challenge for Mayawati government - Indian Express
Content:
The actress spills the beans on reality shows

What is the format of your new reality show Jalwa 1 2 Ka 4?
The show involves singing, acting and dancing. A theme will be given to the contestants and they'll have to create an act around it.

Will the scripts for the acts be created by the contestants?
We'll obviously have some help from scriptwriters, but we'll have to do a lot of work ourselves.

Do you think that increasingly the reality shows are scripted?
My first reality show was Nach Baliye. Back then we were all so new to the idea. We had no idea what to do, so everything was fresh. We didn't cook up anything. But by the end, we'd figured out what works and what doesn't. It's the same now. People see what worked before and they go ahead and try out those same formulae. But I wouldn't blame the contestants entirely. It also depends on the questions that they're asked on the show by the hosts or the judges. If a certain kind of question is asked, everyone will react the same way, so it looks scripted.

Do you think that's why there's an audience for such shows?
If a person is revealing their innermost thoughts on the screen, then of course people want to see it. It's natural. As for whether these people can control themselves on screen, it's very difficult. They come on the show thinking that they can master their emotions, but trust me, it's very difficult. The first day of rehearsals and they're bawling their hearts out. And that baring of emotions |is something that everyone, unwittingly or otherwise, is very attracted to.

You're also starring in another show. Tell us about that.
I have a cameo on Meet Mila De O Rabba. It's a very spicy cameo. But I won't reveal more than that. You have to watch the show to find out more.

And how about a music album?
Making a music album is hard work and I haven't gotten down to creating a new one. But as soon as I get a good idea, I'll start working on it.

Any chances of seeing you with your husband Varun Badola on screen?
Not in the near future.

Heading: Five districts bordering Nepal safe haven for smugglers - Indian Express
Content:
The growing clamour for representation in polity among Koris — a Dalit sub-caste — poses a new problem for the Bahujan Samaj Party.

The Koris, a dominant sub-caste with more population than Jatavs (the sub-caste of Mayawati) have no representation in the party. Gathering under the banner of Akhil Bharatiya Kori-Koli Samaj, they have now raised voice against the BSP government, demanding political, economic and social rights.

The community leaders have decided to oppose the BSP candidates in the coming Lok Sabha polls.

Pradeep Kumar Kori, an advocate and the convenor of the Samaj, said the BSP government was providing sops only to Jatavs and neglecting the Koris altogether.

Of the 65 Dalit sub-castes in state, the Koris comprised over 5 per cent of the Dalit population, whereas the Jatavs comprise a mere 4 per cent. "But for the BSP, we are not as trusted a vote bank as the Jatavs and the party has consciously denied us representation," he said. "No member from our community was given ticket from the reserve seats in the 2007 assembly elections." The community has been given representation by parties like the Congress, BJP and the Samajwadi Party.

But Mayawati, Kori said, was against the idea of emergence of the Kori community as an organised vote bank like the Jatavs.

"In the next Lok Sabha elections, the community will lend support to the party in the best position to defeat the BSP," he warned. "We have convened a rally of all non-Jatav Dalit sub-castes in Allahabad on November 20 to chalk out our strategy."

Besides demanding adequate reservation in government jobs, education and other sectors, the organisation has asked setting up statues of Sant Kabir in all parts of the state and rechristening Jhansi district after freedom fighter Jhalkari Bai.

Kori said the community will wait to see which political party promises to implement quota as recommended by the "Social Justice Committee" set up by former state chief minister Rajnath Singh in 2000-01.

The Kori community is known as Koli in other parts of the country, particularly in Rajasthan, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh. In each of the 80 parliamentary constituencies of Uttar Pradesh, the Kori population ranges from 30,000 to 70,000.

"The people of our community are spread out across Bundelkhand, Agra, Saharanpur, Kanpur and Meerut, but still we lag behind in every field," Kori said. Currently, the organisation is conducting political campaigns in Allahabad, Kaushambi, Mirzapur and Fatehpur.

Heading: State minority panel for survey of urban slum areas - Indian Express
Content:
A 10-km stretch in each of the five districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh bordering Nepal has become a new trouble spot for the intelligence and security agencies of the country.

According to sources in the Intelligence Bureau (IB) and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), a Nepalese mobile network has been found operating in a 10-km stretch within the Indian territory.

And in spite getting hold of mobile numbers of certain offenders, the security agencies — including Customs, IB, Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), state intelligence department and the Uttar Police Police — have failed to trace the calls.

This has put the smugglers dealing in narcotics, arms and ammunition, timber, gold and fake Indian currency notes operating across the border in an advantageous position. The gangs involved operate within the 10-km stretch, using Nepali mobile numbers.

Recently, a Delhi CBI team was probing the fake currency racket and was on the lookout for a Bihar-based dealer operating from the Buxar area.

While collecting information, the officers got hold of the dealer's mobile number.

Later, it was found that the number belongs to a Nepal-based mobile operator and belonged in the same series as the number of the racket's Kathmandu-based kingpin.

The CBI team, however, failed to track the owner of the phone.

For 10 days, a five-member team stayed on the border at East Champaran in Bihar, seeking help of the Nepal Police, but to no avail.

Deputy Inspector General Anil Agrawal of the Sashastra Seema Bal, Lucknow Headquarters, said: "Earlier, Indian networks used to operate across the border. But recently, the Union government has issued directives to ensure that Indian networks are disconnected at a distance of 500 m from the border."

He added: "Our agencies are facing problems probably because there are no such norms in Nepal. The surveillance of a phone is conducted with the equipment available with the mobile-network-service-provider. The agencies had no authority to seek the same from the Nepal-based service providers."

According to IB records, of the 1,664-km Indo-Nepal border, a stretch of 821 km lies in Uttar Pradesh. Of this, 391 km is spread across five districts of the state — Maharajganj, Sidhhartha Nagar, Balrampur, Shravasti and Bahraich.

Sources in the Intelligence Bureau claimed that around 320 villages on the 391-km stretch have become a safe haven for smugglers and criminals. The villagers are paid for providing them with logistics.

Heading: House of legislator’s murder witness attacked - Indian Express
Content:
With the state government all set to introduce new schemes for the minorities, the Uttar Pradesh Minority Commission (UPMC) is trying to ensure that the communities can reap maximum benefits from the programmes.

According to an official in the commission, it will write to the state government to conduct a survey of urban slum areas and find out the exact number of people belonging to the minority community living there. The survey, which will be conducted in different phases, will help the commission to ensure that each member benefits from the schemes.

Ghyasuddin Ahmed, UPMC Chairman, said: "The government is doing its best for the welfare of the minorities. The commission will also try to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries enjoy the benefits. We will ask district administrations to conduct a survey of the urban poor areas, especially those, which have been marked as the minority-dominated areas."

He added: "In these areas, the population ratios keep changing. We need to identify the new places and the correct number of people who can be the beneficiaries." When it comes to developing an area, factors such as providing medical facilities, schools, etc are important and need to be reviewed and revised regularly in case of a floating population. "The ratio of minorities and other communities in an urban poor area should be checked at least once in every five years," said Ahmed. The commission will hold a meeting in the next week to finalise the points based on which the survey will be conducted.

Heading: 11 districts to get degree colleges - Indian Express
Content:
The house of Rukshana, an eyewitness in BSP legislator Raju Pal's murder, was attacked on Thursday night at Karelabagh Colony. About six miscreants hurled stones and opened fire in front of Rukshana's house. Rukshana and her husband were not at home.

On Thursday morning, the Kareli police had lodged FIR against 11 people on Ruksana's complaint and arrested one. Rukshana alleged she was being intimidated by the goons of an MP, who was also an accused in the legislator's murder.

The Kareli police, however, said the attack could not be connected to the Raju Pal's murder case, as the accused were behind bars. The BSP, meanwhile, have demanded a detailed inquiry into the matter. Since, there were over six FIRs lodged previously in the BSP regime against MP Atiq Ahmad and others for intimidating witnesses, the district police have started an inquiry.

Puja Pal, BSP legislator and widow of Raju Pal, said she had demanded police protection for all witnesses.

SSP Ashok Muttha Jain said: "The cause of the attack, it seems, was that the miscreants wanted to teach Rukshana and her husband a lesson for objecting to their drinking and gambling in front of their house. She has also been given an armed policeman for security," he said.

Heading: Experts urge citizens to replace kerosene lamps with solar panels - Indian Express
Content:
One degree college to be set up in every district initially

Eleven districts in Uttar Pradesh are set to get their first government degree colleges. The state government has initiated a process to set up these colleges at affordable costs.

The districts are Ghaziabad, Bijnaur, Mainpuri, Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Gonda, Bahraich, Maharajganj, Kushi Nagar, Jaunpur and Kaushambi.

Till date, of the 71 distrcits in the state, only 60 had government district colleges.

"Initially, at least one degree college will be set up in every district at a cost of Rs 152.50 lakh each," Regional Higher Education Officer S A Ali said.

"All the concerned districts magistrates have been asked to identify at least 5,000 square metre area for a college. In Gonda and Bahraich, land has already been demarcated. Both the districts have sanctioned the money required for the purpose," he added.

Ali further said the district magistrates have been given strict instructions to identify land near cities or towns where transport facility was readily available.

According to an official in the state Higher Education department, initially, Arts stream courses will be introduced in these colleges.

Later, other streams like Science and Commerce will be added depending upon the interest of the students, the official added.

At present, there are 12 state universities, 125 government degree colleges, 335 aided degree colleges and 1,622 self-financed degree colleges all over the state. "In Lucknow, there are only three government degree colleges, which are not sufficient to accommodate the large number of students. Therefore, the students mostly go to the five government-aided degree colleges and 60 self-financed colleges," the official said.

Besides, there is only one government degree college in Faizabad.

While Gonda district has two government-aided and 23 self-financed colleges, Bahraich has three aided and 10 self-financed colleges.

The problem area
Though the state government is on its way to open degree colleges in 11 districts, scarcity of teachers will be a major problem.

Higher Education Director Dr Mia Jan said: "Teachers from district headquarters will be transferred to the new degree colleges. We have already asked the state government to recruit more teachers."

At present, there are 1,950 teachers in 125 government degree colleges, 8,270 teachers in 335 government-aided and 1,622 self-financed degree colleges. The ideal ratio between teacher and students should be 1:10.

"In UP, the ratio varies around 1:50. At some colleges, the ratio is to 1:100," Jan said. In the current academic session, there are 21.9 lakh students (13.40 lakh boys and 8.50 lakh girls) enrolled in higher educational courses across the state.

Currently, 500 posts were lying vacant for teachers in government degree colleges and 2,500 in private colleges.

"The list of vacancies has been sent to the Public Service Commission and Higher Education Commission," the director added.
— ENS

Heading: ‘SIMI’ threatens to blow up temple - Indian Express
Content:
To encourage the state's rural populace to replace kerosene lamps with solar panels, industry experts converged on Friday to discuss the benefits of clean development mechanism.

Speaking at the seminar organised by Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry and IBS, Professor Rakesh Goel of Business School of Institute of Chartered Financial Analysts of India, Lucknow branch, said: " By eliminating approximately 100 million kerosene lamps used in rural India for lighting and by adopting solar panels to produce electricity, carbon dioxide emissions can be reduced and rural health improved simultaneously."

Currently around 60 million households use 100 million kerosene lanterns. By adopting alternate sources of energy such as solar power and biogas, India can prevent 100 kg of carbon dioxide emissions per year.

In order to spread awareness about the process of obtaining carbon credits and claiming them, lectures on Kyoto Protocol and clean development mechanisms were conducted during the seminar.

Clean development mechanisms, one of the three methods in the Kyoto Protocol, encourage cleaner development in growing countries and also brings an infusion of investments and technologies. "Considering the need to reduce pollution levels and save energy, we must opt for clean development mechanisms and reap its benefits," said Sudhir Kumar, Principal Secretary, NEDA, department of additional sources of energy.

Talking about recent advancements in the sustainable energy sector, Goel said the government could now avoid Rs 15,000 crore on subsidies every year due to the new initiatives undertaken by banks and solar energy firms such as Tata BP Solar.

According to Goel, solar energy mechanisms were now available to the average villager at an economical rate. "The per unit cost of electricity is Rs 265, which can now be replaced with solar panels," he said.

Solar energy being cleaner and greener will enable users to receive carbon credits — using the Kyoto Protocol — which can then be exchanged with developed countries.

Showcasing a clean development model, a private electrical firm Sukhbir Agro and Energy has recently set up a 15 Mega Watt power plant at Ghazipur near Barabanki, which runs on agricultural waste. While the project is not profitable on a stand-alone basis, the premium obtained from carbon credits is helping the company reap benefits. Arya Gramin Bank's social effort that enabled villagers to buy solar panels was also highlighted.

Heading: Detonators seized in Chopan area - Indian Express
Content: The authorities of the Gorakhnath Temple received an anonymous phone call and letter on Thursday threatening to eliminate BJP legislator Yogi Adityanath and blow up the temple. The letter was signed "SIMI, Meerut". Adityanath is the head of the temple administration. SSP (Gorakhpur) R K Srivastava said: "We are trying to trace the place from where the call was made. One of the employees at the temple had taken the call around 6.55 pm. The letter had come in mail." An FIR had been registered at the Gorakhnath police station.

Heading: Rationalise tax rates, says council - Indian Express
Content: The Sonebhadra police seized five quintals of ammonium nitrate, 10 detonators and gelatin rods from two persons in the Chopan area on Friday. Sonbhadra SP Ram Kumar said, "The accused — Dilip Kumar Bhartiya and Javed Ahmed — were involved in supplying the substances to mining contractors."

Heading: BJP plans to woo first-time voters - Indian Express
Content: The state advisory council has emphasised the need to rationalise tax rates under the new regime of the Value Added Tax. The council is headed by the BSP general secretary and the Rajya Sabha MP Satish Mishra. While reviewing the progress of tax collections by the Commercial Tax Department on Friday, Mishra directed the officials to expedite the process of computerisation of the department. For augmenting tax recovery, he directed the officials to set up special camps for registration of traders and shopkeepers. It also reviewed the progress of the Panchayat Raj department.

Heading: 3 held for killing witness to clash - Indian Express
Content: Getting into the poll mode, BJP now plans to woo the first-time voters. In a meeting of its senior leaders, headed by the state election in-charge Kalraj Mishra, the party has decided to organise Navmatdata Sammelan (new voter meet) at regional levels. Mishra said: "The BJP has very strong chances in the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. Candidates will be decided soon."

Heading: Diwali ke side effects: Gastronomic trouble for foodies - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons were arrested by the Salem Tabri police on Thursday for the murder of 55-year-old Vijay Kumar, a resident of Hira Nagar on Noorwala road.

According to the police, Vijay Kumar was an eyewitness in a clash between two rival gangs on August 9.

Kumar was found dead near the New Vegetable market in the locality on October 23.

The trio was nabbed at a checkpost on Noorwala road and identified as Jasbir Singh Baba alias Bindri, Sunny Chawla, a resident of Chhawni mohalla, and Anil Kumar, a resident of Azad Nagar.

Addressing a press conference today, Superintendent of Police (City III) Sajjan Singh Cheema and Deputy Superintendent of Police Paramjit Singh Pannu said Bindri, a notorious criminal, was the main accused.

A case of murder was registered against Babloo, Jasbir alias Baba, Indri and Kechhi on a complaint by Vijay Kumar's brother, Ashok Kumar.

Two of the accused are still absconding, added Cheema.

Wife, 'lover' arrested for driver's murder in Sahnewal

A woman and her alleged paramour were arrested by the Sahnewal police on Thursday on charges of murder.

The arrested were identified as Varinder Kaur and Sikandar Singh.

The duo allegedly stabbed the woman's husband, Shamsher Singh, to death at Nandpur village on October 13. Shamsher Singh was a tempo driver.

The Sahnewal police had registered a case of murder against unidentified persons on the complaint of the deceased's mother, Gurjit Kaur.

According to the police, Varinder Kaur had illicit relations with Sikandar Singh.

The two plotted Shamsher Singh's murder in order to clear the path for their marriage.

Heading: Poor rehri owners soft targets for LMC? - Indian Express
Content:
Even after the fervour of the festival of lights has dimmed, the merry gourmet still has his plate full. Only now, the menu includes stomach disorders, gastritis and throat infections.

It seems that the Diwali rush has shifted from the markets to doctor's clinics where diabetics, heart patients and hypertensive patients are queuing up after indulging their palate this festive season.

Erratic eating or overeating is the culprit, say doctors. "This happens every year. People move from house to house wishing Diwali. And at each stop, they are served cold drinks, tea and snacks. At the end of the day, such erratic eating leads to gastritis disorders. Eating excessive dry fruits causes more problems as winters have not yet arrived," said Dr Ravinder Vatasyan, a city-based ayurvedacharya.

He is, however, quick to add: "But this year the number of such patients was quite low as many residents are already suffering from viral fever or dengue."

Deputy medical superintendent at Kapoor Hospital, Dr Harkamal Sidhu, said: "This is an annual affair. We expect all our heart patients and diabetics to return for check-ups within this week. The festive season offers a variety of enticements and Punjabis cannot resist good food," she laughs.

Dr Sidhu added: "The binge is not limited to Diwali. People tend to overeat all though the winter season, which raises their sugar and blood pressure levels. I advise every one to keep their intake under control in the coming season if they want to reduce their visits to doctors."`

Heading: Stand-off resolved? PAU says yes, employees say no - Indian Express
Content:
Strange are the ways in which the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation (LMC) functions.

It is curious how the civic officials managed to remove only six specific rehris in a market full of encroachments in Sarabha Nagar on Thursday evening.

The rehri owners have alleged that they were deliberately targeted by the LMC officials as they are migrants and poor.

One such rehri owner, who did not want to be named, said: "A team of LMC officials, along with some residents of the area, asked us to leave the area or face the music. Basically, they want us to pay Rs 300 per month for allowing us to run our business here. We already pay a fixed fee to the civic body but the residents keep threatening us of eviction time and again."

Another rehri owner added: "When we refused to pay up, the residents bought in the LMC officials. The worst part is that no erring shop-owner was brought to book but we, who depend on our daily earnings for livelihood, have been asked to vacate."

Municipal Corporation Commissioner B S Ghuman said: "I will take action against the civic officials involved. My office does not provide anyone the authority to target the poor. I have also asked the aggrieved parties to meet me so that I can ascertain the exact situation."

Parliamentary Secretary (local bodies) and Ludhiana West MLA, Harish Rai Dhandha, said: "It is beyond my comprehension why the LMC officials chose to bother just six people when over 200 acres of the city are under encroachment. The entire Sidhwan Canal belt near Model Town extension has been encroached upon.

"The LMC officials should perform their duty with complete honesty and clear all encroachment or simply lay off," added Dhandha.

Incidentally, a similar state of affairs had been reported two months ago when a few residents had threatened the rehri owners.

The situation settled only after a few well-known faces of the city intervened.

Heading: Ludhiana lads bring home the silver - Indian Express
Content:
The status of the dispute between the Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) authorities and the non-teaching employees' union has become unclear now.
