While the PAU, in a press statement released on Friday, claimed that "the matter of issuing advisory letters to some non-teaching PAU employees was amicably resolved after Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang met representatives of the union, the employees do not echo the same sentiments.

Harbans Singh Mundi, president of the PAU Employees' Union, said: "The meeting was amicable and we hope that the V-C accepts our demands. If not, the future course of action will be decided on November 4."

The demands include: appointing a secretary to the V-C from the non-teaching cadre, withdrawing the order demanding action against the non-teaching employees who participated in a rally on September 24.

The V-C, meanwhile, issued a virtual gag order to the employees today. "One is an employee of the university first and then a member of the union. The recent reckless comments that appeared in various newspapers on behalf of the employees' union could be damaging to the institution's reputation. Since all employees and teachers are part of the set-up, preemptive steps like going to the press over non-issues should be avoided.

"Rights exist in tandem with responsibilities and taking the confrontational route without exploring other means of dialogue will only vitiate the otherwise congenial environment

of the university. A copy of the union's press releases would also be sent to the

V-C's office in future to avoid miscommunication," stated Kang.

In reply, Mundi said some of the facts were misquoted in the media and added that he plans to send a rejoinder to this effect to the press. "But there was no discussion of sending our press communication to the V-C office," he added.

Asked about the inconsistencies between the PAU's and the union's version of the minutes of the meeting. Lakhwinder Singh Sandhu, vice-president of the union, said: "The V-C will get all his answers in our rally on November 5."

Heading: ‘Conservation agriculture has assumed significance’ - Indian Express
Content:
Three players from the city were part of the team that finished second at the 54th National School Cricket U-16 Championship held in Gujarat

Three young players have brought laurels to the city by winning silver medals at the 54th National School Cricket U-16 Championship, held at Jam Nagar in Gujarat from October 16 to 22.

The team from Uttar Pradesh finished first while Punjab stood second.

All the three — Ajayvir Singh, Abhayjit Singh and Nikhil Bhardwaj — are Class X students of Nankana Sahib Public School, Gill Road, Kundan Vidya Mandir and BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary School, Shastri Nagar, respectively.

Speaking for all three, Ajayvir said: "We were awarded silver medals, a cash prize of Rs 1,250 each and a certificate of participation. I took up cricket as a hobby in Class VIII. But now I am planning it as a career. We are thankful to Harbhajan Singh, our coach who has taught us the basics in the best possible way."

How does the trio juggle studies with play? "We don't practice during exams. But all through the year, we follow a rigorous practice regimen for two hours daily," says Ajayvir.

Ajayvir's father, Jasvir Singh, is an agriculturist and sarpanch of Jasdev Singh Nagar.

He said: "We are thankful to the school authorities for encouraging and inspiring my son."

Harmeet Kaur, principal of Nankana Sahib Public School, said: "It was Ajayvir's determination and Harbhajan's guidance that helped the team put up a good show at the tournament."

Heading: Founder’s Day celebrated at San Jain School - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Kenneth D. Sayre, Regional Agronomist for Asia of International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre (CIMMYT), visited Punjab Agricultural University on Friday.

During discussions with the Vice-Chancellor, Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Dr Sayre said that conservation agriculture had gained significance in view of adverse affects of intensive agriculture on natural resource base, including soil and water.

Dr Sayre elaborated on the benefits of machinery like Happy Seeder that facilitated crop residue management and planting of wheat in combine harvested rice. He said that the tractor mounted machine was capable of managing the rice straw residue in strips. Happy Seeder cuts and spreads the stubble and loose straw and sows wheat while retaining the rice residue as surface mulch.

It drills the wheat seed without land preparation in rice standing stubbles just after rice harvesting. The cost of the machine is an important criterion, said Dr Sayre, adding that costly machinery should be made available on hire basis by constituting cooperative societies. He highlighted that studies on economics of technologies were pertinent in conservation agriculture. He also discussed the programmes of rice-wheat consortium in Asia.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Kang said re-organisation of research priority was a must to address the changing needs. He mentioned that Happy Seeder was sustainable solution as part of conservation agriculture. He said that PAU had a strong linkage with CIMMYT in wheat improvement and protection programmes. Dr Kang presented Dr Sayre with information brochures about the university on the occasion. Presenting a synoptic view of the research programmes on cereals, Dr P.S. Minhas, Director of Research, said that technologies aimed at resource conservation were receiving a focus at PAU.

Dr Sayre visited the Department of Farm Power and Machinery and interacted with the scientists there about farm machinery in general and Happy Seeder in particular. Dr I.S.Dhaliwal, Head of the Department, said that Happy Seeder had given encouraging results and that 35 HP tractor for operating it was being used besides bringing in further fine tuning of the machine.

Dr H.S. Sidhu said that sowing wheat with Happy Seeder in residual moisture resulted in saving irrigation water, ensured timely plantaton of crop, reduced weed infestation, enhanced soil fertility, reduced pollution, increased soil microbial activity and yield. Chopped residue as mulch helped in moisture and temperature conservation, he added.

Heading: NGO Aagaz gets Godfrey Phillips bravery award - Indian Express
Content:
San Jain Senior Secondary School celebrated 139th birthday of Shrimad Vijay Vallabh Surishwar in the school premises today. The day was celebrated as Founder's Day and prize distribution function under the name "Vallabh Darbar".

Teams from different schools participated in competitions like group dances, group songs, qwwalis etc.

Sharanjit Singh Dhillon, Member of Parliament, was the chief guest. While Harish Rai Dhanda, chief parliamentary secretary, Punjab, presided over the function while Harish Bedi, MLA, Manmohan Singh Jain and Surinder Dawar were the guests of honour. Magazines of both the schools, SAN Jain Senior Secondary School and SAN Jain Model Senior Secondary School, Daresi Road, were also released on the occasion.

Heading: Shahi Imam raps Raj Thakre - Indian Express
Content:
Aagaz, a non-government organisation of Punjab Aagaz Charitable Foundation, has received 17th Godfrey Phillips bravery award for "its courageous activities." It is a special award introduced as "Social act of courage" by Godfrey.

The organization was short-listed among the states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab and Haryana, according to a press release issued by the NGO.

Prabha Devi, Governor of Himachal Pradesh, honoured the winners by presenting awards along with the certificates.

Godfrey has also given a cheque of Rs 11,000 to the organisation which will help them in continuing their efforts.

The Governor appreciated Aagaz for its efforts in helping the rural women and children by providing them an opportunity to earn their livelihood.

Preeti Kansal, General Secretary, Aagaz Charitable Foundation, said, "We have a firm belief that the role of women, their mental make-up and social-economic status is the basic for shaping our future society. Thus there is a dire need for social and economic upliftment of women. We are proud to have been recognized for our efforts. Our organization since its existence had been working for social causes and will keep on doing the same for as long as it exists."

Heading: IOL Chemicals posts profit - Indian Express
Content:
All India Majlis Ahrar Party on Friday condemned Raj Thakre, President of Maharashtra Nav Nirman Sena, for his "dictatorial policies."

Addressing a press conference, Shahi Imam of Punjab Maulana Habib-ur-Rehman said, "Raj Thakre is forcing people of other states to use Marathi language. This way he is trying to weaken the unity of the country."

He alleged that the Maharashtra government was favouring Raj Thakre, because of which goondaism was on the rise in the state.

He said, "Raj Thakre is just raising his voice for Marathi, thus showing great disregard to all those martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the country." Shahi Imam demanded that Congress high command should immediately intervene and resolve this sensitive issue.

Heading: Hunjan hospital to start orthopilot centre this month - Indian Express
Content:
IOL Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals Ltd, a manufacturer of industrial chemicals and bulk drugs, has released performance results for the quarter/half year ended September 30.

According to a press release, the profit after tax for the quarter ending on September 30 went up by 25.53 % to Rs 4.16 crore from Rs 3.32 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

The operating profit for the quarter went up to Rs 8.25 crore against Rs 8.12 crore reported in the corresponding quarter last year.

The income for the company during the quarter remained almost the same at Rs 80.01 crores while the earning per share increased to Rs 3.05 from Rs 2.76, added the release.

Heading: Congmen pay tributes to Indira Gandhi - Indian Express
Content:
Hunjan Bone and Joint Hospital will launch a new Orthopilot Centre (computer-assisted joint replacement surgery) and will be conducting live surgery with orthopilot navigation system on November 15 at the hospital situated on Kochar market road.

Addressing a press conference here on Friday, Dr Hunjan told mediapersons that orthopilot used infra-red camera, computer with sophisticated software to provide the real time, patient-specific information during surgery while virtually eliminating the need for expensive and radiation intensive CT and MRI scans before the surgery.

Heading: PU Diamond Jubilee celebrations to conclude without PM - Indian Express
Content:
The leaders and party workers of the Congress paid rich tributes to the late former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her 25th death anniversary at the Congress Bhawan here today.

The function was presided over by the District Congress (Urban) President Jagmohan Sharma. Addressing the party workers and the leaders, Sharma called upon them to follow into the footsteps of the late leader. He said that Indira Gandhi was a strong lady and she had set an example for everyone that a how strong a woman could be.

He said that Indira Gandhi had made the country proud in many fields. District Youth Congress president Dimple Rana and other party leaders including Usha Malhotra, Ajit Singh Bhangani, Amarjit Oberoi, Sameer Sharma, Ranjit Singh Saini, Shamlal Bhagat, Gurcharan Saini and Gurpreet Gill were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Equestrian Championship gets underway - Indian Express
Content:
After a long wait for the Prime Minister, authorities at Panjab University have finally decided to conclude the Diamond Jubilee celebrations in the campus on November 1.

The celebrations were to conclude on October 1 initially but they were extended by a month.

The PM, who is an alumnus of the university, had been approached by the University for inaugurating the celebrations, but the authorities are yet to receive a reply.

Tight lipped on the PM'S visit, university officials refused to comment on the issue. Dean Student Welfare Prof Naval Kishore said, "We are concluding the Diamond Jubilee celebrations on November 1 and I do not have any information about the PM's visit." The authorities were waiting for a confirmation from the PM's office to unveil a heritage museum as well as release a book on the history of the university to mark the celebrations.

Heading: BSNL Club, Chandigarh Table Tennis Club claim titles - Indian Express
Content:
The 4th Punjab Horse Show and State Equestrian Championship which was inaugurated today at Punjab Police Academy, Phillaur by the former Punjab DGP M.S. Bhullar got underway. The championship will conclude on November 2.

According to the organisers of the event, the Olympic events of show jumping and dressage as well as the International events of tent pegging and endurance, one day event and horsemanship by Nihangs will be held in the championship.

Adding to the fervour of the tournament, there will be horse breed display, dancing horses, obedient horses and age group competitions for children in open, sub-junior, junior and senior categories. Teams from all member district units and clubs are participating in the three-day long championship. There will also be joy rides on horse, camel and elephant for children and carriage rides for all.

Heading: Cricket has been rags-to-riches for this fish seller - Indian Express
Content:
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited Club (BSNL) and Chandigarh Table Tennis Club clinched the men's and women's team titles in the 21st Chandigarh State Table Tennis Championship at the Sector 23 Table Tennis Hall on Friday.

Dev Saini won the decisive match by defeating Harish Kumar by 11-8, 11-9, 11-8 to steer BSNL Club towards 3-2 win over Audit Club in the men's category. In the opening match Dev Saini went down to Vikas Sharma by 11-8, 9-11, 8-11, 10-12. However, Manish Bhardwaj pulled back one for BSNL Club as he rallied to beat Harish Kumar by 11-8, 11-9, 9-11, 11-8. Mayank Kapoor gave BSNL the lead when he registered a 11-8, 11-9, 11-8 win over Amod Dixit. Vikas Sharma held his nerves and put Audit Club at par when he edged past Manish Bhardwaj by 11-8, 11-9, 9-11, 11-9.

In the women's category, Naina Suri defeated Bhawna by 11-9, 11-4, 9-11, 10-12, 12-10 to take Chandigarh Table Tennis Club towards a 3-2 win over Manav Mangal Coaching Centre after both the teams were locked at 2-2.

Aditya Pandey and Kayani, both of Manav Mangal School claimed the sub-junior boys' and girls' singles title. Aditya Pandey defeated Mayank Kapoor of DAV Public School, Sector 8 by 11-8, 11-6, 11-8, 11-8 in the final while Kalyani prevailed over Rajeshwari of Carmel Convent, Sector 9 by 11-3, 8-11, 11-7, 11-4, 15-17, 11-3.

Pareen Verma and Divakash, both of DAV Public School, Sector 8 won the cadet girls' and cadet boys' singles titles, respectively.

Heading: Volleyball meet postponed till December - Indian Express
Content:
For the Punjab opener Ravi Inder Singh Rajji, the past year has been a roller coaster ride. He made his first-class debut for Punjab, went on to play in the Duleep Trophy and capped it up with a place in the Challengers Trophy teams. Ravi, who turns 21 on November 4, couldn't have asked for more: especially, considering how moving up the cricket ladder has given the Patiala player's family some financial standing.

Ravi, whose father sells fish for a living for a hand-to-mouth family, himself has this to say about the dream season: "When I look back, I can't believe my luck. Playing alongside big names and at the highest domestic level has not only given me confidence but hope for future too. I will try to maintain my form this season too and see how far I can go."

Ravi played in six Ranji matches last year and scored 398. "I need to convert my 40s and 50s into big scores. Maybe I need to learn more from experienced players like Pankaj Dharmani and Ravneet Ricky," Ravi feels. Punjab's first match this season is against defending champions Delhi at Delhi beginning November 3 and Ravi is all geared up. "For openers the need is to see off the new ball and then play the spinners with a positive mind. I am working on my sweep shot as Delhi has some good spinners in their side," he says.

Ravi also appeared for selection trials for the Deccan Chargers (Hyderabad) for the second edition of the Indian Premier League but could not make the cut. "My main focus is to concentrate on my Ranji performances and if I perform well chances will come my way."

Ravi knows cricket has given him and his family a new lease of life. He still helps his father sell fish when he is in Patiala but the future could be better, as he says "Once I become an established cricketer, I would ask my father to stop selling fish and come up with some business. For that I need to keep performing well for Punjab…And like every cricketer I also dream of donning the India colours."

Heading: Angad anchors MCM Blue Caps win - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh State Volleyball Championship for sub-junior boys and girls and senior (men and women) scheduled to be held from November 1 to 3 has been postponed and now the championship will take place from December 5 to 7 at Sports Complex, Sector 7.

According to Chandigarh Volleyball Association (CVA), interested teams who want to participate in the event should contact and submit their entries to Suresh Kumar, volleyball coach at Sports Complex, Sector 7 before December 3.

In the senior category, players will be selected on the basis of their performance for the camp for participation of Chandigarh State Team in the 57th National championship to be held from December 19 to 28 at Vishakhapatanam. Meanwhile, the probable sub-junior players will be selected on trial basis which will be held on November 8 at 4 pm at Sports Complex, Sector 7.

Heading: Industry hails Kalia for heeding demand on mixed-land use - Indian Express
Content:
Bolstered by a rollicking 139-run partnership between Angad Chahal (92) and Abhishek (31), MCM Blue Caps registered an emphatic 71 run victory over Desh Prem Azad Cricket Academy and entered the final of the Inter-academy Cricket Tournament for Under-14 being organised by DPAC Academy at the St Stephen's School grounds, Sector 45 on Friday.

Electing to bat first after wining the toss, MCM Blue Caps amassed 224 runs in 29.4 overs. After they lost their first two wickets cheaply, Angad Chahal and Abhishek built the innings and stitched 139-run partnership for the third wicket. Angad's knock of 92 runs included 10 boundaries and five towering sixes while Abhishek hit four boundaries in his polished knock of 31 runs. Talwinder Singh senior and Talwinder Singh junior snared two wickets each for DPAC Academy.

Chasing the target, DPAC Academy could muster only 153 runs for the loss of six wickets in the allotted 30 overs. Jagpreet emerged as the top scorer with 77 runs which included 13 boundaries and one huge six. Jagpreet and Daksh Aggarwal (15) tried to resurrect the inning with a 46-run partnership for the third wicket. Harpreet and Ravi Sahani scalped two wickets each.

Brief scores:
MCM Blue Caps-36: 224 in 29.4 overs (Angad Chahal 92, Abhishek 31, Ravi Sahani 21, Arshu 25, Talwinder Singh Junior 2 for 19, Talwinder Singh senior 2 for 25, Amrit Singh 2 for 41); DPAC Academy: 153 for 6 in 30 overs (Jagpreet Singh 77 no, Daksh Aggarwal 15, Gurashish 10, Harpreet Singh 2 for 17, Ravi Sahani 2 for 23).

Heading: Upgraded IOB branch inaugurated - Indian Express
Content:
Members of Chamber of Industrial and Commercial Undertakings (CICU) and United Cycle and Parts Manufacturers Association (UCPMA) have thanked the Local Bodies Minister Manoranjan Kalia for considering their demand to declare areas with thick industrial growth into designated industrial areas.

Charanjit Singh Vishwakarma, President of UCPMA, stated that a memorandum in this regard was given to the Minister on Vishwakarma Day celebrations and the minister had agreed to this demand.

Avtar Singh, general secretary of CICU, also thanked the minister for giving this assurance. Avtar Singh also requested Kalia and Hira Singh Gabria to declare Janta Nagar and Shimlapuri localities also as mix-land use areas by issuing an early notification because units in these localities had been operating for more than 30 years. Ajit Singj Kular, T.R. Misra, Upkar Singh, Balbir Singh Mankoo and many others were also present on the occassion.

Heading: Right step: say schools on right to education bill - Indian Express
Content:
T. Venkat Reddy, General Manager, Indian Overseas Bank, today inaugurated the upgraded branch of the bank at Guru Nanak Girls College, Mullanpur extension counter. This is the 54th branch of the bank in the region.

The bank offers mobile SMS alert facility, internet banking with the facility to deposit tax on-line, multi-city cheques and core banking solutions. Out of 54 branches in Ludhiana region, 51 branches are under CBS, said Gupta.

The bank is planning to open a new branch at Nakodar very shortly, he said. Senior manager of the branch, Darshan Singh, senior manager, Mullapur Mandi branch, S.P. Goyal were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Ex-workers all set to reclaim factory as owners - Indian Express
Content:
Schools welcome move; will it work on the ground, ask some

Leading private schools have welcomed the Right to Education Bill cleared by the Union Cabinet, which aims at free and compulsory education for children between 6 and 14 years of age. While welcoming the move, some schools have also expressed their reservations on whether it'll be implemented in the proper manner.

Among the other salient features of the bill are 25 per cent reservation in private schools for disadvantaged children from the neighbourhood at the entry level and doing away with donation, capitation and interviewing of the child or the parents as part of the screening procedure.

Dr Vidya Yerawadekar, principal and director of the Symbiosis International Society said, "I am happy that the cabinet finally cleared the bill. Its provisions are more than welcome. As far as Symbiosis is concerned, we have already implemented some of them. For instance, we do not interview students or parents before admitting the child to the kindergarten."

When asked whether accommodating 25 per cent underprivileged children will be a financial burden on the school, Yerawadekar said, "Yes some burden will have to be borne by the school as well as parents of other children. I am sure they will cooperate with us."

Madhavi Kapur, founder-principal of Rewachand Bhojwani Academy, too welcomed the cabinet decision saying it would help other children in connecting with the real world. "It was high time we had such a bill to ensure holistic education for all," she said.

Dr A L Deshmukh, vice-principal of Laxmanrao Apte Prashala, although supportive of the bill, was sceptical about its implementation. "As a policy, the bill is very good and with rural and underprivileged children getting quality education, it will help in arresting wastage of talent. However, it is obvious that the bill has been cleared in view of the upcoming elections. The gap between policy and implementation of the bill should be plugged and then truly, the needy will benefit from it," he said.

Dr Mohan Deshpande, city-based educationist, said the bill would ensure accessibility to quality education for all. "The situation in government schools is very bad, be it Zilla Parishad schools or ashram shalas. The bill will ensure quality education for all," he said.

The state government, which had been entrusted with the task of scrutinising the bill, had cleared the draft legislation early this month without diluting the content.

Heading: School exams inch closer, but life is still a picnic in city - Indian Express
Content:
November 7 is going to be a momentous day for 210 erstwhile workers of Garware Nylon Ltd. It is on this day, twelve years after their company shut down, they will reclaim their rights and dues as they become owners of the nine-acre company land in Ahmednagar. These workers have raised money to purchase the land for Rs 6.01 crore and are now going to start a Rs 52 crore corrugated box factory as a joint venture with Pradeep Kate, an industrialist and leader of a national political party.

Over 60-70 workers met under the aegis of the Common People's Front (CLF) in Nigdi on Friday. Workers were asked to pitch in to become shareholders in the new factory.

"Once the land is bought, we will start our company. The idea is to get manufacturing machines from China and we hope to break even in six months," said Kate, who is investing Rs 25 crore in the new company. The nine-acre industrial unit in Ahmednagar has around 60,000 sq feet built up commercial space, which Kate said, could be leased out to other companies. "Already many companies including Godrej Agrovet have approached us to rent the space. We could get rental money up to Rs 6 lakh a month," said Kate.

The workers were galvanised into action in February when the third unit of Garware was being auctioned in the high court. Around 210 workers under Pimpri-Chinchwad based Common People's Front objected that the bidding price of Rs 2.35 crore was far less than the market price. When the court asked them to get better bids, they decided to buy the land themselves.

The workers won the bid for the land worth Rs 6.01 crore. Since then they have paid the court Rs 5.1 crore. Another Rs 92 lakh will be deposited by November 7. This will probably be the first such instance. Their next step is to revoke the previous auctions of Garware Nylon at Pimpri and Sarola in Satara district. They have alleged that their bids were far too low and have suggested an investigation and re-auction.

"This is a turning point in the history of the Indian workers movement. Not only do these workers become owners of the factory, they have also blown the lid off the existence of the powerful cartel that buys these factories for a pittance when their actual market worth is many times more," said Dominic Lobo, head of the Common People's Front.

The CLF is now planning a writ petition to challenge the previous auctioning of land in Pimpri and Sarola.

It was in 1996 that the three units of the Garware Nylon at Pimpri, Ahmednagar and Sarola shut down after accumulated losses of over Rs 300 crore and years of loyal service came to naught when over 1,200 workers lost jobs. Many workers who had to take up odd jobs to make ends meet in the last 12 years have come ahead to stake a claim in the factory. Ganpath Sangame worked with the factory for over 25 years before he lost his job. He was making ends meet by working with a goldsmith before he passed away seven years ago. His wife Sulochana has put together Rs 1.10 lakh by mortgaging jewellery to contribute towards this workers' effort to buy the Garware land.

Heading: Crematorium fire: PMC health officials held guilty - Indian Express
Content:
The demand for picnic spots in Konkan region is high, popular spots booked till November 5

When the mood to celebrate is in, exam fears are certainly out.

The rescheduling of school examinations because of the recent Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) has not dampened the spirits of picnickers during the Diwali vacation.

The signs of this is that all the major picnic spots around the city are buzzing with activity and almost all the facilities run by the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) have been booked to capacity till November 5.

Around 70 schools in the city had participated in the CYG extravaganza forcing all the schools to reschedule term-end exams to post-Diwali.

The decision taken in September had made most parents, who had already drawn up their Diwali vacation plans, quite unhappy.

But looking at the reservation charts of the MTDC, it seems the examination bug has not bitten into the mood to enjoy, either among the students or their parents.

According to Ashok Khamkat, marketing manager of Pune region of MTDC, the demand for picnic spots in Konkan region was high.

"Spots like Ganpatipule, Tarkarli, Murud, Dive Aagar, Murud-Janjira, Harne and Vengurla are packed till November 5," he said.

"The main attraction in Kokan are the seashores. Facilities like snorkelling and scuba-diving provided at Tarkarli beach have a high demand," said Vijay Chavan, general manager, MTDC.

"Every day, around 200 tourists, mostly from Mumbai and Pune, enjoy snorkelling and scuba-diving at Tarkarli. As the water remains clean and calm from October to May, the facility has many takers. This time we haven't seen any dip in the number of visitors," he said.

Chavan said MTDC had plans to start scuba-diving and snorkelling at other places in Konkan region and also develop spots like Amboli, Kharepatan and Vengurla to attract more visitors.

"The tourists are preferring hill stations like Mahabaleswar, Panhala, Bhandardara and Karla," said Khamkar.

"The unique feature this time is that tourists have arranged their tours during he days of Diwali too," he said. He added that there was also a huge beeline of people for pilgrimage spots like Shirdi.

Make the best of it, take a safari at Tadoba
The Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC ) has started a special Jungle Safari package at Tadoba Sanctuary in Vidarbha.

"The MTDC provides a bus from Nagpur to Tadoba every Saturday. The bus starts at 9 am and reaches Tadoba at noon. There, the tourists are taken for a safari in the jungle. Tourist can enjoy a cultural programme in the evening. On Sunday morning, there will be another safari through the jungle and at noon the tourists are taken to Baba Amte's Anandvan from where they are brought back to Nagpur at night," said Vijay Chavan, general manager, MTDC.

The charge for this jungle safari is Rs 4,000 per person. The cost covers transportation and food.

Heading: AFK officials to citizens: Don’t use roads near factory - Indian Express
Content:
The committee report recommends action against Avon company; 'Sun Enviro gave illegal sub-contract' , Mathkari slams PMC

Pointing out that Sun Enviro Management Pvt Ltd, which had been given the task of bio-medical waste disposal near Kailash crematorium, had in turn given an unlawful sub-contract to a private firm for the disposal of deodorant cans that ultimately led to a fire killing seven labourers, a committee appointed by Pune Municipal Corporation has held the civic health department officials guilty for their negligence in not visiting the disposal plant site regularly.

BJP corporator Vikas Mathkari, who made available a copy of this committee report to mediapersons on Friday, however said that this exercise of inquiry committee report does not put the responsibility of the incident on any particular official. He said, "Even 50 days after the accident, no concrete action has been taken against the contractor. The committee had submitted the report to Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi on October 8, which he has not yet made public, which clearly shows that the PMC wants to protect its officials." Seven labourers had died due to grave injuries which they suffered after a major fire broke out at the bio-medical disposal plant near Kailash crematorium on Raja Bahadur Mill Road on September 11. After this, the PMC ordered a probe into the incident that was carried out by K C Karkar, civic octroi department head. The report was submitted by additional commissioner M S Devnikar.

Among other things, the report says, "Without seeking any permission from PMC, Sun Enviro had struck a deal with Manohar Chatsingh Sotte of Avon Company and given him a sub-contract to dispose of the deodorant spray cans at the incinerator. The employees of this company would remain at the incinerator to ensure the disposal of these cans. These products used to be carried at the disposal plant from Mumbai. Since these cans and its contents were highly inflammable, permission from Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) was mandatory, which they did not have. Besides, this company did not take any precautionary firefighting measures considering the inflammable contents."

The report points out that even though the contract had been given to Sun Enviro, it was the responsibility of civic health officials including assistant medical officer Dhananjay Chandakakar, ward officers, ward commissioner, health inspectors, and ultimately chief health officer Dr Pramod Dhaigude for the negligence in their duties and not visiting the disposal unit plant for keeping a check on the functioning.

The report has recommended seeking clarification from the health department officials. The report recommends action against Avon company for illegally dumping the cans at the unit. The committee has also suggested that the particular incinerator be started again to sort out the problems of bio-medical waste within the city.

Heading: Forest dept daily wagers want permanent status - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the security has been further tightened at Ammunition Factory, Khadki, nation's premier arms production unit, officials have appealed to citizens to avoid using roads in the vicinity of the factory. The appeal comes in the wake of the "rigorous" security measures being implemented and the increased incidents of thefts at the factory premises.

AFK security chief Col S N Sabnis said while security at the four gates at factory premises has been further stepped up, they are also rigorously implementing the security at the two gates leading to the vicinity of the factory. "At the two gates one is the Tank Road and the one from Khadki bazaar side, residents make life difficult for our security personnel. They try to force their way through the gates despite being told by the security personnel not to do so. They indulge in arguments with security personnel and at times it leads to ugly scenes," said Col Sabnis. "All these despite the fact that the factory has put up big boards at the gates highlighting those who are eligible to use the roads."

Col Sabnis said only those who have been issued valid identity cards by the factory are permitted to use roads in the vicinity of the factory. "Only defence employees of AFK and three other factories are permitted to use the roads in the vicinity of the factory. So far, we have issued 5500 such identity cards. Only these persons can use the roads near the factory. Others are not allowed to do so," he said. "Residents who do not possess valid I-cards, produce bank pass books or some companies card to force their way through the gates," he said. Col Sabnis said in view of the security concerns, the factory would like to appeal to general citizens to cooperate with them and avoid using the roads closer to the factory. Pointing out that the roads in the vicinity of the factory are used as short-cut to head for Vishrantwadi, Yerawada, Khadki and other parts of the city, Col Sabnis said the regular traffic jams on Holkar bridge are creating problems. "It is hoped that the new bridge planned by the civic official comes up fast so that commuters stop using short-cuts."

The factory officials have been forced to implement tighter security measures as the latest incident of theft only highlighted the point that security can be breached by those intending to smuggle out the arms.

On Monday, the city police reported that 31-year-old Bholenath Bhegde, a worker with AFK, was caught selling bullets smuggled out of the factory premises.

He had reportedly smuggled out the bullets through his tiffin box. Bhege is a resident of Range Hills.

He was selling the bullets to a man identified as Santosh Pawar at Nashik Phatawhen both of themwere caught. Both of them are in police custody till Saturday.

Heading: Collector wants more staff for CFC, sends proposal to state govt - Indian Express
Content:
Daily wage workers of the forest department are up in arms against the forest department demanding that they too be made permanent employees. A directive passed by the state government in 1994 states that all those who had completed five years of service before November 1, 1994 should be made permanent.

According to Prakash Shinde, head of the Vankamgar Sanghatna, said, "While the number of officers in the forest department has steadily increased over the years, the daily wage workers are yet to become permanent employees. It is ironic that even after directives have been issued by the industrial and labour courts, and in some cases even by the High Court and Supreme Court, there has been no progress."

Across the state, there are around 18,000 workers who work on daily wage basis in the forest department, the social forestry department and the forest development corporation of Maharashtra, some of them have been working for over twenty years but are yet to enjoy the privileges of a permanent job like medical insurance, better wages, government quarters and so on, Shinde said.

However, when contacted, G D Valse, divisional forest officer, planning, said, "We are aware that there are such cases. In some of them, stay orders from the respective court have been obtained while in cases where directives from the Supreme Court have been issued, they are sent to the higher office in Nagpur for approval from where it is sent to Mantralaya in Mumbai for further verification. As and when the directive from the state government is received, we will make these workers permanent."

"There are different schemes under which the daily wage workers like the EGS (employment guarantee scheme), SGRY (Sampoorna Gramin Rojgar Yojna), MREGS (Maharashtra Rural employment guarantee scheme) under the government regulation of 1994.

Only those who have been appointed under the Planned Scheme, where a worker who has completed 240 days of work in a year, from 1989-1994 will be made permanent. Under the plan, we have a number of people who have been made permanent. However, unless we receive the final orders from the state government, we cannot make everyone permanent," Valse said.

The Pune circle, which includes Pune and Solapur, is home to 350-400 such workers. Even though they might have been working here for the last 15-20 years, they would get their arrears and back-wages only if they become permanent staff, he said.

In August, the state government had formed a committee under Babanrao Pachpute (State Forest Minister), Harshvardhan Patil (Minister of State for Women and Child Development) and Balasaheb Thorat (State Minister for Agriculture, Water Conservation. and Khar Lands) to discuss the issues faced by the daily wage workers. However, the findings and recommendations of the committee are yet to be made public.

"The daily pay of these workers is Rs 90, which means their monthly earning is around Rs 2,250. How can they support their families with such a meagre amount? Even after getting orders from the Supreme Court, why this delay in making them permanent?" Shinde said.

"We will organise an 'Andholan' on November 17 in front of State Forest Minister Babanrao Pachpute's residence here.

Heading: Baker’s Basket tennis: Dixon in finals - Indian Express
Content:
District collector Chandrakant Dalvi will soon send a fresh proposal to the state government demanding more staff for the Citizens' Facilitation Centre (CFC) in the collectorate.

Additional chief secretary of state revenue and forest department Neela Satyanarayan has asked Dalvi to send the proposal.

Dalvi said that this will address the problem of staff shortage as the collectorate always had to pull out staff from other departments for the CFC which see a lot of rush during admission periods.

"Now, besides our staff we have also appointed an outside agency. If we get more staff, this will not be required and we will be able to relieve officers from other departments,'' he said. Satyanarayan, who reviewed the situation, was happy with the collectorate's efforts to improve the pendency of cases. As shortage of computers is also a problem, Satyanarayan has asked the collector to send a proposal demanding more computers. "Full computerisation and speedy disposal of cases are on top of the agenda,''said Dalvi.

During a tour to the collectorate on Friday, Satyanarayan inspected the record room and also assessed the situation of pendency of cases. She also reviewed the six bundle system under the Anderson's manual. Recently the Collectorate had cleared up the record room and computerised all data.

Heading: Left high and dry - Indian Express
Content:
Brent Dixon defeated Aditya Gokhale in three sets, in what was by far the match of the tournament in the boys' under-13 category of the Baker's Basket Tennis tournament held at the Ladies Club Tennis Courts on Friday.

Dixon and Gokhale engaged in a thrilling contest that lasted for around three hours. Both players fought hard for each and every point. The opening set went into a tiebreak with Dixon edging past Gokhale 7 points to 5.

Gokhale, RCBC Open Junior Champion, came back strongly, however, and won the second set 6-2. The final set, just like the first, went down to the wire. Both players fought tooth and nail for every point. The set was tied at 6-6 and the game saw its second tiebreaker. Again it was Dixon who managed to hold his nerve and win it 7-5. He wrapped up the match and booked a place in the final, which will take place on Saturday.

Heading: Krishi-dindi to kick off today - Indian Express
Content:
Aspirants for constable jobs protest at Shivajinagar police headquarters as police reject them after they failed to produce domicile certificate

More than 60 candidates gathered at the police headquarters in Shivajinagar today asking why they had been sent letters of rejection even after producing certificates of eligibility to appear for interviews for the post of constables over a month ago.

"We filled the necessary forms to appear for the interview on August 27 and also submitted the copies of all necessary documents to the police. The police had then asked us to submit photocopies of domicile certificate. The police also accepted the receipt that the collectorate gives when you apply for domicile certificate. The police said that they could give the copies of the domicile certificate on the day of the interview," said Mayur Chavan, Yuvraj Yadav and Popat Sanap.

"But after October 20, my friends and I got letters from the police saying we have been rejected as we do not have domicile certificates. Now, when we have come here to ask them on what grounds have they rejected us, some police officials have asked us to go to the court if possible and get a stay order against the recruitments," said a rejected candidate.

Applicants present in the Shivajinagar police headquarters said that the police officials cited that over 35,000 thousand applications were received by the police from across the state. Out of this, they selected 27,000.

Speaking on the issue, Deputy Commissioner of Police Avinash Rokade said, "those candidates who did not fit the parameters necessary for the job or did not have the necessary documents at the time of submission of forms have been disqualified."

Heading: China town - Indian Express
Content:
The month-long krishi-dindi (farmers' procession) will be launched in 33 districts in the city today.

An initiative of the state agriculture department, the project is aimed at acquainting farmers with new techniques and the latest government schemes through exhibitions and technical presentations in their villages. Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar will flag off the dindi at the College of Agriculture here.

The dindi will have a 'krushi rath' and will carry a mobile exhibition on agriculture, displaying various schemes, agro technology for different crops, watershed development programme, food security campaign, micro-irrigation and agro-processing, said Uday Deshmukh, deputy director (information). The event will also have a mascot called Krushilaxmi.

The dindi will cover 63 villages across every district in a month. "Five agriculture officers from each sub-division will make presentations about various government schemes and manage the rally. Experts in sericulture, livestock, dairy production and fishery from the College of Agriculture will accompany the rally.

'Conservation of land resources' week will also be observed during the dindi from November 1-7.

Deshpande pointed out that the agriculture department has various schemes for farmers but they never reach them due to poor communication.

"The officers who will be travelling along with the dindi have been trained in Amravati and Pune," he added.

Heading: LAST BITE with Mugdha Godse - Indian Express
Content:
Adding to the fleet of Chinese restaurants, is the latest Tian Di, which promises to serve the authentic cuisine from the mainland

One fleeting look and Tian Di gives a convincing portrayal of a restaurant in China. Right from the red, white and green colours to the wind chimes, the Chinese lanterns or even the artifacts on the wall of the restaurant compel to indulge over the Chinese cuisine in its most genuine savour.

"The cuisine is about the concept of heaven and earth. I have spent almost eight weeks in China to experience the flavour of their food. In fact the master chef, Yuan Vwei Thong is one of Beijing's best chefs. The authenticity has been so taken care of that we have imported not only the ingredients but also the artifacts, furniture and a lot of other interiors that are based on the Feng-shui theme. The intention is to retain the real tinge of Chinese cuisine as well as refrain people from the Indianised version of it," says Taronish Karkaria, executive director who has been into the hospitality services for the last five years.

Tian Di aims to cater to the Chinese food lovers as well as the increasing corporate crowd. With dishes such as kai-chi chicken, shanghai potato and fried squid, there is also a variety of noodles and fried rice. What makes it easier for the wallet are the offers like- the executive veg lunch priced at Rs 195, non veg for Rs 225 and seafood lunch for Rs 295.

The most interesting dish on the card is the Beijing Duck. Defining the true gastronomy, the preparation requires extreme craftsmanship since the entire cooked duck is brought on the table. The dish requires a two-hour intimation where as another dish called the Beggar's chicken needs to be ordered a day in advance for its exclusive preparation.

An exciting offer that Tian Di has is that the visitors can buy most of the displays in the restaurant including the chairs. "We have quite interesting objects on display that are picked up randomly from China and since the restaurant is in the Krome mall in Hadapsar that has all kinds of home decor, we decided to promote the materials too. Everything comes with a price tag," smiles Karkaria.

Heading: TURNING OVER - Indian Express
Content: The last memorable meal I had was in Dubai during this Diwali season. I was there for the promotion of my film Fashion and the team dined together. It was at the Meredian Hotel. What added spice to the meal was the otherworldly ambience and delicious dishes. I was there for dinner. Some of the most striking dishes I had were  chicken steak with veggies and different kinds of salads. The greek salad was a tasty delight. My favourite dining experience would be in an ambience which is open and breezy and that is exactly what it was. A beach is the perfect place to dine for me with the lovely sea food delicacies. However, I am going to remember the Dubai meal for quite a long time.

Heading: MEAL TICKET - Indian Express
Content:
Bibimbap
(Pronounced bee-bim-bop)
Don't hesitate to ask for it: Bibimbap is one of Korea's best-known dishes this side of Seoul. Nutritious and delicious, bibimbap is a simple-to-make dish. It just takes steaming hot sticky rice and ladles of vegetable stew or meat to get it right. In Korean, it means mixed meal.

The first mention of bibimbap has been found in a 19th century in anonymous cook book called Siuijeonseo. In the book it's called Buibuimbap.

A raw or fried egg and pieces of beef are the usual additions to a dish of bibimbap. These ingredients are mixed into the dish just before eating. In most of the common Korean households, it's a regular everyday food.

Heading: Piggy's Bank Full - Indian Express
Content:
Succulent Sushi
The Sushi and Tempura festival at Le Meridien held at the Entresol Bar promises to be a culinary delight. Between November 3 and 9 from 7pm to 11.30 pm, the highlight will be the appetizer platter that will have Tuna, Salmon, Shrimp and Scallop Sushi. Exotic dishes such as vinegar rice roll stuffed with avocado and crab roe will be on offer alongside traditional fare like the ever-popular Japanese sticky rice, prawn and seafood tempura and for vegetarians a paneer tempura. One can wash it all down with Choya Sake while enjoying live music by the two piece band, Billy and Eliza.

Heading: Flight of fantasy - Indian Express
Content:
In the city for the promotion of her recent release, Fashion, Priyanka Chopra says that acting is all about reinvention

It might have taken almost over half of the movie to make Priyanka Chopra aka Piggy Chops a showstopper in her recent release- Fashion; but in real life, she is undoubtedly a showstopper already. Dressed in black, the dusky, girl-next-door of Bollywood with her charming appearance at the show of her film Fashion, caught the audience unawares at E-Square when she dropped in-between the screening with director Madhur Bhandarkar and Mughda Godse.

The model-turned-actor who plays the lead in Fashion, a story a super model, however comments that despite the modeling background, she had to put in extra efforts to get ready for the role. "I had been a model for only four months before I got into films, so in a way I still had to prepare and relearn and rehearse a lot. Seasoned models like Diandra, Alicia and Mugdha gave me tips on the correct walk and precise postures to carry off particular outfits." Chopra is said to be wearing about 137 different outfits for this film. In response to the queries on the murky details of the fashion industry she reveals, "I have been a part of the fashion world, but then in my real life I haven't come across most of the situations that are shown in the film." She further adds, "Sometimes I did not agree with what I was portraying in the film and that really affected me after a shoot."

Having started her acting career with films like Andaaz and Aitraaz followed by a string of films like Big Brother, Love Story 2050, God Tussi Great Ho, Chamku and Drona that failed to do well at the box office, Chopra justifies her move to Madhur Bhandarkar's brand of filmmaking as, "Acting for me is about reinvention. I want to experiment with as many roles as possible. I have done action, thrillers and comedy. I have in fact played a villain as well. Fashion is slightly more intense woman oriented story and I felt it was a challenging role. My next film Dostana is again a complete entertainer. I like to keep people guessing."

So what's next? And she says candidly "I like to work in films executed on a nice big scale as it helps to project the director's vision better. My next film would be Dostana, which is releasing this month after which Kaminay and What's your Rashee would hit the screens next year."

Heading: Purohit a patriotic man, say his neighbours - Indian Express
Content:
Theatre Academy, Pune revives Satish Alekar's 1979 play Begum Barve for Ranga Shankara Theatre Festival

At 28, he breathed life into the character of Begum Barve, at 58 he again resurrects the soul of a woman trapped in a man's body. It was 1979 when Satish Alekar, Chandrakant Kale, Ramesh Medhekar and Mohan Agashe came together to bring to life the enticing and seductive world of the Marathi musicals of the Balgandharv era starkly contrasting it to the plight of a transvestite.

Now in the year 2008 for the third time the quartet comes together to revive the play with the time transition acting as a catalyst to better the performance of the actors. For so feels Kale whose small time female impersonator role as Begum Barve had Naseeruddin Shah packing up his shoot in New Delhi to see the show. "Reviving a play is always a great experience. This is the third time we are doing that and every time we revive this play we as actors step up and arrive at another level of performance. The maturity that has grown over the years betters our performance every time we revive the play," shares Kale.

The play that operates on more than one level provides a vast canvas to paint the many layers of life and fantasy. The intermittent existence of the two is what draws the audience to the edge of its seats every time Jawadekar and Barve come together to create a fantasy of their own. "The play revolves around how male chauvinism drives our society. How even after being beaten up by Shyamrao, Barve still goes about hunting for food to satiate Shyamrao's hunger. I feel even though the play has the 1890s Balgandharv era in its backdrop, it still makes the present audience relate to it in many ways," shares Mohan Agashe who plays the foul-mouthed drunkard Shyamrao, Barve's patron.

Barve, a charming androgynous from the Marathi musicals, who uses incense and song to weave a web of illusion and seduction in his desperate quest to escape poverty and sexual exploitation, enthralled its audience in 1979 when it opened in Delhi. Way ahead of its times, Satish Alekar's Begum Barve had critics applauding hard for the play and now when the third time its revived Begum Barve come alive with the same emotional turmoil, mockery and irony, all without any trace of the maudlin. With its original cast intact and the same electrifying charge permeating the atmosphere, the play promises to recreate the same world that flitted between reality and abstraction all over again. "The irony is that the protagonist is able to cope with reality because he does not live in reality," elaborates Agashe.

The music, dating back to the 1890s, is what the audience might find hard to relate to but according to Alekar the oppression of Barve is what every individual can identify with. "The music of the Sangeet Natak tradition presented in Bakgandharva's style might be little tough for the audience to relate to but the idea of not living in reality to cope with it is something every soul today can associate with and so I think the revival of this play holds relevance in today's context too," says Alekar.

(The play will be staged at Bharatnatya Mandir at 5.30 pm today)

Heading: DC to enquire into recovery of 200 female foetuses - Indian Express
Content:
The neighbours of Lt Col Prasad Purohit vouch for his patriotism.

While the serving armyman was being grilled in Mumbai by the Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS), his residence at Erandwane, off Law College Road, was being virtually besieged by the TV and print media.

No family member of Lt Col Purohit was available for comment, but people staying in the neighbourhood said he was a patriotic man who would never do anything to harm the nation.

It was also learnt that he had been coached for the service selection board (SSB) interview by Lt Col Jayant Chitale (Retd) of the Maharashtra Military Foundation (MMF). "Purohit attended my SSB training course for seven days in February 1993. He was commissioned in the army and as per my knowledge, was an outstanding officer who had a high degree of patriotism," said Chitale, who had once floated the idea of a Commando Academy for setting up suicide squads to carry out attacks in Pakistan. "I am not sure about his involvement in the Malegaon blasts. But the fact is that many army officers are angry with the government's failure in tackling terrorism and may think of their own ways of combating it," he said.

Meanwhile, a neighbour of Lt Col Purohit said, "He visits his Pune house once in a while. We never had a long interaction with him. But we consider him to be a very patriotic man."

Heading: Haryana Day brings joy for senior citizens - Indian Express
Content:
In an endeavour to send a message to officers allegedly responsible for encouraging female foeticide and violation of PNDT Act in Gurgaon, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Deputy Commissioner (DC), Gurgaon, to conduct an administrative enquiry.

The enquiry has been ordered after the HC took serious note of the matter in which nearly 200 female foetuses were recovered from a deep well underground septic tank at Buala Nursing Home, Pataudi, Gurgaon few months ago.

"An administrative enquiry shall be conducted by Deputy Commissioner (DC), Gurgaon into incident relating to recovery of female foetus from septic tank of Buala Nursing Home...in particular regarding lapses on part of any officer," a division bench headed by the HC Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur ruled.

The report is to be submitted within three months, as per the HC orders.

The directions were passed in wake of a public interest litigation (PIL) demanding strict action against those encouraging and facilitating female foeticide. During the pendency of the petition, the law officers for Punjab and Haryana submitted that enquiries have already been marked in various districts in imilar matters. The law officer for Punjab government even submitted that an enquiry had been marked by the Deputy Commissioner Patiala in a case and those found guilty will be proceeded against shortly. Moreover, FIRs have also been registered against few guilty medical officers.

Taking a similar stand, the law officer for Haryana government submitted that the matter is being looked into seriously and those officers found guilty have been proceeded against already.

Heading: Media committee constituted, Rana appointed chairman - Indian Express
Content:
Providing special facilities to the senior citizens in the state, Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda today announced the decision to launch two new schemes for their benefit, besides a scheme for patients of heamophilia on the occasion of Haryana Day, falling tomorrow.

Hooda said that it had been decided to provide 50 per cent concession to women above 60 years of age in bus fare in state roadways buses. It would benefit about six lakh women.

Another scheme to provide spectacles to senior citizens of below poverty line families would be implemented from Saturday. The scheme would benefit about five lakh persons and cost the state exchequer about Rs 10 crore.

As per the scheme launched for the benefit of haemophilic persons, the Health Department would provide free AHF treatment to heamophilia patients on episode-basis through recognised NGOs or institutions. He also said that the Haryana State Blood Transfusion Council would prepare smart cards (photo ID cards) of all patients of haemophilia, besides providing them free education upto class 10 in government schools and free travel facility to the nearest health facility.

Heading: On a roll - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, who has been planning cabinet expansion and appointment of BJP functionaries decided to open the first channel for political appointments yesterday.

Ganesh Dutt, party's district chief in Shimla was appointed as vice-chairman of Himachal Pradesh Housing and Urban Development Authority (HIMUDA). Dutt had held this post during Dhumal's earlier tenure also.

Rajender Rana, BJP's spokesman for a long time and Dhumal's close confidant, has been appointed as Chairman of the newly constituted Media Advisory Committee.

This is first time when Dhumal has decided to appoint a chief of media advisory with seven other members, four of them from the organisation. Dr Ashok Kapahtia, who had been party's media incharge during last year's assembly elections has been made the member of the committee with Sanjay Sharma and Parveen Sharma.

Parveen Sharma was party's candidate in Mandi but was later asked to retire.

Rana had been a contender for the assembly ticket from Hamirpur, which was later given to Urmil Thakur, daughter-in-law of BJP's veteran leader Jagdev Chand.

Later his name was also considered for Lok Sabha by-election from Hamirpur but Dhumal's son Anurag Thakur was fielded.

The Chief Minister has finally thought of accommodating Rana in the government.

Bhim Sen, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister, Secretary Information and Public Relations Ram Subhag Singh will be members of the committee with Director Public relations J R Katwal as member secretary.

Dhumal has been under pressure from the party to appoint some of its key-functionaries, who were denied tickets during 2007 elections as chairman and vice-chairman. Though a number of MLAs are also eyeing at official positions, Dhumal appears to be in no hurry to oblige them.

Heading: Poster Shot - Indian Express
Content:
Wondering whatever happened to city model Jonita Doda? Well, our girl's in action once again with a slew of projects

It's been a while since we bumped into this leggy model from the city. In fact, it's been so long, we can't really remember when! And that's perhaps got much to do with the fact that all of us don't watch that many South Indian flicks. For Jonita Doda has been on a roll, quite literally, in the southern part of the country. "I just wrapped up a Kannada film that's due for release in November," mentions Doda who flitted across to the small screen with a kitty of shows, the recent one being as a host for Sahara One's 'Comedy Champions'. "It was a good experience and I got to do a gamut of things but I think I am done with television for the moment," admits Jonita who kick-started her modelling career in the city pretty early on. "I was just out of school when I started modelling after winning many titles," Jonita brushes us up. But down the years which also saw her step out as a choreographer, she decided to return to academics. "That's when I got busy finishing my studies and we didn't get to meet," smiles the model now turned full-time actor.

And work is what brings her home from Mumbai. "I am currently shooting for a Punjabi film titled 'Chak Jawaana'," informs Doda who is paired opposite singer-actor Gurdas Mann. "My character is called Binny and it's a nice youthful film with a message," mentions the actor who was more thrilled to know when told she would be shooting on home turf. "Since I have shifted my base to Mumbai, it's always nice to come home. In fact I look for reasons," laughs Jonita who has also signed on a Hindi film. "Bollywood is where I want to be and frankly the shift to Mumbai hasn't been that tough," admits Jonita who goes on to add, "Mumbai gives you your breathing space and lets you grow as an actor. But I always carry a chip on my shoulder for the fact that I am from Chandigarh. It's a proud feeling." We ditto that.

Heading: Sound Advice - Indian Express
Content: Bollywood buffs, here's a treat you can't miss. As part of a fund raiser, People for Animals, Chandigarh has put up their exhibition cum sale of rare Bollywood posters titled Divas Unveiled. A collector's item, you'll find those dramatically drawn Eastman coloured posters of a bygone era, of films that have been masterpieces. From bestsellers like Sholay, Mother India and Mughal-e-Azam to Raj Kapoor and Amitabh Bachchan series, first edition prints of Aah, Barsaat, Aan, Boot Polish, Sangam, Shri 420, Anarkali, Aar Paar, Kati Patang, Khandaan, Do Ankhen Barah Haath, Daag, Johnny Mera Naam, Don, The Great Gambler, Yaarana, Sholay, Deewar, Trishul, Suhaag, Muquadar Ka Sikander to latest films like Don, Om Shanti Om, Mangal Pandey, Chak de India, Devdas, the posters are on display and for sale at the Government Art Gallery, Sector 10, Chandigarh till November 3. The posters are available in two sizes i.e. 40" x 30" & 30"x 20". The exhibition was formally inaugurated by Ram Niwas, Home Secretary, Chandigarh Administration. The exhibition will remain open from 10 am to 6 pm.

Heading: Back in Scene - Indian Express
Content:
In order to break them, a good musician has to know all the rules, the multi-talented Hunterz whips up his theory

As sharp as a whip. Alveen's always been in life's fast lane, and so, it took no time for his parents to stick to their storm of a son's pet name, Hunterz. "An urban English musician with Arabic, Hindi and Bhangra influences," a heavily Brit accented voice introduces himself at the other end. It takes time to get used to it, but a quick read through his bio and our interaction breaks into simpler compounds - the most outstanding one being the 'first British Asian' to perform with Michael Jackson and UB40, that too live.

"I've born into a very musical family," Hunterz trained in Indian classical music and studied under tabla legend Ustad Sukhwinder Singh 'Pinky' of Benares Gharana. He also has a knack of playing varied instruments, so it comes as no surprise that he can tap a range from tabla, harmonium (percussion) to guitar, bass guitar, drums, piano etc. By the age of nine he was playing with different bands and performing on stage regularly. "After studying from the Guitar Institute of London and participating in the Royal National Theatre's production 'Wicked Yaar', I got into the professional music arena," says Hunterz who made history when shared the stage with King of Pop, Michael Jackson in Mumbai. Wet Wet Wet, Lisa Stansfield, Brand New Heavies, Lou Bega, Sting, UB40, Hans Raj Hans, Malkit Singh, Shin (DCS)...Hunterz whipped up music with the record names. "UB40 was the best. With others, it's like come and go, but with these guys, it's on a different wavelength altogether. They share my music, and we are great friends too," Hunterz was also instrumental in producing Stereo Nation's smash hit album Slave II Fusion. Singer, producer, songwriter, musician, the guy credits his rich environment with his ecclectic influences. "I was brought up in a area surrounded by Sri Lankans, Pakistianis, Bangladeshis, Punjabis, the British and all this trickled down in my music." But what he also credits is his taleem, his training and knowledge sharing process. "If you want to break the rules, you've got to know them real well first," he gives a sound advise, adding that in order to sustain and survive, you've got to be original and earn the respect of your peers and fans. "Else, everyone manages 15 minutes, a year or two and fade out." Hunterz wanted more than that. After a long wait, the musician finally released his debut project 'Most Wanted' in 2003, which propelled him in the international market as a solo artist. Remember the song 'Rehle' and Hans Raj Hans 'Aja Kuriyeh'?

"There was another album with my brothers, and then lot of remixes, but now, I am looking forward to my album, The Masterpiece." Music for a Pakistani film, item number with Sunidhi Chauhan and one with Richa Sharma, Hunterz on a roll. "It's a very competitive world out there, you've got to churn out something new, something fresh everyday." But is Indian music a global phenomenon? "Of course, Asian music is taken very seriously. Americans have been using big samples from Asian music, and the biggest market is the UK."

For Hunterz, the most veratile artist is Apache Indian, and the guru of all, late Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. "I've learned that you need to be open and grow with time, only then will you be successful and alive." Another sound advise.

Heading: New Fizz - Indian Express
Content:
With two films — Karzz and EMI — hitting the screens within a fortnight, we might hazard a guess that this is Urmila Matondkar's comeback year. But ask Matondkar and the once-Rangeela girl would shrug: "I was never out of the scene. It was just that the scripts were not appealing enough. I don't do films just because I have to be in the limelight."

In EMI, which will be released on November 7, Matondkar plays a widow who needs a personal loan to make ends meet, after her husband commits suicide. "It is very different from my role of a vamp in Karzz," said Matondkar, dressed in a flowing green dress. The actor might not have had a string of box-office hits but has evidently been spared the need to take a loan in real life.

And if she is to be believed, the film has ensured that she will never take one in future. "I never knew there was a thriving underground business of recovery agents," she rolled her eyes in disbelief. Now with two films down, she is all set to let her hair down and go home.

Heading: Stitch in time - Indian Express
Content: Coca-cola India has announced the launch of its latest product innovation under the Fanta brand umbrella. The new 'Fanta Apple' is a refreshing apple flavoured sparkling drink developed especially for Indian consumers. Targeted at the young and the restless, the consumer proposition is best explained by the communication tagline - "Go Bite".  As part of the launch, the company also announced the signing up of the new Fanta brand ambassador- the young and charming, Genelia D'Souza of 'Bommarilu', 'Boys' and 'Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na' fame. Fanta Apple has been made available in a range of pack sizes - 200 ml & 300 ml returnable glass bottles (RGB) priced at Rs 8 and Rs 10 respectively. In addition, the apple flavoured drink has also been made available in mobile 500 ml PET pack priced at Rs 22. According to Venkatesh Kini, Vice-President- Marketing, Coca-Cola India, "This product has been developed specially for Indian palates. Apple is one of the most preferred fruits in the country."

Heading: First Romance Hero - Indian Express
Content:
After making their debut on the ramps of the Wills Lifestyle Fashion Week, this designer couple makes a special visit to Mohali's NIIFT where they first spun their dreams

It's a proud moment for all. The institute's director calls them "notoriously creative" while a teacher remembers them as "the bright sparks". Proving both of them right is the couple we meet on NIIFT Mohali's campus on Friday afternoon. Hemant Lalwani and his partner (both in profession and marriage) Nandita Raipurani are just breathing easy after a hectic Wills Lifestyle Fashion Week that saw the duo debut in style. Interestingly, both are former fashion design students having graduated from NIIFT in the year 2002. "Whenever we are interviewed we always make it a point to mention that we are from NIIFT Mohali and not NIFT, Delhi," laughs Nandita who along with Hemant is conducting a workshop for the present batch of students at Mohali.

"It's the least we can do for our alma mater," chorus the couple who got raving reviews with their debut collection. "We titled it 'Wardrobe Rock Art'. It's our take on the super feminine yet vibrant and on-the-move Indian woman," explains Nandita who likes to term their style as a lot of "mix and match." "While our silhouettes are Western, we have Indian themes running right through. Like this time we combined hand paint with dabka," Hemant pitches in with the details.

Having previously worked independently with designers like Malini Ramani and Aparna Jagdhari, Hemant and Nandita fell in love with each other and their individual creativity on campus. "But we both had a singular focus. That was to start our own label," Nandita speaks up. Today, the two retail out of Hong Kong, Dubai, London, New York, Jakarta and through Kimaya stores in India. "As students you are unclear of your future. So were we but we kept on track and worked hard towards making the dream come true," the two chorus out the advice.

Since they are all set for Autumn-Winter 08 and are already working for the summer ahead, we couldn't help but ask them to dish out trends. "The colour grey is in. As far as ensembles go, low-waist is out and high-waists are in," lists out Nandita as Hemant adds, "We did a range of high-waist skirts and trousers in our Fashion Week collection as well. There's a lot of masculine fashion for women like cuffed shirts, formal trousers, shirts et al," sums up Hemant. Got it!

Heading: Lull after financial storm - Indian Express
Content:
He made an impact in Jodhaa Akbar. Now catch Punjab's own Sonu Sood as the romantic lead

Sonu Sood, best remembered as Sujamal in Jodhaa Akbar, is finally playing the romantic lead. He will be seen serenading khallas girl Eesha Koppikhar in Ek Vivah— Aisa Bhi releasing this November.With this film, the 33-year-old actor has two reasons to smile. "I will finally be doing something other than action and I'll get to play the guitar," smiles Sood. Shooting is complete for the Kaushik Ghatak directed film who's previously directed Kyunki saas bhi kabhi bahu thi and Sanjivni. Sood insists the film will be completely different from Ghatak's specialty, of saas bahu dramas. But cheesy family dramas are Rajshri Productions' forte, remember? "I play Prem an aspiring singer from Bhopal who meets Esha and falls in love with her voice. He has to wait for 12 years until he can marry her," says Sood, sounding optimistic about the screen play. Typically, Koppikar's character is simple and blemish free, a pretty girl who plays the harmonium and worships a tulsi plant in her courtyard. Clichéd though the plot may sound, playing a romantic lead in a Rajshri Production is a big step for a bit actor like Sood.

Heading: Bickering in Bathinda Congress comes to fore - Indian Express
Content:
Markets melt, Indo-Pak trade freezes Volume down by 50 per cent; trucks stand still, traders worried

The financial meltdown and strengthening of the US dollar has hit the Indo-Pak trade through Attari-Wagah border land route hard.

The traders are worried, as there has been over 50 per cent fall in the total volume of export and import. There has also been a decrease in demand of various commodities, including green vegetables, in Pakistan.

So dismal is the situation that no goods truck was able to cross over to Pakistan in the last two days. The Pakistan's economy is experiencing troubled times with inflation escalating, leading to a sharp fall in the demand of daily need commodities.

"The financial trouble worldwide has impacted the Indo-Pak trade too due to the ripple effect in the Asian markets. There is insecurity in Pakistan's market, and strengthening of the US dollar against Pakistani Rupee is adding to our woes," said Rajdeep Uppal, a leading exporter of goods to Pakistan. Uppal said import of cement from Pakistan and export of vegetables, especially green chilies, tomatoes and potatoes, livestock, meat and some electronic goods, had given a major impetus to the trade between the two countries earlier this year.

"The year began on a promising note, as trucks were allowed to cross over to the international border. The trade was picking up when financial upheaval led to the slowdown, which is worrisome," said Om Parkash, alias Latti Shah, president of the Amritsar-Lahore Exporters-Importers' Association.

He said fluctuation had started in June, but October was the worst month, as now only potatoes were in demand in Pakistan. "The lower liquidity and extra caution being taken by the banks to give credit is yet another reason for the lull," said Shah, adding that 5 per cent duty being imposed by the Pakistan's government on imports from India was a big hurdle in bilateral trade.

The last available figures show that the volume of trade had touched Rs 800 crore annually, but if the meltdown continues, the figure would fall to Rs 400 crore.

The Customs Department figures reveal that import of cement from Pakistan had started a year ago and its volume rose from 480 metric tonnes in 2007 to 60,000 metric tonnes in April-May this year. "But then the steady decline started and volume of cement import could not go beyond 35,000 metric tonnes in August-September," said Customs officials.

Customs and Excise Commissioner Talkeshwar Singh admitted that the number of trucks crossing over has fallen by 50 per cent. "There is a decline in the volume of trade, as markets are volatile at present," he said. However, Gunbir Singh, state vice-convener of the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII), said the slowdown of trade through Attari was a short-term effect.

"To beat the inflation, Pakistan will have to open trade of common goods from India. It is only a matter of time. I feel that the trade will bounce back to the original volume again," he said, adding that business would cross the figure of Rs 1,000 crore.

Heading: Three held for attempt to kill Dera follower in Mansa - Indian Express
Content:
Infighting in the Bathinda Congress came to the fore today on the occasion of a party function held to mark the 24th death anniversary of slain Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Congress MLAs, Gurpreet Kangar from Rampura Phul and Makhan Singh from Pacca Kalan, chose not to attend the function presided over by state party chief Mohinder Singh Kaypee, alleging that urban unit of the district Congress did not invite them and deliberately sidelined them.

Congress MLA from Nathana Ajaib Singh Bhatti, who also did not attend the function, however, claimed that he had some "urgent work". The three MLAs accorded a welcome to the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief near Rose Garden before the function.

"The party high command had asked the urban unit of the Congress to organise the function. They (urban unit) did not invite us," said Kangar.

Makhan Singh was equally vocal in expressing his resentment. "We waited for two hours on the road to welcome the party president. We would have attended the function had we been invited," he said, adding that he received a call from the urban unit chief at 8:30 am, saying that the party chief was coming at 11:30 am. "Though the party chief had talked to me a few days ago, the urban unit, being the organisers, should have also roped me in," said Makhan.

Incidentally, Kangar, Makhan and Bhatti are considered to be Capt Amarinder Singh loyalists.

Harminder Jassi, who is believed to be from leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal's camp, was the only MLA from Bathinda district constituencies to attend the function.

Ashok Kumar, district president of the urban unit of the Congress, however, said the MLAs who were complaining had been invited by the PPCC. "Even I had made telephone calls to Makhan Singh and Ajaib Bhatti," claimed Ashok. "They are new and young leaders of the party. They do not know much about party's culture," fumed Ashok.

Kaypee, while ruling out any factionalism in the party, said MLAs had come to welcome him and there could be some differences which would be ironed out.

Kaypee said while Bhattal could not make it to the function as she was in Nanded, Amarinder could not come due to some personal work. Earlier, Kaypee hailed Indira Gandhi and urged the Congress workers to follow her ideology.

Heading: Machine out of order: doctors refuse to operate - Indian Express
Content:
Terrorists and criminals continue to lure innocents into their fold. This revelation came out during the interrogation of Sarabjit Singh alias Makhan Singh, a close associate of terrorist Paramjit Singh Panjwar who was involved in masterminding the attack on a Dera Sacha Sauda supporter in Bhikhi in Mansa district last month.

While Sarabjit was arrested recently from Delhi and was being interrogated by the Patiala Police for the last eight days, his three accomplices were nabbed today for trying to kill Bhola Singh, a supporter of Dera Sacha Sauda and businessman in Bhikhi, on September 6.

Patiala SSP SK Asthana said the three arrested included Didar Singh alias Dari of Baba Bakala in Amritsar, Bahal Singh alias Bala of Singhpura in Killianwali in Sirsa and Ajmer Singh of Langianwali in Gurdaspur district.
