The three were to initially carry out the killing of Bhola Singh's brother Mithu Singh, who was a member of the 15-member committee of Dera Sacha Sauda. They later attempted to kill Bhola, but he survived with injuries.

Bala was lured by Sarabjit Singh into his fold on the pretext of helping him settle a personal enmity with a local villager. Bala is the fourth such person enticed by terrorists after Bagicha Singh, Amarjit Singh and Gobind Kaur, who were arrested from Patiala in a case of attack on Dera Sacha Sauda chief.

Incidentally, Sarabjit, a resident of Sardoolgarh, is also close to Baba Bakshish Singh, a Patiala resident who is wanted for masterminding the attack on Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh in Karnal last year. Asthana said Sarabjit has been in touch with Panjwar and Bakshish over telephone and the police were now trying to zero in on the latter.

Panjwar is presently in Pakistan and aiding terrorist activities, which also have support of splinter groups in the USA, the UK and Canada, Asthana said.

The police have recovered a motorcycle used by the three while trying to kill Bhola, besides a 9-mm pistol, some live cartridges and 200 grams of smack from their possession.

They were presented before the local magistrate for their police remand. Search for the fourth accused was on, said Asthana.

Heading: Phoolka for travel ban on perpetrators of anti-Sikh riots - Indian Express
Content:
Over two dozen operations have been held up in Urology department of the IGMC Hospital where the lone telescope available for carrying out trans urethral resection of prostrate (TUR) has been out of order since past two days.

Sources said the department should have had three such instruments but the repeated demands have fallen on deaf ears of hospital administration.

The Urology department at IGMC Hospital in Shimla is the only one in the state that conducts TUR surgery. On an average 25 patients come here each month from far off places.

One patient, on the condition of anonymity said, "I was to be operated on October 29 but as the machine was not functioning the doctors did not operate. Now I do not know whether to stay back or go somewhere else for treatment."

Though the doctors of Urology department refused to talk about the issue, Principal of IGMC, Dr Surender Kashyap said, "The doctors should not stall operations just because the telescope is damaged. Conventional methods can be used rather than causing inconvenience to the patients."

He said the hospital was trying to get the telescope repaired or replaced. "It is a costly instrument and it may take time for things to get back to normal," he added.

The telescope is used to operate patients of bladder cancer and prostrate. When there was no machine in the state the prostrate operations was done by conventional method but the bladder cancer patients had to go out of the state for treatment.

Heading: Energy-efficient building to be awarded - Indian Express
Content:
Supreme Court senior advocate and former senior standing counsel for the Union government Harvinder Singh Phoolka addressed MPs in UK Parliament ahead of the 24th anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

The event was hosted by British Parliamentarian Rob Marris, who is also the Chair of the All Party Parliamentary Group for UK Sikhs. Phoolka, who spoke in the Jubilee Hall in the UK House, trained guns at Congress leaders, including Jagdish Tytler, and demanded a worldwide travel ban on them.

Phoolka has been representing as the counsel for the 1984 riot victims and fighting for their rights for decades. Phoolka said a coalition to campaign for a worldwide travel ban on those involved in genocide and crimes against humanity had now been put in place. Responding to a query by The Indian Express through e-mail today, he said the coalition comprising Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, Liberty and Redress Trust, would be a powerful medium to press for the demand.

The event was attended by a group of MPs, including Minister John Spellar and Shadow Attorney General Edward Garnier. Phoolka said the focus of his lecture was to emphasise that the persons committing "communal violence" to terrorise a community were no less than terrorists. "We requested MPs to impress upon the UK government not to allow Tytler and others to enter," he said.

Phoolka alleged, "The 1984 genocide was the beginning of the government-sponsored violence against a minority community in India."

He said had the guilty of 1984 riots been punished, the killing of Christians would not have taken place. Kevin Laue, a Zimbabwean rights lawyer representing the Redress Trust, explained the steps that were needed to ensure that there was a political will to implement the travel ban.

Heading: Akali Dal factions clash at wedding of Cong man’s son - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Energy Development Agency (PEDA) has introduced energy conservation awards to encourage energy efficiency in large and small-scale industry, government and commercial buildings, educational institutions, agriculture sector, poultry farms and domestic sector.

Bikram Singh Majithia, Science and Technology and Non-Conventional Energy Minister, today said these awards have been instituted to encourage people to conserve energy. The minister said investment grade energy audit of 10 government buildings has been started and recommendations by the consultant to bring energy efficiency would be implemented by the departments concerned.

Majithia said the government has decided to introduce energy efficient municipal street-lighting system in Amritsar, Jalandhar, Ludhiana, Patiala and Bathinda.

The government would also initiate energy efficiency in district administration complexes in Ludhiana, Patiala, Bathinda, Sangrur and mini-secretariat in Chandigarh. The PEDA has made a detailed project report for these projects and tenders would be floated by the Local Government Department and the PWD (B&R).

TPS Sidhu, Chief Executive, PEDA, said details for participation in the award programme would be available on the website of the Punjab government and the agency.

This scheme has been formulated in line with the guidelines of Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, Government of India. He said the award would carry cash, memento and certificate.

Heading: Dengue cases on rise in Amritsar, officials wait for the chill to set in - Indian Express
Content:
Two Akalis factions clashed at a Congressman's function in which over a dozen rounds were fired in the air from AK-47 rifles snatched from official security guards.

The ceremony of marriage of son of Bhupinder Singh Bhindu, an influential Congress leader from Majitha, was in full swing at Maharaja Marriage Palace on GT Road when the two groups, one led by Zila Parishad chief Rajinder Singh Pappu and other by Gurpreet Singh Bhoewal, got into a verbal spat. Pappu's son Dipu reportedly opened fire, which was returned by Kala and Ghuk, Bhoewal supporters. Both the local leaders are close to minister Bikram Singh Majithia.

Bhindu said Akalis tried to disrupt the party, but he did not want any police report to be filed. Verka police station SHO Satwant Singh Sidhu said though no one has come forward to lodge the complaint, they have registered a case under Section 336 of IPC and the Arms Act and action would be initiated against the security guards from whose rifles the fires were shot. DSP Balkar Singh said they have started investigations.

Heading: Man, 2 sons get life term for twin murder - Indian Express
Content:
Instead of taking steps to control dengue in the city, the district health officials are waiting for the weather god to intervene and bring down the temperature.

The increasing number of dengue patients admitted to various hospitals is giving sleeplessness nights to the health officials, who have so far failed to check the disease.

Sources said till date, more than 173 dengue patients have been treated and 10 more were admitted to Guru Nanak

Dev Hospital.

Dr RPS Boparai, Medical Superintendent of the hospital, said doctors were waiting for the weather gods to turn merciful. "The number of dengue patients will come down in the next couple of days when the temperature lowers, as mosquitoes die in cold weather," he said.

Ten patients were undergoing treatment at Fortis Escorts Heart and Super-specialty Hospital, said Medical Superintendent Dr HP Singh.

"We have done the best we could. Number of cases will come down with change in weather," said Dr Lehamber Singh, Amritsar Civil Surgeon.

Heading: Refused parole, inmate goes on hunger strike - Indian Express
Content:
The court of Additional Session Judge RS Rai today awarded life sentences to three persons, a man and his two sons, in a twin murder case, where a couple was shot dead in November 2005 in Bathinda.

Ashok Kumar and his sons, Deep Rattan and Amardeep, both in their twenties, were booked for murder, attempt to murder and under a section of the Arms Act on November 8, 2005, after Raj Kumar and his wife Pushpa were shot dead and their son Jatin was injured in firing from a .32 bore licensed weapon.

Raj and Ashok, both brothers, were locked in a property dispute, said advocate Nand Lal Garg, the counsel for rosecution.

The court awarded two sentences of life imprisonment to the three and a fine of Rs 20,000 each. For attempt to murder, besides a fine of Rs 5,000, Ashok got seven years' imprisonment, while his sons were awarded five years each.

The court also awarded another sentence of three years to Ashok under the Arms Act. The sentences would run concurrently.

"It is good that justice has been done. But today's verdict also refreshed the disturbing memories of the most unfortunate incident that occurred in my life about three years ago," said Reema, daughter of the deceased couple and a practicing lawyer in Bathinda.

Heading: Four policemen suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Satya Prakash, serving a life term at Model Jail in Kanda near Shimla, is on a hunger strike since past 20 days to protest against refusal of parole. Even though he is admitted to the IGMC hospital, he refuses to eat anything.

Talking to The Indian Express Satya Prakash said the jail authorities have been denying him parole since two years for which they have not given any reason. "People are sent in jail to give a chance to improve but with such injustice they are trying to make us criminals ," Satya Prakash said. In his letters to the Governor and the Chief Minister, he has alleged corruption against in the jail authorities with regard to purchase of wollen clothes for the inmates, medicines and food items. "Inmates are not taken to hospital for many days even after being referred by the jail doctors.

The administration should conduct inquiry into the deaths of four inmates who died last year," he demanded. The jail authorities have refuted his charges. Jaigopal Singh Losta, jail superintendent said, "The Session Judge visits every two months and other senior officers of the department are also aware about the ground reality."On refusal of parole, he said the higher authorities have denied parol on basis of his conduct in the last few years. "Sitting on a hunger strike, he is forcing us to prosecute him under Section 52 of the Prisons Act," said Losta.

Apart from Prakash, another prisoner, Amrish Rana has also levelled the charges of corruption, inhumane treatment of prisoners and smuggling of drugs into the jail.

Heading: 55 injured in bus accidents - Indian Express
Content:
After an undertrial, arrested by Narcotics Bureau of Solan, escaped, Superintendent of Police suspended four cops on the charge of negligence of duty.

The accused Ajmer Singh, resident of Shivalik Enclave of Mohali, was nabbed along with his son Balwinder Singh by Chandigarh Narcotics Bureau at Barotiwala this month. He was sent to judicial custody by the Kasauli court on October 20. After which he was shifted to a sub jail of the town.

The undertrial was admitted to regional hospital after he complained of chest pain on October 24. The district police had deployed four cops in the hospital.

However, Ajmer Singh managed to escape in the morning, putting question mark on the functioning of the police.

Superintendent of Police SPS Verma said soon after receiving the information, all exit points were sealed and a manhunt was launched to nab the culprit. Verma said Head Constable Ramji Dass, Constables Harish Kumar, Rajesh Kumar and Pawan Kumar have been suspensed and a departmental enquiry has also been initiated against them. Messages have also been flashed to the police of neighbouring states, he added.

Heading: Family of gangrape victim seeks CBI probe - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 55 persons were injured in two separate bus accidents, in Shimla district, near Rampur, and Sirmour district. Twenty five persons were injured when a Himachal Road Transport Corporation bus number HP-5320 from Pulwahal on route to Shimla fell in a 200 feet-deep gorge at Bhadoli in district Sirmour.

Police personnel at Rajgarh police station said all injured were referred to Indira Gandhi Medical College and Hospital in Shimla and are reported to be out of danger. The cause of accident is yet to be ascertained, said the Police.

In other incident, 30 persons traveling for a marriage party in private bus number HP-27-0146 were injured when the bus went out of control and crashed into the side of the mountain. The accident happened at 9.30 p.m. at Racholi near Rampur.

The injured were immediately rescued and sent to Rampur hospital for first aid. The bus was going from Magara near Jhakri to Dohi village near Delath in Rampur

Heading: Haryana to pay its share for airport project ‘in a week’ - Indian Express
Content:
It has been more than 45 days since a 17-year-old girl, a resident of Panchkula, was gangraped in Sector 4 here. With no breakthrough in the case till now, her family members have asked for a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). In a written complaint to Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Haryana DGP and the IG, Ambala Range, the family said since the Panchkula police had failed to make any headway till now, an inquiry should be conducted by an independent body or the CBI.

The family has also expressed dissatisfaction with the investigations being made by the police in the case. The victim was gangraped and tortured by a group of four on September 16 in the garage of a Haryana government office in Sector 4. According to the family, the accused included a woman, Chhavi, who was the victim's senior at college.

"It is very disappointing that the police have failed to arrest the accused. And it was only after several requests made to the police that they decided to get the sketches of Jitesh, the main accused, and Chhavi made. Every time we ask them about the status of the case, we are told that investigations are on," said a relative of the victim on the condition of anonymity.

He added that the police were trying to establish that no woman was involved in the crime. "Every time we are called by the police and asked to narrate the incident, we tell them about the role of Chhavi, who along with the other youths tortured the girl and is one of the main accused in the case. But the police refuse to believe this for reasons best known to them," said the relative.

The family said the victim had now been taken to Kurukshetra where she would stay with her relatives and prepare for her examinations.

Station House Officer (SHO) Inspector Surjit Kumar confirmed that there was no development in the case till date. Talking to Newsline, Panchkula Superintendent of Police Sandeep Khirwar said: "The victim was recently called for investigation. We are on the job and are trying to trace the accused."

Arrested in September, the two other accused are in judicial custody.

The family will meet Haryana DGP Ranjiv Dalal and CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Monday.

Action by police

September 22: Aman Ahuja, resident of Sector 10, arrested, taken on one day remand and then sent to judicial custody

September 26: Jatin, a resident of Sector 4, arrested, taken on five-day remand. Police fail to crack the case and the accused is sent to judicial custody

October 22: Sketches of the main accused released

Heading: Retire after 60, HC tells PU teachers - Indian Express
Content:
CM Hooda had earlier gone on record saying the money would not be paid to Punjab, but to the JVC to be formed

After repeatedly objecting to making direct payment to Punjab as its share of the money spent on land acquisition for the Chandigarh International Airport, Haryana government has reportedly succumbed to pressure and agreed to pay Rs 230 crore to its neighbour as its share.

The money for the infrastructure cost would be paid by Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) through the Town and Country Planning Department, despite the fact that the Joint Venture Committee (JVC) is still to be formed between Haryana and Punjab. "The money will be paid in a week's time," said T C Gupta, Chief Administrator, HUDA.

The agreement to this effect was arrived at the meeting of the tripartite committee, comprising Haryana,Punjab and the Airport Authority of India, in September.

Haryana has denied any delay in the payment of its share. "It was agreed at the meeting in September that Haryana will pay the money in about a month's time. There is no hitch in the payment as is made out to be. The process was on and the money will be paid soon," said Samir Mathur, Secretary, Transport and Civil Aviation, Haryana.

The state had earlier insisted that it will pay money for the airport only to the JVC and not to Punjab directly. CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda had gone on record asserting that the money would not be paid to Punjab directly.

Haryana had also vehemently objected to Punjab's decision of calling it Mohali International Airport, arguing that the airport was part of Chandigarh, the capital of both sates, and therefore should be named Chandigarh International Airport.

It is a fact though that because of the geographical constraints, the international terminal of Chandigarh Airport had to be located in Mohali, Punjab. So Punjab had acquired land in Mohali at a cost of Rs 460.82 crore. As per the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Haryana, Punjab and the Airport Authority of India (AAI) on April 4 last, the two states together hold 49 percent stake, while AAI has 51 per cent stake in the project.

It was also agreed to engage Pricewaterhouse Cooper as consultants for incorporating the JVC required for setting up the project. The consultants gave a presentation to Haryana and Punjab officials yesterday.

Heading: Legal retainer tells V-C to relieve 58 teachers with immediate effect - Indian Express
Content:
Petitions dismissed : Court makes it clear teachers who have crossed 60 but are continuing in service, owing to an earlier stay, will have to go

The Punjab and Haryana High Court has fixed the retirement age for teachers of Panjab University at 60 years. On Friday, it dismissed a bunch of petitions filed by PU teachers who had sought an enhancement in the retirement age from 60 to 62 years.

A Division Bench comprising Justice Ashutosh Mohunta and Justice Rajan Gupta quashed the petitions after long arguments that continued for more than three and a half hours. The Bench made it clear that all teachers at PU who had crossed 60 years of age would have to go. The judgment will affect many teachers who have crossed 60 but are still continuing in service, owing to a stay granted by the HC in the past.

The petitioners had taken the stand that PU was a central university and since the retirement age of a teacher in a central university had been extended to 62 years, it should be applied to PU too.

Contesting the plea, advocate Anupam Gupta, legal retainer for the university and senior standing counsel for the UT Administration, submitted that the direction could not be applied to PU as it was not a central university. Gupta said PU was an inter-state university and could not fall in the category of centrally-funded university since it was not completely supported by the Central government and 40 per cent of the funds came from the Punjab government.

The counsel appearing for the teachers had taken the stand that the term 'central university' did not have a definition as such. Calling the term a "bureaucratic imagination", the counsel had stated that if PU was not a central university, it fell in the category of centrally-funded university.

Rubbishing the claims, Gupta submitted that the term 'central university' was defined under Article 371 (E) of the Constitution and that it was also used in Parliamentary laws.

Heading: Mohali to do with 4-hr water supply in Nov - Indian Express
Content:
Legal retainer for Panjab University advocate Anupam Gupta has advised the Vice-Chancellor to relieve all 58 professors who have crossed 60 years of age with immediate effect.

Earlier in the day, the timing of the judgment, on the last day of the month, dismissing all petitions that sought enhancement in the retirement age of teachers had sent the Panjab University authorities into a tizzy. They were in a fix as to whether the professors, whose tenure ended on October 31 and those who were continuing even after crossing 60 years of age should be relieved or not. Allowing them to continue would have meant they would become entitled to the next month's salary.

Since the order was verbally pronounced in the open court, the PU authorities had initially decided to wait for the written judgment. A legal opinion was, however, sought from the legal retainer late evening. Making it clear that allowing the 58 professors to continue may raise question marks over the functioning of the university, Gupta have a detailed legal opinion that these teachers should be relieved immediately.

There are as many as 58 professors, including heads of several departments, who are continuing beyond the age of 60 years.

Prominent among those set to retire are Prof D N Johar, chairperson, Department of Laws; Aruna Goya, chairperson, Department of Correspondence Studies; Prof S K Kulkarni, Dean, University Instructions; and R S Grewal, director, UILS.

"I have advised the Vice-Chancellor that since the High Court has pronounced that the writ petitions are dismissed, the interim orders merged in the final order cannot outlive the dismissal. It will not be proper or in the public interest for the university to allow teachers beyond the age of 60 years to continue after this month. If they are allowed to do so despite the dismissal, it may invite audit objection and also objections from the Government of India and the Government of Punjab because they bear the financial liability of teachers' salaries. Any laxity on part of the university in the matter will be suspected," reads Gupta's legal opinion.

Despite repeated attempts, Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti was not available for comments.

Another problem, meanwhile, stares at PU after the HC judgment. With the university already facing a shortage of around 250 lecturers and professors, losing 58 professors means it is in for a bigger faculty crunch. According to sources, an emergency Syndicate meeting has been called on Saturday to discuss the issue where a concrete decision in this regard is likely to be taken.

The departments are largely dependent on guest faculty at present. In all, 121 lecturers and professors are on the university rolls at present.

With 58 of them on their way out, PU will be left with almost half its faculty strength.

Heading: Punjab pilot cremated with full state honours - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Phase IX, X, XI, Sector 70, 71 and Mataur village in Mohali will get water supply at full pressure for only four hours a day in November. Repair and replacement work at the water treatment plant in Sector 57 will totally snap the afternoon supply while the evening supply will be at low pressure.

In a statement, executive engineer of the Mohali Water Supply and Sanitation department said water supply in these areas would be at full pressure from 5 am to 9 am during the whole of November, while there would be no supply in the afternoon — noon to 1 pm. Water will be received during the evening supply time from 6 pm to 9 pm, but the pressure will be low.

According to the release, filter beds at the Sector 57 plant, which caters to these pockets, will be repaired and replaced during November.

Heading: Decks cleared for Punjab’s first ‘eco town’ - Indian Express
Content:
Captain Dalip Kataria's widow faints as son lights pyre

Mortal remains of Punjab government pilot Captain Dalip Kataria, who died in a plane crash near Ludhiana on October 29, were consigned to flames with full state honours in Chandigarh on Friday. A contingent of 10 Punjab Police personnel fired in the air and reversed their arms as a mark of respect to the departed soul.

Kataria is survived by his wife Bhawna, two daughters Lopa and Hemal, and his son Kapil. While Lopa is a doctor, Hemal is a pilot too and Kapil an aeronautical engineer.

At the cremation, it was evident that Bhawna has not come to terms with the tragedy yet. She fainted as her son lit the funeral pyre of his father. She regained consciousness after immediate medical treatment.

"She (Bhawna) still doesn't believe Dalip is no more. Both had talked over phone a day before the crash and had planned a long overseas trip with children. But destiny had some other plans for them," said Hemant Kataria, a close relative of the family.

"Kapil was very attached to his father and used to take advice from him on every single issue. He is very depressed and not speaking to anybody except his mother," a close friend of Kapil told Newsline over phone.

Punjab Cooperation Minister Kanwaljit Singh laid a wreath on behalf of the Punjab Chief Minister. Chief Secretary R I Singh and a representative of the Indian Air Force, too, placed wreaths on behalf of the Punjab government and Air Commodore S R K Nair, respectively. Among others present were Viswajit Khanna, Secretary, Civil Aviation, Gagandeep Singh Brar, Director, Civil Aviation, and R K Kaushik, Additional Secretary, Political.

Expressing solidarity with the bereaved family, Kanwaljit Singh said the state had lost an experienced pilot and it was a great loss. He assured the family of all support and cooperation on behalf of the government.

Heading: Central pollution board to inspect Dera Bassi plant - Indian Express
Content:
Mullanpur draft master plan receives no major objections, suggestions pertain to change of land use only

With no major objection from any government agency or the public, way seems to have been paved to develop 6,109 hectares of land spread across 33 villages in the periphery of Chandigarh. This will be Punjab's first eco town, as envisaged in the Master Plan of Mullanpur Local Planning Area.

The development assumes significance as the Master Plan of Nayagaon, comprising Karoran, Kansal and Nada villages in the north-east of Chandigarh, had hit the roadblock early this month. The Punjab Forest department had objected to the development and expansion plans envisaged by the Department of Local Government in the draft Master Plan of Nayagaon-2021 released in August.

The Town and Country Planning department, however, has received over 70 objections and suggestions from the public on the draft notification of the Mullanpur Master Plan, which mainly relates to the change of land use and location of certain facilities planned in the area.

Experts from Jurong Consultants Private Limited of Singapore, in the Master Plan submitted to the Punjab government last month, had proposed Mullanpur as a low density, country living, resort centre and northern gateway to Greater Mohali.

Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal had also given his nod on September 27, to invite public objections and suggestions on the draft Master Plan within a month.

All public objections and suggestions received will be taken up for consideration and disposal in the next meeting of the Punjab Town and Country Planning Board, headed by the CM, which will also give an order on the final notification of the master plan for implementation, said a senior official.

Earlier, the Master Plan submitted by the Singapore-based experts, who have been engaged by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), had been adopted without any change or modification either by GMADA or the Town and Country Planning department.

The Mullanpur Master Plan was urgently required to accord change of land use permission for any new project coming up in the area.

With top politicians and bureaucrats having stakes in Mullanpur, the master plan will require all the existing structures to conform to the future planning criteria.

While 33 per cent of the total 6,109 hectares of Mullanpur land is locked under the Punjab Land Preservation Act (PLPA) thereby prohibiting any change of land use or development, 24.4 per cent land was proposed for residential use.

In the remaining 42.6 per cent land, 9.3 per cent was proposed for agricultural use, 6.9 per cent reserved for villages, 3.5 per cent for institutional purposes, 3.4 per cent for mixed-use development, 2.5 per cent for industrial (knowledge village), 2.3 per cent restricted, 0.2 per cent for transport hub and 14.5 per cent for other purposes like water bodies, roads and built-up area among others.

The 33 per cent PLPA land will be used as green spaces, open spaces, recreational purposes and parks.

The master plan presents an opportunity for a well-managed 'eco-town' environment with a variety of new and exciting developments to encourage diversified growth in tourism that balances economic growth with environmental, cultural and community values.

Mullanpur as an 'eco-town' is envisioned to rise as a distinctive and sustainable playground of the Greater Mohali region. The existing rivers and their surrounding waterfronts will be upgraded to become prime physical assets of Mullanpur, which was proposed to offer new lifestyle for the 21st century.

Mullanpur has been planned with new ideas to protect the environmental, historical and cultural resources, capitalise on the regional assets and resources to promote a dynamic and sustainable economic development and to ensure equitable distribution of resources — environmental, economic and social.

The master plan has proposed a population of two lakh in Mullanpur till 2031 and 3.5 lakh by 2056 with a gross residential density of 100 persons per acre.

SPECIAL VIEW CONCEPTS

The Mullanpur Master Plan envisages special view concepts of eco-tourism, health village, knowledge village, eco-park, a technology park, information technology park, transport hub. Special controls have been prescribed along the Siswan river and to protect the scenic beauty of Shivalik Hills. Different height controls suggested varies from 20-40 metres.

Heading: Speeding bus rams into car, 1 critical - Indian Express
Content:
The chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), New Delhi, will now look into the alleged non-functioning of the effluent treatment plant (ETP) of the Punjab Meats Limited (PML) Industries, Dera Bassi. The PML is owned by Dr A S Bindra, father of ace shooter Abhinav Bindra.

The chairman has been directed to institute a committee to look into the matter and submit a report to the Punjab and Haryana High Court within six weeks.

In a dressing down to the PML Industries for not making the ETP completely functional, the High Court had initially questioned Dr Bindra about why the unit should not be closed.

The owner then requested the Court not to close the unit. The Court then directed Bindra to file an affidavit to the effect that if any discrepancies are found in the functioning of the ETP, it will then be closed with immediate effect.

Bindra had then filed an affidavit that post the inspection by the Central Pollution Control Board, if anything is found amiss, the unit will be closed till the time the discrepancies are removed.Advocate Anand Chhibber, counsel for the PML, said the unit can be inspected by some other agency other than the PPCB, which "has been giving negative reports" against the unit.

On the other hand, Advocate A R Takkar, counsel for PPCB, had said that the inspection could be carried out by the Central Pollution Control Board.

It was after Chhibber had offered the inspection to be carried out by the Thapar Institute that Takkar submitted that the issue should be looked into by a Central agency and not by any private institute.

Takkar also said that the expenses incurred by the central agency should be paid by Dr Bindra who was later directed to deposit Rs 50,000 for the conveyance and other expenses of the committee.

Heading: Teachers of aided schools block traffic on NH-21 in Kharar - Indian Express
Content:
A major tragedy was averted when a speeding bus rammed into a car on the National Highway-21 in Kharar on Friday.

While the car driver Sumeer Sharma, in his mid-20s and a resident of Kharar, was seriously injured, around a dozen bus passengers sustained minor injuries as both the vehicles were badly damaged in the mishap.

According to information, the accident took place around 7.30 am when a private bus coming from Mohali, rammed into an Esteem, which entered the highway from a link road leading to the police station.

The impact of the accident was so strong that the bus dragged the car to a nearby field where the mangled remains of both the vehicles finally settled.

The seriously injured car driver was rushed to the PGI in Chandigarh, where he is struggling for life while the injured bus passengers were taken to a private clinic for first-aid. It was alleged that despite repeated calls, no ambulance was made available from the Kharar Civil Hospital to ferry the car driver to the PGI. The hospital authorities, however, expressed ignorance over the matter.

Heading: Mohali resident booked for fraud - Indian Express
Content:
Serving and retired teachers of the government-aided private schools in Punjab blocked traffic on the Mohali-Kharar-Ropar stretch of the National Highway-21 in Kharar on Friday.

Over 1,000 protesters held thousands of commuters to ransom for an hour as long rows of vehicles came to a standstill on the busy highway connecting Chandigarh with major parts of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.

The agitating teachers gathered out of nowhere on the highway and squatted on the middle of the road near the Bus-Stand Chowk.

The local police, caught unawares, found it difficult to tackle such a massive protest in the absence of an adequate force.

Up in arms against the alleged non-payment of their salaries for the last six months, the protesters, led by its state unit president Gurcharan Singh Chahal, raised slogans against the ruling SAD-BJP combine, accusing it of 'back-tracking' from its pre-poll promise of welfare of the private-aided schoolteachers.

The protesters rued that instead of fulfilling the pre-poll promises of lifting the ban on new recruitments, 5 per cent interim relief and increase in medical allowance, the present state government has pushed the aided schoolteachers to starvation without giving any pay for the past six months.

The local police heaved a sigh of relief when the protesters withdrew the demonstration on their own. The protesters, however, threatened to intensify the stir further if the state government failed to take note of their sufferings.

Heading: Chandigarh is fourth emerging metro: study - Indian Express
Content:
Police have booked a resident of Mohali on charges of fraud and forgery with Punjab Information Communications Technology Corporation Limited. The accused has been identified as Satish Kumar Sharma, a resident of Phase 11 in Mohali.

According to police, Satish owned a plot in the Industrial Area in Phase 8, Mohali. He decided to sell it and a deal was struck on September 24, 2008. When the buyer asked for the permanent registration certificate, which is issued by the corporation after clearing all dues, Satish handed over a fake certificate to the buyer.

"There were a few lakh rupees due against the shed and Satish was supposed to deposit the amount with the Corporation before disposing off the plot. But he never deposited the amount," police said.

After the deal, the buyer applied to the Corporation to transfer the ownership of the plot in his name. After going through the records, however, the certificate was found to be fake. The applicant disclosed the matter to the officials of the Corporation and the manager (legal) approached the police with the complaint. After preliminary investigation, a case has been registered against Satish Kumar.

Heading: Liquor being smuggled in truck ‘cavity’ seized - Indian Express
Content:
ASSOCHAM study says city fares well in real estate prices, business environment but lags behind in other parameters necessary for a metro city

Chandigarh comes a close second in real estate prices, financial services and business environment, but lags behind in other five parameters necessary for a metro city, says the ASSOCHAM Eco Pulse Study. The study ranks four tier-II cities — Pune, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Chandigarh — as the most likely contenders for a metro status after Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bangalore and Hyderabad.

They were assessed on eight parameters necessary for a metro city, such as social infrastructure, infrastructure availability, real estate cost and availability, transportation facility (connectivity), presence of quality educational institutes, employment opportunity, facility of financial services and business environment.

According to the analysis, Pune occupies the first position, though it needs to improve on transportation, social infrastructure and financial services. Ahmedabad is the second city with most potential to be a metro, as it provides good infrastructure facilities and connectivity. The study puts Lucknow in the third place as it needs to pick up on infrastructure, business environment and social infrastructure.

Chandigarh, the smallest of the four in terms of area and population, ranks fourth though it fares well in real estate prices, financial services and business environment. At 9.21 per cent, it is the least employment-generating city among the four emerging metros.

Real estate cost and availability

Chandigarh is considered to be the next emerging real estate market after Pune. With the maximum population among the upcoming cities, the Maharashtra town has outpaced the other three cities on this parameter.

Social infrastructure

Chandigarh ranks third on social infrastructure with 81.9 per cent literacy rate and due to the presence of prominent institutes like Institute of Microbial Technology (IMTECH), Centre for Defence and National Strategic Studies (CDNSS). Ahmedabad occupies the first rank with a literacy rate of 79.89 per cent and high-grade institutes Indian Institute of Management (IIM), National Institute of Design (NID), National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) and Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII).

Employment

At 9.21 per cent, Chandigarh is the least employment-generating city. The sectors offering maximum employment are IT, banking, insurance and retail, while Pune has the maximum share of 32.74 per cent in the total jobs tracked by ASSOCHAM Placement Parameter for the period January-June 2008.

Presence of quality educational institutes

Chandigarh occupies third position as the city has a university and eight government colleges, 13 prominent higher learning institutes and one government recognised resource and development centre while Pune and Luchnow rank first and second.

Infrastructure

Pune notches the top position when it comes to sub-parameters like entertainment avenues, malls and multiplexes and star hotels. Chandigarh is placed third in this category.

Connectivity

The parameter of transportation facility is based on a few sub-parameters, such as status of a junction station, railway connectivity with the rest of the country, international airport and the number of national highways passing through the city. Chandigarh ranks last on this front with a non-junction railway station, a domestic airport and only two national highways touching the city. Lucknow occupies the first rank in good connectivity.

Educational facilities

This parameter includes sub-parameters like the presence of central and state universities, other renowned/qualified institutions and presence of R&D centres. Chandigarh ranks third while Pune, home to nine universities, 80-100 public and private institutes along with six government-recognised R& D centres, tops in this parameter.

Financial services

Chandigarh is placed second on sub-parameters such as number of offices of scheduled commercial banks, density of offices of scheduled commercial banks per population, number of accounts of the scheduled commercial banks per population, presence of brokerage firms, stock exchange and transparency in trading system. Lucknow occupies the first position while both Pune and Ahmedabad are placed third in the study.

Business environment

Chandigarh ranks second after Pune on parameters such as progressive government policies, investment scenario, availability of office space, availability of relatively better infrastructure and rising quality of life that drives demand for products.

Heading: Councillors too complain of receiving muddy water in supply - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Police arrested two persons on late Thursday night for allegedly attempting to smuggle nearly 36 cartons of Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) by hiding it in a "cavity" made in the truck.

According to the police, they received a tip off about the liquor to be smuggled out from the city. The police party intercepted a truck (UP-15-J-8427) carrying the liquor late last night.

"The driver of the truck Rashid Ali, from Meerut, was signalled to stop. The driver stopped the truck and very confidently took the policemen to the rear side for checking. There were no cartons of liquor," said Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Jagbir Singh.

The police found an extra cavity at the floor of the truck between the driver's cabin and the rear side of the truck. The driver was asked to remove the plate from the floor of the truck and open the cavity.

"When the driver removed the plate, we found cartons of IMFL liquor. There were 36 cartons containing 12 bottles each in both the cavities," added the DSP.

The truck driver was arrested along with his cleaner Ashok Kumar, who also belonged to Meerut.

The driver disclosed that he was smuggling out the liquor from a liquor vend in Sector 19 to Meerut.

"It is a new trend adopted by smugglers and these miscreants have been using this modus operandi for the past few months. We have intensified our efforts to nab them," said Singh.

A case under the Excise Act has been registered against both the driver and the cleaner. The DSP said they would initiate appropriate action against the liquor vend owner.

Heading: Haryana power corporation to refund penalty - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of the city have often been seen complaining about receiving muddy water in supply. Friday was the turn of the Municipal Corporation councillors.

The issue came up for discussion at the MC House Meet. Councillor Dr Pam Rajput claimed she had stored such samples of water for the officials to see. "It is hazardous for the health of the residents. The problems in water supply should be checked. I boil the water before drinking and a layer of mud settles at the bottom every time," she said.

She added, "Not everyone can afford to filter water before drinking it or buy aquaguards. Health of the residents should be a priority of the concerned officials."

Similar sentiments were echoed by councillor Anu Chatrath, a resident of Sector 15. "We have been storing water samples thrice a day at my house. Every time there is mud in the water. The officials need to rectify the error. With so many diseases being spread through contaminated water, quality of water should be improved."

For the past few days, a number of residents had come up with similar complaints. A resident of Sector 28 had complained of receiving muddy water in supply and another resident of Sector 21 had stated that the water supply to their house had been contaminated for more than a week and was not rectified despite several complaints.

Later, an MC official said that the complaints were being looked into and the problem would be taken care of soon.

Heading: Movie reviews - Indian Express
Content:
Not only the Capital, but also its satellite cities can boast of a less noisy and cleaner Diwali this year. While some did not burst crackers due to the market crash, others abstained from them to protest the recent terror attacks.

Air and noise pollution levels on October 27, 28 and 29 dropped by over 15 per cent in most parts of Gurgaon compared to Diwali last year. Met officials said on Wednesday (the day after Diwali) that the sky was clear as against the usual smog which hangs over the city immediately after the festival.

According to the Deputy Commissioner, Deepti Umashankar, the pollution level was checked at various places across the city over three days. "The suspended particulate matter (SPM) was 832 micro gram per metre cube (mg/Nm^3) as compared to last years 978. The level of respiratory problems intensifying RSPM was at 520 this year compared to 621 in 2007. On the day of Diwali, the level of sulphur dioxide (SO2) was 36 and nitrogen oxide (NOX) was 67 micro gram per metre cube," said Umashankar. She added last year, the level of SPM was 978, RSPM level was 621, SO2 was 49 and NOX level was 77.

According to the DC, the noise pollution level was also checked on Mehrauli-Gurgaon road (near Mall area), bus stand, Sector-4 and 14 which was also five to seven per cent less than last year.

"This shows people are bursting less crackers and it is a good sign for environmentalists," she added. Dr Sanjay Verma, MS, senior consultant ophthalmologist, Paras Hospital said, "The eye is most commonly affected organ of the body due to direct exposure and its fragile nature. Fire crackers can cause severe irreversible changes in the eyes such as corneal burns, cataracts, retinal detachment and permanent damage to other structure of the eyes. Last year, we received 12 eye emergency cases but this year only four cases were reported of which two needed surgeries. This is attributed to the significant reduction in crackers and higher awareness among people."

Dr Aushotosh Shukla, HoD, internal medicine, Artemis Health Institute, said: "The suspended particles less than one micron trigger respiratory function disorder. Also the cases of burn injuries are on the rise during around this time of the year. However, this year we received 30-40 per cent less cases of respiratory disorder as well as cases of burns in our emergency."

Heading: Illegal constructions razed in Sector 55 - Indian Express
Content:
Fashion
CAST: Priyanka Chopra, Kangana Ranaut, Mugdha Godse, Samir Soni, Arjun Bajwa, Arbaaz Khan, Kitu Gidwani, Harsh Chhaya, Raj Babbar;
DIRECTOR: Madhur Bhandarkar
Fashion, an ultra-close look at the fashion industry, is a mix of the strange and the familiar: that's what happens when you pick your film out from the headlines. It's Madhur Bhandarkar's forte, and with his latest, he's got the mix just right: the glamour and the dark underbelly, the highs and the lows.
Enough to titillate, not to alienate, making it very watchable.
Telling his story through a starry-eyed small-town beauty queen is a clever stroke — he makes it a strong hook for a million girls like Meghna Mathur (Priyanka), all of whom want to head to Mumbai to become, as the character says, a supermodel. But again, like in Bhandarkar's others, the semblance of a plot is just an excuse to string together a series of scenes in which People like Us think happen to People like Them — the director kowtows to public perception, adding just the right amount of 'masala' to whet appetites. Models smoke, drink and sleep their way up. The only successful designers are gay. Coke is the ultimate accessory of the beautiful people, and that's not something that comes out of a bottle.
But Fashion is a more sophisticated film than, say, Page 3 — the director is no longer shocked at salaciousness and sleaze, and that matter-of-factness of the taking is what makes the film so seductive.
Little about his film is new or unknown but Bhandarkar is not here to give us fresh takes. He wants to give us a bird's eye view or, in this case, a fly on the wall, of cat fights in the green room, bitter rivalries, behind-the-scenes chaos in frenetic fashion shows. Leggy models sashaying on the ramp are daily fodder for our TV screens. Despite the disclaimer, Gitanjali Nagpal's ravaged face is clearly the inspiration for Kangana's self-destructive character. The wardrobe malfunction — the bustier that fell off, exposing the model's torso, which ran endlessly on 24-hour news channels — is in the movie too. And the blond designer who will sit only in the front row, boyfriend in tow, can only be, okay, we're not telling.
Cleavage is king here, so should we say queen, given the profusion of gay people in this movie, all of whom are 'oh-so-creative'. Followed by a procession of never-ending legs, tight midriffs and toned butts. Bhandarkar adds a few individual quirks to his stereotypes, so that a limp-wristed designer becomes Samir Soni, a hard-headed celebrity handler becomes Kitu Gidwani, a millionaire playboy preying upon ambitious young girls becomes Arbaaz Khan.
The super-attractive trio that holds it together is topped by Priyanka, with the criminally short-changed Kangana and the vivacious first-timer Mugdha, kept firmly below.
Priyanka's heavyweight presence makes sure that much of the focus in on her, and she's good, but bland. Who knows what the movie would have been like if Kangana's character had been given more play — I would take the edgy Kangana any day over the surface smart but ultimately prissy Priyanka.
It could also have done with being shorter. Like its characters, it gets played out in long loops. Fashion is interesting, without being particularly insightful.

Golmaal returns
CAST:Ajay Devgan, Kareena Kapoor, Arshad Warsi, Tusshar Kapoor, Vrajesh Hirjee, Shreyas Talpade, Amrita Arora, Celina Jaitley, Anjana Sukhani
DIRECTOR: Rohit Shetty
The Golmaal gang is back. This time around, they are running around Goa, trying to be as silly as the last time, but they can't quite hack it. It's hard being foolish and funny at the same time.
The first Golmaal wasn't scintillating, and this follow-up suffers from what most sequels do: the male leads, barring one, are the same but it's not even the same-old, same-old. You have seen the gags before, and the lines are risqué ¿ some, in fact, are in plain bad taste — without being smart.
Kareena, who is supposed to be the star of this show, turns out to be a big factor in this flick being the way it is. There's nothing particularly new about a suspicious wife keeping tabs on her husband, and there's nothing particularly new in the way Kareena plays it: because it's a Balaji production, she's called Ekta, and all she seems to do is to watch soppy 'saas-bahu' serials which come from the stable.
Her spouse, played by Ajay, matches her step by step: he can't muster up enough enthusiasm to give anything novel to his role, other than show off his size-zero waist, just like his heroine's. Only, unlike her, he doesn't bare it all the time.
The rest struggle to rise above the script.
Arshad Warsi, playing a hysterical cop, laughs like a hyena. Vrajesh does some bungee jumping in a kiddie plastic pool. Celina, Amrita and Anjana could be interchangeable. Only Shreyas Talpade, sliding in and out of a slippery character called Anthony Gonsalves, creates some mirth. As well as Tusshar, who plays dumb here, with a great deal of expression. Not much else happens. What else can you expect from a movie which has lines like 'shaque, what the f***'?
Shucks.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

Heading: Insurance firm to reimburse Rs 2.8 lakh as medical claim - Indian Express
Content:
The Enforcement Wing of the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) demolished illegal constructions in 54 houses in Sector 55 on Friday.

Out of these, 40 were existing constructions on the government land and illegal additions had been made on them. In three cases, owners had added an additional floor in violation of the rules. Seven ongoing illegal constructions were also demolished. Four of the constructions raised had already been served notices. According to rules, no fresh construction can be carried out without prior information and approval from the board.

The demolitions began around 10 am and continued till evening amid heavy police protection. The additional SHO of Sector 39 police station was also present on the spot and 30 labourers were involved in the drive.

Housing Board secretary Kamlesh Kumar was present on the spot as duty magistrate. The demolitions were conducted under the supervision of executive engineer (enforcement) Sunil Malik. The officials reported that the housing board is adopting serious steps against the violations which had been directed by the Administration.

More anti-encroachment drives are expected on Monday and in the coming week in Sectors 38, 39, 41, 44 and 47.

Housing board computerises allotte accounts

Keeping pace with modernisation and technological advancement, the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) has computerised the allottee accounts. Under process in a phased manner, the CHB is providing information of allottee's account on its website. As many as 50 CHB schemes have been made online on the official website, www.chb.co.in. Of the total 125 schemes, the rest will be uploaded in the next 20 days as reported by the senior officials.

"With the commitment to provide better public service to the residents through e-governance which is efficient and cost effective, the CHB has computerised the allottee accounts for various housing schemes," said Kamlesh Kumar, secretary, CHB.

Personal details of an allottee including date of birth, mobile number, PAN number, house number, sector, cost of house, bank name as well as the payment details including the dates of payment, installment paid and amount paid are available on the website.

Heading: Car stereo thieves still on the prowl in Panchkula - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the New India Assurance Company to pay an insurance claim equivalent to Australian $ 8,265 (Rs 2.8 lakh) to a Mohali resident who undertook an Overseas Mediclaim Policy and spent the amount for a surgery abroad.

The insurance company has also been directed to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation for causing mental harassment to the complainant and an additional amount of Rs 5,000 as costs of litigation.

The complainant, Banta Singh, claimed that he was to go to Australia to meet his family, and thus had obtained an Overseas Mediclaim Policy for a period of 90 days commencing May 17, 2007 for which he paid a premium of Rs 4,000.

The said policy provided indemnity for all medical expenses incurred and for any loss or damage sustained during the period of insurance.

He proceeded to Australia in the month of May 2007 and during his stay there, he complained of urine retention and visited the Unified Health Care Group. After examination, the doctors operated him for TPR (Transurethral Prostatic Resection).

It was averred that for medical treatment expenses, consultation and other charges, he incurred a total cost of Australian $ 8,265.

Accordingly, a claim was lodged with the insurance company for the reimbursement of medical expenses. The insurance company, however, repudiated the claims.

In its reply, the New India Insurance Company maintained that the claim was being repudiated as per the terms and conditions of their policy. The company pleaded that the claim was denied after taking the medical opinion of the doctor concerned, who stated that the complainant was given the option of having the surgery performed then at Melbourne or two months later in India.

The claim, stated the company, was payable only for emergency treatment and not for the treatment which could have been avoided.

The Forum observed that it was a better option for the complainant to have his surgery performed in Melbourne, given the potential difficulty with prolonged catheterisation.

The Forum, headed by president Jagroop Singh Mahal, stated that the doctors attending upon the complainant had said that the complainant had to be operated for his prostate immediately as the problem had recurred very soon.

Heading: Recession blows: NRIs stay away from investment in realty sector - Indian Express
Content:
With a number of car stereo thefts having been reported from Panchkula over the last few months, there is growing apprehension among residents. The police suspect it to be the handiwork of a gang but significant breakthroughs have not been made so far.

Thefts in 2008

February 2

Stereos stolen from four cars in Sector 16

Stereo thefts were reported from four adjoining houses in Sector 16, Panchkula, on February 2 earlier this year. The residents found the car glasses damaged with stereos and other important documents missing.

The police had also allegedly showed reluctance in registering a case.

September 15

Stereos stolen from seven cars in Sector 2

As many as seven cases of stereo theft were reported from Sector 2 on September 15. Around 5.30 in the morning, the residents claimed to have found the stereos missing from their cars and the police was informed immediately.

October 6

Stereos stolen from 10 cars in Sector 4

Stereos from as many as ten cars were stolen from residences in Sector 4 in the early hours of October 6.

Residents apprehensive

Talking to Newsline, Manoj Kumar, a resident of Sector 6, Panchkula, said, "The city is not safe for residents, as every second day some crime or the other is reported. Despite the fact that every time the police claim of getting vital clues, they fail to nab the accused."

Kumar added: "It is high time that night duties are carried out responsibly by police officials. Round-the-clock patrolling is necessary to check such crimes."

Officials answer

A senior officer said, "It seems to be the work of a gang as in all the cases the modus operandi appears the same. We are trying hard and will soon get a breakthrough in the case." The official added that efforts were being made to increase the night patrolling in the city.

Heading: Final draw of Sec-63 CHB scheme on Nov 10 - Indian Express
Content:
Another blow of the global meltdown has been felt by the already bleeding realty estate industry. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are avoiding coming home this year and not investing in property, something that brokers look forward to every year.

NRIs from across Punjab prefer investing in residential properties in and around Chandigarh, Jalandhar, Amritsar, Patiala and Ludhiana. This year, however, they have decided to stay put and not return home.

"The situation is very bad at present and is expected to grow worse in future," says Kamaljeet Singh, president of the NRI Sabha in Jalandhar. He added that the impact of the global meltdown has been felt by all the sectors and real estate is one of the worst hit.

Property brokers across the city agree that the recession has further dealt a blow on the real estate industry, which was already going through a bad phase.

"The time between September and January is when we see deals taking place, as this is the time when NRIs normally arrive in the city. But no interest has been shown by the NRIs this year owing to the recession," says Gurpreet Singh, a property consultant.

"North Indians tend to invest in real estate as compared to south Indians who invest in shares. There has certainly been a huge impact of the global financial crisis on such investments. Many Indians have suffered financial losses and that has affected their plans to invest in real estate in India," says Rawinder Singh Guru, a permanent resident of Canada.

Heading: Revision of photo electoral roll held - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Housing Board has decided on November 10 as the date for the final draw of Sector 63 Housing Board Flats Scheme.

More than three months after the preliminary draw on July 30, the shortlisted applicants were eagerly awaiting a date for the final draw.

After the preliminary draw, officials had claimed that the final draw would be organised within one month. The reason for the delay, officials say, was the time taken to scrutinise the documents of the shortlisted applicants.

Applicants were reported suffering financial losses as more than 80 per cent of them had applied for the scheme through banks. "The three-month delay is unjustified as the idea to hold the preliminary draw to cut down on scrutiny and ultimately the interim time period is in question. We have financed the application money through banks for which we are paying interest every day," said an applicant.

In the preliminary draw, 3,420 slips were taken out for 1,804 flats in all four categories for which there were 21,587 applicants.

Moreover, 174 shortlisted applicants were disqualified in the initial scrutiny on various grounds. Out of these 174, around 120 are estimated to be approved as eligible and the rest around 50 as ineligible during the process of appeal to the CHB chairman by them.

As per officials, the detailed list of the eligible candidates will be put on its official website — www.chb.co.in.

Heading: HRD ministry to provide 82,000 scholarships for higher education - Indian Express
Content:
A meeting chaired by RK Rao, UT deputy commissioner-cum-electoral registration officer, regarding the special summary revision of photo electoral roll-2009 with reference to the instructions issued by the Election Commission of India, was held today.

It was decided in the meeting that as areas of booth level officers (BLOs) falling under the jurisdiction of the assistant electoral registration officers (AEROs) have been changed, they will now be placed on the website of the Election department. The AEROs will also train BLOs under their jurisdiction and a compliance report will then be forwarded to the Election department.

It was decided that AEROs will hold a meeting with gram sabha or local bodies and residents welfare associations under their respective jurisdictions.

A citizen will have to attach a residence proof by for a new enrollment. It was also decided that no form will be accepted without a proof and in case, the applicant has recently migrated to Chandigarh, a certificate of deletion of his name from his previous constituency will also have to be submitted.

The EC has also introduced a new form for submission of photographs for preparation of the elector photo identity cards.

Heading: Students clash in PU hostel mess - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to recognise meritorious students belonging to low-income families, the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Department of Higher Education, will provide 82,000 scholarships to Class XII students for graduate/post-graduate studies. This will be decided on the student's performance in his Senior Secondary Examination or its equivalent, with a minimum aggregate of 80 per cent.

The scholarship titled "Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students" will provide students with financial assistance to meet their daily expenses while pursuing higher education.

It will be given to students in colleges and universities and also to those pursuing professional courses like medical, engineering among others.

The total number of scholarships will be divided among the state boards based on the population of the state, in the age group of 18-25 years, after segregating the share of the Central Board of Secondary Education and the Indian Certificate of Secondary Examination on the basis of number of students passing out from various boards in the country.

The detailed guidelines regarding the scheme can be viewed from the website www.cbse.nic.in. The last date for submitting of applications is November 5, 2008 for the CBSE candidates.

Heading: Schools welcome reintroduction of moral science in syllabus - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Department of Chemical Engineering, Panjab University, allegedly clashed around 10 pm on Friday night in the mess at Hostel number 3. The incident took place when students were eating their dinner.

Four students sustained injuries in the clash that apparently sparked off owing to some past rivalry.

According to the police, two students — Ashish Batra and Jalal Mani — entered into a verbal duel in the mess over a minor issue related to campaigning during student elections in the university.

While the two were engaged in a physical face-off, other students started hurling plates and glasses over each other's supporters.

The canteen owner intimated the police that reached the spot and pacified the groups.

Four students including Ashish Batra, Swarnjeet and Jalal Mani were arrested and also taken to the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital, Sector 16, for medical aid.

Heading: Chandigarh Carnival to be held on Nov 22, 23 - Indian Express
Content:
School authorities have welcomed the decision of the Education department to reintroduce moral science education in schools.

This is being done with a view to instill moral values in children from a young age onwards.

The department has been laying a lot of emphasis on moral education among students and has taken various initiatives in the last one year, which includes organising a Moral Education Week in schools during assembly.

The schools at present do not have moral science as a subject in their syllabus.

Welcoming the proposal, Dr Vinod Sharma of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 18, said: "The department has taken a positive step. It is essential for students to study moral science as it will help in their overall development. Considering the materialistic outlook the current generation has, the significance of the subject increases all the more."

"Moral science can never lose its relevance and never become obsolete. It is good that the department is thinking on reintroducing the subject. The students will definitely benefit from this," said a teacher of Government Model High School, Sector 29.

Talking about the same, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools) said: "We aim to introduce the subject not only in local schools but in as many schools as possible. It is essential for students to realise the importance of being a good human being. We are working on the details of the project and it will be initiated as soon as possible, keeping in view the guidelines and requirements of the Central Board of Secondary Education."

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Amit Mehta - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day Chandigarh Carnival will be celebrated on November 22 and 23 under the theme 'Fun and Games'. UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (retd) will inaugurate the carnival at 11 am on November 22 at Leisure Valley, Sector 10.

Students of Chandigarh College of Art will design the main entrance of the carnival. The three academies, namely Chandigarh Sangeet Natak Akademi, Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi and Chandigarh Sahitya Kala Akademi, will also put their exhibits depicting the different art streams at the festival.

A Mega Musical Nite (November 22) and Mega Laughter Show (November 23) will be the main attraction of the carnival this year.

The Administration also plans to delight the audience with a high-quality fireworks show on the Mega Musical Nite eve.

A rally of carnival floats will also be taken from Leisure Valley, via Matka Chowk and Cricket Stadium roundabout, to the Rose Garden.

At a meeting today, UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas emphasised that the event must not end up as a disappointing affair.

Heading: Former DUSU leaders jump - Indian Express
Content:
CII Executive, Constituency: Rajendra Nagar, Area: Inderpuri

For the past three terms, Pooran Chand Yogi has been his area's MLA. Amit, 29, says the MLA has visited his area just once or twice. "There has not been any development in our area. Whenever we have gone to our MLA with our issues, he said things were not in his hands," says Amit. "He wins because this is a BJP dominated area. I think people should be more sensible before casting their vote," he adds.

On Inderpuri drain
"We have a big open drain right at the entrance of the colony. On several occasions, we have asked our MLA to get it covered. But nothing has been done. The drain has not been cleaned for years and it worsens during monsoon," he says.

On parking problem
"Every second day, people have fights for parking space. People are ready to pay for parking, but I don't understand why all the multi-level parking projects get delayed. The government should have taken the problem seriously," says Amit.

On BRT
"It is a pity how the government has wasted our money in the BRT corridor. They conduct studies, but still make mistakes. I hope the government that comes to power acts sensibly and does not waste our money," he says.

Heading: Royal tussle in Cong for Chandni Chowk seat - Indian Express
Content:
Years after they impressed the young minds of Delhi University with peppy slogans, former office-bearers of the Delhi University Students Union (DUSU) are now eyeing the upcoming Assembly elections. If the number of interested candidates is any indication, the elections will see a number of young faces, experienced in the art of politics since their student days, fighting for the coveted posts.

According to NSUI sources, at least six former office-bearers of DUSU and two DU student activists are in the race for Congress tickets. Big names include Ragini Nayak, Anil Choudhary, Virendra Singh Vaishist, Harsh Chaudhury, Ashok Basoya and Alka Lamba. From the ABVP, Nakul Bhardwaj and Anil Jha are leading the camp for fresh faces in the BJP. Other names include Jaiveer Rana, Jitender Choudhury, Ajay Choudhury, Ashish Sood and Satish Upadhyay.

When asked if being "new" contestants will in a way jeopardise their chances to win, a former DUSU office-bearer, on condition of anonymity, said: "Being young does not mean we are new. Each student leader has been actively working for the last few years and so people in their area know them well and that is what counts."

Commenting on whether winning the DUSU elections will help in preparing for the Assembly elections, a former ABVP leader said there is a huge difference between the two. "From the point of the ABVP, DUSU elections only help in learning about the organisational structure of a party and nothing else," he said.

For both NSUI and ABVP, student leaders are expected to bring a youthful image to their area. Mukesh Shukla, an ABVP leader said: "When young people in the age of 30-35 contest against older contestants, they give a youthful image to campaigning. Also, being former leaders of DUSU, they get students to campaign for them."

When not contesting, student activists are also expected to help in campaigning for other candidates of the Congress and the BJP.

Anand Pandey, the national spokesperson of NSUI, says, "Before elections, there is door-to-door campaigning to be done and on the day of the elections there are hundreds of booths to be looked after. Obviously, the students play a big role in mobilising supporters."

Heading: BJP meets, but no list in sight yet - Indian Express
Content:
Backed by Kapil Sibal, MLA Prahlad Singh Sawhney and Delhi Congress president's son Mudit Agarwal lock horns for a seat

With the final list of Congress candidates still not visible, a royal fight for a ticket is on for the Chandni Chowk Assembly constituency between sitting MLA Prahlad Singh Sawhney and Delhi Congress president J P Agarwal's son Mudit Agarwal.

Much before the selection process for candidates had started, stories on the tussle between 56-year-old Sawhney and 37-year-old Mudit had been doing the rounds. Sawhney has been in politics since 1983 and is said to be close to MP Kapil Sibal. J P Agarwal, on the other hand, is running from pillar to post to get a seat for his son.

Senior leaders however, are tightlipped.

J P Agarwal had been canvassing for his son, although the party high command was not happy with this move. "Chandni Chowk is an important seat and J P Agarwal would not risk it by putting up his son, who is a first-timer. If Mudit loses, it will be detrimental for his father, too. He had also asked party high command to consider Mudit for the Shalimar Bagh seat," said a senior leader.

Toeing the party line, J P Agarwal had been denying all along that his son would not be running for polls. Mudit, who runs a garment export business, also denied it. "I am not planning to jump into politics at any time. These are merely rumours," he said.

Chandni Chowk constituency has nearly 1.6 lakh voters and the voter turnout here is less than 40 per cent. Other than traders in the Azad Market and Nawab Ganj areas, it also has the posh Rajpur Road and Civil Lines area. The Tibetan settlement at Majnu Ka Tila also falls in this constituency.

"Mudit's name had been doing the rounds for a long time. Every father would want his son to do well, so even if J P Agarwal supports him there is no problem. The party high command has assured me that I will be the candidate for this seat," Sawhney told Newsline.

Sawhney had won his first election in 1983 when he was elected as a member of Delhi corporation, where he served till 1990. He was also chairman of the house. In 1998, he fought the assembly polls from Chandni Chowk and won by 8,500 votes. The next term, too he was successfully elected with a margin of 11,500 votes.

Heading: Just Qawwali - Indian Express
Content:
irants, meanwhile, raise the pitch against 'outsiders' getting poll tickets

The BJP election committee met for six hours on Friday but could not zero in on 70 candidates for the Assembly polls on November 29. The Delhi unit of the party has till date managed to select 33 names, and all these names will be screened and finalised by the party headquarters.

City BJP leaders were scheduled to present the 33 names at the party's Ashoka Road headquarters at 6 pm but the top brass was busy discussing the list for Madhya Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir till late evening. "Party president Rajnath Singh told us to complete our list tomorrow and present the final report," Delhi BJP president Dr Harsh Vardhan said.

The election committee will, thus, sit down again on Saturday at 10 am.

The 33 candidates 'finalised' by the city unit includes names of 19 sitting MLAs. The other 14 seats 'decided' are: Timarpur, Adarsh Nagar, Badli, Bawana, Mundka, Sultanpur, Mangolpuri, Shakur Basti, Tri Nagar, Chandni Chowk, Model Town, Madipur, Patel Nagar and Rajouri Garden. Of these, Adarsh Nagar and Rajouri Garden have been given to allies Shiromani Akali Dal.     

But even as Delhi BJP leaders were brainstorming, there were signs of rebellion brewing outside. Several frustrated ticket-seekers began a protest outside the party office against some of the 'outsider candidates' — those who do not reside in the constituency from where their names have been pitched. Some of the protestors even manhandled Delhi BJP chief Harsh Vardhan while he was entering the party office for the election committee meeting.

Vani Tripathi, picked by the party for Vikaspuri constituency, was among those whose candidature was derided by the protestors. Tripathi lives in Gole Market. "She does not even know the area's topography. How do you think she is going to manage?" a block-level worker from Vikaspuri asked.

In East Delhi, there is grouse against student leader Nakul Bhardwaj's name being proposed for the Patparganj seat. Protestors said though Bhardwaj's brother had been living in the area for long, he himself moved in barely six months ago.

Similar is the complaint in Vishwas Nagar as party workers from the area said local candidate Kuldeep Chel was ignored. Instead, senior leaders are trying to finalise O P Sharma's candidature, they said.

For the newly formed constituency Kirari, Delhi BJP has chosen Anil Jha, who lives in Katwaria Sarai. There was also massive protest against Mongolpuri candidate Yogesh Attre. "Attre lives in Kheda village, some 20 kilometres from Mongolpuri," ticket aspirant from the area, Roshan Valmiki, said.

Attre, he said, does not have an idea of the area. "He doesn't even know local BJP workers. The party would only serve the seat to (Congress minister) Rajkumar Chauhan this way."

Santosh Parkhi, a woman candidate eyeing the Bawana seat, came with an entourage to protest. The party has selected former MLA Chand Ram for the seat. Elected in 1993, Ram had not managed a nomination since then. "BJP talks about 33 per cent reservation for women in elections," Parkhi said, "but ground realities are vastly different."

Senior leaders talked tough on the protests. Harsh Vardhan said, "Anyone flexing muscle in support or in opposition of any candidate will not be considered for a ticket."

Heading: Illegal hoardings to be removed - Indian Express
Content: In these troubled times, a little cross-border musical harmony helps. Thursday evening saw a qawwali concert organised by the Indian Women's Press Corps and the Indian Council for Cultural Relations. Called Mehfil-e-Shama Parvana, the concert at Siri Fort Auditorium saw an all-male qawwali troupe from Pakistan battle their wit, vocals and musical talent with an all-female troupe from India. While the men were led by Muhammad Zaman Zaki Taji, the women were led by Chanchal Bharti (in the picture), one of the few women qawwals. "We're trying to preserve and nurture an age-old tradition which requires a lot of dedication," said Bharti. "We cannot play to the gallery or tune our music to suit popular tastes." Taji nodded: "Not many people listen to it these days, but as long as there is a dargah, there will be qawwali."

Heading: City, family pray for ex-Stephen’s principal - Indian Express
Content:
In a fresh order issued on Friday, the MCD chairman standing committee has asked the commissioner to remove all illegal political hoardings put up in various parts of the city in violation of the Model Code of Conduct for Delhi Assembly polls.

"We have issued clear-cut directions that violation of the model code will not be tolerated at all. The Commissioner has been asked to ensure that all illegal hoardings, irrespective of their parties, are removed," said Gupta.

A meeting of the Standing Committee on Friday witnessed uproar when Congress councillors alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party has put up hoardings all over the city, including on corporation properties, in violation of the model code.

"The BJP is misusing its power. There are more posters of the BJP members than of the Congress," alleged Leader of the Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma demanding that all illegal signboards be removed soon.

Gupta, however, said the Congress is "politicising" the issue. He has asked the commissioner to submit the report at the next meeting of the Committee.
