Heading: Jamia Nagar learns the police story: all about encounter - Indian Express
Content:
Loneliness and chaos collide in the exhibition "Zeitgeist" at Gallery Romain Roland at Alliance Francaise. The photographs, paintings, sculptures and video-installation of eight artists show a withering streak of hopelessness, sometimes even nihilism. If Kriti Arora's photograph has a light-eyed girl clutching a barbwire fence in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, Gauri Gill goes far out to New Jersey to show a dull matrimonial conference in progress.

Delhi-based Gill's work is from her exhibition "The Americans" that is currently going on at the Chicago Cultural Center and shows a slice of life of NRIs in the US. "I moved to the US in the mid-1990s and much of my work springs from my personal experiences," says the 38-year-old. Meanwhile, Arora used the camera as her canvas when she escorted her journalist mother to strife-torn Kashmir. "The camera serves as a notebook, recording events," says Arora, 38.

If Vibha Galhotra's White Noise (bottom) has the rampant construction in metros embossed on paper, Manil Gupta's delightfully eerie Malfunctioning Phantasmagoria series (left), all watercolours on archival paper, highlights a malfunctioning growth on a man's body.

"The works are multi-layered and cut across the medium," says Latika Gupta, curator of the show, who brought together the artists, including environmentalist Ravi Agarwal, Nicola Durvasula, Kumar Kanti Sen and Mithu Sen. The works begin at Rs 40,000 and go up to Rs 6 lakh.

(The show moves to Palette Art Gallery and is on till November 5)

Heading: Viru’s turn of fate - Indian Express
Content:
The police for the first time explained the September 19 encounter at Batla House in a formal public-police interaction at Jamia Nagar on Friday evening. Attended by hundreds of residents, the event was marked by a robust exchange between angry and complaining residents and Delhi Police officials, who gave assurances and got across their point of view and version of the events.

DCP (Southeast) Ajay Chaudhary fielded questions and spoke of circumstances in the area after the encounter, which left Inspector M C Sharma and two terror suspects dead. Chaudhary assured residents that there had been misunderstandings and misinterpretations due to lack of communication between residents and the police. "We will give every resident and every problem faced by residents a patient hearing," he said.

Rizwanur Mashir, president of Shaheen Bagh RWA, said, "We have had a history of producing scholars and leaders from this area but the silent sanctions imposed on us are not warranted."

Residents alleged that the police and the administration have started imposing sanctions on locals. They said people have been been "warned" to stay away from Jamia Nagar. Parvez Khan, area resident and cameraperson with a TV news channel, said: "The problem is not with the police or the media. It is only an aftermath of the generalisation and stereotyping that has followed the infamous encounter."

A M Ansari, a retired librarian who lives in the area, said, "No company delivers food and other items here. Even schools have stopped sending their buses to the area." Many others said buses drop their children outside Jamia Nagar, near New Friends Colony. They also alleged that the police have disallowed all construction work in the area now.

RWA members said at least 74 buses have stopped coming into Jamia Nagar and hundreds of students have suffered as a result. Residents also criticised the Jamia Nagar police station SHO and other policemen posted there for resorting to "illegitimate arrests" on occasions.

Agreeing that crime rate of the area was among the lowest in Delhi, DCP Chaudhary said, "The problems are legitimate and much work will have to be done about them. We will initiate action on the matter." He refused to share further details.

The event was organised by the NGO 'Journalists' Association for People', formed by journalists living in Jamia Nagar.

Heading: Lucky 13 - Indian Express
Content:
Coach Sharma recalls Virender Sehwag's early penchant for bowling

He spun big and viciously to bamboozle the Australian batsmen. Taking on the role of a part-time bowler, he surprised everyone with his performance on Friday, but Virender Sehwag is perhaps the one specialist bowler India never had, thanks to his explosive batting. During his school days, he was repeatedly told to just concentrate on his batting — despite his immense liking to roll his arm over at every single opportunity.

Coach AN Sharma recalls Sehwag's school days, when the India opener would grab at every chance to bowl. "He just loved to bowl. Whenever I was late in reaching a match, he would quietly bowl medium-pace with the new ball before bowling off-spin with the old. There were so many times when he opened the bowling for us as a seamer. He's as gifted an off-spinner as a batsman. He can get the ball to turn really big and it was a difficult choice for us to make. But when I did make it, I told him categorically to concentrate on his batting. I couldn't keep him off the ball, so I told him to first finish his batting, and then complete knocking before even touching the ball at the nets," he says.

Making the most of chances
On Saturday, Sehwag will be eyeing his first ever five-wicket haul in Test cricket. The 30-year old also speaks about his love for bowling, but rues the fact that he doesn't get as many bowling opportunities with Anil Kumble and Harbhajan Singh in the team as the main spinners. "Anil bhai was injured so someone had to bowl. I got this opportunity to bowl 20 overs after a long time. I just wanted to contain the runs and that's what I did, and in the process also got the wickets," says Sehwag. He adds: "No batsman can be satisfied without scoring runs but I am happy to have contributed to the team's cause. It's my job. I have a chance to claim my first five-wicket haul."

Pitch playing tricks
Sehwag insists that some of his balls during the match on Friday were almost unplayable with the Ferozeshah Kotla pitch playing all kinds of tricks.

Sharma, however, believes there's a method to his unplayable deliveries as well. "I always believe that a young spinner needs to bowl medium-pace for sometime before bowling spin. That will help develop his muscles, so that a spinner can get as much purchase off the wicket when he hits the deck. So if Viru got the ball to turn and bounce, I am not surprised at all," he says.

Sharma has few qualms in Sehwag being billed as an all-rounder at this stage of his career. "What was important was to set his priorities early on. I wanted him to become a batsman because he showed better qualities in that department. That he's managed to keep up his bowling alongside is brilliant," he concludes.

Heading: ‘Why no money for underprivileged in private schools for books, uniform?’ - Indian Express
Content:
In its thirteenth year, The Great Indian Rock gets a bunch of foreign bands and travels to seven cities

Thirteen years ago, a festival called The Great Indian Rock began with bands from across the country competing at Delhi's open-air theatre Hamsadhwani. This season, with the name tweaked a little to The Fuel Great Indian Rock, the fest will have a new avatar as it transforms into a national concert tour, spanning seven cities — Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad and Shillong— with 21 Indian bands and three international acts. "The festival has always aimed at providing local bands a platform to write and perform good, original music. It is not a competition anymore, it is purely bands in concert," says Amit Saigal, founder of the festival.

After the fest kicked off at Mumbai's Andheri Sports Complex on Friday, it plays out in Delhi on November 1 and 2 with myriad subgenres of rock spelt out by bands such as Them Clones, Kryptos, Undying Inc and Frequency alongside the hard rock act put forth by the Swedish band Freak Kitchen (in the picture) and the Norwegian black metal bands Sahg and Satyricon. "The foreign bands and the Indian bands together will add to the festival since it's always good to mix things and see what comes out of it," says Saigal. "Well, to be honest there is nothing super happening in the western hemisphere. It is here that all the energy is happening," says Mattias Eklundh, vocalist and

guitarist of Freak Kitchen, which also performed at the fest last year and have been so smitten by the country's rock and raga that in their upcoming album they have Indian classical musicians like flautist V Selvaganesh playing.

But it is a first for Sahg and most of the Indian bands. Saigal says all that mattered in choosing them was a good, original song. "It doesn't matter how fast you play, it is all about good song writing," he says. And with bands putting out their originals and pushing the envelope, this season seems to be bigger than ever.

The show starts at 5 pm at Hamsadhwani amphitheatre.
Tickets are priced at Rs 250.
Contact greatindianrock.com

Heading: 34 years on, schizophrenic murder accused continues to face court trials - Indian Express
Content:
Seven months into the academic session, the Delhi government is yet to pay Rs 1,000 each to more than 8,000 underprivileged children studying in 334 private schools across the city, says an application before the High Court.

In fact, the application says, the government is yet to pay the grant to more than 30,000 students admitted in these schools since 2004.

The money, promised by the government in a law enacted last year, is meant for students from the poor strata, enrolled in plush private schools, to buy school uniform and books.

On November 5, the Delhi High Court will hear an application seeking judicial intervention into why the government's failure so far to "disburse" money for uniforms and books despite penning the Delhi School Education (Free Seats for Students Belonging to Economically Weaker Sections) Order, 2006.

The law came into force in January 2007 after a legal battle since 2004. The High Court directed "several hundred unaided, recognised private schools in Delhi" functioning on public land given by the DDA to open its doors to provide financially backward students free seats. The judgment, later converted into a law by the government, said, "Students admitted against free seats shall get financial assistance, at par with the students of government schools, for expenditure on account of uniform and books."

As per an application filed by advocate Ashok Agarwal, the Delhi government's Education Secretary ought to have disbursed the amount to students through heads of the schools concerned. But, "almost seven months since commencement of the academic year 2008-09, the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) students have not received any money," it says.

The applicant, Ashok Agarwal, spearheaded the "three-year PIL campaign" for free-ship in the High Court.

Of 334 private schools with 21,394 earmarked EWS seats, 8,607 poor students have been admitted in 2008-09 session, says details submitted in High Court by the government in September.

"It is estimated that not less than 30,000 students are presently studying in different classes in these 384 unaided recognised private schools under the EWS quota," Agarwal said. As per the government's 2006 order, all these schools, he said, are obliged to reserve 20 per cent seats for EWS students. "If this provision is fully implemented, it is estimated that more than 1.5 lakh students would benefit."

On the difference in number of schools in which students are to benefit from the government grant, Aggarwal said only 334 of the 384 institutions given land by the DDA have submitted details of students admitted through EWS quota. The government, he said, had set aside Rs 3 crore for this project.

Agarwal said he went forward with his decision to approach the court after the Education Secretary failed to respond to his letter — sent on October 23 — seeking clarification about the "delay" in granting the aid money.

Najimi Waziri, senior counsel of Delhi government, said, "I am unable to comment on the issue now. We will say our part in the court."

Newsline could not Education minister Arvinder Singh Lovely despite repeated attempts.

FIGURE IT OUT
GOVT SAYS 334 private schools have 21,394 seats earmarked for poor students 8,607 EWS category students admitted in 2008-09
ASHOK AGGARWAL SAYS 30,000 (approx) EWS students in 384 private schools. As per government's 2006 order, all these schools are obliged to reserve 20 per cent seats for EWS

Heading: Modasa blast: Police give clean chit to Sadhvi, others - Indian Express
Content:
Hospital superintendent seeks withdrawal of criminal charges to treat him as a civil patient

It's 3 pm, and as Barkya Ramji Gimbhal, declared a chronic schizophrenic patient, looks out of the iron bars of his cell, a State Reserve Police jawan walks into the corridor of the Vadodara Hospital for Mental Health and unlocks the room. Barkya is taken to the canteen where he would be served tea and snacks, which has become a routine for almost eight years now.

The shocking part of Barkya's story is the court trials for a murder he committed in Velugam, an interior village near Khanvel in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, in 1974. Entangled in the legal wrangles, the case has posed a serious question against the legal system, as despite being a chronic schizophrenic patient, he continues to be an undertrial.

"It is true that Barkya is chronic schizophrenic. We have communicated with the investigating agencies in Silvassa and asked them to do the needful and drop the criminal charges so that we can treat him as a civil patient," hospital superintendent Rakesh Shah told Newsline.

According to Sub-Inspector K B Mahajan, who is handling the case, the incident took place on September 29, 1974 when Barkya allegedly killed his mother Gangiben with a sharp-edged weapon. According to the FIR registered with the Surangi outpost, Barkya had indulged into an argument with his mother over food before killing her.

"A month after the incident, he was taken to the Chief Medical Officer C J Bhatt in Silvassa for a medical check up. On December 26, 1974 he was declared 'mentally disturbed' by the concerned officials," said Mahajan.

"Considering the observations by the medical officers, he was released on bail and his cousin Deval Vartha was given his custody. Vartha was asked to produce Barkya before the court as and when required," he said.

Tired of looking after Barkya and answering to the court orders and police inquiry, Vartha washed his hands off the case after some time. With this, Barkya once again landed in the Surat sub-jail on May 15, 2000. Mahajan said, "He was sent to the psychiatry department of Surat Civil Hospital and also to the Vadodara Hospital for Mental Health for treatment."

After a short treatment and medication, Barkya was again sent to the Silvassa sub-jail in August 2000. After spending around three years in the jail, the Silvassa Sessions Judge issued an order on November 27, 2003 that the 'accused' should be shifted to the Vadodara Hospital for Mental Health. Since then, Barkya is undergoing treatment there.

Meanwhile, realising the complications in the case, the hospital superintendent wrote a letter to the Union Home Ministry, a copy of which is with Newsline, requesting withdrawal of the charges against Barkya so that he can be treated as a civil patient. Even a team of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) visited the patient and observed that the criminal charges should be dropped.

Following by the communication from Shah, a letter was shot by Mohinder Singh, Director (Judicial Cell), Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi to the Dadra Nagar Haveli administrator on September 3, 2008. The letter requested that "a detailed report in the matter along with their views may please be furnished to this Ministry at the earliest".

Now, it is the Silvassa public prosecutor Orland Mirinda who is likely to bring an end to the woes of the man who does not even remember his crime.

"Though I have not received the case papers as of now, from the information I have received, it is clear that whatever happened was not proper. We will try to remove the criminal charges as soon as possible," Mirinda said.

The withdrawal of the criminal charges, however, may not be the end to the probelems of Barkya. Pavlus Navsa Gimbhal, nephew of Barkya, said: "We have 24 acres of land which belong to our grandfather who has not made any will. Today, the eldest nephew is handling the land, which belongs to Barkya. But he is not ready to take care of his uncle. We don't have money to go to Vadodara and do the formalities to release our uncle on bail."

Heading: Malegaon blast: Mumbai ATS team looks for Vadodara link - Indian Express
Content:
Sabarkantha police team meets Mumbai police; says interrogation is still on but it is too early to reach any conclusion

Giving a clean chit to Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur and others arrested in connection with the September 29 Malegaon blast, the Gujarat Police on Friday said that none of them were involved in the similar blast that claimed one life in Modasa the same day.

Deputy Superintendent of Police, Sabarkantha, K K Mysorewala, who is heading the Modasa blast case, said, "We have interrogated all the five who are currently in the custody of Mumbai police in connection with the Malegaon blast. None of them, however, are involved in the Modasa blast."

Mysorewala along with four other personnel of the Sabarkantha district police were in Mumbai on Friday for investigations in the case.

The team headed by Sabarkantha Superintendent of Police R B Brahmbhatt held discussions with their Mumbai counterparts earlier in the morning.

When asked whether the Mumbai police had claimed to have cracked the Malegaon as well as Modasa blast cases after the arrest of Sadhvi and others, Mysorewala said: "Nothing of this kind was ever communicated to us. The Mumbai police may have enough evidence to link these persons with the Malegaon blast."

Brahmbhatt, however, said that interrogation is still going on and it is too early to reach any conclusion.

The Sabarkantha police have so far questioned over 500 people, including members of saffron outfits like Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Bajrang Dal, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and Akhil Bharthiya Vidyarthi Parishad.

Bombs went off in the Muslim-dominated areas of Modasa in Gujarat and Malegaon in Maharashtra around same time on September 29. A 15-year-old boy had died and several others were injured in Modasa.

Heading: Whale shark tourism to drop anchor at Veraval coast soon - Indian Express
Content:
A team of the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) of the Mumbai police visited the city on October 29 as part of their investigations into the September 29 Malegaon blast.

Officials of the Special Operation Group (SOG) of the Vadodara police, who were part of the investigation, told Newsline that the visiting team had some specific information about links between the Malegaon blast and Vadodara.

"We were just asked to furnish details about some locations in the city which we did. We have not been given any information about who they were searching for and what information they had gathered about the Vadodara link with the blast," said an SOG official.

Heading: VHP man facing sedition charges had procured SIM on fake documents - Indian Express
Content:
NGOs have joined hands with the private sector to make the Rs 300-cr project a success

A new form of adventure — whale shark tourism — is all set to hit the Veraval coast shortly . The private sector and NGOs have already initiated a plan for whale shark tourism without waiting for the government's nod. The infrastructure cost for the project has been pegged at Rs 300 crore.

Abdul Wadood Banatwala, a Veraval-based hotelier and member of the 'Earth Matters Foundation' (EMF), said, "The Veraval coast has enough potential for whale shark tourism. For this, the state government, the Union government, NGOs, local bodies and even the fishermen community will have to pitch in their support."

According to Banatwala, Earth Matters Foundation and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands-based NGO, Green Life Society have already worked out a plan titled 'Whale shark tourism in Veraval—Strategic Plan 2009'. But before going ahead with this, a lot of infrastructural facilities are required at Veraval, including a state-of-the-art hospital, a hotel, a language teaching school, and professional divers among others, he said.

"Once it gets started, tourists from all over the world will visit Veraval. For that, world-class facilities are extremely important to render the project successful. This will put Veraval on the world tourism map," Banatwala said.

He added: "It is purely adventure tourism: quite expensive, risky and above all, whale shark locations are never fixed in the sea. It will cost 15 to 20 thousand rupees per day per head."

In 1997-98, EMF's Mike Pandey along with his team, including Banatwala, had made a film on the whale shark titled Shores of Silence. The film had created remarkable awareness. It had won numerous awards, including three Green Oscars. In 2008, Banatwala was honoured with the 'Eco Warrior Award' by Vice-President Abdul Hamid Ansari.

Whale Shark facts

It is a Schedule-I animal as per the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It is the world's largest fish. Whale sharks grow to a length of 60 feet or more and weigh up to 34 tonnes (in comparison, a big elephant weighs up to six tonnes). Globally, whale sharks inhabit tropical and warm waters. They migrate to areas rich in food. They tend to concentrate at certain places at the same time every year. However, there is no estimate of their precise population.

Heading: Arrest may further widen rift between BJP and VHP - Indian Express
Content:
VHP city general secretary had circulated derogatory SMSes about Chief Minster

Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) city general secretary Ashwin Patel, who is facing sedition charges for sending derogatory SMSes about Chief Minister Narendra Modi, had procured a private telecom company's SIM card for the purpose by providing forged documents.

Investigating police officers said this on Friday, four days after his arrest.

A Local Crime Branch (LCB) team of the Gandhinagar police had arrested Patel from Ranip in Ahmedabad on Monday on charges of sedition, defamation and inflaming communal passions.

He is currently in the custody of Gandhinagar police. The arrest was made after the LCB tracked the mobile phone number from which SMSes were being sent after the July 26 serial blasts in Ahmedabad.

"It was found during our investigations that Patel had procured a Vodafone SIM card by giving a forged driving licence as his address proof. This card was used only for sending these SMSes," said Deputy Superintendent of Police and Investigating Officer M L Ninama.

He added that the SIM card has been sent to the Directorate of Forensic Science (DFS), Gandhinagar for examination.

Sources in the Gandhinagar police said that Patel had procured this SIM card around one-and-a-half-year ago.

"Though Patel's driving licence has his Ahmedabad addresses on it, the one he had submitted as address proof for the card showed he was a resident of Gandhinagar," said Inspector P P Bhatt, who had filed the FIR against Patel.

The police are likely to seek extension of his custody, as his present custody period expires on Saturday.

A prominent chemical businessman in the city, Patel has been associated with the VHP for the last 15 years.

Heading: Thursday’s serial blasts in Assam take a toll on Assamese in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
Parishad plans to approach NHRC against Ashwin Patel's arrest; says charges are fabricated

The rift between the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) seems to be widening further with the police arresting senior VHP functionary Ashwin Patel on charges of sedition.

The charges, according to the police, include circulating derogatory and defamatory SMSes about Chief Minister Narendra Modi.

VHP state general secretary Anil Dave said that Patel's arrest was a clear violation of human rights. "VHP has decided to file a complaint with the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)," Dave told Newsline, adding that the charges were fabricated.

State BJP president Purshottam Rupala, however, denied the charges levelled by the VHP functionaries against the Chief Minister and the state administration, saying he came to know about the development only after police arrested Patel.

Defending the police, he said that as per his information, Patel had been sending highly derogatory messages for quite some time.

The arrest, he said, was made on the basis of a complaint for false SMSes received by some people. "After the SIM card was seized, we came to know about Patel's involvement," he added.

Refusing to comment on the increasing distance between the two outfits, he said it was the BJP which always

defended the VHP. As for VHP office-bearers going to the NHRC, he said everybody is free to approach the rights body.

"The incident is a pure criminal offence of an individual and should not be linked with any organisation," he said.

The VHP, meanwhile, found a strong support from former Gujarat home minister and BJP rebel Gordhan Zadaphia. Zadaphia, who has floated Mahagujarat Janata Party, said the arrest was a breach of human rights as the charges levelled against Patel were false.

He accused the Modi government of "systematically dismantling" each and every infrastructure of the Sangh ideology in the state. "Arresting Patel on false grounds is one of the latest attempts in this direction," he added.

"Whoever dares to criticise the government is targeted and punished by way of ruining his businesses, by misusing the state machinery or through other means like arresting in fake cases," said Zadaphia, extending his support to Patel and VHP in their "hour of crisis". He said the matter would definitely further the gap between the BJP and the VHP.

Seeking anonymity, a senior BJP leader said: "Now there exists a huge gap between the BJP and the VHP." Claiming that the VHP is almost finished now, he said, "Let them move the NHRC. They know that it is only the BJP which has been defending it. It can't get support from any other party."

This is the second instance of registering a sedition case in the state. The first was registered against a few journalists a couple of months ago for writing news items against a senior police functionary.

Heading: WASMO’s bid to provide clean water to schoolkids - Indian Express
Content:
The serial blasts in Assam on Thursday have not only affected the people residing in that state, but also the Assamese who are studying or working in Gujarat.

Zina Rai-Baruah, a fifth semester student of Fashion and Textile at the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Gandhinagar, is a worried girl. She is stuck in her hometown Guwahati after the Thursday blasts.

She told Newsline: "I have to take a flight to New Delhi on Saturday morning at 11 and the airport is almost 2 hours from my place. The situation in the city is not good at the moment and we all are a worried lot, as I need to reach NIFT via New Delhi."

Deepali Das Roy, Zina's mother, who is a lawyer, was lucky to escape unhurt in the blast that took place at the Chief Judicial Magistrate's (CJM) Court campus.

"I had passed through the CJM court only a couple of minutes before the blast. Within minutes, the scene at the campus completely changed," said Roy.

She further said, "Now, we are worried about our daughter, as she has to take a flight to New Delhi on Saturday morning and the situation here has still not improved."

Dhrubajyoti Doley has been pursuing a post-graduate programme in communication management and entrepreneurship in MICA-EDC, Ahmedabad.

He is worried because his maternal aunt was injured in the blast at the Ganeshguri flyover in Guwahati.

He said, "I was really worried and tensed when I got the news. I am not thinking about visiting Guwahati, as it is job placement season in my college, but I am still very worried."

Dilip Doley, maternal uncle of Dhrubajyoti Doley said: "My wife had been to the market in Ganeshguri to buy some stationery and household materials. All of a sudden there was a blast below the flyover and bomb splinters struck her at the back of her head. She received two stitches and was kept under observation in the hospital on Thursday."

Heading: Sealed private hotels rule the roost  in Sasan Gir during  tourist season - Indian Express
Content:
One may call it a small measure. But a programme launched by the State Water Supply Department in primary and secondary schools across Gujarat to educate both students and teachers on how to detect contamination and avail clean potable water, has started yielding positive results. It is also eliciting an overwhelming response from the stakeholders.

Under the programme, the Water and Sanitation Management Organisation (WASMO) — government's implementing agency — has dispatched water quality testing kits to over 29,000 primary schools and 9,000 secondary schools across the state.

Apart from containing basic equipments like chloroscope and H2S vials for checking the residual chlorine in water, the kits carry literature explaining the various parameters for testing bacteriological and chemical contamination in drinking water. The brochures highlighting potable water-related issues, such as chlorination, fluoride and its ill effects on health, have also been provided with the kits.

Each kit also carries a letter written by Chief Minister Narendra Modi addressed to the principals and teachers of these schools, appealing to them to ensure that this special drive to make available potable water to school students is carried out successfully. He has asked them to send progress reports to the WASMO headquarters in Gandhinagar every month.

"The response to the awareness programme has been good since its launch over three months ago. WASMO has already received feedback from over 11,000 schools across Gujarat. More and more schools are reporting to us about how the kits have proved useful to not only the students and teachers, but also to the local community members particularly in rural areas," State Water Supply Secretary V S Gadhvi told Newsline.

Gadhvi said he has directed WASMO officials to prepare a database of the responses being received from these schools. This data will be analysed on a regular basis so as to ascertain which region is facing more potable water-related problems. In fact, the WASMO office also writes back to the schools suggesting remedial measures.

A senior WASMO official said: "The principal of a primary school in Mehsana district informed us that how a small measure of bacteriological testing helped the students detect contamination in water. This in turn compelled them to chlorinate the water and clean the overhead tank."

Uttamnagar Primary School at Savli in Vadodara district has reported to WASMO on how a water quality test conducted in the presence of students and locals detected bacteriological contamination in the potable water being supplied through village wells—the only source of water for the school. This made both the school management and the villagers to do regular chlorination of the water.

An interesting feedback has come from Sri Mota Khajadia Taluka School in Patdhari taluka of Rajkot, which talks about how students and teachers were forced to construct a rooftop rainwater harvesting structure after they found a high TDS level in the potable water they were getting from a tubewell dug in the premises.

When the bore-well water was tested non-potable, the well was closed. Soon after, a team of teachers and students started constructing a rooftop rain harvesting structure with the help of the WASMO office in Rajkot. This helped them store over 20,000 litres of water in the underground tank during the last monsoon.

In its bid to enhance the scope of this programme, the WASMO has also taken up a large-scale distribution of water quality field testing kits among village panchayats across Gujarat. The kits are being used for testing chemical parameters of water, namely, residual chlorine, hardness, fluoride, nitrates, turbidity and bacteriological contamination, said Gadhvi.

Besides, problem-specific kits are also being dispatched to panchayat offices to measure TDA level and iron content in drinking water. Village-level water quality testing teams are being trained to use these kits.

Also, anganwadi workers and village-level health functionaries are being trained in potable water testing and maintaining its record. So far, the capacity building programmes have been launched for science teachers in over 8,000 schools and 5,506 anganwadis across the state.

Heading: CM flags off campaign to save the girl child - Indian Express
Content:
A total of Nine hotels in the vicinity of Sasan Gir village, which had been sealed by the Talala Mamlatdar some time ago for not obtaining no-objection certificates (NOC) from the Forest Department, have started functioning again, albeit illegally.

Every year, visitors from far and wide flock to this small village in Junagadh district. The infrastructure to manage tourism here is inadequate with just one functioning government lodge, Sinh Sadan. In the last few years, however, over 30 private hotels have mushroomed to cash in on the heavy tourist inflow.

"Most of the private hotels that exist in Gir have neither obtained NOCs from the Forest Department nor have they followed any licensing formality. Till date, the authorities had paid a blind eye to this issue. But recently, following orders from the Junagadh District Collector, the Talala Mamlatdar had sealed around nine hotels in the vicinity of Sasan Gir forest.

"All of these sealed hotels had already applied for NOCs long ago, but nothing happened due to the lethargic attitude of the Forest

Department. Now, with the tourist season having begun, over 20,000 visitors visit the sanctuary daily and many want to stay back. That's why most of the sealed hotels have started functioning again," said Bharat Chuhan, the owner of a small hotel in Sasan Gir.

When contacted, the Talala Mamlatdar, Amiben Doshi said: "The hotels had been sealed as per power given to me by the Collector, when we came to know that they had not obtained Forest Department NOCs. The local police have to check whether the hotels remain sealed or continue operation. Government holidays are on so we have not been able to follow up on this issue."

The Forest Department, meanwhile, has not taken any interest in the issue. "We are busy managing the heavy traffic of Diwali in the sanctuary and in our interpretation zone, but once this rush recedes, we will look into the matter. As of now, I have not received any file of hotels asking for NOC from us," said L A Chuhan, the Deputy Conservator of Forest, Sasan Gir.

Heading: Local hospitality floors Gujarati expatriates - Indian Express
Content:
On Friday, Shri Somnath Sarva Samaj Beti Bachao Jan Jagruti Yatra 'Shri Somnath Society Save the Daughter Campaign Rally' began from Surat. Chief Minister Narendra Modi flagged it off from Surat. The rally will culminate on November 5.

The aim of this rally is to spread awareness in the society and erase the difference between boys and girls from public mind. Another objective of this rally is to balance the male-female ratio by 2010. The rally will pass through 226 talukas in the state and will halt at nine different places.

On the occasion of the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel, Modi paid floral tributes to the great leader and said that when the whole country has been swept by a wave of terrorism, this rally would convey the message of love, peace and happiness.

"Saving the girl child is not the sole responsibility of the government but of the whole society. There is an urgent need for both the government and the society to come forward and work together for this campaign," Modi added.

On the occasion, novelist Gunvant Shah said, "The society cannot survive without daughters. We as a society need to make ourselves aware that killing a girl child will take the society nowhere."

Madhur Savadi, member of Shri Jaldhara Trust said, "This rally will be a historic moment for Gujarat, as it will create and spread awareness about saving the girl child in every part of the state.

Several MLAs were also present when the rally was flagged off.

Heading: Diwali woes: Graph of emergency cases shoots up in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
It was an emotional day for a group of 17 Gujarati expatriates when they addressed a gathering at the Circuit House Annexe here on Friday. Hansaben Dabi, a non-resident Indian (NRI) who runs a tour agency in Leeds, UK, broke down after receiving an 'unprecedented' hospitality in her 'own' land.

"I have never received such a warm welcome anywhere in the world," she told the audience, which included Minister for NRI Affairs in Gujarat, Jay Narayan Vyas and a host of officials from the State Tourism Department. The NRI group is on a two-week tour of the state.

"I was told about the bomb blasts that took place in July this year. But I was not deterred," said Hansaben, who runs the Hansas Heritage Tours at Leeds that has organised this tour.

"I love Gujarat. People here are very hospitable and loving. I found Gujarati food very delicious. I am enjoying my trip," she said, adding that she plans to organise three to four such tours every year from next year.

Her husband, Kishor Dabhi, who is an engineering lecturer by profession and the tour organiser, told Newsline that there is an 'inner desire' among the Gujarati expatriates to know about their roots and that many of those settled in the UK, Europe, Africa and other countries want to visit their ancestral place.

"I feel at home in Gujarat. People here are extremely hospitable," said Dr Liaqat Ali Parapiya, another UK-based NRI. A professor of Haematology and sub-dean for the International Studies in Leeds Medical College, Dr Parapiya was highly impressed by the economic development of Gujarat, but called for simultaneous social and environmental growth.

Great grandson of Habib Ahmed Parapiya, the first president of the Indian National Congress in Nairobi, Dr Parapiya was accompanied by his British wife and sister Noor Begum Parapiya. His ancestors belonged to Rajkot.

Minister Vyas said it was his experiment to organise heritage tours for the Gujarati expatriates directly through them. "They are important assets of the state. Through them, we can attract foreigners and market Gujarat as a global tourist destination," he said.

Over 2.25 lakh Gujarati NRIs visit the state every year. Vyas expressed hope that the number would cross the three-lakh mark from next year, owing to the efforts being made by the state government through kite festivals and other such public events.

Heading: No kidding! 14-year-old boy sends civic authorities on backfoot with his RTI ‘act’ - Indian Express
Content:
This Diwali, the state's EMRI (Emergency Management and Research Institute) services saw an upswing in the number of emergency cases in general and maternity and RTA (road-traffic accident) cases in particular.

The state registered a predictable rise in the number of burn cases, on an average of eight on a normal day to a total of 83 serious burn cases on the three days of Diwali.

Assault cases have closely followed maternity and RTA cases during this time.

"There has been at least a 10 to 15 per cent increase in the number of emergency cases in all categories (assaults, burns, road accidents, pregnancy related and cardio cases) across the state," said Kaushal Patel, District Manager, EMRI.

Going by the figures, a major upswing was seen in maternity cases on October 27, 28 and 29.

On a normal day, the 108 ambulance service handles about 400 maternity emergencies. However, the number shot up drastically from 532 on Kali Chudas (October 27) to 625 on the New Year day (October 29).

"This drastic increase (30 per cent) in the number of maternity related cases in the Diwali period was due to the sole dependence on emergency services during the festival," Patel said.

"On other days, people generally use personal vehicles to take pregnant women to hospital, as pregnancy is not really regarded as a major emergency. But since it becomes difficult for personal vehicles to commute during festivals, it could be a reason for the escalation," he added.

Similarly, the number of road accident cases across the state increased from 364 on Monday (October 27) to 567 on Wednesday (October 29)—an 80 per cent rise. On a normal day, the cases under the category reach an average of 300.

The number of cardio cases (heart related ailments) shot up from an average of 60 per day to 80 during the festival.

Also, the number of assault-related emergency cases doubled up from 55 to 127 in the three days, when on a normal day there are not more than 20 cases.

An increase in crime during the festive period led to an increase in the assault cases by a whooping 500 per cent.

Heading: ‘Tired of life’, centenarian commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
As the Right to Information Act (RTI) goes on empowering people across rural parts of the country, it has brought 14-year-old Vinit Patel from Visnagar in Mehsana into the national limelight.

Vinit is perhaps the youngest information seeker, who has pushed the local civic authorities on the backfoot with his questions pertaining to irregular water supply to his society and a long pending demand for road connectivity.

Impressed by the move, Mumbai-based Public Concern for Governance Trust (PCGT) has decided to honour the boy with the Navleen Kumar Award for 2008. The award will be handed over to Vinit at a special ceremony in Mumbai on November 5.

"There is an acute problem of water in our society. Also, the residents have for a long time been demanding a road here," said Vinit, a Class VIII student of Sahajanand Secondary School. "I was wondering if something could be done about this, when my father told me that I can seek information from the civic authorities under the RTI Act. My uncle, who had already done something like this in Visnagar, helped me to file the petition in May this year," he added.

"I wanted to know why the water supply to our society was so erratic and sought a lab report of the water. I also asked them as to why there was no road to our society and who all had filed tenders for the road so far," Vinit told Newsline. He further said that as the answers provided by the authorities were unsatisfactory, he approached the Mehsana District Collector, who in turn has asked him to file an application in the prescribed form. "I will file it in the next couple of days," he added.

Talking about the award, he said though it is a good feeling, he would not be able to enjoy the occasion much as he lost his father Pankaj Patel in September.

"It was my father who inspired me to file the application. But he is not with me anymore," he said.

Navleen Kumar Award is given in the name of noted land rights activist who was murdered by the land mafia in Mumbai in June 2006.

The PCGT confers this award in two categories — individual and organisation. While Vinit bags the award in the individual category, Ahmedabad-based Mahiti Adhikar Gujarat Pahel gets it in the organisation category.

Heading: Not allowed to go home on Diwali, convict commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
In an unusual incident, a 100-year-old man committed suicide on Diwali night on October 29 for unknown reasons.

While Makarpura police have started gathering information about the reasons behind the incident, neighbours told the police that the man was mentally disturbed and had none to take care of him.

The police have registered a case of accidental death. Shanabhai Kadam (100) sprinkled some inflammable material on his body and set himself afire. The incident took place at around 10.30 pm and it was registered with Makarpura police at 11.30 pm.

While there was no eyewitness, residents at Tarsali Mali mohalla, where the old man had been residing, noticed Kadam lying in his house and rushed him to the Sir Sayajirao General Hospital for treatment.

"We do not have specific information about the reasons behind the suicide but Kadam's neighbours had told us that he was mentally disturbed," said an official at Makarpura police station.

Heading: Vadodara remembers its ‘Sardar’ on his birthday - Indian Express
Content:
Depressed at not being able to celebrate Diwali with his family, a 35-year-old murder convict of Sabarmati Central Jail, Mayabhai Kapadbhai, allegedly committed suicide by hanging himself in a jail lavatory on Thursday.

Preliminary investigation reveals that Mayabhai, who was serving a life term, had moved an application seeking furlough to go home on Diwali. But the application was rejected, police said.

On Thursday afternoon, some inmates saw Mayabhai hanging from the window grills of a jail lavatory. The Sabarmati police were immediately intimated about it.

Mayabhai, who was lodged in barrack number 3 in ward number 2 of Bada Chakkar area in the high security jail, along with 25 others, was sentenced to life imprisonment for killing nine people in an inter-community clash in Kutch.

Cops are awaiting Mayabhai's autopsy report to ascertain the actual cause of his death. Meanwhile, a complaint of accidental death has been registered and police are investigating the case.

Heading: This Diwali, hospitals were busy nursing burns - Indian Express
Content:
The 134th birth anniversary of Sardar Valabhbhai Patel on Friday was celebrated at his birthplace by numerous people of Karamsad, Anand, Vallabh Vidyanagar and Vadodara.

In the morning, locals and other prominent dignitaries including Dinsha Patel, Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas, and Duleep Mathai, descendant of John Mathai who was independent India's second finance minister, took part in a function held in the honour of the 'Iron Man of India'.

Similar commemorations were held at Charutar Vidya Mandal and at Sardar Patel's birthplace in Karamsad. "Everyone came together and discussed the various episodes of Sardar Patel's life. Many NRIs also attended the function," said Ramesh Prajapati, administrator of Sardar Patel Memorial Trust, Anand.

In Vadodara, the Sardar Bhavan Trust on Friday renamed the road from Lehripura to Kothi Cross roads as Sardar Patel Marg. The route had been named after Sardar Patel by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) way back in 1962; but it was renamed on Friday in a bid to refresh public memory.

"It has been 46 years since the road was named after Sardar Patel, but people hardly remember it. Today, we officially placed tableaus at various points of the Marg to remind people," said Harendrasinh Dayma, administrator of Sardar Bhavan Trust.

The tableaus were put up at various points by the Trust

officials including Nyay Mandir, Jubilee Baug and at Sardar Bhavan. "Apart from this, we also exhibited various books on Sardar Patel so that people can know more about the great leader," Dayma added.

Heading: Armed robbers strike petrol pump, decamp with cash and cellphone - Indian Express
Content:
Hospitals in the state were plagued by cases of burns during Diwali. Medical staff at all the major city hospitals worked hard to attend to the cases. A majority of EMRI Service employees had been on their toes to keep emergency situations under control.

Ahmedabad Civil Hospital registered a total of 12 burn cases in the three day period between October 27 and 29. "All of them are Diwali-related burn cases. Three out of the twelve are major burns while the rest are minor. The number of cases this year is lesser as compared to last year's twenty," said Jayesh Sachde, In-charge of the burn wards at the Civil Hospital.

The VS (Sheth Vadilal Sarabhai) Hospital attended to ten such burn cases, confirmed Resident Medical Officer (RMO), Nirmal Shah. All the ten cases were minor burns. Meanwhile, RMO Lakshaman Taviya at the LG (Lallubhai General) Hospital confirmed a total of 17 Diwali-related burn cases. However, all of them were minor burns.

In Vadodara, over 10 burn cases were registered at the Sir Sayaji General (SSG) Hospital in the last two days. Those injured were between 8 and 20 years of age.

While Sachin Vasava (13) injured both his eyes during an accident on Wednesday evening, Hitesh Patel (14) from Jubelli Baug area had to undergo a plastic surgery. Pradip Somawasi (14) from Kishanwadi was injured after a burning splinter fell onto a stack of crackers at his house. Somawadi suffered 10 per cent burns. Fortunately, most of the others suffered second degree burns. All the patients were discharged after being treated.

More such Diwali-related cases have been suspected at the private hospitals across the city. The Medico Legal Officer (MLO) at the emergency ward of SSG Hospital opined that most cases happened when children handled crackers in the absence of elders.

Heading: Burney meets PoK woman in Kolkata hospital - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old share broker, Aamir Ali Virani, committed suicide by hanging himself from a ceiling fan at his home in Chirag Ali Lane in Abids area late on Thursday night.

Abids police station Sub-Inspector S Srinivas said that the young stockbroker suffered huge losses when the Sensex crashed to 8,000 points on Wednesday. This is the second suicide related to the fluctuating fortunes on the share market in the city in less than two months.

According to the police, for the past five years, Aamir, who was unmarried, had been operating a share trading business from his office Omen Solutions on Chirag Ali Lane. His family members claimed that he had invested heavily in the stock market and in the last one month, he had suffered heavy losses. When asked if they suspected any foul play, the family members said they could not see any other reason for his suicide than the tumbling stock market, S-I Srinivas said.

According to the police, Aamir chose to stay back alone at home on Thursday when his parents and other relatives left for Zamat Khana for prayers. "They returned late in the night and found the front door bolted from inside. When Aamir did not respond to their knocking for over one hour, they broke open the door and found him hanging from a ceiling fan," Abids police said.

His family members told police that Aamir went on buying stocks even when the stock market was going down, hoping that it would recover. Ultimately, when the Sensex fell below 9,000 points, Aamir lost almost all his money. Police suspect that he had invested more than Rs 10 lakh in the share market.

This is the second suicide in the city, following the global market crash. On September 18, Bhupendra, 30, a share broker, had committed suicide with his 25-year-old wife Swati and two-and-a-half-year-old son Akshay at his home in SBH colony in Saidabad area after the Sensex nosedived. Bhupendra blasted an LPG cylinder at his home and all three were charred to death. He was into the share business for more than 10 years.

Heading: WBIC asks all parties to appear for hearing on Tata deal - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani human rights activist and former human rights minister Ansar Burney on Friday visited a woman admitted to a city hospital for over two years. Barao Abdul, claims she is from Harchowal area in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and has been undergoing treatment in the National Medical College and Hospital since August 2006.

"It seems that she is from PoK. The places she has mentioned are there," said Burney, who also took up the cause of Sarabjit Singh who is on death row in Pakistan. "I have taken Barao's pictures. We will upload them on the Internet. I will also get in touch with the PoK government and request them to publish her photos in local newspapers."

Burney, special advisor to the UN Human Rights Commission in Geneva, claimed the woman was in good health. "She said she had no problems, but wanted to go home," he added.

Barao was found in a dishevelled condition on Digha-Contai road in East Midnapur in April 2006. She was admitted to Contai hospital and later shifted to the state hospital in August 2006 after intervention by the state government and Diganto, an NGO.

Seated on bed number one of the psychiatric ward, Barao kept yelling "mujhe wapas jana hai... mujhe ghar pahuncha do."

"She was admitted with severe psychotic disorder," recalled Srijit Das, who has looked after Barao from the beginning.

The Pakistan High Commission in India had tried to secure Barao's return, and Kolkata High Court had in 2006 also ordered the state government to trace her home, but to no avail.

Doctors say Barao has recovered to a great extent. "She is usually cheerful and helps patients in need," said Das. "But sometimes loneliness gets the better of her and then she cries out, 'take me back home'."

When she was hospitalised, Barao could only recall that she had a husband and children and her father's apple orchard was located near her home.

Heading: Kolkata is different, north Indians, minorities welcome here: Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
Following the Calcutta High Court's stay on its order to disclose the details of the Singur deal between Tata Motors and the Bengal government under an RTI appeal, the West Bengal Information Commission (WBIC) has requested all parties involved to appear before it on November 19 for a hearing.

The WBIC letter has been sent to 11 parties, including the chief secretary, principal secretary (commerce and industries), managing director, West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation, Leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee and Tata Motors Ltd.

"We have asked all to send in their written submissions by November 10. While granting a stay on full disclosure of the deal in the public domain, the HC directive had asked us to hold a hearing in which Tata Motors would also be represented," WBIC secretary Nandan Roy said on Friday.

On September 12, the HC had restrained the government and the WBIDC from making the two annexures of the agreement public, which they had signed with Tata Motors on the Singur project. The automaker had taken the government and the WBIDC to court after the latter posted the text of the "general" agreement on its website upon the direction from the WBIC. The commission had received an RTI plea for such disclosure.

The Tatas' lawyer had argued that the WBIC had violated the RTI Act, 2005 by asking the state to display the agreement, citing Section 11(1) of the Act which states in case a third party other than the petitioner and the government is involved — in this case Tata Motors — a submission from is needed for any information to be revealed. The second argument was that the agreement between the three parties was a "trade secret", and that the Nano small car project was in effect a private commercial venture.

Heading: Truckers in Kolkata feel the ripples of Assam blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Calling the spat between the north Indians and Maharashtrians as "parochialism", Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee has assured that such incidents will never occur in the state.

Addressing a gathering of minorities at the foundation laying ceremony of an Urdu-medium school in Rajabazar, Bhattacharjee wondered as to how such restrictions could be imposed within ones own country.

"No one can say that people from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar cannot come to Kolkata. The situation in West Bengal and Kolkata is different. We are proud that Kolkata is a metropolitan city," he said.

The chief minister very clearly expressed his displeasure over the schism that has occurred due to the communal strife in various parts of the country.

"I cannot imagine such a thing happening in West Bengal where Muslims and Christians are attacked. Earlier they were destroying mosques, now they are burning churches," he said.

Bhattacharjee said he has written to the Centre for taking action against the people involved in such crimes.

Talking about the condition of minorities in the state, Bhattacharjee said the government was aware that minorities in the state were lagging behind even before the Sachar Committee report was published.

About 25 per cent of the population in the state are minorities and they are lagging behind because of historical reasons, he added.

"For three years repeatedly I have asked the Centre to have a sub-plan for the development of minorities. But the Centre did not respond and so we have come up with the minority action plan in 12 districts across the state where the Muslim population is high," said Bhattacharjee implying that the state government is keen on the development of the minorities.

The chief minister added that in West Bengal the state government has spent the maximum resources for the development of the minorities in the state compared to any other state in the country.

Rajasthan-Bengal Maitri Paishad
As the country is being torn apart on the basis of regional identities, the CPM is all set to keep such sentiments within the state at bay. This time, it is the Rajasthani community, which the Marxists intend to impress in Kolkata. The first step towards this was the formation of the Rajasthan-Bengal Maitri Paishad that will be formally launched on November 3.

Heading: Malaria on a wild gallop, 3 more dead - Indian Express
Content:
The effect of Thursday's serial blasts in Assam was already being felt in West Bengal. Panic was evident at the office of the Federation of West Bengal Truck Owners Association. Currently around 1,500 trucks are stranded at border areas of Srirampur in Assam and Bashirhat in Cooch Behar district.

"On an average 500 trucks go to Assam from Bengal. But we have not received any bookings for Friday. The truck owners are facing heavy losses," said Federation of West Bengal Truck Owners Association general secretary Satyajit Majumder. The body is also worried about the condition of perishable items.

Sources at the Trade Adviser and Director of Movement's office in Kolkata also confirmed that though rail and air traffic had not been hit, the blasts have dealt a serious blow to the movement of cargo via road — at least for the next few days. More than 500 of the trucks that had left West Bengal on Wednesday and Thursday are now stranded at Beltala in Assam and Fancy Bazar in Guwahati.

Heading: 35 cases in Ward 72 alone - Indian Express
Content:
Negligence of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and the state health department claimed two more lives on Friday.

Tarun Sen (60), a resident of 28B Brajanath Dutta Lane in Ward 48, died of viral encephalitis and Naresh Singh (36), a resident of Hida Ram Banerjee Lane near Bowbazzar in Ward 51, succumbed to malignant malaria in Calcutta Medical College and Hospital.

The KMC is yet to confirm that the deaths occurred due to vector-borne disease.

In Ward 68, Santanu Shikari, a resident of 7/1 Jamir Lane, was found to have contracted dengue and was admitted in National Medical College.

According to the KMC health officials, Naresh was suffering from fever for the past few days. His symptoms indicated malaria and he was admitted to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital on Tuesday. He succumbed to the disease this morning. "I was told by the hospital authorities that the patient has died of malaria, though I did not receive any report yet," said Sanchita Mondal, councillor of Ward 51.

Debdwaipayan Chattopadhyay, Chief Municipal Health Officer (CMHO), refused to confirm that the death had occurred from malaria.

"No confirmatory blood test was conducted by the hospital authorities. The clinical diagnosis indicates malaria," said Chattopadhyay.

Besides, one more death due to malignant malaria has been reported from North 24-Paraganas.

Heading: New schemes to lure drivers to buy new autos - Indian Express
Content:
Ward number 72 in Bhowanipore has been brought to its knees by malaria, but the Kolkata Municipal Corporation is yet to sit up.

Officials connected to the health clinic in Ward 72 admitted that last week, 22 cases of malaria have been reported. This week, the ward has already seen 13 cases ¿ this despite KMC claims that fumigation has been carried out in the area and in the homes of the affected people.

The residents, however, hotly deny it.

Bawaj Kamat, a resident of 25/4 Chakraberia Road (South), who had recently suffered a bout of malaria, said the civic authorities are yet to visit his home and conduct fogging operations.

"Many malaria cases have been reported from this locality and although none of them were fatal, the authorities did not visit any of the homes," he said. "Now my nephew has contracted the disease."

Most residents say the KMC officials have not visited the area in a year. Rajesh Yadav, another resident, said people in the slums are furious about the civic body's negligence.

"Almost every family has suffered from malaria. We go for blood tests, take medicines and recover and then someone else in the family falls ill and the cycle starts again," he said.

Most worry that it is only a matter of time before someone succumbs to the disease. Many of the slum dwellers who had been afflicted with malaria have already left for their villages in Bihar.

Councillor Sachidananda Banerjee confirmed that the KMC is yet to take any action in the area. "The authorities have not visited the ward and taken control of the situation. Neither do they come for spraying. There have been 25 cases of malaria, including malignant malaria and three cases of dengue in the ward, but there has been no positive response from the authorities," said Banerjee.

For now, the health officials at the KMC clinic are only too thankful that no case of dengue has been detected in the area.

Heading: Todis file fresh plea against arrest warrant - Indian Express
Content:
To push forward its plan to take polluting autorickshaws off the road, the state transport department has now dangled another carrot — a Rs 6,000 discount on the purchase of a new vehicle from the manufacturers.

As per the scheme, the state government plans to give a further subsidy of Rs 10,000 to autorickshaw drivers who are willing to purchase a new vehicle. An amount to the tune of Rs 95,000 will be arranged as bank loan by the state government. A new autorickshaw would amount to Rs 1,26,000, of which vehicle owners will have to cough up only Rs 15,000.

The state transport department has also urged the bus and mini-bus owners to come up with suggestions for launching similar schemes.

With the Calcutta High Court giving a directive to phase out vehicles which are more than 15-years-old, the state government has already identified 777 private buses in Kolkata, 600 buses in the suburbs and 200 mini-buses in the city and suburbs, including North and South 24 Parganas and Howrah.

The bus and taxi owners, under the banner of the Bengal Bus Syndicate and Bengal Taxi Association, met state Transport

Minister Subhas Chakraborty on Friday and urged the government not to ban vehicles which are over 15 year old but are non-polluting.

The bus owners have been asking the state government not to take into consideration the age of the vehicle but its pollution status before imposing a ban on it.

"We will not make any such considerations. Bus, mini-buses and taxis more than 15 year old will be pulled off from the streets by March 31 next year," said Chakraborty.

Heading: Patient dies, kin say SSKM staff ‘sought money for treatment’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Todis and Anil Saraogi on Friday filed separate petitions — from an undisclosed location — in the city sessions court challenging the arrest warrant issued against them by the CBI court on October 27.

The magistrate of the CBI court had issued a warrant against Asoke Todi, Pradip Todi and Anil Saraogi. The court also directed the CBI to produce them on November 3, when the case will come up for hearing.

The CBI had filed a chargesheet in the death of Rizwanur Rehman, a computer graphics designer who was found dead on the railway tracks at Patipukur near Dum Dum railway station on September 21, 2007.

The agency had filed the chargesheet on September 22, 2008 and had accused Ashok Todi, father-in-law of Rizwanur; Pradip Todi, Ashok Todi's brother; Anil Saraogi, relative of the Todis; Pappu, friend of the Rizwanur family, and three police officers — Ajoy Kumar, former deputy commissioner, Detective Department; Sukanti Chakraborty, assistant commissioner and Krishnendu Das, sub-inspector — of abetment to suicide.

Subsequently, the CBI court had issued summons asking them to personally appear before the court on October 27. Instead of personal appearance, the Todis and Saraogi had filed a petition for the criminal proceedings to be kept in abeyance.

The lawyer of the Todis argued that the CBI court should not initiate the trials now in compliance with a Supreme Court order passed on October 13.

Rejecting the argument, the CBI court had issued an arrest warrant against the Todis and Saraogi. The CBI had raided the Salt Lake residence of Todi and his office, but failed to trace the accused.

Heading: Parties don’t want EC to write the last word on the wall - Indian Express
Content:
Tension prevailed at the SSKM hospital on Friday morning after the death of an asthma patient, Somnath Roy. The patient's family alleged he was not attended by two hospital staff, who demanded Rs 40 for their services. The accused have been arrested on the basis of a complaint lodged by the victim's family.

As the news of Roy's death reached his relatives and friends they protested in front of the superintendent's office alleging medical negligence and extortion by the hospital attendants. Police had to be called in to bring the situation under control. Roy (40), a resident of Mudiali Road, was admitted to the SSKM with breathing problem at 2 am on Thursday.

"On Thursday night another patient called up and informed us that our brother was in a critical condition and the attendants were not putting on an oxygen mask. When we requested them to do so, the two attendants — Anil and Adesh — asked us to pay Rs 40," said Sanjay Roy, brother of the deceased.

The family has lodged a complaint with the Bhowanipore police station and also submitted a written complaint to the hospital superintendent demanding a probe.

Heading: By December, we must have 20 points: Rozario - Indian Express
Content:
At an all-party meeting on Friday, the representatives of different political parties urged the state Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) to relax the ban imposed earlier by the Election Commission (EC) on putting posters or writing on the walls.

After the meeting Debasish Sen, CEO, said, " I will soon convey the views of the political parties to the EC."

Sen had announced two weeks ago that no political party will be allowed to put posters or write on the walls for election purposes. The EC had also banned the use of property owned by educational institutions for their respective election meeting.

Rabin Deb, CPM leader, said all political parties have expressed displeasure on the ban imposed by the EC. Manas Bhuniya, Congress MLA, echoed the same. He said political parties should take the onus of removing posters from the walls after elections. Mukul Roy, Trinamool parliamentarian, said the EC directive would hamper the interest of small political parties like the Trinamool.

The CEO announced that the draft of the voters list will be published in 51,919 booths across the state on November 10 except in 12 Assembly constituencies.

Claims and objections of the voters will be received in the booths till November 24. The final voters list will be published on January 10, 2009.

The EC is likely to announce the date of the by-election in Nandigram, Para and Sujapur Assembly constituencies soon, Sen added.

The West Bengal State Election Commission, meanwhile, has declared the schedule of the municipal elections, which will be held on November 30. Elections will be held in Howrah, Krishnagar, Behrampore and Jhargram municipalities.

Heading: Tejo rocks: Md Sporting pin hopes on new kid on the block - Indian Express
Content:
East Bengal coach Stanley Rozario has set a target for his players — 20 points at the end of the first phase of the I-League and you will be on course.

The red-and-golds have seven points from five matches. Six more matches are to be played before the first phase ends in December.

"Ideally we would like to have 18 points from those six matches. It's not impossible but very difficult. So I've set a realistic target, that is 20 points from the first leg. It shouldn't be tough considering that we have a very good attacking line-up," Rozario told The Indian Express.

The coach banks on Yakubu Yusif to meet the target. "He (Yakubu) is a fantastic player. He has gelled very well with Sunil Chhetri. The two are complementing each other. In fact, Chhetri has been taking a lot of work-load upfront and is creating free spaces for Yakubu," Rozario observed.

He lamented over the fact that Asim Biswas has been ruled out of the first phase of the tournament. "Asim's absence is a blow. Had he been fit he would have added more sting to our attack. In that case Yakubu would have played as a withdrawn forward to give the combination more variety."

At the same time, he rued missed chances that saw them lose eight points in first five matches.

"We had our chances. We dominated the match against Mumbai FC. We paid heavily for missing a few sitters. Even in the last match against Mohun Bagan, we have the greater ball possession and came very close to scoring a few times despite being reduced to 10 men after Surkumar got the marching orders. Hope, our strikers and the midfielders will be more accurate with their finishing in the upcoming matches," Rozario said.

East Bengal face Mohammedan Sporting in their next match on Sunday. Right back Surkumar Singh is out, suspended. Rahim Nabi is likely to take his place.

"Nabi has the all-round ability. He is good at overlaps, can tackle hard as well. He is the ideal replacement for Surkumar," Rozario commented.

About Md Sporting's Mike Okoro and Theodore Sunday, he said: "They are very good players. So are Baichung (Bhutia) and (Jose) Barreto. But football is a team game and the team has to click rather than the individuals."

Md Sporting's overseas duo had tomented East Bengal defence in the Calcutta Football League. Rozario wants to ensure that doesn't happen again.

Heading: Chirag aim to stop Sporting’s march - Indian Express
Content:
Mohammedan Sporting coach Sabbir Ali appears to be very excited about a new kid on the block. Tejo, a 22-year-old midfielder from Mizoram, who will sign for the black-and-white brigade shortly, has won his heart.

Sabbir is known for his balance. Even he is bowled over by Tejo's talent.

"He (Tejo) reminds me of Samaresh (Pintu) Chowdhury. He has the natural ability to send incisive passes to the strikers. He will have to be more positive in set-piece movements. But he is young and has age on his side," Sabbir told The Indian Express after Md Sporting's practice at Rabindra Sarovar today.

The club wanted to sign him today, couldn't do that owing to some technical difficulties. He is expected to join ranks within a couple of days.

Theodore Sunday has spotted this boy who cut his teeth in competitive football at Dinhara Club in Mizoram league. He then moved to Tripura where Sunday spotted him.

"With Tejo in the midfield, I'm sure our strikers will get lot more balls in the attacking-third. At the same time, the other two midfielders Sovon Chakrabarty and Lalramluaha are also improving. Midfield control will be the key against East Bengal," Sabbir observed.

Meanwhile, Md Sporting have roped in Wasim Feroze, a defender from Kashmir to strengthen the rearguard.

Heading: Neha stuns top seed to win singles title - Indian Express
Content:
Chirag United coach Subrata Bhattacharya aims to upset Sporting Clube de Goa's applecart, but wants to be cautious in his approach.

"Our primary target is to earn a point. They have a very good line-up and are playing very well. We have to bank on counter attacks to upset them," Bhattacharya said after practice on match eve.

His boys had stunned Mahindra United last week and that was a huge morale boost for the team.

The hosts didn't have six frontline players in that game. But Bhattacharya's game-reading and strategy saw them through.

Good news, Nigerian striker Muritala Ali, who missed the last match owing to suspension, would be back tomorrow. Bhattacharya's primary target is to get 22 points, which, according to him, would be sufficient to stay in the top tier.

"Sometimes, discretion is the better part of valour. We are into the I-League top division for the first time. The basic idea should be to stay in the first division. I think if we can get to 22-23 points, we are safe. That, however, doesn't mean we won't try to win.

"Against a more balanced outfit, we have to wait for our chances. The boys did that perfectly against Mahindra. Patience is the key. We have to keep our defence tight to frustrate them," Bhattacharya said.

So far, Chirag have been most impressive of the four Kolkata clubs taking part in this I-League.

Sporting, on the other hand, are on a roll with 12 points from five matches. They, however, will miss midfielder Micky Fernandes, who is out, suspended.

Coach Biwas Gaonkar exuded confidence ahead of the tie. "We will play to win," he said.

Heading: More than 2 lakh Indians living illegally in US - Indian Express
Content:
Unseeded Neha Prasad emerged champions in the girls' under-12 singles of the Bengal Sub-Junior State Tennis Championship 2008 being played at Dakshin Kalikata Sansad (DKS). Neha beat top seed Ishita Tibrewal 6-3, 6-3.

In boys' under-14 and under-16 singles, top seed Shukrit Guha will face No 2 seed Shreedhar Gaggar in the finals. Guha swept past Harsh Gurnani 6-4, 6-1 in the under-14 semifinal and outclassed Subho Halder 6-0, 6-1 in the under-16 semifinal.

Gaggar, after beating Richie Agarwal in under-14 semifinal 6-3, 6-3, went on to play a long two-hour match against top seed Md Sarfaraz in the under-16 semis. He eventually won it, 6-2, 4-6, 7-6.
