"One thing the players should remember is that they are employees of SLC. Every year, we sign about 40 cricketers from the national and 'A' teams. We give them very attractive contracts.

"It is SLC that looks after the players from the junior level and brings them to the level of national cricket by spending a lot of money. SLC should get some money from these cricketers rather than allow them to make payments to some outside agent. This way, we will safeguard our cricketers and make use of the money for cricket development," Ranatunga said.

He also said that the SLC would have to take steps to ensure it becomes the sole representative of its players and earns revenue from any future contract the players sign with other organisations.

The eight IPL teams between them have 13 top Sri Lankan players on three-year contracts, including captain Mahela Jayawardene, Kumar Sangakkara, Muttiah Muralitharan, Sanath Jayasuriya and Chaminda Vaas, for enormous amounts.

But Ranatunga, who led Sri Lanka to their 1996 World Cup title, said Sri Lanka's senior cricket players are paid well in the country, with each of them earning 40-45 million Sri Lankan rupees last year.

He, however, refused to react to reports of a breakdown in ties with the BCCI, following a recent meeting between Indian officials and Lankan representatives to negotiate a multi-million dollar deal.

Ranatunga also said there was no official proposal on the Twenty20 Champions League paying $40 million to SLC for the next 10 years.

Heading: Survivor Clarke rallies Australia with hundred - Indian Express
Content:
After hinting that Sachin Tendulkar was a sore loser, former Australian vice-captain Adam Gilchrist has taken a swipe at the then skipper Sourav Ganguly and spinner Harbhajan Singh, suggesting that the duo had chickened out of their 2004 Nagpur Test fearing a defeat on a grassy wicket.

"When I got to the middle, Ganguly was not there. Dravid was in his blazer, ready for the toss," Gilchrist has written in his yet-to-be-published autobiography 'True colours'. "'Where's Sourav? I said'. Rahul couldn't answer definitively; between the lines I perceived that Sourav might have pulled out from fear of losing a home series," writes Gilchrist, who was himself a stand-by skipper for an injured Ricky Ponting.

Gilchrist felt the hard green top in Nagpur could be the reason for off-spinner Harbhajan making himself unavailable for the match. "Harbhajan was out of Nagpur Test with a 'flu', which he seemed to have contracted when he saw the grassy wicket... I still don't know to this day what was wrong with Ganguly and Harbhajan," he adds.

Gilchrist mentions that speculation was rife that the hard green top was a result of Ganguly's quarrel with the head of the Vidarbha Cricket Association. "There was speculation that Sourav Ganguly was quarrelling with the head of cricket in Nagpur and a rumour that a spicy pitch might be prepared out of spite or revenge against the captain," he says.

Gilchrist had earlier said that Tendulkar had changed his version at the hearing during "Monkeygate" earlier this year in Australia.

Heading: 'Indians were defensive by sending night watchman' - Indian Express
Content:
Michael Clarke survived three dropped chances to score his eighth Test hundred in the third Test in New Delhi on Saturday.

The Australian vice-captain top-scored with 112 before the visitors were 577 all out, conceding a meagre 36-run lead in reply to India's 613 for seven declared.

Australian bowlers then reduced India to 43 for two at close, 79 runs ahead. Brett Lee removed opener Virender Sehwag (16) and fellow paceman Stuart Clark outwitted nightwatchman Ishant Sharma (1).

Gautam Gambhir, who made 206 in the first innings, was 21 not out with Rahul Dravid on five at stumps.

Clarke, dropped on 21, 90 and 94, steered the touring side towards safety with an innings of great application on a slow pitch.

Indian bowlers, made to toil for success, took the last three wickets to end the innings over an hour after tea.

Australia, down 1-0 in the four-match series, rebounded superbly from their 320-run second Test thrashing.

Clarke, who hit a match-winning 151 on Test debut in India in 2004, struck six fours and a six in his six-hour knock before tiredly holing out leg spinner Amit Mishra to long off.

Occasional off spinner Sehwag took five for 104 to claim his maiden five-wicket Test haul, while skipper Anil Kumble overcame a bad left hand injury to take three wickets.

Clarke, 27, dug in to build on the solid foundation laid by fifties from the top four batsmen and added 73 runs for the fifth wicket with Shane Watson (36).

He then shared a partnership of 106 runs for the seventh wicket with Cameron White (44).

India dropped five catches to dent their victory hopes.

Clarke was first dropped on his overnight score by Sharma and then in successive overs off Sehwag, VVS Laxman spilling a running attempt at midwicket before Mishra grassed a simple chance on the mid-wicket boundary.

The fourth and final Test starts in Nagpur on Nov. 6.

Heading: Fielding errors helped Aussies come back: Kirsten - Indian Express
Content:
Having smashed a century to bring Australia back into the third Test, vice-captain Michael Clarke said India were defensive in their approach as they sent Ishant Sharma as the night watchman on Saturday.

"Now we are in a good position. We've seen India sending out a night watchman today, which tells you that they have been pretty defensive in their approach," Clarke said after the fourth and penultimate day's play.

"It will tell you tomorrow, only one team would go for the win and it's Australia. India would not set any target tomorrow, they showed it by deciding to send a night watchman."

Asked if he was expecting a result, Clarke said, 'certainly'.

"We'll try to get a couple of early wickets tomorrow. We'll be attacking tomorrow, will try to get some early wickets, so hope we can bowl them out tomorrow," he said.

Clarke said the pitch was turning now and it would not be easy to get runs.

"Initially, it was not easy getting the first 10 runs. The pitch is turning quite a bit and it would turn even more tomorrow," he said.

On Kumble playing with injury in the little finger of his left hand, the Australian batsman said, "It was absolutely unfortunate for him, even though I'm not sure what kind of injury it is. But the fact that he still took the field and bowled is great for him and great for the Indian team as well."

Heading: Kumble's time is up, says Vengsarkar - Indian Express
Content:
Dropped catches and an unimpressive bowling helped Australia come back into the third cricket Test on the fourth and penultimate day, rued India coach Gary Kirsten.

"It was not a great time on the field for us today. Fielding errors helped the Aussies come back into the match," Kirsten said after India ended the fourth day at 43 for two, an overall lead of 79 runs.

"We started today thinking of really doing something. But we did not take our opportunities. It did not go that way," he said.

The former South African opener admitted the errors could have a bearing on the match.

"The first catch that Ishant Sharma dropped could have a bearing on the match. It's not the same with other two dropped catches because Australia had crossed the 500 mark by then. I don't think we bowled well enough to create those opportunities for ourselves after the lunch. But Aussies took their chances and capitalised on them as well. It can have a huge bearing on the match," he said.

Kirsten, however, did not feel that India missed Harbhajan Singh, who is recuperating from a toe injury.

"Harbhajan would have added value to the team, he is a tremendous bowler. But I think we have enough variety and options in the spin department for the Test. You just have to create the opportunities," he said.

Heading: Time with Sania, India in Mania - Indian Express
Content:
Former chairman of selection committee Dilip Vengsarkar gave a thumbs down to Test skipper Anil Kumble and said that he doesn't foresee the leg-spinner captaining the side after the on-going series against Australia.

Vengsarkar said though Kumble has rendered a yeoman service to the Indian cricket team, his poor form suggested he should quit.

"Kumble has not been performing since the last six to seven Tests. He has been a great servant for the country for the last 18 years but he has not done anything of note in the last few matches, his time is up now," Vengsarkar told a TV channel.

"Kumble looked completely off-color in the match and I don't see him captaining the side after the Nagpur Test," he added.

Vengsarkar felt that Kumble did not handle fellow leggie Amit Mishra properly in the third Test match.

"Mishra was bowling quite well and was getting good zip but still Jumbo under bowled him," Vengsarkar said.

Heading: Why India are appealing against Gambhir ban - Indian Express
Content:
Hopes of a dream final between Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer were dashed Friday when the top two seeds pulled out injured from their quarter-final matches at the Paris Masters.

Federer withdrew with a back injury a few hours before his match against American James Blake, while Nadal quit his showdown with world number six Nikolay Davydenko after losing the first set 6-1.

Wimbledon champion Nadal had the trainer massaging his right thigh and knee at the change of ends when trailing 4-1 and threw in the towel two games later.

The duo's exit left the tournament without any of its top four seeds after number three Novak Djokovic was beaten earlier in the week while fourth-ranked Andy Murray also perished on Friday, going down 7-6, 6-3 to an inspired David Nalbandian. Argentina's Nalbandian kept his Masters Cup hopes alive when he ended Murray's 14-match winning streak in the most spectacular match of the tournament and will meet Davydenko in the last four Saturday.

Nalbandian, 14th in the ATP Race, will qualify for the season-ending tournament if he retains his Paris title. He was, however, reluctant to say if he would take part in the season-ending tournament he won in 2005. "It's not my goal. I'm not thinking about Shanghai because we have the Davis Cup right after, so that's why," he said.

Shanghai questions

Federer was confident of defending his title in Shanghai despite his injury setback. "I've had a lot of back pain over all the years of playing tennis... (but) it's just the first time it's acute during a tournament and it makes me pull out. I'll check it out for the next few days," the Swiss told reporters.

Nadal also struggled with aches and pains during his match and, unlike Federer, was unsure if he would be able to participate in the final event of the year. Asked if he was worried for Shanghai, the Spaniard said: "For sure. Hopefully it will be fine... (but) I don't know."

Nadal's retirement left the fans frustrated and they started booing when it was announced that Federer had handed Blake a walkover into the semi-finals. Blake will meet either fellow American Andy Roddick or local favourite Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the semis.

Murray struggled with his first serve in the opening set and smashed his racket to the ground after being broken in the fourth game. The Scot, however, converted his only break chance to draw level and picked up his game, trying to keep Nalbandian at bay with his slice.

But the Argentine, with a mix of cunning drop shots and powerful groundstrokes, took the tiebreak 7-3. Nalbandian then shifted up another gear, breaking four times in the second set to wrap up victory.

Heading: Gambhir ban: ‘Give it back, but don’t look stupid’ - Indian Express
Content:
Once again, Team India, under the patronage of the BCCI's top brass, have decided to challenge the lawmakers of the International Cricket Council (ICC). Less than a year after the Sydney Test drama surrounding Harbhajan Singh, Gautam Gambhir will appeal against the one-Test ban imposed on him by match-referee Chris Broad.

But this time, the Indians aren't too bothered about the final outcome, they're just hoping to exploit one of the loopholes in the ICC framework so that Gambhir can play the crucial fourth Test. As per the rules, a player is allowed to play pending the decision of his appeal.

The ICC confirmed that they received the official appeal on Friday evening, less than 24 hours after the verdict. The release said that the ICC would appoint an independent 'appeals commissioner' for a hearing in the next 48 hours and that the hearing would be completed within seven days of the appointment.

With just a four-day gap between matches — the fourth Test starts in Nagpur on November 6 — chances are slim that the verdict will be out before the game. If Gambhir is found guilty after the Nagpur match, he will instead miss two one-dayers against England. And, with the selectors already in tangle as more and more ODI contenders have emerged, it'll only help resolving the opening problem for the time being, with both Sachin Tendulkar and Virender Sehwag expected to be available.

Broad pronounced his verdict on Friday morning. He stated in the press release: "The decision to find Gambhir guilty of a level 2 offence is indicative of the fact that any degree of physical contact is unacceptable." Gambhir had, in Thursday night's hearing, pleaded guilty to the charge under rule C1 of the code (level 2), accepting that his conduct was not within the spirit of the game.

Interestingly, while the penalty has been seen as harsh, especially in terms of the 10 per cent fine on Shane Watson, the match referee indicated that he'd been lenient with Gambhir.

"Had Gambhir been charged with and found guilty of a charge under 2.4, due to his previous offence, I would have been obliged to impose a minimum penalty of a two-Test ban. In view of the umpires, the facts of the case — the lightness of the physical conduct and the element of provocation — would not justify such a penalty," he stated.

Heading: Sydney controversy behind Gilchrist's retirement - Indian Express
Content:
Gautam Gambhir's one-Test ban has again drawn attention to the acrimony that has marred India's recent tussles with Australia.

Gambhir was suspended by International Cricket Council (ICC) match referee Chris Broad on Friday for elbowing Shane Watson while taking a run on the opening day of the third Test in New Delhi on Wednesday.

Australia all-rounder Watson was fined for provoking the batsman, the incident bringing to a head a series of verbal clashes forcing the umpires to intervene.

Gambhir was also fined for barging into Shahid Afridi in an ODI against Pakistan last November.

The BCCI has lodged an appeal against his latest ban, which would allow the 27-year-old to play in the fourth and final Test.

This series started in the shadow of India's tour to Australia in January when spinner Harbhajan Singh was at the centre of another storm.

India then overstepped the line again when paceman Zaheer Khan was fined 80 per cent of his fee in the second-Test win in Mohali for a verbal send-off of opener Matthew Hayden after the Australia opener had been dismissed.

Players from both sides made good-behaviour pledges before the series but have since shown scant regard to Broad.

Some pundits say the Indians are adopting a tit-for-tat approach against Australia, who have long been accused of gamesmanship by sledging rival players.

"It is a sign of self-belief," former India captain Ravi Shastri said. "Give back as good as you get but make sure you don't cross the line and look stupid."

"It is India who have played well against Australia in the last three or four years."

PIETERSEN PRAISE

Shastri said England skipper Kevin Pietersen had shown the best way to tackle Australia was to stand up to them.

"Kevin has shown he is capable of backing his words by taking that extra pressure upon himself and performing," he said.

Shastri backed Gambhir's ban and warned players against violating the spirit of the game but also said the Indian verbal response was having its effect on Australia, who trail 1-0 in the series.

In the controversial Sydney Test in January, Harbhajan was initially banned after being found guilty of racially abusing Australia all-rounder Andrew Symonds.

India threatened to pull out of the tour if the ban was upheld and he was eventually let-off with a fine after the charge was downgraded to use of abusive language.

The attitude of the Indian players has changed markedly since they won the Twenty20 World Cup in 2007, beating Australia on their way.

During this series Zaheer, Laxman and Mahendra Singh Dhoni have dubbed Ricky Ponting's side too defensive.

Some pundits say India's young, self-confident players are more aggressive but that the captains should help ease the tension and ensure the focus of attention is firmly on the playing of the game rather than side issues.

Heading: Happy birthday Aishwarya Rai Bachchan! - Indian Express
Content:
The controversial Sydney Test was unlucky for Australia in many ways but the one major blow it dealt to the team was that it resulted in wicket-keeper batsman Adam Gilchrist's decision to quit international cricket.

Gilchrist, whose keeping was being questioned by experts during the series, disclosed in his autobiography 'True colours' that the Sydney Test controversy was actually the last nail in the coffin.

"I certainly did not retire because my sportsmanship was questioned, and I didn't even decide to retire that week but on top of everything else that had gone on I feel the controversies around the Sydney Test were the straw that broke the camel's back," Gilchrist wrote.

The former Australian Vice-captain said he was contemplating retirement from one-dayers since the World Cup in the Caribbean but was not thinking about retiring from Tests until the happenings had started to take a toll on his peace of mind.

"They'd (sister's family) booked their tickets well in advance, thinking it might be my last Test, but I certainly hadn't made the decision. I was beginning to resolve finally on pulling out of one-day cricket, but I wasn't quitting Tests. I hadn't even asked (wife) Mel to come to Adelaide (the venue of the fourth and the final Test against India).

"... we lost the toss and fielded all day, the (Sachin) Tendulkar factory churning out another ton. My concentration wasn't good. Even in the first session I was asking myself, 'Do I really want to just pull out of one-dayers? Should I keep doing both?"

Gilchrist also admitted that his reflexes had slowed down by a fraction of second. "The ball was generally hitting me in the heels of my hands rather than palms. No one would have seen it from the outside, but my hands were continually a fraction of a second late. This had been happening for a little while now, and it was playing on my mind," he added.

The dropped catches in the Sydney Test left Gilchrist's morale so low that he began to think "I was really a batsman who wore gloves, I wasn't a genuine 'keeper".

The Australian, who is respected for his sportsmanship, also revealed how the virtue became a burden on him. "When you are batting and you nick one, you know for sure you are out. The matter is in your hands. Most players pass that responsibility to the umpire. I had decided to take the responsibility for it myself.

"... On walking, I felt isolated ... silently accused to betraying the team. Implicitly, I was made to feel selfish, as if I was walking for the sake of my own clean image, thereby making everyone else look dishonest.

"My action in the 2003 World Cup semi-final had become such a big deal because it held up mirror to every player... (but) that I walked wasn't a judgment on others," he said.

Heading: Pitt’s parents upset with Jolie’s breast-feeding photos? - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, who turned 35 on Saturday, celebrated her birthday shooting for Mani Ratnam's film 'Ravan' in Kerala.

The shooting began on the outskirts of Kochi two days ago after a delay as both Aishwarya and husband Abhishek Bachchan were occupied due to the illness of their respective fathers.

However, both will now be shooting for the film non-stop for a month. This will be their third film with ace director Mani Ratnam. Abhishek has earlier worked with him in 'Yuva' and 'Guru'.

Both films brought Abhishek, who was struggling for box office success then, critical acclaim as an actor. Aishwarya, on the other hand, debuted in his Tamil film 'Iruvar' more than a decade ago. Her last film with Mani was 'Guru'.

Professionally the year has been a good one for the dove-eyed former Miss World as her films 'Jodhaa Akbar' and 'Sarkar Raj' were well appreciated and did satisfactory business.

She has been busy participating in the 'Unforgettable Tour" and completing the first outdoor schedule of her second Tamil film opposite Superstar Rajnikanth in Peru.

Heading: RBI cuts CRR by 1%, repo rate by 0.5% - Indian Express
Content:
Angelina Jolie's breast-feeding pictures in the November issue of 'W' magazine have reportedly left Brad Pitt's parents upset.

'Star' magazine reported that while father Bill Pitt refused to talk about the published photos, mum Jane Pitt has been displeased with the way the couple's kids have been used for advertisement purposes.

Fox News quoted the magazine: "Brad's dad won't talk about it — that means he's upset. Brad's mom feels they're using their children as a marketing campaign tool and thinks it's unacceptable."

The pictures of the actress, who had posed for the cover of the American fashion magazine while breast-feeding one of her 3-month-old twins, had been shot by Brad in mid-August at their French Chateau Miraval.

Heading: RBI measures to induce rate cuts: Bankers - Indian Express
Content:
Home, consumer and corporate loan rates are likely to ease in the near future, with RBI announcing a slew of monetary measures including a one per cent cut in cash reserve and stautory liquidity ratios besides a 0.5 per cent cut in its short term lending rate.

The CRR, the percentage of amount banks are required to keep with the apex bank, has been cut in two tranches of 0.5 per cent effective from October 25 and November 8 to infuse Rs 40,000 crore in to the banking system.

The central bank had already cut CRR by 2.5 per cent to 6.5 per cent last month injecting Rs one lakh crore in to the system. With this cut, the apex bank could have injected Rs 1.4 lakh crore through CRR cut which is now pegged at 5.5 per cent.

The SLR, which is the amount banks have to keep with the RBI in the form of cash, gold or approved securities, was cut temporarily by one per cent earlier to 24 per cent and this cut has been made permanent effective from Novebmber 8.

The RBI also cut its key short term repo rate, the rate at which Reserve Bank lends overnight funds to bank, by 0.5 per cent to 7.5 per cent. Last month repo rate was cut by 1 per cent from 9 per cent to 8 per cent.

With today's measures along with several monetary steps taken last month, the apex bank has so far injected over Rs 2.5 lakh crore in to the system.

Hailing the policy measures, bankers said that they would soon look at reducing their lending and deposit rates in the near future.

Economists said the slew of measures would help to prop up growth, particulalry considering that the inflation has started falling drastically on the back of declining global crude oil and other commodity prices.

Heading: US, European markets post solid gains - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank's move to further cut reserve ratios and short term lending rate (Repo) would induce banks to cut lending rates like commercial, home, auto loans as well as deposit rates, but it may take some time to materialise, bankers said.

"Liquidity per se, ideally speaking or rationally speaking, should bring down the interest rates...But this will take may be a month or two because the banks which have a lot of sanctions in the pipeline, which are yet to crystallize into disbursements," Indian Bank's Association Chairman T S Narayanasami said.

RBI today announced 1 per cent cut in mandatory cash requirement for banks CRR and short-term lending rate repo by 0.5 per cent.

It also announced cut in the requirement for banks to keep proportion of their deposits in government securities SLR by 1 per cent. The 1 per cent cut in CRR and Statutory Liquidity Ratio would infuse another Rs 85,000 crore into the system over and above Rs 1,85,000 crore already injected by the RBI.

ICICI Bank Joint Manging Director Chanda Kochhar said the RBI's move will bring down interest rates.

"Second it is showing the mindset of the regulator that is continuously monitoring the situation and coming up with measures on dynamic basis. I think these are two positives," she said.

CMD of Delhi-based Punjab National Bank, which yesterday cut benchmark prime lending rate, saw single digit rate coming soon. "We see single digit deposit rates soon," PNB CMD K C Chakrabarty.

Chakrabarty had yesterday promised to cut maximum deposit rate by 0.50 per cent to 10 per cent from December one.

Heading: Panasonic in talks to buy Sanyo: Sources - Indian Express
Content:
A rally in US and European share markets stayed on track, delivering solid gains at the end of a month of wild volatility and losses amid fears a deep recession lies ahead.

Equities in Frankfurt, London, New York and Paris have all plunged by 15 to 17 per cent since the beginning of October, and Tokyo lost about one-quarter of its value.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 144.32 points (1.57 per cent) on Friday to close at 9,325.01, pushing gains for blue chips for the week to an eye-popping 11 per cent. But for the month the index was still down 14 per cent.

The NASDAQ composite climbed 1.32 per cent to 1,720.95 and the Standard & Poor's 500 rose 1.54 per cent to 968.75.

In Europe, following a mixed performance in Asia, sentiment brightened: in London, the FTSE 100 index added 2.0 per cent to 4,377.34, while in Paris the CAC 40 rose 2.33 per cent to 3,487.07.

The Frankfurt DAX advanced 2.44 per cent to end the week at 4,987.97. London investors digested news that British bank Barclays was to raise USD 11.7 billion, mostly from investors in oil-rich Abu Dhabi and Qatar, to bolster its finances amid the global credit crunch.

Other markets were mixed. Brazil's Bovespa fell 0.51 per cent and Canada's S&P/TSX lost 0.95 per cent but Mexico's Bolsa rose 0.56 per cent.

Shares fell sharply in Tokyo, down 5.0 per cent, even though Japan's central bank cut its super-low interest rates for the first time in seven years -- by 20 basis points to 0.3 per cent.

Hong Kong closed down 2.5 per cent as investors locked in recent sharp gains sparked by hopes that the credit crunch was easing.

Heading: Mittal lost $50 bn in ArcelorMittal shares - Indian Express
Content:
Japanese electronics maker Panasonic Corp is in talks with Goldman Sachs and two other major shareholders of Sanyo Electric Co Ltd to buy a controlling stake in its smaller rival, company and financial sources said on Saturday.

Sanyo's three main shareholders are Daiwa Securities SMBC, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp and Goldman Sachs.

The combined entity would be Japan's largest electronics maker in revenue terms, surpassing Hitachi Ltd.

Daiwa Securities SMBC is a joint venture between Daiwa Securities Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG), while Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp is Sanyo's main bank and an SMFG unit.

Heading: Craze of the age: Looks and Mileage - Indian Express
Content:
NRI steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal has suffered a USD 50 billion decline in the value of shares he holds in the ArcelorMittal following the global financial meltdown, a leading economic daily has claimed.

Mittal, who owns 45 per cent of the stock in ArcelorMittal, has seen the value of his personal shareholding fall since late June from USD 66 billion to USD 16 billion, 'The Financial Times' claimed in an analysis of the effect of global financial crisis on the steel industry.

"When Mittal talks to investors and analysts next week, he is likely to come in for tough questioning about how much he will cut production in the next few months. He will also be asked to explain the status of the company's expansion programme, in particular two big plants being planned for India, which look likely to be scaled back," the report said.

Noting that Mittal, Chairman and Chief Executive of ArcelorMittal, next week faces the biggest test of his career, the report said "the Indian metals magnate will try to convince investors that his vision of the steel industry still has merit, in spite of the battering the sector has received amid the global financial crisis."

When he presents the third-quarter results of ArcelorMittal on Wednesday from the company's imposing headquarters in the centre of Luxembourg, Mittal will do his best to put a "brave face on a 72 per cent decline in the share price of the world's biggest steelmaker over the past four months."

Heading: Laura is for classes and not masses - Indian Express
Content:
Diwali is one reason in India when market booms up irrespective of the traditional factors that governs it favouring it or not. But the reality this time did not appear to reflect this age-old feeling despite the historical rise in Sensex.

Naveen who manages a home appliances store says sales are pathetic. On asking why the sales are not taking pace he retorts, "Customers are not having money."

RK Goyal of the RK Fabrics says though his shop caters to the middle and upper class markets they are no takers for the stocks this Diwali. Speaking sharply against the recent boom in the Sensex he says that the Sensex is totally in the hands of the multinational companies and it has become a Gambling market than the stock market for the companies.

Anil Tayal of the AG club who is also the Vice-President of the Aurbindo Place Association feels people are less involved in the festivals nowadays.

Tayal who owns a gifts shop says because of the China products flooding the market the branded there are virtually no buyers for the branded products. He explains that any product, which costs around Rs 2,300 is available as Chinese brand for merely 200 to 300 rupees. "Products of China are garbage cheap though they are not durable in the long run but still people go for these because of their competitive prices."

Puneet from Time Emporium, which showcases cell phones, says the market during the season has already gone to 15% and will catch up during the peak of the Diwali festival.

Japesh a floor manager of an eating outlet of a multinational joint of South Delhi says he could not figure out any significant rise in the customers coming to the outlet at this time of Diwali. On the contrary a manager of another multinational outlet asserted a great rise in the influx of people at this time of Diwali.

Ravi Chaddha who works at the sweet shop says though there is a significant rise in the price of sweets still they are doing brisk business because people have to buy sweets at this festive time to gift to their near and dear ones.

Showroom in charge of Adarsh Yamaha Gurmeet believes that people wait the whole year for Diwali and they have Dhanteras (Auspicious day marked by the Hindus for buying something for the household) in mind. Companies launch many attractive schemes such as scratch cards and tours of tourist destinations in India as well as abroad. She maintains though the rising price of petrol is definitely a factor it does not have much impact. Nevertheless the customers coming from the middle class families opts for bikes with a competitive mileage though looks still remains a strong factor.

She also discloses that models have a great influence on the customers. Like the recent campaign of John Abraham for a bike has triggered the sales of that particular model triggering the sales to an unprecedented number.

Suruchi Mishra of Lexus says we have our loyal customer base who frequents us during the festive season. She said that most of our furniture sport traditional Indian designs

Prabhu Dayal Sharma who looks after the state entity UP Handlooms says, "We are having normal business as we keep traditional wardrobe."

Atul Gupta of the Gents collection who keeps brands such as John Players and Jockey says the sales are even worse than that normally happens in on the eve of the new Year. Though this is the season which is supposed to do the brisk business.

Monika and Bhaskar, sales executives at the Pashupati Motors say that companies offer special festive discount to attract the customers. November is specially the boom season because of the festivities, which continues throughout the month. Monika elaborates that of all the customers 45 per cent are young boys though only 5% girls turn out for buying the bikes. Conventionally still 50% of the purchase is done by the families as a whole.

Yuvraj of the Sweetz and Nutz says this Diwali people are specially going in for Chocolates and pastries rather than the traditional Mithais.

Ashwini Sharma, Deputy Showroom Manager of Suhrit Hyundai Sales, as far as sales are concerned this Diwali is no match to the last year's. Sighting the significance of various schemes in attracting the customers he said schemes like last year are not available this time which might also be the reason why customers are not turning up in great numbers.

Heading: Sex-ed in schools: Are we ready? - Indian Express
Content:
Launched yesterday with great fanfare 'Laura' by Skoda Auto India is said to be pitted against Honda Accord and Toyota Camry. Priced just below 17 lakhs the manufacturers have made it clear that it would not be anybody's and everybody's pie.

As Naren Bhiku Ram Jain, president of Federation of All India Trader Association puts it "It has come as a rival to Honda Accord."

Rajesh Kumar a builder present at the grand launch of 'Laura' was quite enthusiastic about the introduction of the new car and described it as a good spacious car with enhanced luggage capacity.

Even though many people called it a costly car N.S Dhingra who owns a hosiery business feels that the car is reasonably priced and will stay in the market.

Bruno Schmid, Counsellor and Counsel at the Embassy of Switzerland said that the newly launched car is beautiful and that more such luxury cars were required for the upwardly mobile Indians.

Bruno's wife Nadia Schmid and her guest from Lebanon, Aida said that they liked cars with soft forms such as this.

Heading: India Speaks: Holding hands OK, kissing not - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi government is soon to launch a book to educate sex in schools. The decision to be enforced will soon become a reality, as the Department of Education and Delhi State AIDS Control Society have already launched on December 1 (World AIDS Day) the handbook for teachers titled 'Yuva'.

The decision was no doubt in keeping with fear of epidemically advancing AIDS. Keeping in mind that large population of the country is living in alarming ignorance of the deadly threat, its importance is even more enhanced.

But the moot question is, will the righteous mission be implemented in the way so as to advance its motto to the target sections of the society in true faith?

Since Independence, so many high-spirited schemes have been launched in this country that only if half of the schemes were implemented in true spirit, we would have scripted quite a different success story instead of slogging to work out the overburdened accountability of a nation.

Look at the fate of our family planning programme. Instead of reaching any substantial success, the project has initiated many social maladies, which have come as even a bigger challenge than the original goal of curbing the ever-growing population.

One of the most notoriously spread side-effect of the family planning programme is that all those families, who have adhered to its slogan of keeping their families short have done so at the cost of girl child.

The disastrous results are for all to see, as some of the most prosperous states in terms of education and economy such as Haryana, Punjab and Delhi are finding themselves at an alarming stage of lowest female sex ratio.

The problem regarding female sex ratio has become so acute in states like Punjab that there have been cases of more than one man sharing a woman as wife. Girls from the poorest sections of Bengal are being allegedly brought to marry youths tired of looking for a girl for themselves in their own region.

Thus we see that the repercussions of the family planning programme, when not implemented with proper homework, can lead to such alarming situations, which becomes a hazard for the society and country.

If care had been taken to preach among the masses, the importance of female child as well and hazards of selective abortion well spread to every nook and corner of the populace, than the country could have reaped even more fruitful rewards of the ambitious programme.

Now the wrongs done to society by the selective abortions have reached an irreparable stage and the basic goal has also lost its way in the meanwhile. The bizarre state of achievements as such is for all of us to see.

Now once again a sort of campaign by the Department of Education to spread awareness about the deadly AIDS disease among the schoolchildren is a very good idea in itself. As per the policy of education department the book has been brought out in two parts. While the first part is for the students of standard sixth to eighth, the second part is destined for the students studying in classes ninth to 12th.

The book deals with issues like sexual harassment contraception and pregnancy. It is welcome to the extent of dealing such sensitive issues related to the teen tantrums that are common at such a stage of life but the kids are left on their own to deal with certain tricky issues, which are obvious at this stage.

But it should always be kept in mind that the delicate minds might react to such untraditional preaching in an absolutely unforeseen manner, which is bound to have unwanted developments within the families in particular and society in general.

It is the children of today, who have the responsibility of shouldering the nation in the coming tomorrows. If we want the rich legacy of our culture, which is replete with values to continue with the challenges of the changing times a greater need of foreground work needs to be done.

Mere launching of a book with subjects such as 'sex' that has been a big taboo in our society since medieval times seems quite an unripe decision and needs a revision or at the least a re-look.

Having said all and bearing in mind the need of modern times, we cannot afford to ignore challenges such as AIDS but the modus operandi of fighting such dangers should be construed on the basis of thorough research and groundwork and not just for the sake of rhetoric.

After seeing all the disastrous failure of programmes like 'family planning' and their unwanted by-products, a developing nation like ours cannot afford to carry out a reckless experiment with the future of this land.

Heading: Firangs from US 'n UK get knotty in Thar - Indian Express
Content:
Just before the beginning of New Year, Meerut a district lying north east of New Delhi, witnessed scary scenes of couples sitting in the park getting thrashed in the full glare of the national television media.

The people roughing up the couples were none else than the uniformed women police of the district.

But when the public came out against this barbarous act on part of the state, the authorities recklessly put the blame on the excuse that, they were receiving regular complaints from the general public and parents in particular about the obscenities going around public places.

With the country going in the transformation phase by the influence of the alien cultures, such an incidence as Meerut gives rise to a debate as to how far should the couples go out in the open so as not to invite unwarranted rage of the society and state playing the spoil sport in their private lives.

"People in India are eligible to elect a government after 18 years of age but they cannot move around with a chap of their choice" protests Arshad Warsi a dental student from Sheikhpura (Bihar). It is a clear-cut case of double standards he asserts as he advises the countrymen to come out of the medieval era.

But Salik from Araria (Bihar) feels that though the couples have a right to freedom even in the open areas the couple should feel the responsibility they ought to shoulder in the public place. And if things go out of place state should interfere to set things right, but in a sensitive way.

Mushkoor from Darbhanga (Bihar) believes that couples moving out in the open cannot be stopped but certain places should be marked for them so that they can have their time out.

Verlia from Tura (Manipur) strongly resents the use of force for the concern for morality cause, as she warns if the free movement of the young couples is frustrated in open places they are going to find new places for themselves which can give rise to new socio-cultural problems.

Conny, who hails from Jilin (China) is quite overt about the conduct of young couples in the public. Holding hands is OK but kissing around in the public places should be something, which should be taken care of by the young couples. On asking how does the Chinese society reacts in such situations she says that, morality has to be followed everywhere.

"We have places in our towns, which are known as points haunted by the young couples. As such families and kids stay away from such places and the couples are also not embarrassed by the unwanted crowd." She strongly puts forward that though couples should be careful, while sporting their demeanor but police should not go around teaching them the dos and don'ts.

Elie from South Korea feels comfortable while admitting that in her country people can move around by holding hands and shoulders of each other and even sporting occasional kisses. "I enjoy a date with my boyfriend but we have joints marked for such activities."

Deepak from Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh) is reluctant to support the couples having their own time in places such as parks. He says that parks are meant for everyone from the families to the elderly people and the kids.

"Couples should not take such places for granted."

Rishi Mishra from Deoghar joins Deepak in supporting the action taken by the lady Inspector in Meerut and hails it as a "Correct step to ensure decorum."

Satish Gupta from Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh) is quite candid, when he reveals that couples have a right to go to parks but they should bear the Indian culture in mind and keep a check on their blatant gestures.

"When my father called from home and desired to pay a visit to parks of Delhi, I was speechless for moment, for it could be embarrassing for me to accompany him, where all such things happen."

Bagdevi from Phulwani (Orissa) hints out that that the couples should be self-cultured instead of the culture being imposed on them.

Ispita too from Phulwani (Orissa) asserts that couples should limit their behaviour to such an extent so that people around them are not embarrassed.

Anjana Bakshi from Damoh (Madhya Pradesh) rubbishes the right of couples moving out in the open as she maintains, State has a right to keep a check on the un-required activities. As it is, college and school goers bunk their classes at the cost of their studies, which is certainly not a good sign for any society.

Vikram from Banda (Bihar) seems quite practical as he exhorts that the couples having their time out in the open have always been in conflict with the conservative society such as India. So, even if parks and other public places should be open to them, care should be taken to ensure that enough notice boards are put around with the do's and don'ts of the particular place be mentioned on them so that the couples can take guard of their activities without causing problems to the common crowd moving around.

Heading: Day after, fear stalks Kokrajhar - Indian Express
Content:
Talk about Rajasthan and vast stretch of deserts cloud your vision about one of the naturally challenged regions of the subcontinent that is India.

Bikaner is a district lying in the northwestern part of the desert state. The sleepy town found in the medieval ages has enough to boast of, when it comes to culture and history.

The rich tradition is still carried on by the structures that dot the city both in the walls and outside it.

The magnificent havelis and forts accompanied with ancient temples in the background of undulating dunes make it one of the most important components of the Golden triangle of Tourism India, which has a merit of attracting largest number of foreign tourists to the land.





A small village called Katariyasar situated a couple of kilometers from this far-flung district has the honour of hosting a camel festival every year in the month of January.

The extravaganza organised by the combined efforts of the district administration and Tourism Department of Rajasthan has very fascinating events as it unfolds in the mild cool breeze of the dunes.

The event has the global presence in the terms of tourists thronging the place from all over the country, as well as far off counties such as Switzerland, France, Austria, England and USA.





The events are as colourful like their description such as 'Tug of War' between foreigners and the local people. Then comes the feast time serving desserts and meals prepared with camel milk giving once in the lifetime experience.

Once the appetite is through its way there is a very unusual race where there is a fierce competition, and the participants are none other than the king of desert.

Camels run like leopards in their bid to win the heart of the foreign visitors and fly with the dust of the desert.

It is just not other place for foreign tourists to have fun and pay for it. It is an experience, which remains with them throughout their lifetime. With the day full of fun and frolic the night seems to be even more eager to embrace the foreign guests and embrace them in its twirls of darkness with a big bonfire with a story of its own.

People from 'Sidh'(Masters) community dance on thick fire barefoot for hours, as people both Indians and foreigners look at them in with awe and praise. Legend has it that these 'Sidh' people, who follow 36 rules as stipulated by their religion and are blessed by the powers to be, so as not to be affected by the heat of the burning embers of the red hot wood turned into burning coke.

It looks as if all the skies scatter over and above the burning embers to bless and witness the magnificent dancers of fire.





But the warmth of the fire is found somewhere else. It is in the ties, which the guests from thousands of miles, who come here to stay for a few days nourish in their hearts. It could also be discovered in the faith reposed in the traditions and rituals of this land.

Local dailies were replete with colourful photos of the groom and bride in the local attire and sporting true Indian colours. Be it Eleanor from UK or Jenny from Netherlands, who disclosed, "Oh we decided to marry in the traditional (Indian) way just two days before the camel festival."

No doubt it would be a lifetime experience for her to carry the sweet memoirs of getting married in a small village.

These marriages were witnessed by agni (the sacred fire) along with hundreds of villagers, who cheered up the whole ceremony by their voluntary co-operation. Pandits (priests) were arranging to ensure the solemnising of marriages with the full recitation of the Vedic hymns (mantras) and religious chores.

As Will from England says, he felt overwhelmed after his marriage. Not only that women kept the whole atmosphere live and homely singing the marriage songs blessing the newly wed they also arranged for the nitty-gritty's of the occasion.

The guests anyways were reveling in the warmth of hosts and the musical bonfires. Whoever said foreigners come to India for tourism alone.!

Heading: Chandrayaan sends first photos of earth’s surface - Indian Express
Content:
Five-year-old Joy Mondol shrieks as he lies on a bed in Kokrajhar's civil hospital. He was walking down the vegetable market with his grandmother when the second blast took place. His grandmother, Arati Debnath, is one of the 21 persons who died in the serial blasts here. Joy has multiple injuries all over his body. "How will I explain to him what has happened," said his father, Bankalal Mondol, who works as a mechanic in Sikkim and had come home to celebrate Kalipuja.

The district has almost come to a halt, but for visits by politicians. The marketplace wears a deserted look. The idol in the local Kalipuja pandal is intact, but there's no one to immerse the idol. Bits of clothes and shoes lie around the blast sites. The police have cordoned off the crater that marks the site of one of the blasts.

"I heard a loud noise and went out of my shop. There was chaos and one could hear only cries of the injured," said Jayanta Pal, who stays near the marketplace where the blast took place.

Sampad Ali, the only earning member of his family, has lost his makeshift shop. "I was busy attending customers when I heard a loud noise and saw a flash of light and dust. Something hit me and I fell unconscious," said Sampad, who is among the 29 injured being treated at the local hospital.

When Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil visited the district, he was greeted by a small but angry mob. "At this moment, I cannot say whether jehadis are involved or not. I will see to it that the guilty are punished," he assured.

Apart from meeting the injured in the hospital and inspecting the blast sites, Patil held a meeting with Bodoland Territorial Council members, who submitted a memorandum to him.

Hagrama Mohilary, chief of the Council, said, "We have requested the Home Minister to provide us a relief package of Rs 50 crore. We have also asked him to deploy additional security forces, besides demanding a high-level inquiry into the incident."

Heading: Chiranjeevi declares support to Telangana - Indian Express
Content:
Nine days after it was launched, Chandrayaan-I, India's first mission to the moon, on Friday sent back the first pictures — that of earth's surface. Pictures of moon's surface will come later after the spacecraft reaches nearer the moon.

Black and white pictures taken by the Terrain Mapping Camera, one of the 11 payloads on-board Chandrayaan-I, showed the landscape around Australia. One of the images showing the northern coast of Australia was taken at 8 am from a height of 9,000 km. The other image was taken at 12.30 pm from a height of 70,000 km and shows Australia's southern coast.

Analysis of the pictures at the ISRO centres showed that the camera was performing just as expected. The pictures were shown to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh when ISRO chairman G Madhavan Nair called on him on Friday to brief him on the successful launch of Chandrayaan, a Government statement said. Nair also told the Prime Minister about the launch sequence and subsequent operations performed on the spacecraft to push it progressively into higher orbits. He informed the Prime Minister that so far everything had gone as per the plan. He presented a model of Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle C-11, which put the spacecraft into space, and also Chandrayaan-I to the PM who congratulated ISRO and the Chandrayaan team on successfully achieving a major milestone in India's space programme.

Now, Chandrayaan-I is orbiting around the earth in an elliptical path in which it will go to a maximum distance of 267,000 km from the earth. It will take six days for Chandrayaan-I to go around the earth once in this orbit.

Heading: Another stockbroker commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Actor-turned-politician Chiranjeevi on Friday extended his party Praja Rajyam's support for the formation of a separate Telangana state if the Centre came up with such a proposal.

The announcement, which is expected to alter political equations in Andhra Pradesh ahead of Assembly elections, was made by the filmstar during his road show in the Telangana heartland.

"It is for the Central Government to take a decision on creation of Telangana state. If it comes up with such a proposal, our party will not stand in the way," he told a gathering in this backward Telangana town in Karimnagar district.

Acknowledging the "sentiments" of people, Chiranjeevi said, "I know the people of this region are overwhelmingly in favour of a separate state. I respect your feelings. If you are convinced that creation of a separate state will ensure rapid development, I am with you."

The actor's announcement was greeted with loud applause from a massive gathering. His fans soon burst crackers and danced with joy.

"Let me declare here and now that my party will support if the Centre comes forward with a proposal to create Telangana state," the actor announced.

The Telangana region had suffered decades of neglect and discrimination, he said, adding the statehood movement reflected the "self-respect" of the people.

With Telangana emerging as a key issue ahead of elections, Chiranjeevi's endorsement of the statehood demand is expected to speed up the process of political re-alignment in the state.

The Telangana Rashtra Samithi and the Left parties are keenly watching the impact of the actor's road show in the region before deciding on poll alliances.

Heading: Quota system all the way as Cong list of 117 is out - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani human rights activist and former human rights minister Ansar Burney on Friday visited a woman admitted to a city hospital for more than two years. The woman, Barao Abdul, claims she is from Harchowal area in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and has been undergoing treatment in the National Medical College and Hospital since August 2006.

"I met the woman. From what I have seen, it seems that she is from PoK. The places she has mentioned are there," said Burney, who also took up the cause of Sarabjit Singh who is on death row in Pakistan. "I have taken Barao's pictures. We will upload them on the internet. I will also get in touch with the PoK Government and request them to publish her photos in local newspapers there."

Burney, the special advisor to the UN Human Rights Commission in Geneva, claimed the woman was in good health. "She said she had no problems in the hospital. But she said she wanted to go back home," he added.

Barao was found in a dishevelled condition on Digha-Contai road in East Midnapur in April 2006. She was admitted, first to Contai hospital and later shifted to the state hospital in August 2006 after intervention by the state Government and Diganto, an NGO.

Seated on bed number one of the psychiatric ward, Barao keeps yelling "mujhe wapas jana hai... mujhe ghar pahuncha do (I want to go back, send me home)".

"She was admitted on August 28, 2006, with severe psychotic disorder," recalled Srijit Das, who has looked after Barao since she was admitted to the state hospital in Kolkata.

The Pakistan High Commission in India had tried to secure Barao's return, and Kolkata High Court had in 2006 also ordered the state Government to find out her home. But nothing happened.

Doctors claim Barao has recovered to a great extent. "She is usually cheerful and helps out patients in need," said Das. "But sometimes loneliness takes the better of the woman and then she cries out, 'take me back home'."

When she was hospitalised, Barao could only recall that she had a husband and children back home and there was an apple orchard near her home that belonged to her father.

Heading: Development is focus of NC 15-yr vision document - Indian Express
Content:
Weeks after Congress president Sonia Gandhi called for an end to "quota system" in the ticket distribution exercise at a Congress Working Committee meeting, the party has resorted to the same to accommodate nominees of top leaders in the faction-ridden Madhya Pradesh unit.

In the list of 117 candidates announced on Friday, influential leaders — including Arjun Singh, Digvijay Singh, Kamal Nath, Jyotiraditya Scindia and Suresh Pachauri, among others — got a fair share of seats, with the Union Commerce Minister getting a lion's share, according to party sources.

At least 35 candidates known to be "loyal" to Kamal Nath were allotted tickets while around 20 recommended by former chief minister Digvijay Singh figured in the list, said sources. Kamal Nath had a major say in the selection of candidates in Mahakaushal region, his stronghold. Digvijay's influence was evident from the list of candidates for Gwalior and Malwa regions.

At a rally in Chhindwara some time back, Digvijay had supported a proposal, floated by former PCC chief Subhash Yadav, that the Union Commerce Minister should lead the party in the election. With many chief ministerial aspirants, notably PCC chief Suresh Pachauri, lodging protest with the party High Command against this move, the Congress had to officially clarify that it would not project any CM candidate. But, given Kamal Nath's apparent influence in ticket distribution exercise, he seems to be gaining ground. Singh has already ruled himself out as a contender for the CM's post and is not even contesting the Assembly election.

Scindia's stamp in Gwalior region was also evident from today's list, although he also had a say in deciding the candidates in other regions, said sources. There were at least 18 Scindia nominees in today's list, said sources. He has, of late, been holding successful public rallies across the state to dispel the perception in a section of party leadership about his influence being confined to one region.

M Veerappa Moily, who headed the Screening Committee on Madhya Pradesh had on Wednesday evening, called a meeting of senior leaders from the state to reconcile their differences over candidates. Ahmed Patel, political secretary to the Congress president, was also present at the meeting. Although Arjun Singh was not in the meeting, the Screening Committee had called on the Human Resource Development Minister twice to seek his views about different candidates. About a dozen candidates, recommended by Arjun, were accommodated in today's list, said sources. Pachauri also managed to get tickets for at least 17 of his nominees, said sources.

Among those who figured in the list included Leader of Opposition in the Assembly Jamuna Devi from Kukshi Assembly constituency, HRD Minister Arjun Singh's son and state campaign committee chairman Ajay Singh from Churhat and Subhash Yadav from Kasrawad.

Heading: 13 securitymen injured in first attack since J-K polls announced - Indian Express
Content:
The National Conference on Friday unveiled its vision document of governance for the next 15 years. The document sets out goals of "self-reliance, eradication of unemployment, environmental conservation and good governance in Jammu and Kashmir".

The vision document comes a week after the party's arch rival People's Democratic Party (PDP) released its self-rule document which advocates "shared sovereignty" between India and Pakistan over Kashmir without redrawing the Line of Control. The NC's document, however, mainly focuses on development and governance in the state.

"The development and the resolution of Kashmir problem are two separate issues," NC president Omar Abdullah said at a press conference at the party headquarters after releasing the 53-page vision document. "We have to de-link the two issues."

Abdullah who was also flanked by party patron and former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah said the party would come with another document that will exclusively deal with the international dimensions of the Kashmir problem. He, however, didn't set any deadline for the document. Abdullah said the vision document is an implementable road map for development and good governance. The vision document promises that the party would encourage sustained dialogue between all stakeholders to arrive at a lasting solution.

"At the political level, the NC Government shall try to convince those who have taken recourse to violence and intimidation as a means to achieve their goal, that the lessons of history are very clear that all social, political discourse are resolved ultimately by discourse and dialogue," Abdullah said. "And in this context NC would strive to make the people understand that restoration of autonomy in its pristine form is the only viable solution."

Heading: Advani draws the line: ‘Sangh links don’t matter, punish if guilty’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the first strike after the seven-phase Assembly election was announced in Jammu and Kashmir, militants on Friday attacked a police station in north Kashmir's Baramulla town, injuring 13 police and CRPF men including two officers.

At the time of the attack, senior police officers were holding a meet with citizens at the police station about the law and order in the town.

The grenade, officials said, exploded on the premises of the police station where CRPF and police jawans were waiting for deployment orders. Among the injured are Inspector and Sub-inspector of CRPF. A police spokesman confirmed the attack. "The seriously injured personnel were referred to Srinagar," the spokesman added.

Senior police officers who were in the police station at the time of the attack had a narrow escape. Soon after the attack, police and CRPF cordoned off the area. Three persons were apprehended by the police from a nearby construction site for questioning.

For the past many days, Baramulla town has been witnessing protests. Baramulla, an important constituency in north Kashmir, is going to polls in the fourth phase of elections.

Heading: UPA lacks political will, ability to fight terror: Advani - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after BJP president Rajnath Singh said an "Aarushi-like case was being built around Pragya" and that "no one believing in the ideology of cultural nationalism could ever be involved in terror attacks", L K Advani on Friday sought to draw a line in the party on the debate over the Sadhvi and former ABVP leader arrested in connection with the Malegaon blast.

"If the Government has any proof against anyone, he/she should be punished even if they have any association with any Sangh Parivar affiliate," the BJP's prime ministerial candidate asserted, indicating that law was supreme for the party.

In an interview with The Indian Express, Rajnath Singh had come to the defence of Pragya Singh Thakur, inviting sharp reactions from the Congress and other non-BJP parties. Advani today indicated that he was inclined to take "let the law take its own course" line, favoured by others in the party such as Arun Jaitley.

However, the party continues to speak in many voices. "In my entire term as (Maharashtra) Home Minister, I never ever came across one single Hindu terrorist," party general secretary and former Maharashtra home minister Gopinath Munde told The Indian Express on Friday. "A Hindu cannot ever become a terrorist."

Asked about the slew of arrests from his home state, including that of the chief of Maharashtra BJP ex-servicemen cell, Munde said: "One cannot arrest someone merely on the basis of a few phone calls. The arrests are an attempt by the (Congress-NCP) Government there to deflect attention from their shortcomings."

Veteran BJP leader Pyarelal Khandelwal endorsed the view, as did another party general secretary, Vinay Katiyar. "A Hindu by virtue of his samskaras (values) cannot ever become a terrorist," Khandelwar told the Express.

Madhya Pradesh minister Kailash Vijayvargiya, who was in Delhi on Friday, added: "I have known Pragya and can vouch for the fact that she is not a terrorist."

On the discordant voices emanating from within the BJP and the wider Sangh Parivar, a top leader said: "Obviously Advani's would be the last word on the issue, even if others are speaking in different voices. A meta-narrative on 'Islamic terrorism being a major threat today' was earlier sought to be circulated by influential functionaries in the party, but Advani intervened to say that religion and terror must not be linked."

Heading: A 2006 probe had also thrown up ex-servicemen, Bhonsala school links - Indian Express
Content:
Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Lal Krishna Advani accused the UPA Government of lacking in political will as well as ability to fight terror and reiterated the BJP's demand for a legal system and legal structure to fight terrorism.

Advani, who arrived here on Friday, also called for exerting diplomatic pressure on Bangladesh so that it stopped terrorists from using its soil for anti-India activities.

"The ISI of Pakistan is sending lot of elements into India through Bangladesh. We must exert diplomatic pressure on Bangladesh and compel it to stop such things. Bangladesh must not be used for anti-India activities," he told newspersons before flying back to New Delhi.

Advani described Thursday's blasts in Guwahati, Kokrajhar, Barpeta Road and Bongaigaon as the "biggest" terrorist strike in the country so far and held the Assam Government responsible for it. "The Centre and the Assam Government must be held equally responsible for the abysmal failure to protect the lives of common people," he said.

The senior BJP leader also said that forces from across the border were directly involved in the Assam blasts. "Till the other day, we only had information of local hands in the blasts in different parts of the country.

Direct involvement of forces from across the border was not evident until the blasts here on Thursday," he said.

Advani also came down heavily on the ULFA which had issued a denial immediately after the blasts. "Don't spare the ULFA. It cannot be exonerated just because it had issued a prompt denial," he said.

The former deputy prime minister also suspected SIMI's involvement in the blasts, claiming the outfit was operating under other names in Assam. He particularly mentioned Muslim Students Association of Assam (MUSA) and Muslim United Liberation Front of Assam (MULTA) as frontal wings of the SIMI in the state.

Heading: Cabinet nod for Right to Education Bill - Indian Express
Content:
While the arrest of former Army major Ramesh Upadhyay and questioning of Lt Col Prasad Purohit in connection with the September 29 blasts in Malegaon and Modasa has raised serious concerns, a probe conducted by the Maharashtra Anti Terror Squad two years ago had thrown up similar startling revelations about retired servicemen providing weapons and explosives training to Hindu hardline outfits in the state.

A probe into an April 5, 2006, accidental pipe-bomb blast at Nanded had indicated the role of a former Indian Navy official in training Bajrang Dal activists. Significantly, it had identified Bhonsala Military School in Nashik — whose name has also come up in connection with the Malegaon blasts — as the place where such training camps were organised under the supervision of "ex-servicemen and a senior retired Intelligence Bureau (IB) official".

Subsequent to its investigations, the ATS had named Sanatkumar Ragvithal Bhate, a retired Navy officer hailing from Pune, as one of the several witnesses in the case.

In his statements to the ATS recorded on April 20 and May 18, 2006, Bhate stated that he had been associated with the RSS since 1996. He claimed that in March or April 2000, he had received a telephone call from a Bajrang Dal office located near the Saraswati Mandir School in Pune, and was allegedly asked by Bajrang Dal leader Milind Parade to train his activists in the use of gelatine sticks at a camp in the city. Bhate stated that he trained around 50 activists, including Himanshu Panse, who was arrested for the Nanded pipe-blomb blast.

In his statements, Bhate said he was asked by Parade to help at a bigger camp organised the Bhonsala Military School, and that for this, Parade and three of his associates carried 300 gelatine sticks with them from Pune. Bhate told ATS investigators that the camp had been organised by the RSS and about 115 activists from across the country were trained in karate, ground obstacles and firing of revolvers. Two retired ex-serviceman and a senior retired officer from the IB were also present, he stated.

The ATS chargesheet in the case states that Panse and another accused, Maroti Keshav Wagh, underwent 40 days of training at the school.

Additional Director General of Police (Railways) K P Raghuvanshi, who was ATS chief at the time, told The Indian Express: "Some of the arrested accused in the Nanded blast also mentioned that they had received training from a former Army officer whom they referred to as 'fauji'. However, we could not get further details in this regard due to a lack of leads. I do not remember the finer details of the case."

Calling it unfortunate that defence officials were being found to be involved in acts of terror, Raghuvanshi recalled meeting Lt Col Purohit at a coordination meeting as he was a military intelligence officer.

Heading: Senior IPS officer serves legal notice to minister - Indian Express
Content:
The UPA Government has given its nod to the Right to Education Bill promising free and compulsory education for children between 6-14 age group.

"The Bill has been considered at several levels by the Group of Ministers (GoM). The Cabinet has approved the text of the Bill," Finance Minister P Chidambaram told reporters on Friday about the decision taken at the Cabinet meeting a day before. This proposal for this legislation has been languishing with the Government since the Parliament passed the 86th Constitutional amendment giving every child between the age of 6 and 14 years the right to free and compulsory educationin December 2002.

The Bill had hit a deadlock over how the states and the Centre will share the financial burden. Subsequently, the Cabinet had referred the issue to a Group of Ministers, which in August, worked out a burden sharing formula acceptable to both sides. Chidambaram, however, refrained from divulging more details citing the code of conduct imposed by the Election Commission in the wake of the state elections.

In another decision, the Cabinet on Friday decided to introduce the South Asian University (SAU) Bill before the Parliament. The idea of setting up SAU was proposed by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh during the 13th SAARC Summit held in Dhaka in 2005. For the purpose of setting up the university, which is aimed at providing world-class facilities and professional faculty to students and researchers from SAARC countries, the Delhi Development Authority will allot 100 acres of land near Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) in Delhi.

In another major decision, the Cabinet has decided to enact the Public Funded Research and Development (Protection, Utilisation, and Regulation of Intellectual Property) Bill. Apart from providing for scientists and researchers claiming for their share into the intellectual property generated in government funded research and labs, the Bill would also provide uniform legal framework for protection and utilisation of the intellectual property rights generated by Government funding.

Heading: Sri Lankan President to visit India on November 12 - Indian Express
Content:
Senior IPS officer and former Gaya SP Paresh Saxena has served a legal notice to Urban Development Minister Bhola Prasad Singh, warning that a defamation suit would be filed against him if he did not apologise for using libelous language against the officer.

Saxena, who was transferred as Gaya SP three months ago, reportedly for passing "adverse comments" against a senior JD(U) leader in his supervision report in connection with LJP leader and former MP Rajesh Kumar's murder in 2005, alleged through the legal notice that Singh "insulted him publicly during his stint in Gaya" allegedly for "pursuing the case against the JD(U) leader holding an important post".

Saxena's lawyer Ritesh Kumar said the legal notice was served on the BJP minister under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure mandating a 60-day period before filing a defamation suit against a Government official.

The lawyer said the minister "insulted and demoralised" the officer and used "libelous and defamatory" language at a function in Gaya for not presenting a bouquet to the minister. Saxena, after being transferred to the police head- quarters here, decided to serve a legal notice. The IPS officer sought to know if "the unwarranted insult" was the price of his "integrity and honesty".

"I have not yet received the notice. Government officials have to follow protocol in a parliamentary democracy," said Singh. As for allegations that he was behind the officer's transfer, Singh said he would answer through legal channels.

Heading: Widow of Amarnath activist in BJP 2nd list for J-K polls - Indian Express
Content:
Pressure from key UPA ally, DMK, to act on the Sri Lanka situation may have eased for the time being, but India will get Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa as a visitor by mid-November.

It is learnt that Rajapaksa has confirmed his participation at the BIMSTEC summit on November 13. He is expected to arrive late on November 12.

BIMSTEC is a trade grouping of seven countries in the region around Bay of Bengal, which includes Bangladesh, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, besides India and Sri Lanka.

The Lankan President's one-on-one meeting with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh is being worked upon by the diplomats of both sides, on the sidelines of the summit, which is likely to be attended by heads of other countries as well.

During the meeting, talks are expected to be held on a proposed agreement where Tamil fishermen will get licences for fishing in certain identified areas and will not be fired at by the Lankan Navy.

Heading: Nun rape: SI, four other policemen suspended - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP Central Election Committee on Friday released its second list for Jammu and Kashmir and first for Madhya Pradesh. The party hopes to finalise its Delhi list and complete its Madhya Pradesh list on Saturday.

The highlight of the party's second J&K list was the name of Shilpi, the wife of Kuldeep Dogra, who has been fielded from the Bishna seat in Jammu. Kuldeep's self-immolation bid had ignited the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti stir in Jammu in a big way.

Calling for "due share in power structure for Jammu", the BJP hopes to make a huge impact on the Hindu-dominated seats of Jammu. Other prominent names on the list are former Union minister of state for defence Chaman Lal Gupta from Jammu (West), BJP J&K unit president Ashok Khajuria from Jammu (East) and former state unit president Nirmal Singh from Jammu (Gandhinagar).

The party's second list of 39 candidates has 27 names from the Jammu region and 12 from the Valley. "Of these, 27 candidates will contest from the Jammu region and 12 from the Kashmir valley. We have decided to support three candidates of the Union Territories Front in the Leh-Ladakh region," said BJP general secretary, in charge of J&K elections, Arun Jaitley. He added the party's main objective was to ensure that there was no split in the "nationalist votes". The party plans to contest as many as 55 seats on its symbol in the 87-member House.

The party will also support a couple of candidates with "nationalist credentials" in the Valley. The BJP hopes to make huge gains in the Hindu-dominated seats of Jammu. The party has not fielded any member of the Sri Amarnath Sangarsh Samiti. "It is well-known that all BJP members from the state were supporting the Amarnath agitation," Jaitley said.

For the 230-member House in Madhya Pradesh, the BJP finalised the candidature for 115 seats. In its first list, as many as 28 sitting MLAs have been denied party tickets while 47 will contest again under the saffron banner.

Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will contest from his old constituency Budhni. The party also denied tickets to 27 sitting MLAs, including one Cabinet minister, Narain Kabirpanthi. "The list of 115 names has 19 OBCs, 20 Scheduled Caste and 33 Scheduled Tribe candidates. Fourteen women have also been fielded in the first list," said party general secretary Ananth Kumar.

Heading: RSS pracharak in police net for ‘helping’ abductors of girl - Indian Express
Content:
The Orissa Government on Friday suspended five policemen of Orissa State Armed Police, who allegedly stood watching as a 29-year-old Roman Catholic nun was gang-raped in Kandhamal district, on charges of official misconduct and negligence of duty.

Sub-Inspector Rasananda Mallick, Havildar Major K N Mohapatra and havildars S K Hamim, J S Khan and B K Mohanty were suspended for alleged dereliction of duty after a four-page joint report by Kandhamal District Collector Dr Krishan Kumar and SP Praveen Kumar proved their inaction, state Home Secretary T K Mishra said. Though the Home Secretary and the Collector refused to reveal details of the report, sources said the report was a damning evidence as to how the police became a mute spectator to the sordid saga of rape, molestation and public humiliation of the nun and the priest.

The five along with a few other jawans of 6th and 7th battalion of OSAP were camping at Kanjamendi-Nuagaon ME School in front of the Jan Vikash NGO where the nun was allegeldly raped and molested and Christian priest Fr Thomas Chellan bashed up during the Kandhamal riots on August 25 afternoon. The nun, at a press conference recently, recounted how she went to the policemen for escaping further humiliation after being raped. "I went to the policemen, asking them to protect me. I sat in between two policemen, but they did not move," she said. Other villagers who witnessed the ordeal of the nun also confirmed that the armed policemen did not fire a single shot from their sophisticated INSAS rifles to scare off the assailants.

The state Government has already suspended Baliguda police station inspector K Narayan Rao on October 4 for his failure in getting the medical report of the rape from the sub-divisional medical hospital near his police station and arrest the accused. With this, the total number of policemen in the district who were suspended in the case has risen to six.

Heading: VHP leader held for anti-Modi SMSes - Indian Express
Content:
The police have detained a former RSS pracharak in Orissa for his alleged role in the abduction of an 18-year-old girl from an impoverished family in coastal Kendrapara district.

The police revealed that they have detained Nayak, 45, on the suspicion of being hand-in-glove with a person accused of abducting the girl. The girl, a resident of Jadupur villager in Patkura block of Kendrapara, was reportedly lured to Bhubaneswar by her uncle Baikuntha Biswal on May 11 on the promise that he would find her a job. The girl's father, a poor peasant, is suffering from cancer and had allowed his daughter to go with Biswal.

Kendrapara sub-divisional police officer Jaydev Sarangi said Nayak's name came to the fore after police arrested Biswal and his daughter Priyanka Biswal, the missing girl's classmate, on October 25. "During interrogation he revealed the name of Nayak and one Patitapaban Samal. He (Nayak) told us that he had left the girl with Nayak's NGO Sookruti," Sarangi told The Indian Express.
